# Of the Second Volume
## SECOND TREATISE,
### Concerning the
# PRETERNATU-
# RAL HISTORY OF
# BOTH WORLDS. <note>original: "Utriusque Mundi." Fludd’s central philosophy was that the universe (Macrocosm) and the human being (Microcosm) mirror each other in every detail.</note>

->*Divided into three Sections,*<-

In Which
> The First deals with the causes of Meteors <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning, as well as their biological equivalents within the human body.</note>, both Macrocosmic and Microcosmic, and their effects in general.
> The Second treats the particular impressions of Meteors, regarding both favorable and adverse health; and the signs that foretell them in the past, present, and future.
> The Third explains with great precision the method for averting the worst and most unhealthy future outcomes of Meteors, for overcoming their current attacks, and finally for restoring former health that has been lost.

->*By the Author*<-

## ROBERT FLUDD, also known as de Fluctibus, <note>A Latinization of his surname "Fludd," which means "of the floods" or "of the waves."</note> Esquire,
## and Doctor of Medicine of Oxford.

# History of the Preternatural Microcosm

<note>The "Preternatural Microcosm" refers to the human body when it is in an abnormal or diseased state, or influenced by forces beyond the ordinary course of nature.</note>

The second Treatise of the Microcosm <note>The "Little World," a common Renaissance concept where the human body reflects the structure of the universe</note>, which concerns the art of Medicine, is divided into 3 Sections, of which:

- **The First treats of the**
    - { Theosophical <note>Divine wisdom and its relation to the body</note>,
    - { Cabalistic <note>Mystical traditions, often involving the Hebrew alphabet, applied to healing</note>,
    - { Physiological,
    - **Portions of Medicine, which we have treated extensively in this present Volume.**

- **The Second is divided into three portions; of which**
    <margin>All of these are reduced into a single Section, occupying the space of one volume.</margin>
    - **The First concerns the healthy or healing part of medicine (which is called <term>hygieinón</term> <note>original Greek: "υγιεινόν"; the study of health preservation</note>), showing the method for maintaining health, either:**
        - **Super-celestial** <note>Influences from the divine realm, beyond the stars</note>
            - By the divine influence moving downwards.
            - By the prayers of the good penetrating upwards.
            - By a life of piety resisting the assaults of wicked Demons.
        - **Celestial** <note>Influences from the stars and planets</note>
            - By the observation of malevolent aspects <note>The geometric angles between planets</note> and caution in avoiding their effects.
            - By the science of repelling the misfortunes of both the Planets and the fixed stars, and preventing their malice.
        - **Elemental:**
            - **By the external quality of the elements. In which consists:**
                - The climate of the location.
                - The four quarters of the year: { Hot, Cold, Moist, Dry. }
                - The disposition of the weather.
            - **By the internal respect and factors peculiar to the body: under which are contained:**
                - Dietary regimen.
                - Complexion <note>The unique balance of "humors"—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—in an individual</note>.
                - Age.
                - Motion and Rest.
                - Exercises.
                - Affects of the mind <note>Emotions and passions</note>.
    - **The Second concerns preternatural "meteors" <note>In Renaissance medicine, "meteors" refer to vapors, winds, or disturbances inside the body that mimic atmospheric phenomena like storms</note> or unhealthy and morbid things. See A.**

- **The Third narrates the cunning skill for discussing and dispelling those "meteors" that behave preternaturally. See B.**

# TO THE BENEVOLENT OBSERVER,
## HEALTH OF SOUL AND BODY
->IN THE MESSIAH.<-

Behold, Dear Reader, in the most holy and ineffable name of Almighty God, uniquely belonging to Him alone, and in the living and fiery inspiration and divine breath of the individual symbols of the Trinity—namely the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit—contained in the characters Yod, Vav, and He <note>original: י. ו. & ה.</note>, I have successfully begun to proclaim to the world some mysteries of that wonderful name, namely YHWH <note>original: יהוה; the Tetragrammaton</note>, brought forth from them in a supersubstantial manner. Having crossed the midpoint of this task without any mental obstacle, I have finally reached the end, completion, and peak of this work at a fortunate and desired level of perfection. May my glorious God also grant that, by the most powerful pronunciation of that unique, incomparable, and supreme name, and by its ineffable whisper, as if by fiery arrows drawn from His quiver—stronger than any fortress—the slanders of the mockers <note>original: "Momorum"; referring to Momus, the Greek god of mockery and criticism</note> and the malevolent may be cast headlong into the Stygian waves of wretched oblivion. May the babbling of the sons of ignorance be submerged in the foolish waters of the Lake of Lethe <note>A river in the underworld associated with forgetfulness</note>, and may the rebukes of the insane and the disciples of worldly wisdom be repelled all the way to the center of darkness. For the ineffable word of the Lord (in which alone is truth and perfection) shall remain forever; while the false deceits of the Devil, the vain delusions of the world, and the deceptive phantoms of the spirit of darkness shall perish, vanish, be reduced to nothing, and be driven into eternal exile from all human memory.

To you, therefore, O brothers of true doctrine and more abstruse Philosophy—flying high on the wings of divine mystery—and to you, disciples of my order, who are removed from hateful derision, perverse obstinacy, and wicked cursing, and who desire with me to penetrate into the sanctuary of truth and the monastery of the secret theosophy of mysteries; to you, I say, indeed to you alone, do I turn the thread of my speech and discourse.

And although I confess that I have brought this work to light, published it, and revealed it to your eyes according to the smallness of my capacity and intellect (which I know to be meager) based on thought and contemplation alone (with no practical experience preceding it), nevertheless, if you explore the matter a little more accurately with the exalted mind of a true and sincere Christian, you will perceive with an open gaze and enlightened eyes that the principles of our sciences are derived from the sacred fountain and the origin of all truth, rather than from the vain and uncertain opinions of the <term>Ethnics</term><note>original: "Ethnicorum"; Fludd uses this to refer to non-Christian, particularly ancient Greek or Roman, philosophers whose wisdom he considers secondary to divine revelation.</note>. Indeed, we consider it a form of idolatry to venerate the opinions and inventions of those who worship foreign gods (while neglecting the spring of all wisdom and knowledge) with such devotion and stubbornness, as if no learning could be acquired in the method of preserving health, the diagnosis of diseases, or the knowledge of preparing and applying medicines to restore original health, except through Pagan spirits—namely, the Greek, Arabic, or Latin schools. In fact, we are informed by the excellent teaching of the Prophet of how impious and profane this imitation of Pagan doctrine is; he teaches us that it is not fitting to desert the fountain of all wisdom and seek art, science, and understanding in foreign regions, *as did the children of Hagar <note>original: "Agareni"</note> and those who were in Teman: for they never recognized the way of true wisdom. the Prophet seems to argue for the difference between the vain opinion of the world—born in the womb of darkness from the uncertain sins of men and overwhelmed by ignorance, then brought forth into the light by a sort of aborted, rash, and untimely effort—and that unique, most holy, and only true knowledge handed down from JEHOVAH God through the Word or Wisdom (which is the unanimous Spirit of discipline) to just men distinguished by their piety.

Therefore, considering the discrepancy between these types of knowledge—the divine and the human—again and again, the Royal Psalmist <note>referring to King David, the traditional author of the Psalms</note> (being well-versed in both) and exulting in the divine spirit, driven as if by the stings of truth, bursts out in these words: *Psalm 119:99-100. I have become more intelligent than all my teachers, because the testimonies of God are my meditation; I am more prudent than the elders, because I likewise keep your commands.* <note>original: "Ps. 119. 125." Note: The author's citation numbering differs slightly from modern Bibles.</note> The Prophet Daniel also very clearly indicated this difference between divine and human wisdom to King Nebuchadnezzar in the second chapter: *The mystery which the King asks, the Wise men, Magicians, Soothsayers, and Diviners are unable to show the king; but there is a God in heaven revealing mysteries, who will indicate to you, O King, what things are to come in the final times.* Even the Magicians and wise men of Egypt confessed to King Pharaoh, in these express words, that the true knowledge of Jehovah presides and rules over their deceptive arts: *This is the finger of God, etc.*

But I seem to see certain people already murmuring and smiling, who, being deeply immersed in the abyss of unbelief and the mud of ignorance, will object: What do the sacred letters have to do with the art of medicine? Where are the differences of diseases, the causes, signs, prognostics, and the subsequent method of curing to be investigated in the Bible of the divine word? Is it even possible that in the sacred context, medicines suitable for every disease can be found? To these people I respond in a single word (if indeed they desire to be held in the place of wise men): Read, read through, and by reading, understand; and I will undoubtedly satisfy your doubts. But if it does not please you to grant even so small a bit of honor to me and my works, I beseech you not to despise this Christian admonition of mine, relying on the obstinacy or rather impudence of others; flee from the oracles of creatures, and listen to the voice of the Creator with fear and reverence. Adore Him alone, and His word joined with the Holy Spirit, lest you be considered disciples or followers of King Ahaziah <note>original: "Azachiae"</note>, who, when affected by a certain disease, commanded his men to consult Beelzebub, the false and dung-like <note>original: "stercoreum"; a play on the name Baal-Zebub, often interpreted mockingly by Hebrew writers as 'Lord of Dung'</note> god of Ekron, neglecting JEHOVAH the God of Gods, to ask whether he would recover his health from that illness. Because of this, the wrath of JEHOVAH was excited against him, and he died without any help from that false god. *2 Kings 1:16.*

May JEHOVAH be with me, the refuge and protection of my salvation, and may He exalt my horn on high <note>A biblical metaphor for increasing one's strength and status</note>, so that, with His kindness assisting, I may be able to taste and sample the life-giving liquid of His wisdom in this life. By this, I may finally and happily reach the peak of the true jubilee, the height of the Sabbath and rest—the supreme gate of intelligence and closer to the divine presence—by a favorable deity, a lucky omen, and the kind breath of the divine
->Spirit.<-

To whom I respond in almost a single word (if indeed they desire to be held in the place of the wise): Read, read through, but also understand by reading; and I will undoubtedly satisfy your doubts. But if it does not please you to grant so little honor to me and my works, I beseech you: do not, relying on obstinacy or rather impudence, despise this my Christian admonition for the sake of others. ### POSTSCRIPT.

*Lest anyone be discouraged from reading these books of ours, we wish first of all to advise the Reader that an exact knowledge of the Hebrew language is by no means required to understand them; but rather, a simple familiarity with the Hebrew characters <note>The letters of the alphabet.</note> is enough to grasp this work of ours. For indeed, by observing these external or man-made shapes, anyone can correctly proceed toward the truly formal characters—whether <term>Metaphysical</term> <note>Relating to the spiritual or abstract realm beyond the physical.</note> or <term>Physical</term> <note>Relating to the material or natural world.</note> and natural—and can apply themselves usefully to them. For no mystery is found in these merely common and external letters; instead, it resides in those truly spiritual and fiery characters <note>The author suggests a mystical or Kabbalistic view where letters possess an inner spiritual essence or "divine fire."</note> which lie hidden beneath them—just like a treasure in a chest, or a kernel inside a husk. Indeed, those hidden characters are, as it were, the soul and life of these visible ones. One need only commit to memory, therefore, the shapes of those common letters, since beyond that, no further difficulty of the Hebrew language is required for this work of ours. The letters, moreover, are these: א, ב, ג, ד, ה, etc.* <note>The Hebrew letters Aleph, Beth, Gimel, Daleth, and He.</note>

## Prelude on the Nature of the Principle.

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'H' decorated with scrolling foliage and floral patterns.</image-desc>This word *Principle* <note>original Latin: "Principium"</note> appears in the Holy Scriptures written in this way: בראשית <note>original Hebrew: "Bereshith"</note>, which is to say, "In the beginning." This word is derived from the primitive word or root ראש <note>original Hebrew: "Rosh"</note>, which signifies a head, a summit, a peak, or a top. However, if we use the <term>Cabalistic</term> <note>Referring to Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism that interprets the hidden meanings of the Hebrew Bible, often through the shapes and numerical values of its letters.</note> method to carefully observe the characters of this word, we can investigate the order of the entire creation of the world through them. We shall then perceive every portion of the spherical machinery of the universe, each differing from the other in its specific properties.

For the letter ר <note>Resh</note> denotes, in the first place, something like a void or an empty space, and consequently, darkness; for the letter *Resh* is a symbol of poverty and want. Conversely, the letter ש <note>Shin</note> is a symbol of fullness, proving that this void and emptiness—this solitude—is now filled with the presence and light of א <note>Aleph</note>, or <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The personal name of God in the Hebrew Bible.</note>. Furthermore, *Shin* signifies a fiery spirit or "illuminated waters." Finally, א <note>Aleph</note> is the medium and the principle by which the void and the foul, dismal poverty of that ר <note>Resh</note>—or the abyss, upon whose face there was darkness—is removed. Through it, the water, or ה <note>He</note>, which was hidden in the womb of י <note>Iod</note>, is illuminated and brought to life. Thus, *Shin*, having been clarified and animated by light, is transformed into ש; which is the <term>hieroglyphic</term> <note>A symbol representing a concept; here, the author views Hebrew letters as sacred symbols of cosmic truths.</note> of the heavens.

Therefore, just as the word "Bereshith" had its origin with ר <note>Resh</note>, representing poverty, foulness, and deficiency, so too was the first principle of all things empty, void, or dark. This was due to the absence and lack of light and grace; it was called <term>hyle</term> <note>From the Greek word for "matter"; in philosophy, it refers to the raw, formless "stuff" of the universe before it is organized by God.</note> and "something in potential," insofar as it lacked all apparent grace and light, and was consequently "nothing in act"—since every "act" or reality is derived from the living presence of divine light. 

But when Jehovah, the <term>Monad</term> <note>The "One" or the indivisible source of all being.</note> hiding within the darkness and reflecting the glow of His own light back into Himself (and who is therefore called the "Dark Aleph" relative to our own capacity to understand), wished to reveal Himself—that is, to shine out of the darkness—then He is called the "Manifest Aleph." Hence, in the writings of Moses, the very first word of the chapter was בראשית <note>In the beginning</note>; and following that was the name אלהים <note>Elohim / God</note>, where the letter א <note>Aleph</note> appears as if emerging from a dark cloud. 

Thus is verified that passage in Job 12:22: *He reveals the foundations out of the darkness and brings the shadow of death into the light.* That manifest and bright א <note>Aleph</note> is the first emanation from the "Dark Aleph"; that is, it is the mingling of the rays of the Light Aleph with the spirit of darkness. This Aleph is now called י <note>Iod</note>, which is the character and symbol for the number ten. In this, according to the logic of common arithmetic, unity (which is the Dark Aleph, or that which shines only in itself as a center or point) is joined with a zero; that is, it is mixed with the spirit of darkness, ר <note>Resh</note>. 

For this reason, the number ten is written by common people as "10," but in a mystical manner as יא: where the Aleph-Unity makes the Resh-Darkness into something actual out of what appeared to be nothing. That is, it renders the most beautiful form out of the deformed. Thus, the ו <note>Vav</note> following the ש <note>Shin</note> is a symbol of the first emanation from Aleph, hidden in the womb of matter <note>original: "hylæ"</note>, and therefore called "dark" by the Cabalists. For this reason, it is taken for the Messiah or the "Hidden Aleph," which the name יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God.</note> contains within itself by its own power. Finally, by the mixing of this with the spirit of darkness now revealed, ש <note>Shin</note> is produced, which is the sign or pattern of fire or created light—that is, the illuminated Spirit.

From this, we see in this word בראשית <note>Bereshith</note> three images of the properties of the Holy Trinity, as if in a mirror. The "Dark Aleph," signified by ר <note>Resh</note>, is compared to the Father or Unity; the "Light Aleph" to the Son, the Word, or Duality; and the ש <note>Shin</note> to the Holy Spirit proceeding from both. Since the mother of the worldly spirit was darkness or matter, and the father was the light that gave form to the waters (the Light Aleph), it is evident that *Shin* proceeds from ר <note>Resh</note> and א <note>Aleph</note>; therefore, it occupies the third and last place in the aforementioned word. 

From this, we can consider how the great mystery of the Trinity exists in every Hebrew word, insofar as almost all roots, according to the Hebrews, are composed of three characters. But where a root exceeds the number three, there the mystery of the <term>supersubstantial</term> and substantial world is also encompassed. For example, that ineffable voice יהוה <note>Jehovah</note> denotes through the י <note>Iod</note> the same thing as the Light Aleph looking down from a dark cloud, yet still dwelling in the highest heaven of heavens. But truly, the three following letters are the roots of the created world; for according to their pattern, the regions of the world were formed, as we shall clearly demonstrate in what follows. 

Thus, when ש <note>Shin</note> and ת <note>Tav</note> are mixed with א <note>Aleph</note>, they denote the "act" of the created world. For *Shin* and *Tav* are letters of the final order of the alphabet, and fall outside the number of the ten fingers <note>A reference to basic units of counting or the ten Sephirot</note>. Hence they denote composition, which does not exist in God or in the Archetype. Therefore, *Shin* and *Tav* are two of the "mothers" or secondary principles; insofar as *Shin* is taken here for the Dark Aleph, while *Tav* denotes the element of earth. 

But the first universal principle is the wondrous <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>; its characters are the primary specific principles, according to whose pattern the world was created. And these characters possess the true simplicity of the digits: insofar as י <note>Iod</note> is like the Dark Aleph, partly hidden in a cloud and partly shining forth; and ו <note>Vav</note> is the symbol for the number six, just as ה <note>He</note> is the figure for the number five, which are contained within the first order of the number ten. Therefore, the י <note>Iod</note> is the same as the Aleph, both dark and light; and ה <note>He</note> is the same as the spirit enclosed in darkness, and the same...

# Section I. Portion I. Prelude.

...indeed, because the letter ש <note>original Hebrew: "Shin"</note> is either an illuminated spirit or a spirit mingled with light. But we shall speak of these things more broadly and copiously below.

As for why we have called these characters first the primary elements of things, and then later the secondary ones, receive the reasoning briefly as follows: Hebrew letters are called elements as if they were <term>Hylementa</term> <note>A portmanteau created by the author combining the Greek word *hyle* (matter) and the Latin *elementa* (elements), suggesting that the letters are the basic components of matter itself.</note>, that is, formal characters delineated by the fiery Spirit of God, the eternal Creator, upon the material surface of *hyle* <note>The primordial, formless "stuff" or void from which the universe was created.</note>, or the shapeless and gloomy principle. Hence it is said by the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Practitioners of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism that seeks to understand the relationship between the eternal, mysterious Infinite and the mortal, finite universe.</note> that God wrote His law into a fiery globe by means of dark fire upon white fire. And these twenty-two letters, from which the said scripture is formed, are handed down as being the foundations of the world and of all creatures which exist and are named within it; and every word and every created thing is from them. From their impressions into matter, all things—just as if from a seal pressed into wax—obtain their images, names, and virtues.

In the first part of this first Portion, therefore, we shall establish a discourse concerning the three primary and uncreated metaphysical principles, or Archetypal and supersubstantial Elements, or the mystic characters appropriated to the unique ineffable name of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, יהוה (YHWH).</note>, namely יהוה <note>original Hebrew: YHWH</note>; that is, concerning light, spirit, and fire, or the fiery spirit. 

In the second part of the first Portion, we shall treat the three secondary, created, and physical principles, or the mundane and substantial Elements, or the secret characters produced according to the pattern of the characters of that ineffable name יהוה; namely, concerning darkness, waters, and created light. 

And in the third part of the first Portion, we shall make some brief and hurried remarks concerning the three Microcosmic principles derived immediately from the aforementioned, namely, the Body, the Spirit, and the Soul. This, therefore, will be our intention in this first portion of the first Section; this is the complete sense, or the target of our mind.

</margin>ALTHOUGH some perhaps—considering only the outward appearance of worldly things or creatures with their physical and purely bodily eyes, rather than contemplating their inner nature with spiritual and formal vision—will think it ridiculous to enclose the essences of things within the symbolic types of letters, they might object with a reasoning that seems probable enough to men: that letters are merely accidents brought into the world by human invention, so that one person might convey his meaning to another through written characters. Nevertheless, if they look at the matter a little more closely, they will perceive that in the case of the Hebrew letters, the matter stands quite differently. For these were not invented by man, but were formally brought forth from the mouth of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter divine name of God, YHWH.</note> at the beginning of the world, and were engraved as fiery characters into the womb of <term>hyle</term> <note>The primordial "stuff" or matter of the universe.</note>. Their forces and virtues were sent out from the dark matter through the voice and the word "LET THERE BE" <note>original: "FIAT"</note>, breathed out, exhaled, and trumpeted forth with a wondrous tone. Hence, it was the opinion of the <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Mystics of the Kabbalah.</note> that God wrote His law in a fiery globe by means of dark fire upon white fire <note>original: "ignem fuscum super ignem candidum"</note>. From this, <term>Ramban of Gerona</term> <note>original: "Rambam Gerundensis"; refers to Nachmanides, a 13th-century Sephardic scholar and Kabbalist.</note> says: "It appears to us through the Kabbalah that the writing was in dark fire upon the back of white fire." And from this comes that passage in Deuteronomy 33: "From His right hand went a fiery law for them," etc. Similarly, the Kabbalists argue that the art of transposing letters is necessary so that <term>In the Torah</term> <note>original Hebrew: בתורה, "Be-Torah"</note> may be transformed into <term>In Nature</term> <note>original Hebrew: בטבע, "Be-Teva"</note>. By this, the sense of the primary letters is changed from the confusion that had appeared in the fiery globe, so that it became possible, as it were, to lead them out of Chaos and read them here and there. For this reason, it happened that these letters (as <term>Blaise de Vigenère</term> <note>original: "Basilius Vigenerus"; a French diplomat and alchemist.</note> quite wisely recounts) are called "Elements" as if they were <term>Hylementa</term> <note>A wordplay combining "Hyle" (matter) and "Elementa" (elements).</note>, that is, formal impressions upon the obscure and dark paper of matter. For these letters, as <term>Abraham in the Sefer Yetzirah</term> <note>original: "Abraham Ietzirah"; referring to the "Book of Formation," an early Kabbalistic text traditionally attributed to the patriarch Abraham.</note> testifies in the first chapter on creation, carry the essences of things into the material cloud. Hence also Socrates argues in the *Cratylus* that the imitation of essence consists in letters and syllables.

And the <term>Zohar</term> <note>original: "Zoar"; the foundational work in the literature of Jewish mysticism.</note> says that when Adam imposed true and proper names upon all things, he composed every name of every thing through the holy letters, which denote the influences of the stars destined for the ministry and service of the things ordained. These letters in matter are like the parts of the body, while their vowel points and accents take the place of spirit and life. Yet this life or this spirit, depicted before the images of the living in dead letters on paper, lay hidden and concealed until the time of the wise <term>Ezra</term> <note>The biblical scribe credited with settling the canon of the Hebrew Bible and its script.</note>.

And another says that the law which God gave to Moses on the two tables was written in one continuous flow and manner without any separation of syllables or words; and that it penetrated from one side to the other, so that, according to the opinion of the Rabbis, one could read it in manifold ways and reasons according to the imagination of the reader: namely, from right to left, forwards and backwards, from top to bottom, and across. But truly, God reserved for Himself and His elect the hidden and secret significance of these characters concerning the divine mystery or the revelation of the divine majesty, according to which God revealed Himself; the secret of which consisted partly in the form of the characters, and partly in the true and proper distinction of the words. This, therefore, is the reason why the Mosaic law used to be read in so many different ways and changed into such diverse meanings. According to this, David said in Psalm 119, verse 29: "Remove from me the way of falsehood, and graciously grant me your law; the way of truth and of your precepts."

# INTRODUCTION.

...of them; *Teach me the way of your statutes*: <note>original: "Doce me viam statutorum"</note> And *Psalm 87:7*: *Teach me your way, O Jehovah, and I will walk in your truth.* And in *Job 11, verse 6*, it is declared that the law of God is manifold. Similarly, in the administration of the law, Moses said to the people in *Deuteronomy 30:15*: *I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing; therefore choose life, that you and your seed may live.* And Christ himself, according to *Matthew 5, verse 18*, said: *Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish, but to fulfill*; here he speaks of the spiritual law, which is not to be interpreted according to the letter, but according to the spirit. Hence it was said in *Nehemiah 8:7*, that Ezra explained the meaning of the law to the people, and gave them understanding through the scripture itself. For this same reason, Gregory of Nazianzus <note>A 4th-century Church Father known as "the Theologian."</note> says in his book *On the State of Bishops*: "To the many, he gives the law which is the letter; but to the few above the many, he gives that which is the spirit." And in his first book *On Theology*, he maintains that the tablets were inscribed solidly on both sides because of the manifest <note>the obvious or literal meaning</note> and the occult <note>the hidden or mystical meaning</note> aspects of the law; the former for the many who remain below, the latter for the few who reach upward.

From these things it is clear that Moses delivered the text of the law to the common people, but reserved the mystery, the parables, and the symbols for himself and the more excellent men. Hence St. Paul says in *2 Corinthians 3*: *The letter is dead, but the spirit gives life.* Therefore, when I speak of "letters" in the following pages, you should know and understand that I am not making mention of those dead characters depicted by human hands, but of the *formal letters and fiery spirit*, <note>In Kabbalah, letters are seen as living spiritual forces rather than just marks on a page.</note> or the "ink of light" described by the hand of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter divine name of God, YHWH.</note>; these were expressed at the very beginning of creation for the specific formation of every creature. 

From this, both Hebrew and Christian interpreters have observed that **Elohim** <note>A Hebrew name for God, often associated with the power of creation.</note> established works on each day of creation that correspond to numbers in a progressive order. In the first appearance of divine light, or the first day, through the purification of the simple waters and by the power of the presence of the aforementioned luminous spirit, *one* work was produced: namely, *light*. On the *second* day, two: namely the firmament (or the middle heaven) and the division of the waters. On the *third* day, three works: the gathering of the submerged waters into their designated place, the *positioning of the earth* (which was the first appearance and rest of the underlying darkness at the center of the universal machine), and also the germination of fruits from it. On the *fourth* day, *four* diverse works were created: namely the stars, the Sun, the Moon, and then their placement or position. On the *fifth* day, five works: namely the fish, the cattle, the birds, and also their blessing. On the *sixth* day, six: which are the land animals, man, woman, their blessing, the power given to them, and their food. Thus, through the addition of **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>—which denotes the unity of the Creator himself—the total produced appears to be 22. 

For this reason, each of these Hebrew letters is a symbol of a certain number: 
א is 1, ב is 2, ג is 3, ד is 4, ה is 5, ו is 6, ז is 7, ח is 8, ט is 9, י is 10, כ is 20, ל is 30, מ is 40, נ is 50, ס is 60, ע is 70, פ is 80, צ is 90, ק is 100, ר is 200, ש is 300, ת is 400. 
<note>The following are "final" forms of letters used at the ends of words, often assigned higher values in Gematria.</note>
ך is 500, ם is 600, ן is 700, ף is 800, ץ is 900, א̅ is 1000, ב̅ is 2000, ג̅ is 3000, and so on. In this way, each individual number has a peculiar power in the things produced by creation.

From these things, therefore, it seems clear that the 22 elements of the Hebrews are the foundation of the world and of all creatures within it, which are both found and named therein. Every word and every created thing comes from them, and from their permutations <note>The "revolutions" or combinations of letters.</note> they receive their name, their being, and their virtue. This is certainly no wonder, because each letter is the very form or formal figure of a different outgoing of the Speech, or the Word, or the Messiah, breathed from the mouth of the ineffable Tetragrammaton. He sits within his dark palace, gilded inside with uncreated occult light, amidst the dark **hyle** <note>A Greek term for "prime matter" or the raw material of the universe.</note>. By the various illuminations of his life-giving Spirit, various fiery letters are produced, and according to the variety of those spiritual letters or characters, various appearances, species, and natures are produced in the world. To these things, proper names and being are attributed according to the hidden condition of their character. 

Thus, according to the secret disposition of these elements, God taught Adam to apply a suitable name to every creature. And this is why these letters were not originally "Hebrew," but were in truth *holy and divine*; consequently, the speeches uttered through them are called "Holy." It was through the characters of these elements that Jehovah spoke with the Patriarchs, Prophets, and holy men. For since He Himself is holy, His language must undoubtedly be sacrosanct. However, after the Babylonian confusion <note>The Tower of Babel.</note> and the production of a multitude of languages on earth, this holy language remained incorrupt and without depravity with a certain man named Heber <note>Eber, the biblical ancestor from whom the term "Hebrew" is traditionally derived.</note>; and subsequently, the Hebrew language and Hebrew letters were named after him. Yet neither Heber nor anyone else invented them; rather, they flowed down immediately from God himself to Heber. Hence, even today, the wiser men call it the "Holy Language" rather than the "Hebrew Language," and its elements are likewise called "Holy," since the sacrosanct Jehovah used them in both speaking and writing, and delivered them to man as they are still held today. 

With these living, formal, and fiery letters the sacrosanct Elohim spoke in the beginning, and as soon as the word was made, all things were made. Abraham seems to hint at this same thing in the *Jetzirah* <note>The Sefer Yetzirah, or "Book of Formation," a foundational work of Jewish mysticism.</note> or "Creation," where he teaches that the world and everything contained in the world were born from the 22 letters. Namely, he made **א מ ש** <note>Aleph, Mem, Shin</note> the three mothers of all created things. By the dark **א** <note>Aleph</note>, he understood darkness and the earth itself; by **ש** <note>Shin</note>, fire or light; and by **מ** <note>Mem</note>, the spirit or the universal waters. Furthermore, from the seven double elements—namely **ב ג ד כ פ ר ת** <note>Bet, Gimel, Dalet, Kaph, Pe, Resh, Tav</note>—proceeded both the bodies and the souls of the 7 wandering stars, which they call Planets. These elements are called "double" because they are made from a double spirit: namely from the **Empyrean** <note>The highest heaven of pure fire.</note>, which is the soul of the Planets, and the **Ethereal**, which is their body. And again, the twelve signs of the Zodiac are subject to the twelve simple letters—namely **ה ו ז ח ט י ל נ ס ע צ ק** <note>He, Vav, Zayin, Chet, Tet, Yod, Lamed, Nun, Samekh, Ayin, Tsadi, Qoph</note>—and are constituted by their living and formal presence. From the influences of all these, all other lower things were produced.

From this it is evident, according to **Blaise de Vigenère** <note>original: "Blasei Vin." A 16th-century French diplomat and alchemist who wrote on secret ciphers and the Hebrew alphabet.</note>, that the 22 characters of the letters (or living hieroglyphics) are the "Ideas" of all creatures, both those already formed and those yet to be formed. For all things are known through their own proper and genuine naming, which cannot be represented to us except through speech or writing. Hence, sculpture and painting, along with other things of this sort, are like branches or streams flowing from the aforementioned fountains. We conclude, therefore, that it is not only likely but most certain, that each particular shape of the said holy elements signifies some special work of creation. And...

### SECTION I. PART I.

This is declared all the more evidently, because God concluded each of His actions in creation with the demonstration or particle *Eth* <note>original: "אֶת" — a Hebrew grammatical marker often left untranslated, but here interpreted mystically as the "Alpha and Omega" or the totality of the alphabet.</note>, which is taken to mean a sign, figure, character, letter, or form; it happened so that all things in creation would be encompassed by that limitation or boundary: *In the beginning God created [Eth] the heavens...* <note>original: "בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם" — Genesis 1:1</note> that is, God created the figure, sign, character, or letter of the heavens, etc. This letter is *Shin* [שׁ]; insofar as it is the symbol of created fire, which consists of the spirit—which is the fuel or nourishment of the burning light—and the light itself, which is the action within the spirit or the "patient" <note>the receptive element</note> water; and both together are called fire. Hence the highest heaven is called the *Empyrean* <term>Empyrean: the highest part of heaven, traditionally thought to be composed of pure fire or light</term>, that is, fiery; and the middle is called *Ethereal*, as if it were fiery air.

And from this, you may know most certainly and clearly in the Kabbalistic art <note>the tradition of Jewish mysticism</note> that the twenty-two formal or fiery letters of the characters were the pigments and foundations in the blackest veil of *hyle* <term>hyle: a Greek term for primordial, unformed matter</term> for both the world and the law. This indeed seems to be confirmed by the following assertion of Moses; for God said to Moses: *Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you;* indeed, they shall believe in it <note>original: "בּוֹ" (Bo)</note>, that is, in the 22, forever. For the letter *Beth* [ב] signifies 2, and *Vau* [ו] signifies two <note>The author is using a form of Gematria, or numerical symbolism, where the word "Bo" (in it) equals 22, though standard values differ; he likely links them to the 22 letters of the alphabet.</note>. It is necessary, therefore, for a true Kabbalist to believe, and to receive with unique love and a pleasant, joyful mind, with joy and confidence. Hence the Royal Psalmist also says in Psalm 70: *Let them exult and rejoice in you* <note>original: "בָּךְ" (Bak)</note>, that is, in the twenty-two, those who seek: for the twenty-two letters, as has been told, exist as the foundations of the world and the law; insofar as through their mediation Jehovah spoke, and by the Word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and all their powers by the spirit from His mouth.

But truly, just as three properties of the one most high, supersubstantial, and uncreated Being are established over all created things—which rule over all things like kings and are known to moderate everything in this world—so among these 22 letters or elements, only three are found to be princes and fathers of the one ineffable Name <note>the Tetragrammaton, JHVH</note>, constituting the "super-essential" essence. These preside over all the others like Emperors, and are perceived to beget and produce all those inferior letters through a stupendous birth. Moreover, among the other characters, these three—and no others besides them—are found to be spherical and circular on account of their excellence. This argues that, just as a spherical figure described in the art of Geometry is known to be more worthy and excellent than all other figures (insofar as by its capacity it encompasses and contains all other geometric figures within itself), so also these spherical characters embrace all the other 19 characters—indeed, even the entire nature or spirit of the world—as if with the arms of their infinity. They send their power into the spirit, and through the spirit or the waters encompassed by their embrace, down to the very center of the periphery.

Therefore, the Founder of things used these merely spiritual and formal characters for the production and revelation of His ineffable name; for without them, His supersubstantial essence could not be explained by a living voice or indicated to men. Hence, when Moses asked of God, "What is your name?" the Almighty replied to him, *Ehyeh* <note>original: "אהיה" — "I AM"</note>, that is: *J.H.V.H.*, that is, *my name forever, and this is my memorial from generation to generation.*

From these things it is clear that this unique, sole, ineffable, and eternal name of God could not have been explained without the utterance of these three perfect or spherical letters. Hence, these three letters can not ineptly be called the "fathers of the uncreated world"; or rather, they are three symbols of the one Father and Founder, namely of the one spirit and uncreated essence. Just as three "mothers" are said by Abraham in the *Jetzirah* <term>Jetzirah: The *Sefer Yetzirah* or Book of Formation, an ancient text on how the world was created through letters and numbers</term> to be *Aleph* [א], *Mem* [מ], and *Shin* [שׁ]; so that *Aleph* in creation corresponds with *Iod* [י], which was its image before creation, and denotes the simple light in creation, as well as its opposite, namely the darkness in which *Aleph* existed before their creation. Hence *Aleph* is sometimes called "the dark one"; which proves that God, before creation, shone back into Himself according to that word of the Psalmist: *And He made darkness His secret place.* But God, wishing to shine upon the world out of the darkness, is called the "obscure Aleph turned into the lucid." Hence it is written: *As its darkness is, so is its light.*

Abraham wished in the *Jetzirah* for *Aleph* [א] to signify the element of earth, and elsewhere the "land of the living," arguing for permanence and fixity; and thus it encompasses the darkness, which is the pavilion of Jehovah. It also denotes the eternal Father, who is the source of uncreated light; and thus it is compared with *Iod* [י], or the power of the Tetragrammaton, or the soul of the Messiah.

Likewise *Mem* [מ], which is the symbol of the created waters, is referred to the *He* [ה] of the ineffable or Archetypal Name, which is attributed to the uncreated spirit. And just as the mass of waters in *Mem* is divided into the thick and the subtle through the interposition of the firmament or the nature of *Shin* [שׁ]; so also the universal upper *He* [ה] is distinguished from the lower *He* by the power of *Vau* [ו].

Therefore, the mothers of the world are called *Aleph, Mem, Shin* [א מ שׁ]; because just as a woman, who is less perfect than a man, receives and suffers the actions of the man (that is, she receives his impressions like the wax of a seal), so those letters received the impressions of things to be created from the uncreated fathers—that is, from the properties of the spherical and super-essential elements of the ineffable name, the Tetragrammaton: namely *Iod*, *He*, and *Vau*. For *Iod* in *Aleph* acts toward the creation of light, and the uncreated spirit *He* acts toward the adaptation of the waters in *Mem*, and *Vau* in *Shin*.

For just as *Vau*, which is the symbol of the number six, secretly contains and is completed by *He* (five) and *Aleph* (unity)—which denotes light, and consequently proves light in the middle spirit, or the soul of the world, or the Messiah in the tabernacle of the Sun—so also *Shin*, denoting an illuminated *Mem* or an ignited spirit, designates the sphere of equality. This is the proportion of light by weight with the intermediate watery spirit. Hence *Aleph* is a single purity and simplicity, namely the emanation of light in creation as the agent; *Mem* is its receptacle, or a second simple nature springing forth from the darkness; from the mixture of these, *Shin* is made. Its character denotes three in unity, namely the Trinity in a moist nature.

And in this way the world was made by the "mothers," produced from the womb of *hyle* into the world at creation, according to the pattern of the Archetypal world, which was produced from the "fathers" (or the elementary principles of the ineffable name *Iod, He, Vau*) through a progression from unity to *Iod*. From this, therefore, it happens that we establish various kinds of principles or Elements regarding created things, agreeing in the number three. Some of these are primary, uncreated, and supersubstantial—namely those three of the Archetypal world which are encompassed in the ineffable name: namely *Iod* or the Father, and *Vau* or the Son, and the double *He*, or the Spirit joining the father *Iod* with the son *Vau*, and again the son...

The power of Jehovah [יהוה] acts upon the "mothers" <note>In Kabbalah, the "Mother Letters" (Aleph, Mem, Shin) are the primary building blocks of creation.</note> of the world; and these mothers further pour out the actions of the power of that Tetragrammaton <term>Tetragrammaton: the "four-letter" name of God (YHWH), considered the most sacred and powerful name in Western mysticism</term> into all creatures, but more splendidly and abundantly into man, the microcosm and most noble creature. However, as it seems to me, there is another certain Microcosm even more divine than man and closer to God Himself; which is (as I believe) that "homunculus" <term>homunculus: a "little man" or artificial life-form described in the works of the alchemist Paracelsus</term> of Paracelsus, of whom he sang so many wonders in his works. ## CHAPTER II.

### How the created world—both the great and the small—is arranged according to the Idea of the Ineffable Name of the Archetype?

<margin>"</margin> First, it must be known that the world was made according to the exemplar of the living God—that is, in imitation of the characters of His ineffable name—as if His fiery and living characters were seen in a worldly mirror. <margin>"</margin> Hence Hermes Trismegistus called the world the image and exemplar of God; and Moses said that man was formed <margin>"</margin> according to the exemplar of Jehovah. Hermes called man the "image of the world" insofar as he contains the parts of the world within himself. This is also what the wise Ecclesiastes affirms in chapter 3:11: *God has placed the world (or the age) in the heart of man, so that man might not find out the work that God does from the beginning to the end.* From this it is certain that the tangible world <margin>"</margin> was described in the Archetype <term>Archetype: the original divine blueprint or "ideal" version of a thing that exists in the mind of God</term> before its creation through an ideal and supersubstantial sketch; as was man in both—that is, <margin>"</margin> before and after creation. Thus we read in Exodus 25:40: *See that you make them according to the structures of those things shown to you on this mountain*; and in 26:30: *So shall you raise up that tabernacle, according to its fittingness, which was shown to you to be seen on this mountain*; and in 25:9: *Let them make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them entirely, according to the structure of the tabernacle itself and the structure of all its furnishings which I will show you; so shall you do.* Similarly, we read that Noah's ark was previously described by God; and the Royal Prophet [David] boasted that he had received the description of the temple from the hands of God. The Cabalists <note>Practitioners of Kabbalah, a Jewish mystical tradition that explores the relationship between the infinite God and the finite universe.</note> relate that all these things were formed in the image of both the Archetypal and the tangible world, both greater and smaller. Therefore, I have proposed here to explain the correspondence of the Archetypal world, or the characters of the ineffable name, with the greater and smaller created worlds alike. In this way it may appear more clearly how the created world, both visible and invisible, is like the very wax receiving the characters of the ineffable seal, YHWH [יהוה]. From this it will be evidently proved that, just as a seal crafted with art leaves in wax a certain sign similar to itself (which is called the image of the seal), so too the seal of the Creator left its icon in the passive spirit of the world. Indeed, the world possesses from its origin the real essence, footprints, and presence of the very Tetragrammaton-Word, through which a thing so noble and beautiful lives and exists. And since in that great and ineffable seal four characters are found, but only three differing in kind from one another <note>The name יהוה (YHWH) consists of four letters, but the letter ה (He) appears twice, leaving three unique letters: Iod, He, and Vau.</note>, we shall in this place reveal the nature, arrangement, and significance of each of them, so that we may more easily arrive at the teaching and understanding of what follows. But first, we will adapt the shining and fire-white ineffable name to the parts of the created world, so that we may perceive from there more readily—as if in a mirror—how the members of the created world arise from the properties of the primary elements' figures and icons: *Iod*, *He*, and *Vau*. # INTRODUCTION.

10. Thus it is that **Yod** <note>The Hebrew letter י (Iod or Yod)</note> is seen among the Kabbalists to be that letter from which all others proceed, and into which they all return; indeed, it stands in relation to the other letters as a point does to a line, which begins from a point and ends in a point. And since nothing is simpler than a point, **Yod** is said to symbolize the simplicity of the divine essence among the letters of the Tetragrammaton <note>The sacred four-letter name of God: יהוה (IHVH)</note>, all of which are most perfect and circular. And from this, it is said that **Yod** occultly contains the whole Tetragrammaton within itself, and signifies the same thing as יהוה <note>Jehovah/Yahweh</note>. And because it is that center from which the first emanation flowed out into the intellectual world or the region of **He** <note>The Hebrew letter ה</note>, it therefore represents the Father of all things, from whom all things appear to be procreated in a twofold passive spirit: the manifest **He** above, and the **He** below; and a middle spirit hidden in **Vau** <note>The Hebrew letter ו</note> by the power of the word hidden in the spirit of **Vau**, which overcomes the hidden spirit of the firmament through unity—that is, the simplicity of emanation, denoting the only Son from the Father. Thus, we cannot see the spirit of the Sun because of its light—that is, because of the external clarity of the divine radiance—because unity or divinity predominates in the **He** that is hidden beneath the rays. From this **Yod**, therefore, the Father of all things, proceeds the life and multiplication of all through generation, as from a fountain, and without it, the seed cannot be multiplied.

It was not, therefore, without a great mystery that God commanded **Yod** to be taken from the name of *Sarai* and divided into a double **He**: for among the Hebrews, **He** denotes five; and a double five making 10 is, according to the reckoning of Kabbalistic numbers, the same as **Yod** <note>In Hebrew numerology (Gematria), Yod = 10 and He = 5. By splitting the Yod (10) into two He's (5+5), God changed Abram to Abraham and Sarai to Sarah, enabling them to conceive.</note>. One of these God commanded to be added to the name of *Abram*, and the other to the name of *Sarai*: whence *Abram* is changed into *Abraham*, and *Sarai* into *Sarah*, signifying that if the paternal blessing of **Yod** given to the woman's name *Sarai* and denied to *Abram* were equally distributed to both, it would follow that both would be rendered fertile and fruitful; which could not happen without this partition. For it very often happens that the same woman, through the heat of her own nature, might exhaust the husband's seed, and vice-versa.

Finally, let us see that **Yod** is above all things, sitting and triumphing over the highest peaks of the world, and yet its emanation or "the Word" fills the universal spirit of the world. Therefore, the world was formed according to the model of this name, the Tetragrammaton, and the heavens or their regions were ordered and given essence according to the distinction of the letters of His voice. And although in what follows we shall mention **Vau** ו and **He** ה ה, treating them as the created heavens or regions of the world, we nevertheless wish it to be understood that we are proposing the image in place of the thing itself, or the reflection in a mirror in place of the true subject. For the created universal spirit is nothing but a mirror in which the idea and reflection of the essence-giving and ineffable Tetragrammaton is seen. From this it follows that **Yod** denotes the uncreated age, or the beauty of the super-substantial world, according to whose image the substantial world was made.

The threefold region proceeding from it—namely, **He**, **Vau**, and **He**—denotes the uncreated ideas or icons of the heavens or regions of the world to be established, so that from the presence of the spherical, formal, and central letter **Yod**, the material world acquired a similar round figure. Indeed, through the emanation of the uncreated **Yod** into the spirit of the Son, **Vau**, the Empyrean heaven was made, which was created from spirit and light just as *Iah* <note>original: "יה" - a shortened name of God</note> came from the fiery and lucid super-substantial essence of **Yod** itself in the higher **He**. Similarly, *Iah* placing his tabernacle in the womb of **Vau** ו, in which the middle **He** is hidden (for unity predominating over five produces **Vau** ו), denotes in the created world the invisible spirit of the mass of the sun in the middle heaven, in which unity alone, or the specific light, is discerned, while the spirit of **He** is obscured. And this heaven is compared to *Iah* יה, insofar as its soul is *Iah*; but its whole is **Vau** ו, and that **Vau** is called the "Seal of God," by which *Ehieh* <note>original: "אהיה" - meaning "I AM," the name God gave Moses at the burning bush.</note> is accustomed to mark all things with life. Finally, the whole יהוה <note>Jehovah</note> descends into the final **He** or the lowest created heaven, and becomes יהוה existing in the whole, in every part, and outside and beyond the whole. And since these characters are all spherical, every heaven, being crafted according to the model of one of them, was created in a round and spherical form. This, then, is the way in which the lower world was established according to the figure and image of the Archetypal world, and the essence of the Archetypal creator, יהוה Jehovah.

And although יהוה appears to be three spirits, these three are nevertheless but a single universal spirit after the image of that uncreated spirit, according to whose icon and model it was made. Indeed, according to Rabbi Azariel in his *Commentary on Holiness*, the Word and the voice are produced from the spirit, not by the opening of lips, nor by the speech of the tongue, nor by the breath of man; and these three are one spirit, because God is one. Hence Abraham says in the *Yetzirah* <note>The Sefer Yetzirah or "Book of Formation," an early Kabbalistic text.</note> concerning creation: "One spirit is the living God; blessed be He and blessed be His name, who lives forever." Voice, and spirit, and Word—this is the Holy Spirit, two spirits from the spirit. And the Rabbis wrote in the *Book of Speculation*: "These three, which are one, have a proportion among themselves as the One, the Uniting, and the United—that is, the beginning, the middle, and the end." This is also our meaning: that **Yod** is the One, **Vau** is the Uniting, and the two extreme spirits are the United. Hence **Vau** ו is most often used as a conjunction <note>The letter Vau in Hebrew serves as the word "and."</note> among the Hebrews. So also in the world we see that through the ethereal spirit, the intellectual soul is introduced into the lower world. Thus we read that nature is the intermediate bond, by whose connection two opposites are joined: namely, divine light is drawn into a dark prison, and is retained in it for the use of the body—namely, for reason, life, and motion. Thus we call Jesus Christ the mediator and the bond through whom we are gathered together and have communion with the Father. And in this way, we have the presence of the Tetragrammaton expanded through the universal spirit of the world. Whence Jehovah is said to be in the heavens and on the earth; and it is said that the heavens are the place of His throne, and the earth the footstool of His feet; as if it were said that **Yod** is outside the highest heaven as the head, and **He** the place of the shoulders, and **Vau** the place of the visible sun <unclear>and the feet</unclear> in the lowest **He**. But of these things, more clearly below.

**ה He**, the Hebrew letter, is among the Kabbalists a symbol of the spirit of <unclear>breathing</unclear>; it denotes this world or the present age, just as **Yod** denotes the world to come. From this, it is clear that it is the hieroglyphic of the world-spirit, or of the waters, whose upper mass the firmament divided from the lower, the hieroglyphic of which is **ו Vau**. This letter is round, and when joined with **Yod**, it represents the light created on the first day; or with **Vau**, it represents the waters created on the third day and those closest to the darkness reflected at the center. Whence, by the waters from which all things were made, Moses understood the image of the <unclear>holy</unclear> name of the Tetragrammaton, by which all things were made.

**ו Vau** is the symbol of the spiritual bond; hence it denotes a hook or something twisted back, as if a hook retaining and joining things that exist in an opposite manner: namely, light with darkness, hot with cold, and uniting the quarreling elements in harmonious peace. And the unity over the **He** (five) in the **Vau** ו represents the way in which all discordant things are united. It is therefore the hieroglyphic of the Messiah, by whose union universal harmony and concord are completed. And in this way, we have that—

Rather, **Iod** or *Elhai* is the shining fountain of living waters, and the Soul of the Messiah is the sparkling river of life. But more on these things below at greater length.

### How is the world numbered by the ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton?

The numerical proportion of the world—by which it is ordered and first distributed into different regions, and then subdivided into spheres differing in nature—consists in a <unclear>gene</unclear>ral respect to the ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton יהוה <note>The sacred four-letter name of God: Yahweh or Jehovah</note>. For in the first place, we <unclear>stima</unclear>te the cube of the number three; according to which the world's root, its square, and its cube, and consequently its perfection, are produced. Let us therefore consider the ineffable name in its parts or letters, and we find that **Iod** (י) denotes 10, the first **He** (ה) 5, **Vau** (ו) 6, and the later or final **He** (ה) 5. When these numbers are added together, they produce Twenty-six; if **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, א, representing unity or the number 1</note>, which is unity, is added to this product, it produces Twenty-seven. This is that cube of the number three <note>3 x 3 x 3 = 27</note>, whose praises Plato so greatly sang in his *Timaeus* concerning the production of the world. Or, working another way, we find in this ineffable name three letters that differ from one another, namely **I-H-V** (יהו). By multiplying this triple number <note>The "three-ness" of the distinct letters</note> by itself, and then multiplying the result again by the root, it brings forth 27. But if we wish to proceed further into the details, the product of the triple number **I-H-V** (יהו) multiplied by itself will be 9. <header>SECTION I. PORTION I.</header>

### *We say that God, as Ehieh <note>original: "Ehieh," a Hebrew name for God meaning "I Am" or "Existence"</note> or Iod <note>The first letter of the divine name, י (Y), often associated with the point of creation</note>, is the just and benevolent judge of worldly affairs, holding in his right hand the vertical needle or balance-beam of nature's scales, weighing all things by the weights of justice—that is, according to the merit of their matter. Therefore, he placed the light things in one pan and pressed the heavy things into the pan opposite it; the moderator, or the vertical needle of the scale of justice, is the intermediate spirit.*

We see, therefore, that the pan of purity, simplicity, and lightness is that **He** <note>The second letter of the name, ה (H)</note> which exists closer to **Iod**; the other pan, however, is the final and lowest **He** <note>The fourth letter of the name, ה (H), associated with the physical world</note> opposite it, in which the gross and heavy things—both the opaque and the transparent, namely water, earth, and the other elements—are included. The moderator or tongue of these pans, the needle of judgment and justice, is **Vau** <note>The third letter, ו (W/V), which looks like a vertical line and acts as a grammatical "link" or "and"</note>; this is the moderator, the mediator, and the true governor of both weights. Because in this element of the *Tetragrammaton* <note>The four-letter name of God: יהוה</note> unity is found above the value of **He**, through that unity (I say) the balance-beam **Vau** is sustained by God as **Iod**, as if by a rope or cord; **Iod** is the judge, while **Vau** is the mediator bringing forth truth and sincerity, like a testimony of truth before the judge.

In clearly the same way, the *Messiah* produces testimony of those things which are in the heavens and those on the earth; he is the only truth, wisdom, and justice, through which any thing is either exalted in honor according to its dignity, or cast down into the depths in disgrace according to its merit. Thus, because of the purity and simplicity of the matter or spirit of the Empyrean heaven <note>The highest, most spiritual realm of fire and light</note>, he causes its substance to be raised upward toward the lucid fountain in the most excellent pan of honor; but conversely, he allows the elementary heaven to be pressed downward toward the lower regions because of its impurity, coarseness, weight, and dark density. In the middle is **Vau**, sustained by the right hand of **Iod** or *Jehovah* himself; by the power and abundance of his spirit, the first **He** is exalted, and on the contrary, by the lack of that same spirit, the final **He** is suppressed. For thus we see that *Jehovah* in his wisdom has disposed all things by composing them according to his justice; and yet that divine wisdom has the root of its essence in the Father, since the Son is said to go forth from the center of the Father. For thus the *Messiah*—or the Natural God, or rather God in nature, or the power of the *Tetragrammaton* descending into moist nature and giving it existence—is joined to **Iod**, the fountain of light and the root of the divine tree in nature, in such a way that he can no more be separated or divided from **Iod** than a solar ray can be from the Sun.

We see, therefore, in the composition of the world, that just as **Vau** is the nexus or bond, and a sort of copulative conjunction <note>In grammar, a word that joins two parts of a sentence</note> connecting the upper **He** with the lower **He**, so also is the firmament <note>The sky or the dividing line between the heavens and the earth</note> that which both distinguishes and joins the Empyrean Spirit with the elementary spirit; that is, it separates the waters above from the waters below; and yet it is the nexus and bond through which, and by the mediation of which, the worldly mind is introduced by degrees into the lowest region of the world.

But to produce testimonies supporting this opinion of ours from the most holy scriptures, we read in *Proverbs* 3:19 that *Jehovah* God established the heavens by his wisdom. Here, therefore, the needle of the scale of nature is clearly declared to be **Vau**, or the wisdom of *Jehovah* remaining fixed in his solar tabernacle. Next, we find in *Job* 38:37: *He who made a weight for the winds, and set the waters in measure.* Here the two pans of the scale are expressed along with the matter contained in them. For by "winds" he seems to understand the thinner spirits, which are weighed in the upper pan (since, as declared above, **He** is the symbol of spirit, breath, and wind); and by "waters" he intended to indicate the gross spirits contained in the lowest **He**, or the more depressed pan.

Moreover, that holy man *Job* seems to denote this inequality of natural weights in the same place with these words: *Who numbered the heavens in power? And who made those things falling from the heavens to rest? When the dust hardened into that hardness, and the clods cleaved together.* Similarly, that same wise man in chapter 26:7 says that God *suspended the earth over nothing, and bound the waters in the thick clouds.* Here, then, he places **Vau** (God in nature) as the needle of the scale indicating the truth, the earth as the lower pan, and the clouds as the upper pan, according to *Job* 35:5: *Look at the heaven, and behold the higher clouds, that they are high above you;* all of which he seems to assert are suspended and bound in their own proper places. But let us hear, I pray, what the Divine *Mercury Trismegistus* <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure Hermes Trismegistus, supposed author of the Hermetic Corpus</note> says in this case in the *Pimander*, chapter 3: *A holy splendor flourished,* (he says) *which led the elements down beneath the sand and moist nature; and all the Gods loved the feminine nature; and when they had been indistinct, the light things soon flew up into the high region; the heavy things settled beneath the moist sand. When things had been distinguished and set in motion, which were carried by a fiery spirit, the heaven shone forth <note>original: "emicuit"</note> into seven circles.* What else does that wise man mean here, other than that the light spirit is carried upward, but the heavy downward, and that all things are raised by the fiery spirit—that is, by the balance **Vau**—or, due to its absence, are precipitated downward toward the center of the periphery.

Therefore, the axis of this worldly or natural scale is the axis of the world; the highest part of which is the Arctic or northern pole, or the North Wind, which is sublimated high toward the summit of the heavens. Its opposite end is like the Antarctic or Southern pole, which is pressed down toward the depths of the earth. The midday of this axis is *Phoebus* <note>The Sun</note> himself in his exaltation, which is attributed to the palace of **Vau** or the *Messiah*. Nor indeed do these things differ from the speech of that man as wise as he was patient, *Job* 26:7: *God stretched out the North on high over the empty and the void—that is, he made the heaven revolve over the Northern pole—and suspended the whole earth at the bottom over nothing.*

From these things it is evidently clear that the *Tetragrammaton*, dividing the universal spirit into two parts by the firmament, has disposed each of them in the world by various weights. Hence, therefore, it says in *Job* 28:25:

### *We say that God, as **I Am** <note>original: "Ehieh," a Hebrew name for God meaning "I Am" or "Existence"</note> or **Yod** <note>original: "Iod." The first letter of the divine name, י (Y), often associated with the point of creation</note>, is the just and benevolent judge of worldly affairs, holding in his right hand the vertical needle or balance-beam of nature's scales, weighing all things by the weights of justice—that is, according to the merit of their matter. Therefore, he placed the light things in one pan and pressed the heavy things into the pan opposite it; the moderator, or the vertical needle of the scale of justice, is the intermediate spirit.*

We see, therefore, that the pan of purity, simplicity, and lightness is that **He** <note>The second letter of the name, ה (H)</note> which exists closer to **Yod**; the other pan, however, is the final and lowest **He** <note>The fourth letter of the name, ה (H), associated with the physical world</note> opposite it, in which the gross and heavy things—both the opaque and the transparent, namely water, earth, and the other elements—are included. The moderator or tongue of these pans, the needle of judgment and justice, is **Vav** <note>The third letter, ו (W/V), which looks like a vertical line and acts as a grammatical "link" or "and"</note>; this is the moderator, the mediator, and the true governor of both weights. Because in this element of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God: יהוה</note> unity is found above the value of **He**, through that unity (I say) ...

### SECTION I.
### PORTION I.
### PART I.

## Book I.

# Concerning SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.
<note>original: "De Principiis Supersubstantialibus." Supersubstantial refers to that which exists above or beyond material substance; in mystical theology, it describes the essence of God which transcends all categories of being.</note>

### CHAPTER I.

*Concerning the production of the three uncreated principles, first in the superessential world, and then afterwards in the created world; and how the dark Aleph is converted into the luminous Aleph.*

---

<image-desc>A large decorative drop cap 'T' set within a square frame featuring intricate floral and foliate designs.</image-desc>

The first three numerations <note>original: "numerationes," referring to the Sephirot, the ten creative powers or "numberings" in Kabbalah</note> out of those ten divine ones enumerated by the Kabbalists—namely כתר *Kether* or the Crown, which is referred to the divine essence אהיה *Ehieh* <note>original: "I am," the name God gave to Moses in Exodus 3:14</note> and particularly represents the Father; and חכמה *Chokhmah*, that is, Wisdom, which refers to the most holy name יהוה [YHWH]; and בינה *Binah*, that is, Prudence or Intelligence, to which the name of God אלהים [Elohim] is attributed—are said by the Kabbalists to be the three highest and supreme numerations. These are, as it were, a single seat upon which sits the Holy One, the Holy of Holies, the Lord God of Sabaoth. The infinity and most absolute essence of these three highest Kabbalistic numerations (which Christians call the three persons in the divinity), while it is withdrawn into the abyss of darkness and remains idle without any external action—that is, looking toward nothing (according to that saying of Hermes Trismegistus in the *Asclepius*: "The Monad <note>The number one; the ultimate unity from which all things arise</note> generated the Monad before the construction of the world, and reflected its ardor into itself"; and according to Psalm 18:11: *He made darkness his secret place* etc., because, as Hermes Trismegistus says in the *Poimandres*, "He did not wish to change his form," but Genesis 1:2: *Darkness was upon the face of the deep*, or according to that same Hermes: "All things were not converted into a pleasant light, nor did the horrific shadow slip away from the face of the mind into a moist nature," or, to use the words of the Royal Prophet, Psalm 18:12: *Before the brightness in his presence the dark clouds did not pass away*), for this reason that essence is called by the Hebrews <margin>Nothing</margin> אין *Ein*, that is, "nothing," or "non-being," as well as "without end," which is אן-סוף *Ein-Sof*. We call it this because we suffer from such poverty of intellect in divine matters that we judge those things which do not appear no differently than those which do not exist, saying that those things which are not revealed to our understanding are "not." 

And hence it is that the dark א Aleph <note>Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Here, the "dark Aleph" symbolizes God in his hidden, unmanifested state.</note> (indeed according to that word of the Prophet in Psalm 18:11: *God making darkness his secret place, and surrounded by the darkest waters, which served him as a veil*) is so called; which nevertheless is converted into a luminous Aleph according to his good pleasure. Whence it is found written: *As is its darkness, so also is its light* [Psalm 139:12]. And indeed this conversion of the dark Aleph into the luminous one is declared by that passage of Hermes Trismegistus in *Poimandres* I: "And suddenly he changed his form; and behold, all things were converted into a pleasant light" etc. Similarly Psalm 18:12: *At the brightness of his presence, the clouds passed away, and the springs of waters appeared, and the foundations of the world were revealed* etc. And when Aleph wished to go forth and manifest itself from the immense darkness, then the Kabbalists called it the "Great Aleph," insofar as it appears through its presence as the cause of all things through the ב Beth <note>The second letter of the Hebrew alphabet, signifying the start of the material creation.</note> immediately following it.

<margin>ב <note>The letter Beth</note></margin>

which is the first production in the Deity and the principle of alteration: Whence it is nicknamed **ראשית**, that is, the beginning <note>original: "Reshith," the first word of Genesis</note>, even though it be the second emanation of infinity, that is, the second Kabbalistic numeration <note>The Sephirah Chokhmah or Wisdom</note>, through which all things were made: Whence it is left written: *All things in wisdom*: And in this way the first efflux is the second numeration; because the limit of generation is the son: There remains, however, a medium in the word **אן** between Aleph and Nun, which is **י** <term>Jod</term>; since it is the mark of the holy name **יה** <term>Jah</term>: both of whose characters, if they are inserted into the name **בן** [Son] by turns, will be **בינה**, that is, **Binah**—intelligence, prudence, or providence; to which is attributed Adonai the Spirit, etc.

From these things, therefore, we see the opinions of the Kabbalists regarding the orders of emanation of the second and third properties from the same **Alpha**, or the same essence of the Deity—namely from the crown, or the father, or the root. **Beth**, Wisdom, the Son, is the first emanation of supersubstantial light; from both of which intelligence, prudence, or the Spirit proceeds by a secondary emanation; as if one were to say: From the father the son or Word, and from both the Holy Spirit; or according to worldly consideration: God, the Mind, and the Intellectual Spirit; or God as Light, and the Universal Spirit, which among created things is compared to the Holy Spirit. And in this way is verified that assertion of David in Psalm 33:6: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and all their power by the spirit of his mouth:* since here **Jehovah**, his **Word**, and his **Spirit** are enumerated, and are said to differ in the worldly workmanship and distinct properties in the structure of the spherical machine: For by his word God disposed that work into a most beautiful figure, and by his spirit he applied power, motion, and action to the spirit from which that fabric was composed.

Therefore, the **Alpha** was dark as far as human understanding is concerned, before it shone upon the world, and it was called the **Lesser Alpha**; insofar as it was unity alone; or rather the source and origin of the unity of all unities; than which nothing smaller, more subtle, or more meager can be imagined: from which, in the idea of the Archetype <note>The original blueprint or divine pattern of the universe</note>, flowed **Beth**, or duality; that is, Monad from Monad; since one and one make two; and then through another unity there is a reflection into itself; so that in unity the Trinity is found; and in the Trinity, Unity: and thus the **Most Holy Triangle** <note>original: "Trigonus Sacrosanctus"</note> is produced in the supersubstantial idea, before the darkness is illuminated, and while Aleph is said to be dark in the image of those things which must be brought forth according to the type of this divinity in the building of the world; namely, after the example of an Architect, who, being about to build a house, is accustomed first to delineate its figure and parts intentionally in his mind, before he proceeds to actually lead his work into action. Furthermore,
