the Archetype Aleph, by its third emanation, or the repetition of its unity or entity, reflected its rays into itself, not otherwise than when two lines are given making an angle, it is necessary that a third be added for the reduction of these lines into a single superficial nature, whence a triangle is made; which if it happens, there will be a progression from unity into infinity, and suddenly the darkness will be illuminated as if in the blink of an eye.

But this primary distinction of the divine unity into properties—that is, the going out first from a point as if to a line, and then from a line to a surface—denotes that the divine intention is to produce a superficial thing first; and because that number three (the ternary) multiplied by itself constitutes nine, therefore by this kind of

The Speaker, the Father, commanded it to be made; and the Word, the Son, did as commanded; but the Spirit of the Speaker and the Word perfected all things by power.

Thus, according to a ninefold disposition in the form of the first emanation of the Archetype, which was linear, the first heaven was divided into nine orders of Angels; likewise the second, which is superficial, the middle heaven into nine spheres; and the lowest, which is Cubic, is similarly distributed into nine regions. Thus the luminous and manifest Aleph is called **Great**, since it extends itself from the circumference all the way to the center; which consists in a thousandfold proportion; For the first heaven is composed of numbers of tens, the second of hundreds, and the lowest of thousands, as we have declared in our treatise *On Divine Numbers* <note>original: "De numeris divinis," likely Fludd's own work</note>; beyond which number there is no progression: And hence it is that the **Great Aleph** in Hebrew numeration denotes one thousand: For, just as the width of the **Lesser Aleph** is 9—namely 3 multiplied by itself; to which if the small Aleph be added, the Luminous Aleph is produced—so, if according to the intention of Plato, 9 be disposed according to the order of the unities of their root, in this way 9 9 9, and Aleph be added to them, the **Great Aleph** will be produced, namely one thousand; which is the limit of created things, or the end of the appearance of the Luminous and revealed Aleph from its supersubstantial throne to the center of the created machine.

SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK I.

## CHAPTER II.

### *How the small or dark Aleph in its unity mystically contains that ineffable four-lettered name, Jehovah, within itself; and consequently, how the great and bright Aleph is nothing other than Jehovah himself described symbolically.*

Indeed, let it not seem a wonder to you that the Hebrews signified not only the Creator but even created things themselves symbolically through letters. For although those letters used by the Hebrews today may be "dead" to us—mere human inventions used to indicate the intentions of things in writing—we nevertheless claim that these characters were originally delivered formally by God himself to the first man, Adam. They were described as fiery figures in the dark <term>hyle</term> <note>original: "hyla," referring to primordial matter or the substance of the universe before it was formed</note>, as if in a universal book. From this they were called "elements," as if they were <term>Hyle-ments</term>, meaning they carry the material essences of things, just as is clearly explained in the <margin>Yetzirah</margin> *Book of Formation* <note>original: "Ietzirah Abrahæ," the Sefer Yetzirah, an ancient text on the creation of the world through the Hebrew alphabet</note> of Abraham. 

Hence the <margin>Zohar</margin> <note>The foundational work of Jewish mysticism</note> said that Adam imposed true and proper names upon things, composing every name of every thing through letters that denote the influences of the stars destined for the ministry and service of the things they signify. These letters are, as it were, parts of the body, and the accents are in the place of spirit and life. And it is from this that the Kabbalists assert that God wrote the Law into a fiery globe by "dark fire upon white fire," as Nachmanides of Girona <note>original: "Rambam Gerundensis." Though the text says Rambam (usually Maimonides), the reference to Girona and the "fire on fire" description refers to Ramban (Nachmanides).</note> reports, according to that verse in Deuteronomy 33: *From his right hand went a fiery law for them.* From this also, the Kabbalists maintain that some creature in creation is attributed to every letter. 

But among these letters, Abraham placed three in his <margin>א מ ש <note>Aleph, Mem, Shin</note></margin> *Book of Formation* as the "fathers" or foundations from which the entire world was crafted: namely Aleph, Shin, and Mem. Of these, Aleph is referred to the Father, establishing all things; Mem to the Son, stabilizing all things; and Shin to the Holy or Fiery Spirit, vivifying all things. For Mem symbolically denotes the universal water, and Shin denotes fire, with power and action attributed to it. And so the three persons of the holy and individual Divinity went out from the most holy and super-essential tabernacle of eternity into the abyss of deformity for the construction of the world. 

Indeed, all of these are contained within the ineffable four-lettered name <note>The Tetragrammaton, יהוה (YHWH)</note> no differently than that very name was contained in the "lesser" or "obscure" Aleph before the creation of the world in a symbolic and mystical manner. Thus, the "great" and "bright" or "apparent" Aleph is nothing other than the presence of Jehovah in the creation of the world. Indeed, before the beginning, this name could not be signified without Aleph, insofar as Aleph was unity and simple, while Jehovah was the Tetragrammaton—that is, consisting of four. And therefore, the power and essence of that miraculous name is reduced into the single and principal letter, Aleph. 

For, as it seems to me, Jehovah was the first Alpha and the Being of Beings, arranged into four letters or characters for the creation of the world according to the likeness of Aleph. Hence <term>Jod</term> <note>The letter י</note> is the head and highest crown in creation, denoting the number ten, in which Aleph enters into the composition; and its three following parts correspond to the regions of the world, as we shall declare below. 

Furthermore, that <margin>א <image-desc>The Hebrew letter Aleph annotated to show its components (two Jods and a Vav).</image-desc></margin> Jehovah is symbolically contained in **א** <note>Aleph</note> is clearly declared by the fact that in Jehovah there is Jod, which signifies ten, and a double *He*, signifying the same arithmetically as Jod (for twice five is ten), and besides this, *Vav* is found there. Let us therefore examine the parts of the letter **א** <note>Aleph</note> itself; we shall find these four letters of Jehovah within it, partly by arithmetic value and partly by geometric shape. For its right wing is <term>Jod</term>, arranged in its own proper position like this: **י**; its left wing is another <term>Jod</term>, but arranged in a contrary way, like this: <note>The Jod character is printed in an inverted or mirrored orientation here.</note>**י**. It declares by this very fact that it stands there for the double **ה** <term>He</term>; so that its contrary arrangement declares its arithmetic equality with Jehovah <note>In Kabbalistic math, the name יהוה equals 26 (10+5+6+5). The letter Aleph is drawn as a slanted Vav (6) with two Jods (10+10), also totaling 26.</note>. Finally, the body of the Aleph is the <term>Vav</term> itself, designated like this: **| א |**. 

And so, in the unity or primary letter Aleph (**א**), the four letters of Jehovah (**יהוה**) are contained by Kabbalistic reasoning. From these we see that the ineffable name Tetragrammaton is the Alpha and Omega: namely, the "small Aleph," which is unity (1), and the "great Aleph," or the number one thousand (1,000), beyond whose denomination there is no progression. Consequently, it is evident that Jehovah is the most absolute, super-substantial nature of God, without any respect to things yet to be created, insofar as he is the hidden and 

->dark Aleph, as far as human understanding goes;<-
->and yet, that he is also that miraculous exemplar,<-
->according to which the Macrocosm is said to be created,<-
->the likeness of the creator, as we shall<-

OF SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.

### CHAPTER III.

->That the ineffable word, the Tetragrammaton, contains the properties of the most holy Trinity in the creation of the world: and how its parts, or letters, relate to the composition and constitution of that world.<-

Indeed, if we look closely at the parts of the bright Aleph or the letters of the word <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH, often rendered as Jehovah</note> with a diligent gaze, we will perceive that it is a most polished mirror, in which the figure and image of the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World" or the universe as a whole, reflecting the "Microcosm" of man</note> is most exactly drawn in living characters. And hence it is that the wondrous name יהוה [Jehovah] refers to חכמה <term>Hochma</term> <note>original: "Hochma," the second Sephirah, representing Divine Wisdom</note>, that is, the wisdom by which all things were made by Aleph—which is unity, the crown, and the father, and Jehovah without regard [to specific manifestation]. This is the Word coming forth from the dark Aleph, by which the heavens were established. Although this is the second <term>numeration</term> <note>original: "numeratio," a term for a Sephirah or divine emanation</note>, or emanation, or Sephiroth, it is nonetheless called the "Beginning" because the world was crafted from it. 

This is the first procession from the Father, who is hidden in the secret place of darkness, into the universal matter or water deformed by darkness, so that He might cleanse them and drive away all foul impurity to the center by His presence, according to that saying of the Wise Man: 

>*Prov. 8. v. 22. Jehovah possessed Wisdom in the beginning of his way, before his works, before that time; she was anointed before the age; before the beginning, before the origins of the earth, when there were no depths or abysses, she was brought forth, when there were no springs abounding with water; before the mountains were settled, and before the hills she was formed; when the earth was not yet made, when he prepared the heavens, she was there; when he set a compass upon the face of the depth, when he established the clouds above, when he strengthened the fountains of the deep, when he gave the sea its decree, and to the waters, that they should not transgress the command of his mouth, when he appointed the foundations of the earth, then was Wisdom with him as a master-worker composing all things, playing before him at all times,* etc. 

And hence St. John calls her the Word of Jehovah, through whom all things were made, and without whom nothing was made that was made; likewise the beginning of things, and indeed Jehovah himself, in whom was the life of created things; which life was the light of men. And that light shines in the darkness, both universal and particular, and the darkness did not comprehend it, insofar as it is incomprehensible and infinite; He was in the world, and the world was made through him, etc. 

From these things it is clearly evident that the Wisdom of God is his very Word; which is of the same <term>supersubstantial</term> <note>Existing beyond or above the nature of physical substance</note> essence with him, and consequently is included in the ineffable Tetragrammaton, and is as it were the Tetragrammaton or Jehovah himself, who made everything that was made by the efficacy of his spirit. Therefore, the idea of the entire Macrocosm can be seen and perceived in this incomprehensible mirror from head to foot—that is, from its circumference to the center of the structure; indeed, according to its exact idea and model, all parts of the world are numbered, measured, and weighed. Hence it is called the Idea of the Archetypal God. 

For as pertains to the numbering of the world, we find that the first letter י, namely <term>Jod</term>, denotes ten, and the second ה [He] five, and the third ו <term>Vau</term> six, and the last ה [He] five. When these are added together, they produce 26; and if א [Aleph] is added to these, which is the first unity, they constitute 27. Or proceeding another way, we find that in the name יהוה there are only three different letters [Y, H, and W]: this number multiplied by itself produces 9, or a square, denoting the same number of simple orders of angels, and the same number of moving celestial spheres, as well as regions in the elementary world. For 9 multiplied again by its root [3] produces 27, which are the degrees by which the world is measured. And, if those three 9s are properly arranged in the Platonic manner in this order—9 9 9—they show a unique numbering of the world, although the <margin>Cabalistæ</margin> <note>Kabbalists</note> prefer to present this through numbers and the thirty-two paths; namely, the 10 <term>Sephiroth</term> <note>The ten attributes or emanations of God in Kabbalah</note>, and the twenty-two formal and most holy letters of the Hebrews.

From these things, therefore, you see that we have measured the semi-diameter of the worldly machine or workmanship in 27 parts or degrees, and distinguished its whole by the numbers 9 9 9 according to the ineffable name Tetragrammaton. But now let us see how we can derive its spherical and circular figure. With due observation, we will perceive that all the letters of that name are not only vowels but even circular and spherical in the numbers they produce, whether linear, square, or cubic. Thus י [Jod] denoting 10, multiplied by itself, produces a square of 100; which again multiplied by 10 produces 1000, and so on from ten to ten unto infinity. Thus ה [He], that is five, multiplied by itself brings 25 for the square, and 125 for the cube. Similarly, ו [Vau], denoting 6, multiplied by itself makes 36, which again multiplied by 6 produces 216, which number is its cube. Indeed, no other numbers are accustomed to do this except these three; wherefore these numbers are called perfectly spherical. Furthermore, even if the arithmetic value of the letter ה [He, which is 5] becomes the center of some sphere, and that sphere is divided into ten equal parts, and 9 is placed opposite 1 through the diameter, and 8 opposite 2, 7 opposite 3, 6 opposite 4, and 5 opposite 5, we shall observe with open eyes that five and ten are circular and spherical letters, as is clearly demonstrated in our *Tractatu nostro de numeris divinis* <note>Treatise on Divine Numbers</note>, chapter 16; the demonstration of which we have noted here.

SECT. I. PORT. I. PART. I. LIB. I.

[A circular diagram illustrating the divine structure of the universe through the Hebrew <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, יהוה or YHWH</note>. At the center is a small circle containing the Hebrew letter <term>Jod</term> <note>י, the first letter of the name</note>. Thus, by these arguments it is shown that all the letters of the ineffable name, the Tetragrammaton, are circular. Nor is it surprising that God chose such a proportion and figure to reveal His ineffable name to the world, since the spherical shape is the most capacious, most abundant, and most perfect of all. And this is the reason why He divided each of the 27 partitions of the <term>semidiameter</term> <note>the radius of a circle</note> into as many sections of the circumference, which we have called spheres or orbs; according to which He—from whom Moses sought His name—replied: *I am He who was, who is, and who shall be:* <note>original: "Ego sum qui sui, qui sum, & qui ero," a variation of the declaration in Exodus 3:14</note> Here, I say, the Father of Eternity, with glowing turns, daily and through every age of the world, revolves from east to west and from west to east in a wondrous and incomprehensible manner.

Similarly, if we wish to investigate the weights of worldly things and the distinct balancing of the heavens—by which scales of justice they are suspended in the vast spirit—within the name יהוה [Jehovah], and to contemplate them as if in a mirror, we shall find in it the entire geometrical proportion of the world and its disposition in weight, discovered by this method according to our speculation with open eyes.

Let **Jod** [י] be the beginning, or the first letter of the Tetragrammaton, like a bright **Aleph** [א], beginning to look upon the deformity of <term>hyle</term> <note>original: "hylæ," referring to primordial, unformed matter</note> with a luminous and splendid countenance. Its gaze, stretched downward toward the earth or the center, alters the disposition of the entire round machine of the radius and conforms it to the nature and perfection of its own appearance. And hence it is said in *Genesis 1*, immediately after the creation of light: *And God saw the light, that it was good, etc.* Then He made the firmament in the midst of the waters, by which He divided the waters that are under the firmament from those that were above; and it was so. And afterward, in the creation of the earth and the sea, Moses says: *And He saw that it was good.* From these things it is manifest that God, by the goodness of His essence (which alone is good, and nothing else), made the entire matter of the world similar to Himself through the participation of His goodness.

Let us therefore examine the nature of the formal letters of the Tetragrammaton itself, and we shall find that in all things it agrees with the parts of the world itself; which were made by them just as they themselves have existed from eternity. And this is the cause why the <term>soul of the world</term> <note>original: "anima mundi," the animating spirit of the universe</note> denotes God the Father, who is the Father of Light, by the eternal and everlasting ineffable power of its creator:

**Jod** [י] denotes God the Father, who is the Father of Light; indeed, among the <term>Kabbalists</term> <note>original: "Cabalistas," practitioners of Jewish mysticism</note>, this formal letter signifies the same thing as Jehovah.

The flow and first emanation of this light passing through the spirit is understood by the first **He** [ה], which denotes spirit and breathing, positioned immediately between the superior and most simple spirit (which we attribute to the Spirit of the Lord, insofar as He was moved over the waters) and the final **He** [ה], which is compared to the gross spirit or the waters under the firmament.

**Vau** [ו], therefore, is the symbol of the Son or the **Word** <note>original: "Verbi"</note>, joined with the Father, **Jod**, by the power and bond of the prior spirit, or the first **He**. Thus, the first **He** refers to the purest waters or spirit which are above the firmament, and the latter **He** to the waters which are gathered below the firmament. 

**Vau** is as it were the firmament, or the soul of the firmament, separating the prior and spiritual waters from the dense and corruptible waters—or a benevolent glue coupling and uniting both the lower and superior waters. This **Vau** is indeed that *Word of the Lord, by which the heavens were established*, or the firmament, according to the sentiment of the Royal Prophet [David], who *placed his tabernacle in the Sun*, constantly infusing life into lower things; for in Him is *life and light shining in the darkness*, as is held in the Gospel of St. John. Indeed, this is that bond which joins the divine and supracelestial spirit with that which is elementary and corporeal; without which...

ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.

By an unbreakable bond, a nature so divine could not undergo such a lowly condition as to first enter a dense spirit liable to changes, and then later inhabit a body so opaque while joined to it. And this is generally why <term>Vau</term><note>The third letter of the divine name, ו</note> is taken among the Hebrews as a copulative conjunction—connecting the preceding word with the following one. Therefore, <term>Jod</term><note>The first letter, י, representing the Father or the initial spark of creation</note> is the illuminating Father, the emanation of whose light, penetrating through the first <term>He</term><note>The second letter, ה, often associated with the Holy Spirit or "spiritual waters"</note> (or the pure waters) on the first day, created the firmament by its presence on the second day. This separated the pure waters (or superior spirits) from the impure and inferior waters, which are also dense spirits. Finally, by its presence—after the inferior waters were purified on the third day and their dreg-like impurity was driven back to the center—it placed its tabernacle in the Sun. 

For this reason, it should be noted that the letters in the <term>Tetragrammaton</term><note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> are arranged according to the nature and position of the parts of the world, which flowed forth from the ineffable essence of these formal letters. Thus it happens that between the <term>Empyrean heaven</term><note>The highest, most spiritual part of heaven, associated with fire and light</note> (or spiritual waters) and the elementary heaven (or the denser and more visible waters), the firmament is located; and in its middle is the solar tabernacle of the Divinity. This tabernacle relates to both the inferior and superior waters, insofar as it first receives the gifts and the succession of light from the Father, Jod, through the spiritual sea (namely, through the first He), which it then dispenses into the inferior waters—signified by the latter <term>Vau</term>—and the creatures living within them. The subtler part of these waters is called Air, the middle part Water, and the gross and dreg-filled part is the Earth itself. 

In this way, therefore, we have the world with its parts suspended in their proper places by the weight of justice through the power of the great name, the Tetragrammaton; specifically, by the power of the Word and the Holy Spirit, proceeding first from Jod and then from Vau. From this it follows that a twofold difference of waters is found in the world; just as in the ineffable name <term>Jehovah</term><note>A Latinized rendering of the Tetragrammaton</note> we find a double or twin letter He.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*How we may derive the reason for health and sickness from the letters of Jehovah; and how Jehovah is understood either in terms of mercy, or of justice and punishment.*<-

From the preceding points you can gather that in the miraculous Tetragrammaton, Jod is like God Himself, existing outside of all matter, looking out from His eternal and <term>supersubstantial</term><note>Existing beyond the realm of physical substance or being</note> kingdom into the depths of the vast <term>hyle</term><note>original: "hylae," a Greek term for primordial matter or chaos</note>. The remaining subsequent letters of His name, differing from one another, are two properties or emanations of the sacrosanct Trinity immersing themselves into the darkness. Of these, <term>He</term> is the letter of spirit, breath, wind, and all spiritual things. According to the testimony of St. Peter, these things consist of water and through water—indeed, they are the water itself, both subtle and thick. This letter is the symbol of the Holy Spirit in its third emanation, proceeding from Jod on one side and from Vau on the other. 

Hence, the first He in <term>Jehovah</term><note>original: "יהוה"</note> is the spirit, or the most noble, subtle, and health-giving spiritual water; indeed, it is the very fountain of life because of that fiery emanation which proceeded immediately from the mouth of Jod. It sits upon the highest peaks of the spherical machine (or the heavens) on the eternal throne, outside of all matter. By Jod's fiery and precious spirit, that next Spirit is called holy and health-giving, filled on all sides with the nectar-like rays of life, and endowed, as it were, with the breath of life. 

Therefore, Jod spoke first, and Vau is His Word—the truest Tree of Life planted by Jod (the Tetragrammaton) in the Empyrean heaven, beside the immense river of the super-celestial Paradise (or the sea of precious spirits and waters, the liquid of life) with infinite branches or rays. And the Spirit proceeding from both is said to be "carried over those burning and god-like waters." Whoever is fashioned from their elements is rendered immortal; they are not accustomed to ever falling ill, nor do they suffer the passion and disturbance that come from darkness—just as we can perceive in the <term>intelligences</term><note>A term for angels or purely spiritual beings</note> or angels of every order living in that blessed sea. Indeed, Jod is accustomed to pouring this liquid of life through the Word and Spirit into the lower regions, by which that lower Paradise is also filled for the health of creatures, and especially of men. Indeed, the Royal Psalmist sang this to us in Psalm 36 in these words:

> *The mercy and kindness of Jehovah is from the heavens, etc. You preserve men and beasts, O Jehovah; Oh, how precious is your kindness and mercy, when the children of men betake themselves to the shadow of your wings; they are most abundantly filled with the fatness of your house, and you give them to drink from the torrent of your delights: since with you is the fountain of life; in your light we shall enjoy light, etc.*

Indeed, this is that mercy and grace, or the "fatness of the house of God," which is the truest balm of life, which far surpasses the nature of sin, as is taught in Romans 5:20. And hence, Psalm 85: *Show us your mercy, and grant us your salvation*; as if he had said that salvation comes forth and happens to men by means of the mercy of Jehovah. And Wisdom 16: *Your mercy coming shall heal the children, whom the teeth of the hunting dragons have overcome*; and in the same place: *Neither herb nor ointment shall heal them, but your Word, O Lord, which heals...*<note>The Latin text cuts off at "ser-" which is the beginning of "sermo" (Word/Speech).</note>

# CHAPTER IV.

## *How we may derive the logic of health and sickness from the letters of Jehovah; and how Jehovah is understood either from the side of mercy, or of justice and punishment.*

From what has been said, you can gather that in the marvelous Tetragrammaton, *Jod* is like God Himself, beyond all matter, looking out from His eternal and supersubstantial kingdom into the depths of vast <term>hyle</term><note>original: "hylae vastae viscera." Hyle is the Greek term for primordial matter or "the void."</note>. The remaining subsequent letters of His name, differing from one another, are two properties or emanations of the most holy Trinity, immersing themselves into the darkness. Among these, *He*—which is the symbol of the spirit, breath, wind, and all spiritual things (which, according to Saint Peter, are from water and through water; indeed, they are the waters themselves, both subtle and thick)—is the symbol of the Holy Spirit, the third emanation, proceeding from *Jod* on one side and from *Vau* on the other. 

Thus, the first *He* in the name *Jehovah* is the spirit, or the most noble, subtle, and health-giving spiritual water; indeed, it is the very fountain of life because of that fiery emanation which proceeded immediately from the mouth of *Jod*. *Jod* sits upon the eternal throne above the highest peaks of the spherical machine (the heavens) beyond all matter. By His fiery and precious breath, that Spirit closest to Him is called holy and health-giving, filled on all sides with nectar-like rays of life, and endowed, as it were, with the breath of life. First, therefore, *Jod* spoke, and *Vau* is His Word—the truest Tree of Life, planted by the immense river of the super-celestial Paradise, or the sea of precious spirits and the waters (the liquid of life), with infinite branches or rays from *Jod* Himself (or the Tetragrammaton) in the Empyrean heaven. 

And the spirit proceeding from both was said to be "carried over those burning and god-like waters," from whose elements whoever is fashioned is rendered immortal; they are never accustomed to be sick, and they do not suffer the passion and disturbance that come from darkness—just as we can perceive in the Intelligences or Angels of every order living in that blessed sea. Indeed, *Jod* is accustomed to pour this liquid of life through the Word and Spirit into the lower regions, by which that lower Paradise is also filled for the health of creatures, and especially of men. This is what the Royal Psalmist sang to us. <margin>Psalm 36.</margin>

For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we shall enjoy light, etc.*

### SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK I.

...the one who heals all things: Similarly *Job 10:12: You have exercised the kindness of life toward me, and your visitation has preserved my Spirit;* And *Proverbs 3:18: Life is a tree to those who lay hold of wisdom;* And *Proverbs 10:11: The fountain of life flows from the mouth of the righteous.* Similarly, in Proverbs 11, we are taught that the life of man is the Spirit of Jehovah, as in *Genesis 2:7 and Deuteronomy 30:20: Jehovah himself is your life, and the length of your days;* and so in the rest. By these we are taught that the Spirit—imbued by the first emanation of essential clarity and the purest vision of God—is life-giving, attributing life to the superior waters and to all creatures dwelling in them.

Whence it happens that the first <term>He</term><note>The Hebrew letter ה, associated here with the first "breath" or spirit of creation.</note> is joined to <term>Jod</term><note>The Hebrew letter י, the point of divine origin.</note> itself on the first day of creation, and it becomes <term>Jah</term><note>יה, one of the names of God, representing the first stage of manifestation.</note>: and thus the moist spirit, or the subtle superior water, is illuminated—namely the first <term>He</term>—through the first emanation from <term>Jod</term> itself. For in this way the <term>Empyrean</term><note>The highest heaven, traditionally thought to be composed of pure light or fire.</note> heaven was made; thus wisdom was created first of all, and the understanding of prudence from eternity; whose source is the Word of God in the highest, that is, on the <term>supersubstantial</term><note>Existing above or beyond the level of physical matter or substance.</note> throne of Jehovah, as the very words of Ecclesiasticus say in *chapter 1:4.* And this is the reason that this is called the intellectual heaven; whose "passive intellect" is brought into action by the rays of God proceeding immediately from the <term>Jod</term> of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term><note>The sacred four-letter Name of God, YHWH.</note>. This shining power is called the "active intellect"; which is like a golden tree of life emanating from the eternal root <term>Jod</term>, which is <term>Ehieh</term><note>The Hebrew name "I Am" (אהיה), signifying pure existence.</note>; whose processing in the first <term>Ehieh</term> is also said to "flow outward."

And in this way <term>Jod</term>, in its first procession into matter, joined with <term>He</term>—making the supreme portion of spirits or waters into <term>Jah</term> or <term>יה</term>—denotes the method by which God, expanding Himself from unity, begins to migrate from His point and simplicity into a material line for the creation of all things. For just as two numbers constitute the first number, and two points a minimal line, so also <term>Jod</term>—which is a point proceeding from its own unity into the unity of matter—produces a line or duality. And just as before the creation of the world He had no name except the one, ineffable, and most simple, namely <term>Jod</term>, spoken according to His unique essence—or a bright and appearing <term>Aleph</term><note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, א, often symbolizing the oneness of God.</note> (which indeed is the same as the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> of the ideal world)—so also after the sending of His "countenance" into <term>hyle</term><note>The Greek term for primordial, unformed matter.</note>, all names taken from His works are attributed to Him. Whence that unique and hidden name, the <term>Tetragrammaton</term>, is called the *separated name* appropriated to Him, in which there is no participation <note>Meaning it refers to God's essence alone, independent of creation.</note>. But His other glorious names have meaning with participation, insofar as they are taken from the works which were discovered, as <term>Moses the Egyptian</term><note>Referring to the medieval philosopher Moses Maimonides (1138–1204).</note> testifies. Therefore, His first name, taken from the first work, is <term>Jah</term>, <term>יה</term>, the name of essence, merit, and attribution: whence it is found in *Psalm 130:3: If you, Jah, should mark iniquities, etc.*

> Hence <term>Jod</term> is named, insofar as it looks into the darkness: And again in *Exodus 15: Jah is my strength and my praise;* insofar as through the creation of wisdom, the strength of strengths was produced into the world, according to that saying of <term>Hermes Trismegistus</term><note>The legendary founder of Hermeticism and alchemy.</note> in the <term>Emerald Tablet</term><note>A foundational alchemical text (Tabula Smaragdina) attributed to Hermes Trismegistus.</note>; *This is the strong strength of all strength, because it overcomes every subtle thing and penetrates every solid thing; thus the world was created, etc.*

Similarly, <term>Jah</term> denotes kindness toward the whole world and the creatures of the world: Nor is it a wonder, because <term>Jod</term>, which is the symbol of the Father, denotes clemency and mercy, insofar as it is the office of a father to have mercy on his children, according to that *Psalm 103.*

Wherefore <term>Jod</term>, which is the parent of the spirit—that is, the one who brings it into being—fills and activates it everywhere with His mercy by the power of His rays. And from this kindness and grace of His infused into the darkness, the supreme Spirit is prepared, the Spirit of <term>Jod</term> is carried over it, and that spirit thus illuminated is called the light created on the first day; from whose full influence, and the grace and kindness of the hidden <term>Jod</term> of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term>, things are led from potentiality into act. Angels are procreated from the simple fire or light of <term>Jod</term> and the spirit <term>He</term>, <term>Metattron</term><note>Metatron, a high-ranking archangel often identified as the "Prince of the Presence" or the Soul of the World.</note> or the Soul of the World is placed over nature, and life is communicated to every created thing.

Oh, infinite power of things, and ineffable goodness and mercy of <term>Jod</term>, by which all things overwhelmed by darkness and oblivion are produced from a lethal and sad captivity into light and being, and from potentiality into act! Is this not an admirable sign of kindness and mercy? Indeed, from this fountain of kindness, from this origin of created wisdom, from this nectar of the "supereffential" Word and true "potable gold," from this divine balsam and no other, has flowed the method of protecting the health of creatures, the remedy for driving away sickness, the way of repelling diabolical injuries, and the logic and medicine for suppressing infernal rage and malice; yes, even the power of extinguishing or uprooting the poison of death itself (which first crept into the world by the malice of the Devil), and of suppressing its lethal blow and violence. In this [light] there is neither disease, nor violence, nor death, nor any impediment of nature; for in it is concord, unity, life, action, and light, which resists all actions of darkness whatsoever: Hence *Psalm 80:4: By the light of the face of God we shall be saved.*

This <term>He</term>, therefore, is the created principle of things, or rather the Spirit created through the union and influx of the uncreated light of the Word itself into it; by whose admirable presence that whole Spirit <term>He</term>, thus illuminated by <term>Jah</term> (<term>יה</term>), is called "created light"; although it is Spirit only brought from the potentiality of matter into act by the presence of uncreated light. Whence the Spirit so created, because of its illumination and the dominion of light within it, is called light; which light, however, if it be taken simply as the emanation from the uncreated <term>Jod</term>—

From this, therefore, the error of those who condemned the Pagan <note>original: "Philosophos Ethnicos"</note> philosophers is revealed, because they called Nature "God," and God himself "Nature": For when they spoke of nature, they understood that which they called "invisible fire," from which <term>Zoroaster</term> and <term>Heraclitus</term> taught that all things were brought forth.

From these points it is clear that by "nature" they wished to hint at the essential light floating in the universal moist nature; as if they were saying the fiery and Holy Spirit <term>Jod</term>, which "was carried in and over the waters" <note>A reference to Genesis 1:2.</note>, or the universal Spirit: For such light is of the true and simple essence of <term>Jod</term> itself, or the <term>Tetragrammaton</term><note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>; so that it can no more be separated from its eternal nature than a solar ray, which is indivisible, can be separated from the Sun.

And although this divine light extends itself through the created <term>Macrocosm</term><note>The universe or "Great World," as opposed to the "Microcosm" of man.</note>, as if proceeding from unity into a multitude of matter, its rays are nevertheless bound to their root no differently than the branches of some tree are bound to their trunk and origin.

And this is a quite permissible and by no means contemptible reason why <term>Democritus</term>, and <term>Orpheus</term>, and many of the <term>Pythagoreans</term> thought that a certain God or soul presided over every single thing, and that all things were full of Gods; they established divine honors for these, and dedicated prayers and sacrifices to them, and pursued them with diverse worship and veneration: But finally, they recognized that all these souls or species of light were to be reduced to one "soul of the world" <note>original: "anima mundi"</note>, and all Gods were to be referred back to one Jupiter.

Hence, therefore, <term>Plato</term> says; *Do not speak of God without light:* And a certain man in his chemical art <note>Referring to Alchemical literature.</note> clearly cries out, *that there is nothing in the very circle of the firmament that bears a greater likeness to God than the soul of the world and light itself: Indeed,* he says, *any thing claims as much of God for itself as it is capable of receiving light.*

And this is the reason that <term>Augustine</term> says in his book *On Free Will*; *light holds the first place among bodies.* Must we not also, to return to the fountain of all truth, note what the Psalmist says in *Psalm 103:1 and 104:19: Light is the cloak and garment of God?* Do we not also read in Saint John, *that the Word was in the beginning with God, and that all things were made through it, and without it nothing was made that has been made? for in it was life, and that life was the light of men, and that light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it: And this was the one that was in the world, and the world was made through it, and the world did not know it:* <note>A translation of John 1:1-10.</note>

By which words the Apostle seems most exactly to confirm all that doctrine which Moses produced in the first chapter of Genesis; for he clearly teaches us in that place that by the Word of the Lord "LET IT BE" or "BE," and by the presence of his spirit—which was carried over the waters, proceeding from the father and the son—light, or rather the spirit, was adorned and created in a marvelous way on the first day; For light does not undergo "creation" insofar as it is the true act of <term>Jehovah</term>, sent out immediately from the Holy heavens to create spiritual things, or the waters hidden in the belly of the <term>Hyle</term><note>A Greek term used here for primordial, unformed matter.</note>; that is, to lead them out of darkness and as if from nothing into light and action.

Here, therefore, with a ready mind we uncover how nature itself is called God: namely, insofar as the light of Jehovah, which is his essential emanation, is present in the universal moist nature; which the Pagans also thereafter called God, wrongly taking the created matter for the divine essence and form, or the most holy creating light. And in this way God is considered in the "concrete," receiving various names for himself according to his works, and not according to his being: But indeed, insofar as God—the "dark <term>Aleph</term>"—is considered in the "abstract," he remains without any respect to created things; that is, in his simple and infinite essence in his supersubstantial kingdom, and on the sublime throne of eternity, sitting triumphantly above the highest summit or apex of his "round machine" <note>A common metaphor for the spherical universe.</note>, and outside all the limits of the waters. From which it is clearly evident how God is truly said to be inside and outside all things, and how he exists everywhere and nowhere inclusively, and how he is infinite and encompassed by no boundary. We have, therefore, in this way an intellectual vision of <term>Jah</term> himself, or the first emanation of <term>Jod</term> itself, which is the symbol of the ineffable Tetragrammaton, filling the whole space of the three primary numbers 9 9 9. ## CHAPTER V.

### On the placement of the letter *Vau* between both *He*s; and on the production of the firmament made on the third day; likewise on the great mystery of the Angel *Metatron*.

<margin>If</margin> **N**ow, that we may arrive at the second production of God and the creation of the firmament itself, it must be understood that the "established heavens" are nothing other than the firmament itself. As the Psalmist testifies, "By the word of the Lord the heavens were established"; therefore, it was also by the Word of the Lord that the firmament was made, intersecting and dividing the upper waters from the lower waters. I say the firmament was *made*; that is, that <term>middle spirit</term> <note>Also known as the "ether," thought to be a subtle substance filling the space between the stars and the earth.</note>, which is called "ethereal," was brought into action through the presence and act of the most holy light. Indeed, this light mixed itself with that spirit, clarifying and giving it form. Thus, by the uncreated power of **Jehovah**, the intermediate spirit was created between the waters—or rather, between the subtler spirits and those that are grosser and denser, both the luminous and the opaque. Hence it is clear that the eternal power of this heaven is the mediator between the super-celestial throne of God the Father and this earth, and between the subtle and gross waters, between God and man, and between the mind and the body. From him, therefore, descend the gifts of life and health to all lower things, by which putrid air is corrected, the malice of fire is brought into the fellowship of peace, bitter waters recover their sweetness, sick bodies regain health and receive growth through generation, and vegetables that seemed dead are observed to turn green again and multiply every year. All these gifts are accustomed to flow into the world from that supreme wisdom, either the angel **Metatron**, or the universal soul of the world, or the first emanation from *Jod* <note>The first letter of the divine name, representing the initial point of creation.</note>, as we shall declare below.

We say, therefore, that after the first irradiation from God had informed the first **Jah** <note>Hebrew: יה (Jod-He), the first half of the divine name.</note>, or the supreme part of the world, it descended into the middle place covered in darkness. There it took on the form of **Vau** <note>Hebrew: ו, the third letter.</note>, which in arithmetic denotes the number 6, and thus it encompasses **He** and **He** <note>Hebrew: ה, which equals 5.</note>—that is, five plus one, which makes 6. In this way, it is interposed under the form of the letter *Vau* between the two *He*s of the name **Jehovah** (יהוה). This indicates the *He* as the middle spirit and the other *He* as the unity within that same spirit; just as the *Jod* entering into the first *He* at the beginning proved unity in the composition. From this it follows that the upper *Jod* added to the name makes *Jah* (יה), signifying God or the Being of all things. So also *Vau*, placed after the Spirit already created—namely the lower *He*—makes ***Hu*** <note>original: "Hu" (הוא), meaning "He" or "Him."</note>, which is "Himself." This word is written with an **Aleph** (א), thus: **הוא**. Nevertheless, the *Aleph* is not pronounced, but is expressed there for the symbolic representation of the Trinity in that unity which exceeds the five of *He* and constitutes the six of *Vau*. This is even more clearly denoted by the Tetragrammaton **Ehieh** (אהיה) <note>original: אהיה, meaning "I Am."</note>; where *Jod* is placed for *Jod*, and *Jod* in the middle is in the place of *Vau*, proving that *Jod* in the middle of the *He* of the firmament signifies *Vau*. This is the "One" and the *He*, or the "One over He," which indicates the number 100. And so the first Being in the supreme spirit, and "Himself" in the middle—that is, the same Being in the middle—is as if he were the **Messiah** himself, or the power of the Tetragrammaton, or the Soul of the World. This is the angel **Metatron**, as he exists in his created spirit, in whom is the name of God **Shaddai** <note>original: "Sadai" (שדי). In Hebrew numerology, both Metatron and Shaddai equal 314.</note> by an equal number according to the calculation of the Cabalists. They say this is the very Angel of whom **Jehovah** spoke in Exodus 23:

> For my name is in him,

that is, in the spiritual body or the moist spirit of all nature. In him, **Jehovah**, or **Ehieh**—that is, the crown of *Jod*—is said by the Cabalists to have sealed the world through his seal **JHV** (יהו). This is called **Truth** <note>original: "Emeth" (אמת).</note>, because it is born by multiplying within itself. Thus **JHV**, being the seal of the world, has impressed itself into this middle and even the lowest world. By this impression, he left the image of *He* and *Jod*—that is, of the Father and the Word—joined together into unity through the Spirit *He*. Therefore, just as the characters of a common seal are left exactly in the wax and give form to a shapeless mass;
<margin>"</margin> so also **Ehieh**, through this seal **JHV**, introduced the image of the Father's *He* with the unity of the Spirit *Jod*
<margin>"</margin> proceeding from him, and the wonderful presence of the Word swimming within it, as signets into the visible world.
<margin>"</margin> By these, the idea of the intellectual world was infused into the lowest and sensible world, raising it out of darkness
<margin>"</margin> and building it in its own image. With the living characters of the Word, which sails in the sea of the visible world,
<margin>"</margin> he gives life to, creates, and disposes all things according to the decree of the Eternal Speaker. From the **Jod**
<margin>"</margin> and the **He** of this divine seal, the spiritual and intellectual characters of the Divine Mind are imprinted upon
<margin>"</margin> the rational soul. And the **Vau** mixes those characters flowing into the ethereal spirit with the breath of life,
<margin>"</margin> so that all these may be infused into the opaque and elemental human body, where the soul may serve the body.
**Vau**, therefore, or the Word, is the immediate author of the heavens and all creatures. From these things, it is clear why Nature itself was called "God" by the ancient philosophers—though incorrectly—because God himself, or the Word who is God, mixes himself into the moist nature. Consequently, they mistakenly took the created thing for the Creator; namely, for the Word, which is God in nature. By his spirit and power, all things live, and all things exist as they are. For God is not called the "Word" except insofar as he possessed the property from the Speaker to be poured out from the mouth of the Speaker into the things to be created and their continuation in the world. While he is one in essence with the first person speaking—namely, one God—they differ in property, because the Word is brought forth into the world or moist nature, while the Speaker is in his kingdom without any regard for matter. And yet these two persons are essence...

# ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES:

...ce one and the same: Thus we see in man, that the word is not spoken, before it is brought forth into the air or moist nature; and then by means of the Spirit the voice is produced, and from the voice the word proceeds; though the Spirit of the man speaking, and of the word brought forth or sent out into the air, is the same in essence, and of the same entity. Does not **Mercurius Trismegistus** confirm all these things with the most manifest words in his *Pimander*, Book 1? where he speaks in these words: 

<margin>1</margin> *Pimander*, the mind of divine power, changed its form, and suddenly revealed the universe: 
<margin>2</margin> For I beheld a certain immense spectacle; namely, all things converted into light, exceedingly sweet and pleasant. 

This is that dark <term>Aleph</term> <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet (א), here representing the hidden, unmanifest Godhead.</note>, or the mind of divine power, going out into the act of the world, but reflecting back upon itself; suddenly it becomes the bright *Aleph*, or doubling itself in the number ten in the form of <term>Jod</term> <note>The tenth Hebrew letter (י), which looks like a point or seed; the author sees it as the "manifest" version of Aleph.</note>. By its bright emanation, it has now entered into the formless <term>hyle</term> <note>original: "hylen"; the primordial matter or "stuff" of the universe before it is given shape.</note>, and caused all things hidden and subject to shadows to appear; that is, it is converted into light, or a pleasant glow, and thus that illuminated light created on the first day is named. 

But now, that we may observe that this first emanation is the Word in shadow and yet illuminating, I would like you to attend to the following discourse of the Sage, which is of this sort: *A little after, a certain horrifying shadow was gliding down in an oblique revolution, and was migrating into a moist nature, then agitated by an ineffable countenance; thence a certain great smoke erupted into a sound; from the sound a voice went forth, which I thought to be the voice of light: From this voice of light the Word came forth; but this moist nature standing by cherished it,* etc. 

By these words the Philosopher seems to indicate that from the **י Jod**, the unity of the Tetragrammaton, the light first flowed forth—as if from a fountain of light into the first **ה He**—expelling the darkness from it by manifesting what was hidden. And the Spirit, which was enclosed in the shadows gliding down in an oblique revolution, eagerly embraced that most beautiful, God-born, and <term>superessential</term> <note>Beyond the category of "essence" or "being"; used to describe God's existence as higher than anything we can define.</note> light sent out from the eternal mind of the **Jod** by the first emanation. By the divine power thus enclosed in it, an eruption from the darkness occurs; in that eruption, a voice is produced, and with the voice, the Word. This Word is the power of the first emanation sounding from the **Jod**, or **Jehovah**. It is brought forth not in vain, but so effective in strength that it sounds and speaks through the sound; and the Word thus enunciated imprints the sense of the speech with fiery and formal characters upon the surface of the dark Chaos. It does so in such a way that it is impossible for the effect not to follow, according to that saying: *Not even a tittle or iota from his words shall fall to the earth* <note>original: "Nullum & ne apex quidem aut iota..." A reference to Matthew 5:18.</note>; that is, it shall not perish or be brought forth in vain. And elsewhere: *The Word of Jehovah shall remain forever.* 

It is, he says, the voice of light, or the voice of the **Jod** itself, or of the Father of light first brought forth into the **ה He**; from which the Empyrean heaven was made, from whose pure elements the intelligences of every kind are procreated. Then it was brought into the middle **ו Vau**, which is contained within the *Vau*; and the firmament was made. And finally, <insert>into the last</insert> **ה He**; and the lowest heaven was made. These three heavens are indeed fashioned from water, whether more gross or subtle, and they differ from one another according to the greater or lesser dominion of the divine emanation. For the more that most simple, God-like essence predominates in the world, the purer, cleaner, more transparent, and subtler is that part of the world—whether we call it the moist spirit or the water. 

Hence, as St. John says in chapter 1: *The Word was in the beginning* (that is, in the infinite shadow or matter); *And the Word was with God; and God was the Word: and this was in the beginning with God: All things were made through him: and without him was made nothing that was made: In him was life, and the light of men: And the light shines in the darkness* (that is, in the horrifying shadow) *and the darkness did not comprehend it* (that is, it erupted from the darkness and gave forth a sound), etc. *He was in the world, and the world was made through him,* etc. 

Therefore, just as God, the "dark Aleph," was the first unity outside the created world and before its creation, so too his first emanation is that through which the Word, the Messiah, or the Power of the Tetragrammaton entered into the world. Indeed, it is that very Word—which is of the same essence as the **Aleph**, **Jod**, **Jah**, **Ehieh**, and the **Tetragrammaton**—that speaks. Just as the *Aleph* was the first unity in the Archetypal and ideal world, outlining the ideal figure of the world to be built; so his Word, expressed through the **ו Vau** into the **ה He**, is the unity and principle of the ideal world, reducing that world into a real arrangement and sensible form. 

And hence it is written in Zechariah that the Tetragrammaton God shall be **יהוה** <note>Jehovah</note>, that is, *one*, and his name **יהוה**, that is, *one*. And he is called Alpha and Omega and **יהוה**, that is, one, as he who is the principle of the one. Yet this is properly said of the Word, as is understood in the Apocalypse. And then I find that God is not called <term>Lo</term> <note>Hebrew לא, meaning "Not."</note> "one," just as he is not called "Being" (*Ens*); forasmuch as he is above all Being, as he from whom everything that is emanates. Wherefore he is called by the most contemplative thinkers <term>Ain</term> <note>Hebrew אין, meaning "Nothing" or "Non-Being" in the sense of being beyond any definition of existence.</note>, that is, "Non-Being"; as we read in Exodus 17: *Is the Lord "Being" (Jesh), or "Non-Being" (Ain)?* And elsewhere he is called *Ain* and *Jesh*, that is, Being and Non-Being. For insofar as he is in a created spiritual being, he is called "Being," which is the Word; but truly, insofar as he is beyond all relation to a created thing, he is called "Non-Being," because he transcends all entity. 

However, I wanted to make known to you in this place how the Hebrew characters agree with the nature of the thing. For the **א Aleph**, signifying God insofar as he is Non-Being and outside all things, has within itself the **א** signifying God as one in the simplicity of his supersubstantial essence, considered in himself without progression into number. And **י Jod** is God found at the end of the simple nine-fold number, where he is ready to enter into matter; and so that he might not be called the "first Being" or "principle," his process is finished by the final letter **ן Nun**. By these things, this Hebrew word [*Ain*] seems to hint that God, as long as he does not go beyond the simple number, should not be taken for "Being." Next, where he is taken for "Being," there we see the **י Jod** included and allowed between the **ה He** and the **ו Vau**—that is, between matter and form, or the moist spirit and fire—both of which the *Jod* itself nourishes, as it were. And thus we see how God is in nature, while yet he is not nature itself. We see also how he is called "Being"; namely, insofar as being proceeds into existence...

...in that place; *This Wisdom is more beautiful than the Sun, and above every arrangement of the stars: compared to light, she is found to be prior! Therefore, this divine light, full of the Spirit and power of **Jehovah**, is the author of harmony, peace, and health. And for this reason, insofar as it regards the generation of things, it is defined by the **Physicists** <note>In this context, "Physicists" refers to natural philosophers or scientists of the 17th century.</note> as *the bond of the elements and the mixing power*; which effects the mixtures of elements in every thing of this sublunary world, and imprints the form appropriate to its species, through which that thing is distinguished and separated from any other thing. Nor is this divine power or "act" in nature of any one color, yet it is a participant in and the creator of all colors; it has no weight or quality, and yet it is the fertile mother of every quality. And this is why the **Pagan Physicists** themselves did not hesitate to assert that God is Nature, and *Nature is God*: so that even all of them concluded by unanimous consent that this very nature is an invisible light or fire, from which all things are born. But in quality, this light differs greatly from the usual laws of nature; for it is neither hot, nor cold, nor moist, nor dry, nor masculine, nor feminine; but by reason of its great perfection, it participates in each of the four natural qualities, because without it there would be no "complexion" <note>In ancient medicine, a "complexion" is the specific balance of the four humors/qualities in a body.</note> in any compound. For the natural qualities of the elements fight against each other and are opposites: this discord and antipathy of the elements she reduces into peace and symphony; so much so, that a union and joining in a composition could not happen, unless there were this honorable "Medium," born from an immortal and eternal lineage; whose role is to penetrate confusedly through all elements, since it participates with each of the said natures, treating them sweetly and kindly, and thus makes and reconciles peace between enemies.

But, to return to the letter **Vau** [ו], just as **Jod** [י], joined with the first **He** [ה] makes **Jah** [יה]—that is, the divine being, which is God himself, **Jod**, descending through his first emanation from his purely formal kingdom (free from all matter) into the material mass of the world, by which the **He** or the "higher universal Spirit" is cleansed from darkness; so also the same Spirit **He**, placed before it, denotes Him. And in this way the Holy Spirit **Jod**, "brooding over the waters" **He**, so unites **Vau** to **Jod** itself, that **Vau** through **He** becomes **Jah** [יה], which is to say, the very same thing as **Jah**. For, just as **Jod**, signifying unity, when joined in creation with **He** (whose value in Arithmetic is 5), makes 6—which product is unity in the Spirit **He**, by which that spirit exists; so also by the same reasoning **Vau**, whose value is 6, indicates in a hidden way **Jah** [יה] and **He** [ה], that is, five and unity, denoting by this very fact that the **Word**, contained in the middle between the two waters under the symbol **Vau**, is of the same **supersubstantial essence** with **Jod** itself in **He**. From these things it is evident that the **Word**, although it fell into the firmament or the "middle heaven" on the second day after the work of the first day was completed, nevertheless holds equal dominion in the **Empyrean heaven** with **Jod**; since they do not differ in essence, but only in property; namely as a son from his father, or as a ray and emanation of immeasurable light from its source. And in this way the seal of all miracles was completed, by whose characters the world and the creatures of the world were created; namely **YHWH** [יהוה], which is the seal of **Ehieh** <note>The divine name "I AM" from Exodus 3:14.</note> or the first divine numbering; in which **Vau** is of the same essence as **Jod**, and symbolically signifies the same thing. Hence, just as **Jod** was the symbol of the **Tetragrammaton** and the Divine Being outside of matter; so **Jah** [יה] is that very thing; that is, the same as **Jod**; as if **Jod** were placed before and then **He** were placed after, and the spirit **He** joined unity with unity, in this way: **YHU** [יהו]. Thus unity and unity, constituting the number two, through the interposition of the Spirit **He** becomes a Trinity and perfection. And this is why, in the production of every creature in creation through the **Word**, both the speaker and likewise his speech, or the Word **FIAT** or **LET IT BE**, are explained together with the Spirit **He** (the medium and receptacle of the voice) in this manner through **Jod**, beginning and ending in this way: **YHWH** [יהוה], that is, *Let there be Light*: **Yehi Or** [יהי אור]. *Let there be* [FIAT], or *LET THERE BE*, an expansion or firmament, and so on in the others; so that by this reasoning we can clearly see that the universal Spirit **He** is nothing but a double **Jod**; or that the unity of one essence is in the Spirit **He**, without which it cannot be produced into action; similarly that the Word of **Jehovah**, and the impressions of the seal of **Ehieh** itself, will remain in creatures forever, according to that sacred saying; *The Word of the Lord remains forever.* From these things it is explained more clearly than light that, after it was commanded, **LET THERE BE** such a creature, the response was made through the same characters,

SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK I.

...as if from their angel or Great Priest Michael, as if it were said "Amen," <note>Hebrew: *Yehi Ken* (יהי כן), meaning "Let it be so."</note>; And it was done so: where the conclusion is made through the final *Nun* [ן], arguing for the perfection of the matter. > For neither herb nor plaster healed them, but your Word, O Lord, which heals all things; You are the Lord, who has power over life and death, etc.

Indeed, by this very admirable power of yours the Israelites were freed from the bites of serpents in the desert; Elijah, and Elisha his disciple, brought so many astounding cures to completion without medicine; indeed, they even recalled the dead themselves to their former life with only a single breath; and far higher things were done by the power and first emanation of Jehovah himself, or by that Christ now incarnate, to the wonder of all. By these acts, he declared himself to the world publicly, and more clearly and evidently than light itself, to be the true God and the saving Word of eternity. Nor indeed was this done by his humanity, which was subject to death, but by his internal divinity; insofar as from the beginning he was the light, life, and salvation of the world, to whom was given the power of saving, of giving life, of overcoming darkness, of defeating evil spirits, and of overcoming death itself by the sword and strength of the **Tetragrammaton**. This Christ was, before his incarnation, that Word יהוה <note>Original: *Jehovah*</note>, that is, "LET IT BE" [FIAT], or that seal יהוה; which is the symbol of truth, and that most holy wisdom of the living, strong God of hosts from which all things were first made, and then are preserved in their essence through those sweet, honey-flowing, and healthy (though invisible) influences until the very end. Whoever has obtained a plentiful enjoyment of this will most easily reach the peak of happiness and blessedness, which is called the highest: and the Wise Man confirms this in Proverbs 3:
> Blessed is the one who finds Wisdom; for her acquisition or trade is better than the trade of silver, and her fruit is more precious than refined gold or **Carbuncles**; and all your delights cannot be compared to her: Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace: She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her: finally, he who enjoys her is blessed.

Nor indeed, if we consider the following words of the Wise Man, shall we find that this wisdom is anything other than that most holy Word of Jehovah, by which all things were made and created: For he connects these words to the preceding ones:
> Jehovah by wisdom founded the earth: he established the heavens by understanding.

So also says the Psalmist; *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were made, etc.*

From which it follows that this divine Spirit, this power of Jehovah, is his kindness and mercy, emanating from him, by which material things submerged in the most miserable darkness were led back to light and liberty, from potentiality into act, and from nothing into a real Being; which is indeed the greatest sign of mercy. And from this it is that kindness is always attributed to the Son, through whom the first heaven—namely the **Empyrean** <term>Empyrean: The highest part of heaven, believed in ancient cosmology to be filled with pure fire or light and to be the dwelling place of God.</term>—was made from nothing as the clearest and most lucid Spirit; and the angels themselves are made from non-beings into the most polished mirrors in which the idea of the divine majesty is seen. Then the firmament is reduced from nothing into the thinnest and most noble Spirit, the food of life, and the foundational and cornerstones are placed for each of its stars, and among these the divine **Carbuncle** <term>Carbuncle: A legendary gemstone of deep red fire; here, Fludd uses it to describe a concentrated point of divine light that serves as the "seed" or foundation of a star.</term> itself is placed from the center of the Creator’s holy throne through the power and operation of the Word, as if it were the first foundation of the Sun. And hence, because of the nobility and splendor of this foundational stone, the Sun was truly chosen as the tabernacle for the Word.

<margin>Gen. 28.</margin> Did not Jacob say in Genesis 28, after he had placed a stone as his pillow and seen in a dream angels descending and ascending by a ladder?
> Surely Jehovah is in this place, yet I did not know it: How terrible is this place: this is none other than the place of God: this place is even the gate of heaven.

He took therefore that stone, which he had placed under his head, and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil over the top of it, and called the name of the place the house of the strong God: "Then," he said, "this stone which I have raised as a pillar or statue shall be the house of God."

In this same way, therefore, the Sun was created; namely, with the most splendid **Carbuncle** being cast first for its foundation, and with the oil or divine food added, it became the house of God and the principal gate of heaven; for without the divine Word there is no passage from earth to heaven. For just as in the beginning or creation there was a leading of light into darkness through the Word: so also on the last day, there will be a leading back of light from darkness, according to that saying in Wisdom 16:
> You lead down to the gates of hell and lead back; that is, from heaven to earth, and from earth to heaven.

But this will perhaps seem impossible to the foolish—that cornerstones should be the foundations of the stars. To them we answer that, just as in creation there was both the fixed and the volatile, and both earth and heaven, so it is certain that those two materials from which God created heaven and earth were the soft and the hard; in the likeness of which both heaven and earth were created as they are; because one is hard and stony, while the other is soft and spiritual: just as the earth stands in relation to the waters...

From here, therefore, arises the tradition of the Pagans, by which they fashioned Apollo, son of Jove, as the God of physicians, and moreover called him the author of medicine because of the life-giving power of his heat. And the Poets themselves sang of him as the slayer of the terrible Dragon Python <note>In Greek myth, Apollo killed the serpent Python, which the author interprets as the triumph over decay and evil.</note>, both because of his nature being opposed to rot, and also because he is observed to drive away lethal poisons, contagious diseases, and the marks of darkness, and to resist the violences of the Devil by his own faculty. Furthermore, Apollo is also said to contain the force and virtue of all divine measurements. And from this also it is that the power of Apollo was handed down by Speusippus the Platonic to consist of many fires, although he himself exists as one and the same. And although this light is invisible by itself, yet by the grace of bodies created with density and receiving its reflections, it is rendered visible and colored by accident. I would not want you to misunderstand me in this place, or believe that I take the visible sun for the mystical body of Christ itself. Far be it, indeed, that I should thrust such profane things upon you; therefore, know that I have spoken only of the super-celestial and invisible sun. ## CHAPTER VI.

->On the nature of the final letter of the Tetragrammaton itself, and how it<-
->refers to the lowest heaven of the world.<-

The final **He** (ה) of the name Tetragrammaton, which is also the end and boundary of that ineffable name, denotes the last and lowest region of the world; and thus this marvelous name extends itself from the eternal world all the way to the center of the created world. Hence it is said: *God is in all things, and outside all things*: For in the measure of a spherical figure, we see that nothing in it is omitted or left unmeasured, if every radius encircling it is occupied from the circumference even to the center.
<margin>ה</margin> Thus also the power of the Tetragrammaton is in the **Jod** (י) in the eternal world; in the first **He** (ה) is the divine mind; in the
<margin>ו</margin> **Vau** (ו) is the celestial Sun and the nature of the stars; in the last **He** (ה) is the elemental power; from whose center, or the middle
<margin>ה</margin> region of the air, it shines out in this heaven, just as the Sun shines from the center and middle of the ethereal region. And this power of the Tetragrammaton, by the testimony of St. Paul and St. John, is *that life-giving Spirit*, who is called the *Messiah, and the light of the world*, who, as was said above, is the ineffable power of the Tetragrammaton and works in its power. And I am led to this by the word *Mashicha* <note>original: משיחה, meaning "Anointed" or Messiah.</note>; whose letters, if transposed according to the <term>Cabalistic method: A tradition of Jewish mysticism that interprets the hidden meanings of the Hebrew Bible through letter permutations and numerical values.</term>, will be *Yishmacha* <note>original: ישמיחה, a permutation suggesting "he shall cause to rejoice" or "he shall flourish."</note>, that is, the *Messiah; who is also called the Word*, who is God himself, and of the same essence as God; by whom all things were made, and without whom nothing was made, etc. And this eternal power is in the eternal world with the Father and the uncreated Spirit, and works in them and with them; since it goes forth from the center of the Father, and the Spirit from the center of both. Therefore, the Spirit and the Son are in the Father; insofar as He, after their procession from Himself, reflected his heat back into Himself; so that now the Father is in the Son, and the Son in the Father, and both in the same Spirit; and all three are one and the same in essence. They are signified in this world—without emanation—by the letter **Aleph** (א), which denotes unity, simplicity, and a kind of point; but with emanation or irradiation, they are signified by **Jod** (י); which is likened to a line, as the first and simplest progression of divine power from its eternal source, Jod. And then this power is called the Uncreated Mind, or the ray of the one God Jod; and being disposed in the center of the Empyrean heaven, it first illuminates the spirit **He** from that place; and then, by procreating His angelic creatures, He gives them power, and perpetually cherishes them with His essence by His rays;
<margin>”</margin> not otherwise than the Sun is accustomed to nourish, vivify, and illuminate innumerable stars with its rays poured around in the middle heaven or "palace of the Sun." Yet He does nothing without the counsel of His father and source, Jod, to whom He was always obedient, according to that saying of the Wise Man in **Proverbs 8: When he formed the heavens above, when he made firm the fountains of the deep, when he set for the sea its limit, etc. when he established the foundations of the earth, I was Wisdom with him like a foster-child <note>original: "alumnus," also translated as "master builder" or "craftsman."</note>, or composing all things, since I am with him in being brought up, and I was in delights daily, rejoicing and playing before him at all times.**

From which it is clear that the Word or Messiah works in the power of Jod in whatever heaven belongs to its creation and stabilization: that is, he observes the will of the father, and being obedient, he is accustomed to perfect it so precisely and carefully that he cannot depart or err from it by even a hair's breadth; indeed, he performed or dispatched the will of his father both on earth and in the heavens by his wonderful action, both in the creation of the world and in its conservation, and will perform it for eternity. But now, on the third day of creation—that is, the third eruption of light out of darkness—the immediate emanation from **Vau** (which is situated in the middle between the double **He He**, that is, between the spiritual or upper waters and the thick or lower waters) which is called the third emanation, or the third-day light from Jod, with respect to the diversity of the triple medium through which it passed, immersed itself into the darkness of the lowest heaven. (These darknesses are indeed now called **Chaos**, since they contain the elements confused and poorly disposed, and quarreling among themselves in their bowels.) And there, it brought forth into light that **He**, or the dense and thick spirit, which had been destitute of light and form; this was delineated in the idea of the wonderful name Tetragrammaton before the ages and from eternity. For God, the Archetype of the Macrocosm and Microcosm <term>Macrocosm and Microcosm: The "Great World" (the universe) and the "Little World" (the human being), viewed as reflections of one another.</term> and of every creature's disposition, ordered the measure, number, and weight in the ideal world before He actually produced them through His Word. Whence **Wisdom 11: You have ordered and tempered all things in measure, number, and weight.** And this was an extraordinary sign or proof of the created light, or the Word, or the power and might, or the emanation and flow of the almighty Jehovah—a sign of kindness, mercy, salvation, and peace.

...foundation; which clearly descended from the middle heaven or firmament into the crude mass of Chaos, for the purpose of <margin>,,</margin> driving back and dispelling the murky darkness of this region, or the ultimate gloom, and for the sake of establishing eternal peace and concord among enemies who were bringing a horrific and continuous war upon one another.
