It dispels its darkness with its own light, drives away the sicknesses of bodies in this world, restrains the madness of the Devil, overcomes death and destruction, and demonstrates through an infallible pattern and proof what becomes the anchor of all faith, announcing to us the liberation of the soul from darkness and captivity. This, I say, is the essence of divinity, this is the symphony of eternal concord, this is the reconciler of peace, this is the inviolable bond of union. Once the darkness has been scattered to the center and around the center—and fixed and secured in the lowest place with a strong chain—this essence has so arranged every element of this lower heaven by its harmony, that peace and friendship are preserved everywhere through the **lowest Vau** <term>Vau: the sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet (ו), representing the number six and often used by Christian Cabalists to symbolize the "Son" or the connecting link between the divine and the material.</term> in the real world (which refers to the **final Vau** of the ineffable name, which was the idea of the eternal and created world at once, and consequently infinite and ineffable). This, therefore, is that honorable medium, whose nature is so sweet, so uniform, so strong and predominant, so essentially effective, so harmonious and symphonic, that whenever it is joined to any thing, it immediately converts that thing into its own composition, changes it as if into its own nature, and renders everything it touches with its spirit obedient to itself. And this Holy Spirit, or God-like virtue, is that which—as if by a certain magical whisper—is accustomed to make all created spirits obedient to itself immediately, even in the blink of an eye, according to that saying of Hermes Trismegistus in the *Emerald Tablet*:

> Thus you shall have the glory of the whole world, and all obscurity shall flee from you; This is the <margin>,,</margin> strong strength of all strength; because it will overcome every subtle thing, and penetrate every solid thing; Thus the world was <margin>,,</margin> created. <note>original: "Sic habebis gloriam totius mundi..." This is a famous alchemical text attributed to Hermes Trismegistus.</note>

This, therefore, is 그 most powerful bond, by which the elements, established in their places by God the **Jod** <term>Jod: the first letter of the Tetragrammaton (י), associated with the Father and the primordial point of creation.</term>—that is, in the region proper to each element—are suspended in the **lowest Vau** in such a way that <margin>,,</margin> concord and peace are maintained among all things! For this reason, He placed the air between fire and water, so that it might be a mediator to both: namely, that by agreeing with water in its moisture, it might float upon it; and by being contiguous to fire, it might soothe and cherish it with its warm moisture. Thus, in this way, it interposes itself between the cold nature of water on one side, and the hot nature of fire on the other, so that one cannot contend with the other through contrary motion and opposing effort. Similarly, the element of water performs a like office and is a mediator of peace between the earth and the air, so that the moisture of the air cannot bring violence to the dryness of the earth. In order that this moderation might be obtained more easily and better, water was made such that it agrees with the air in its moisture; indeed, its kinship or relationship with the air is so great that, through the mediation of heat, it may even be converted into air through refinement. On the opposite side, it has a similar familiarity and kinship with the earth because of its coldness. The bond of all these things in such concord is the virtue of the **Tetragrammaton** <term>Tetragrammaton: the four-letter Hebrew name of God, Y-H-V-H.</term>, interceding first between fire and the ether, then between air and fire, then between air and water, and finally between water and earth; with all of which it also mixes itself in common to produce their essential forms. Hence God is said to be in all things, and all things in Him, and through Him, according to that passage in Job 28:

> Who made a weight for the winds, and weighed the waters by measure; when He set a law for the rains, and a path for the sounding storms; then He saw wisdom, and declared it, and prepared it, and pointed it out to man, and said: Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom itself, etc.

This **Vau** is that formal medium, ruling in the middle heaven or firmament, and reigning in it—as if in a place destined for the Second Person—and holding the scepter. By its mediation and kindness, the supreme spiritual heaven descends into the **corporeal Vau**; or heaven descends into the earth, or the soul into the body through the mediation of the spirit hidden in the **Vau**. Whence it became hidden by the unity of the Word—that is, by the splendor of the Sun, both visible and invisible, not otherwise than the Sun is accustomed to obscure the light of the other stars—manifested by the mediator between **He** (ה) and **Vau** (ו) in the ineffable name. That is, **He** (ה) arithmetically denoting five, and unity making the sixth number, signified under the hieroglyphic **Vau** (ו)—which symbolically designates the firmament—is said by its virtue to separate the lower waters from the higher waters. And <margin>,,</margin> yet, just as the Son in sacred properties cannot exist without the Father, nor the Holy Spirit without both, <margin>,,</margin> so also the firmament cannot exist without the help of the essence of the Empyrean heaven <note>The Empyrean is the highest heaven, the dwelling place of God and pure light.</note>, from which it received a <margin>,,</margin> created soul; nor can the elementary heaven exist without the influence proceeding from both. And from this it follows that, <margin>,,</margin> although the divine unity signified by the **Vau** separated the higher waters from the lowest so that there would be no confusion between spiritual and gross waters, it is nevertheless a mediator through whom the lower waters or gross spirits receive grace, kindness, and life from heaven, attributed to the Father, into which the **Jod** abundantly pours supersubstantial rays from His eternal throne for the quickening and life of both animal and vegetable creatures—first through creation, and then for the continuation and succession of life through generation. From these things it is clear that God, out of His fullness as a fountain of light, through the first sphere of moisture, pours life, form, and a portion of His essence-making light into the second; which at last, nourished by the benefit of the same, is poured further into the third through the power of the Word (insofar as it is right from the remainder) for the consistency of the lower creatures. where the third and lowest sphere of equality is also placed; for there, it is accustomed to wage war with its fiery darts and arrows against the dark waters that besiege it on all sides; these waters are finally scattered by its fiery splendor, so that even the immense mounds and mountains ascending toward the heaven are torn apart by its power, and both the darkness and the thick waters—friends of the darkness—are driven toward the center along with the prince of darkness himself in that strife. Hence the unity of the letter <term>He</term> <note>The second and fourth letter of the Name of God, often associated with the feminine or "receiving" aspect of creation.</note> itself, but joined with the superior <term>He</term>, makes 10. For the letter <term>Mem</term> <note>The OCR likely misread a symbol here; in this context, the author is comparing the shape of the letter He or the concept of the "cipher" to the number zero.</note> is assimilated to He: For, just as the 0 or cipher is nothing by itself, but exists as if in potential toward a number; so also <term>He</term> by itself is overwhelmed by darkness and is nothing. Hence it is said that *God created all things from nothing*, <note>original: "Deus creaverit omnia ex nihilo"</note> that is, from that which does not exist in actuality. But if either the unity is placed before the cipher, or some digit derived from unity is attached to it, it will be a number in actuality: so also, if essence or the <term>Jod</term> <note>The first letter of the Name of God, representing the "point" of creation or the number 10.</note> itself is added to the <term>He</term> overwhelmed by darkness, it produces <term>Jah</term>, <note>The shortened form of God's name (Psalm 68:4), consisting of Jod and He.</note> which is the metaphysical and supreme Being. Similarly in the middle heaven, <term>He</term>, which is hidden and understood within <term>Vau</term> <note>The third letter of the Name, often acting as a bridge or "hook" between the upper and lower worlds.</note>, connected with the manifest superior <term>He</term>, because of the unity by which <term>Jod</term> or <term>Vau</term> exceeds <term>He</term>, denotes the number one hundred, expressed thus as <term>קו</term> <note>Koph and Vau. In Gematria (Hebrew numerology), Koph equals 100.</note>, that is, <term>ק</term>, which is 100. Where unity, or the number ten, immersing itself into the first <term>He</term> and finding itself again in the second <term>He</term>, in the <term>Vau</term> doubling, it multiplies the measure of the spirit in the firmament as many times as it is multiplied in the spirit of the world, and consequently the different spirits or heavens are numbered. Hence 10 multiplied by itself produces the number one hundred; and, since there is the second repetition of unity there, namely in the middle heaven, it denotes the second person, and consequently the character of a double spirit, namely 0 0 or <term>הה</term> (He-He) manifestly preceding, and it is noted hidden in the <term>Vau</term>, and the supernal unity, found in an abstruse manner in the <term>Vau</term>, is placed before the 0 0. Thus 100, or symbolically <term>קו</term>. Hence, as the heaven of <term>Jod</term> is linear, so the heaven of <term>He</term> is superficial or square; insofar as 100 would be the square of the number ten. Finally, <term>Jod</term> is designated and found a third time in the last <term>He</term>; namely, in the first <term>Jod</term> for the first time, and in the last <term>He</term> for the third time, certainly in those manifest things, and in the second place in the <term>He</term> hidden and contained within the <term>Vau</term>, in this manner 1000, or <term>הההי</term>: And thus it is declared that God is *Alpha* and *Omega*; <note>The first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, symbolizing the beginning and the end.</note> by Himself, clearly, in the Archetypal world, insofar as He is <term>Aleph</term>, or unity, which is the beginning of the digits, and <term>Jod</term>, or the number ten, which is their end. Thus we see that the end of the formal, triple, and ideal world without end, namely <term>Jod</term>, is the principle of the real world; which is also called the "lesser bright Aleph."

Similarly in the material world we see that God is also the Alpha and Omega: For <term>Jod</term>, which is the source and principle of the created world, is called the "bright Aleph" by the Kabbalists; whose end is also the "Great Aleph" <term>א</term>, denoting the number one thousand, beyond whose denomination there is no progress: so that in the eternal and uncreated world the "dark Aleph" <term>א</term> (the first origin of unities) is the Alpha: and <term>Jod</term>, which is the bright <term>י</term>, is its Omega. Thus the bright <term>י</term> is the Alpha in the created and composite world; but the Great <term>א</term> is its Omega: From which it clearly appears that <term>א</term> or unity is everything that exists, since it includes all things; it numbers all things by unities; it measures all things by the name of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name YHWH.</note>, which it includes, and of which it exists as a Hieroglyphic, and by the <term>Vau</term>, which is the middle of the scale or balance; consisting in equilibrium, or the perpendicular stylus, whose equally distant weights, the first <term>He</term> and the later <term>He</term> of the ineffable name, clang with a stupendous sound in the composite world and flash with inexplicable light. Therefore, the first person, <term>Jod</term>, first depicted His will, mediating through the divine Word, in the vast book of darkness, as a line in the worldly <term>He</term>, with the living characters of numbers or letters of the first composition, or with fiery and linear figures; and the first heaven was made, and there were produced, according to the doctrine of the Kabbalists, the three mothers of the world, namely <term>א</term> Aleph, <term>מ</term> Mem, and <term>ש</term> Shin, that is, the principle or firmness, assimilated to earth or unity, Water and Fire; <note>In traditional Kabbalah, Aleph is Air, Mem is Water, and Shin is Fire. The author here associates Aleph with Earth or a foundational Unity.</note> To which the first three hierarchies of Angels manifestly respond; just as the regions of the last three <term>He</term>s are most aptly referred to them; namely the earth, ending in the <margin>ה</margin> number one thousand, whose symbol is the Great <term>א</term>; the sphere of humidity, comprising both the gross spirit, namely water, and the subtle spirit whose symbol is <term>מ</term> Mem, and the element of fire, whose character and stigma is <term>ש</term> Shin, emitting its rays upward like fire: Similarly in the firmament <term>ש</term> Shin acts with its light, <term>מ</term> Mem with the solidity of the glowing fires, and <term>א</term> Aleph with the ethereal spirit, or the vehicle of the light of <term>ש</term> Shin itself.

->### ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.<-

...referring to the seven Planets; namely, **Beth** <note>The Hebrew letter ב (B).</note> is referred to the Sun, which letter is indeed a symbol of the Son and the second person of the Trinity, proceeding immediately from **Aleph** <note>The Hebrew letter א (A), representing the Father or the Unity.</note>; hence **Ab** <note>אב, the Hebrew word for "Father."</note> is read as father or root, and it is necessary by relation that the father includes the son. Whence also **Ba** <note>בא</note> among the Chaldeans <note>Ancient inhabitants of Mesopotamia, often cited by Renaissance authors as masters of ancient wisdom and astrology.</note> signifies to produce the first fruit. Therefore, the spirit is vast and the strength is greatest, insofar as it flowed not only from **Aleph**—that is, from God—through an immediate process and emanation, but also contains within itself a double Spirit, just like **Gimel, Daleth, Caph, Phij, Resh,** and **Thau** <note>The letters ג, ד, כ, פ, ר, and ת.</note>; which are referred to Venus, Mercury, the Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars.

From these things it is clear that there is a double portion of this Spirit **He** <note>ה</note> in the heaven. Hence these letters, which are symbols of the Planets, are called "double" <note>In Hebrew grammar, these seven letters (Begadkephat) have two pronunciations, which mystical philosophers linked to the dual nature of the planets.</note> and are always pronounced with an aspiration; from which it is argued that they possess within themselves the superior virtues of **He**, or the Empyrean <note>The highest, most spiritual part of the heavens, composed of pure light or fire.</note> heaven. And this is the reason, as it seems to me, that an angelic Intelligence is said to preside over each Planet; according to whose disposition that Planet moves and acts, both upon the firmament itself and upon the elemental kingdom. Thus, by the power of **Vau** <note>ו, the third letter of the Divine Name.</note> in the ineffable name, the virtues of the superior **He** are infused into the inferior **He**. From this we can certainly gather how glorious is the **Vau**-connection between the two **He** letters between which it is placed; for by it, superior things communicate with inferior ones, and in turn, the inferior things, by embracing the superior, rejoice in them and are given life. This, I say, is the link between the sublime soul and the lowest body; and this again is that powerful and noble bond by which the elements are reduced into a composition and peacefully preserved within it. Indeed, if this bond should fail in any part of the composition, a most certain disease and imbalance follows; since the contrary elements in the composition, through the defect of this most powerful virtue, immediately begin to quarrel and contend with one another, and to rebel within the human Economy <note>The organized system or "management" of the human body.</note>. But if this primordial virtue should fail entirely, inevitable death follows; so much so that if this ethereal nature were to neglect or look away from the lower things, and not cherish them daily, all things would immediately grow sick or languish, and would straightway be reduced to nothing by a swift or sudden death.

But perhaps some scrupulous person will say: if this virtue is an emanation of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>original: "Tetragrammati"; the four-letter name of God (YHWH).</note> itself, why can it not perform the same for the lower things from its own middle heaven, without Empyrean influences gliding down from above, or without the help of intelligences sent from the superior **He** into the region of **Vau**? Since the virtue of both the Empyrean heaven and the firmament is the same essential emanation of light. To which objection we respond that, while the emanation of one and the other is of the same essence—no less than the properties of the Holy Trinity are of the same fountain, nature, and origin—yet when we speak of those emanations or the outflow of divine virtue in Physical creation (that is, in the mixing of divinely infused light), we are not dealing with the nature of uncreated and simply formal light, but with the created spirit in which that light predominates, and which it moves and governs in every action, whether it be metaphysical or physical. And hence it happens that, according to the greater or lesser presence or measure of this light, the spirit is accustomed to be thinner or thicker; since the act of that simple virtue is always to purify the spirits and to remove their rebellious thickness or density. And this is why there are diverse spirits in the world, which produce various effects according to their diversity. This, therefore, is the reason why, although there is unity in the divine outflow or the virtue of the Tetragrammaton, a multitude is nevertheless said to exist in the world due to the variation of matter. Hence the Empyrean spirit is said to be worthier than the Ethereal, and this latter again more noble than the elemental; yet the uncreated light and virtue, by which those spirits are what they are found to be in the said regions of the world, is always the same, and not in the least subject to changes and alterations; since wisdom is *a Holy Spirit of intelligence, unique, simple, subtle, undefiled, harmless or free from passion, stable, certain, having all power;* <note>original: "Spiritus intelligentia Sanctus, unicus, simplex, subtilis, incoinquinatus, innoxius seu passionis expers, stabilis, certus, omnem habens virtutem"</note> and this is an emanation or a certain flow of the brightness of the Almighty, into which nothing defiled enters, as is copiously taught in *Wisdom 7.* <note>Referencing the Book of the Wisdom of Solomon, Chapter 7, in the Apocrypha/Deuterocanon.</note>

But truly, that this unique and invariable virtue or outflow of God, **Jod** <note>י, the first letter of the Divine Name, representing the point of origin.</note>, is named variously and in different ways with its vehicle in diverse spirits, this happens because of the disposition of the spirits themselves in which it swims, and not in respect to its own nature; for it is always the same and invariable, even as God Himself in a fluctuating moist nature. And hence it is that, when we called **Vau** the bond and connection between the two **He** letters, we did not mean the simple and holy emanation from **Jod** by itself and in its absolute essence alone, but the ethereal spirit itself, which is such as it is said to be because of the formal action of the holy virtue within it. For the virtue of the Tetragrammaton acts as if it were a kind of glue or paste, by which the tender nature of the Empyrean heaven, or the intellectual spirit itself, is joined with the elemental nature and the composite, rough, crude, and dense body.

So also, for example, we see that wax or glue is not accustomed to bind paper or a similar thing together unless it is first prepared by heat. And 그 intermediate glue is called the <term>Quintessence</term> <note>original: "Quinta Essentia"; literally the "fifth element," a pure, celestial substance that permeates the universe.</note>—that is, the fifth element, or the intermediate spirit, the vehicle of light or uncreated virtue, enclosing the mystery of the vital soul. This spirit is such a glue and such a medium, whose matter is created; but its form and act, considered simply in and by itself, is the uncreated virtue and ray of **Jod** itself. But the spirit itself, together with its divine soul, is called a created and physical thing; for, if it were called uncreated, we would be lying, insofar as the spirit is created.

# SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK I.

But even if it were said to be absolutely created, we would likewise stray from the truth; because the power giving it form and bringing it from nothingness into action is uncreated. However, insofar as the Spirit itself is given a name—whether it is called the Empyrean Spirit <note>The highest, most refined heaven of pure light and fire.</note>, or the ethereal spirit, or the ether, or the intellect, or reason, or air, or water, etc.—to that extent, it is a creature, because the naming occurs on the side of matter. And this very thing is perceived through the nature of the letter **Vav** <note>ו</note>; which, since in an arithmetical respect it is composed of five and one, it follows that **He** <note>ה, which equals 5</note> and **Yod** <note>י, here likely signifying the unit or the point of origin</note> equal that number. From these, the composition of this heaven is made manifest, consisting namely of light—or the emanation of the radiant **Aleph** <note>א</note>, which is God—and the spirit **He**. Hence, **Vav** is symbolically accepted for the firmament; and the firmament stands for the ethereal spirit, that is, the fiery air, which consists of the radiant **Aleph** and **He**. These are the same as the letter **Shin** <note>ש</note>, the hieroglyphic of the fiery spirit itself. This ether is the same as the quintessence <note>The "fifth element" that transcends the four terrestrial elements</note>; and the quintessence is the same as the vital soul; and the vital soul is the same as the receptacle of the mind in the Empyrean or intellectual spirit; and finally, it is the bond, the knot, and the coupling between the Empyrean spirit and the gross spirit, both of simple things (namely in the elements themselves) and of composite things (as in bodies or things made of elements). And this is the reason why **Vav** is so often used by the Hebrews as a copulative conjunction (meaning "AND"); because it indicates that in natural things, it must couple two extremes. This is even more so because in the great name of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, the **Vav** is placed between the two **He**s; by which they seem to be joined together as if by the conjunction "And." And from this it is said *that no one can know the father except through the son;* <note>original Latin: "quod nemo patrem cognoscere possit nisi per filium," referencing Matthew 11:27</note> Wherefore also the Word is called the *Mediator between man and God*, and between the superior spirit (the spiritual or linear heaven) and the inferior spirit (the elemental and corporeal heaven). For, just as there is no progression from a line to a solid body except through a surface, nor from a root to a cube except through a square, and vice-versa; so also there is no passage from the Empyrean heaven to the elemental heaven except through the firmament; just as there is no transition from unity to the number three, except through the interposition of the number two, which joins the two extremes by the bond of justice.

Hence, the fabric of the world is made to represent the properties of the Trinity. For unless its composition were in a number that distinguishes the highest from the lowest, the subtle from the thick, the light from the dark, and good from evil, it could have no measure or weight. And if the number of its different parts were not three (the ternary), the entire workmanship would be imperfect. In the number two (the binary) there is indeed a beginning and an end, but no middle, because it lacks a conclusion; or there is no conclusion because it lacks a middle. Therefore, in the arrangement of the world, the world would be imperfect through that number. Similarly, if the world were one (unity), then there would be only the principle of the world and creatures; and consequently, no "thing begun" would exist, but all would be one single principle. In this way, the four elements would not be created, but only one. Therefore, it was necessary that the world be constituted from a number that is not imperfect. If it had happened otherwise, the world—that most excellent and beautiful creature of Jehovah—would be imperfect; which would surely be most profane to say or believe. From this it follows that the world is the most noble, most perfect, and most consummate creature, fashioned after the pattern of the Trinity; whose number is three, in which there is a beginning, a middle, and an end. For, even in the ineffable name of the most holy essence of the individual Trinity, the number is found: namely **Yod** <note>י</note> referred to the Father, **He** <note>ה</note> to the Son, and **He** <note>ה</note> to the Holy Spirit. For although there is a double **He** there, yet the first is the conjunction of the second person with the first, **Yod**, and the last is again the bond and gluing together of the **He** after the **Vav** with the **Yod**; so that from the circular letters of the wonderful Tetragrammaton, there occurs a circulation of divine properties in the Archetypal world <note>The world of divine ideas or the "blueprint" of creation</note>. For, as in the drawing of a circle three boundaries are observed—namely the starting point, the middle, and the end; which end in a circle is always the same as the beginning, so that all boundaries become unity—so also it is in the production of the persons of the most holy Trinity. And to this matter, Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with ancient wisdom and alchemy</note> seems to agree in very few words: *The Monad generates a monad, and reflects its own heat back into itself,* <note>original Latin: "Monas generat monadem, & in se ipsam reflectit ardorem suum"</note> as if he were saying: God as Unity spoke through the spirit; through which spirit the Word emanating from His mouth is coupled to Him, and again that Word through the same spirit is brought back into the point of His unity, so that three distinct persons are nothing but unity in essence. But God did this when He first thought about fabricating the world; that is, He first sketched its image in Himself, namely in the ineffable name; according to whose image the entire world was exactly created. Whence it is also said to be *made in the image of God*. So also the Prophet David boasted that he had received the description of the temple from the hand of Jehovah; which is itself said to contain the mystery of the created world.

From these things, therefore, we see that the fabric of the universal world is contained in the miraculous name of the Tetragrammaton; in which the image of the ideal or Archetypal world is symbolically explained, after whose pattern the created world is presented. For, as in the ineffable name **Yod** precedes **He**: so in the creation of the world, the emanation from *Ehieh* <note>The Divine Name "I AM" (אהיה)</note>, which is the Word with the spirit, discovered and stripped of darkness, was the first portion of the spirit. And it is said: *The Spirit of the Lord (which always accompanies the Word) was carried over the waters,* <note>Genesis 1:2</note> that is, over the superior spirits already then revealed and shaped by the light of the spirit through the Word, and created by that shaping. We do not mean, however, that this spirit was the first **He** of the name Tetragrammaton, which was uncreated, and the symbol of the Holy Spirit, through which the first and second person (that is, **Yod** and **Vav**) are joined to each other like glu-

## CHAPTER I.

->*Concerning the primordial cause of health; the many forms of well-being; and that every good, both bodily and spiritual, comes to us from Jah, by means of the Word; Concerning the three principles of health which share one essence; which is the Tetragrammaton itself acting through its own wisdom.*<-

<image-desc>Ornate woodcut drop cap "P" decorated with intertwining vine and leaf patterns.</image-desc>

Since the material and created world has been produced in the manner previously described, according to the pattern of the **Archetypal** <note>The "Archetype" is the original divine blueprint or the mind of God containing the forms of all things.</note> and uncreated formal world, we now judge that we must first investigate with diligent insight how **good**, and then afterwards by what means its opposite, **evil**, entered into the world; for from good, all that which is good is accustomed to proceed. Among all things, **Salvation**, **health**, and the **happiness of life** hold the highest place. Since, therefore, God **Jah** <note>original: "Jah"; a sacred Hebrew name for God, representing the divine essence or the first emanation of light.</note>—that is, the first emanation of God into the letter **He** <note>The Hebrew letter ה (He), often associated in Kabbalah with the divine breath or the Spirit.</note> or the **Empyrean Spirit** <term>Empyrean Spirit: The highest, most refined spiritual substance, associated with the celestial fire of the highest heaven.</term>—is kindness, life, and the very being of every life and creature, we conclude that without a doubt this emanation, mixing itself with the liquid of life, is the author of both spiritual and bodily life. It is the preserver of life in health, and the restorer of health to its former state when it has slipped or fallen away into a "bad harmony" <note>An imbalance of the bodily or spiritual humors.</note>. Indeed, we can very easily prove this in many places from the Holy Scriptures through collected citations.

And yet, if we look into the general nature of health or well-being with the sharpest eyes, we shall immediately perceive with the greatest wonder that three species are subject to it, corresponding to the dispositions of the three spirits of the world. The first of these is **salvation** or **redemption**, which pertains to the soul and body together—or rather to the whole man, as both the life and the tabernacle <note>A metaphor for the physical body as a temporary dwelling for the soul.</note> of life together. This redemption is to be expected in the second life through faith. The second species is properly called **health** <note>original: "salus"</note> or **well-being** <note>original: "valetudo"</note>, which pertains either to the internal disposition of the soul alone, or to the healthy and good temperament of the body alone, along with the good state and condition of both joined together, which ought to occur in this life. The third species is the **liberation** of the whole man from external tribulations. The cause of all these species is the kindness and mercy of **Jah** himself.

This specific name of God <note>The name "Jah".</note> implies kindness, insofar as He is a fire of total purity in an obedient, sweet, and soft spirit. God acts through the flexibility and humility of such a spirit according to His own proper and eternal goodness. On the other hand, in a hard, dense, and rebellious spirit which partakes of darkness, He is said to act harshly and through His **wrath**. And this is the reason why it is said that the eyes of mortals cannot behold God in His own nature; for before His face, mountains and stones...

### CONCERNING SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.

...things melt and dissolve together; and a foul, muddy, dark, and hard body is changed in the blink of an eye at the sight of it. Do we not see that within its very scabbard, the iron of a sword is shattered or consumed by the force of lightning because of its rebellious nature, while the scabbard remains unharmed, as its material is obedient to the impressions of the lightning and is not so rebellious?

How much more, then, will the inexplicable and almighty face of Jehovah work upon those things that are dense and partakers of darkness?

Furthermore, He also frequently hardens the spirit or heart of men, so that He may act more vehemently against them with His own spirit.

Therefore, the **Jod** <note>original: "Jod" or "Yod" (י); the first letter of the Divine Name יהוה, representing the primary spark of creation or the Father.</note> in **Jehovah** <note>original: "יהוה" (YHWH); the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God.</note> is the same as **Jah** <note>original: "יה" (YH); a shortened form of the divine name.</note>; which is a symbol of mercy and kindness, insofar as it exists in an obedient, sweet, and humble spirit. For we see that the same fire varies its effects according to the nature of the medium in which it exists.

Yet fire never changes its own action; rather, the variety of the spirit or matter upon which it acts is the cause of the variety of its effects. Indeed, we are taught by experience that the same heat or the same solar light thins the waters, warms the air, drives moisture upward, harms one temperament, but is a comfort to another; likewise, it brings a headache to some and afflicts them with diseases, while from others it dispels and drives them away. So also, fire enclosed in a cloud brings forth thunder and is clearly visible through the thin air; but when spread out, it rests and is rendered invisible. The same fire, touching some body—even towers and the sturdiest trees—overturns them with wonderful violence, and yet it is one and the same fire. But its object is diverse; and therefore, according to the diversity of its object, it produces diverse effects: namely, harsh ones in the rebellious, and sweet ones in the humble.

And hence it is that God is accustomed to have mercy on those whose spirits are contrite, according to that in *Psalm 33:18: The eyes of Jehovah look toward those who fear Him, and He will rescue their soul from death, etc.* Similarly, *Proverbs 22:4: The rewards of gentleness, humility, and the reverence or fear of Jehovah are riches, glory, and life.*

But these words also denote the obedience and submission of the Spirit, *Proverbs 28:13: He who confesses and forsakes his transgressions shall find mercy.* From this it is clear that God acts in the spirit of a man according to what that man is himself: harshly, I say, in the hard and rebellious; but sweetly and with mercy in the humble and those softened by contrition. For the more a spirit approaches the nature of **Jah** <note>original: "יה" (YH).</note> in **Jehovah** <note>original: "יהוה" (YHWH).</note>, or the angelic spirit, the more kindly is the **Jod** <note>original: "י" (the letter Yod).</note> found within it. And in the name **Jehovah**, the further the letter **Yod** is distant across the three stations, the further the nature of the Spirit is said to be removed from the obedience of the **Jod**, the source of all light and health.

Therefore, the more the human spirit—through the steps of ascent from the final **H** of **Jehovah**—approaches the spirit of **Jod**, the more benevolent it will always find **Jah** to be. And this is the very thing that our Savior taught and preached in *Matthew 5:3: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven; Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth.* Such also are those who are kind in spirit, whence it is said: *Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy; Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God, etc.*

We could bring forward infinite examples of this matter from the sacred scriptures; but it would be too long to introduce them in this place. From these things, therefore, it is clear how the seat of God's kindness is said to be in the heavens, which nevertheless is accustomed to flow abundantly from its source onto the earth. Whence *Psalm 33:5: The earth is full of mercy and kindness.* Indeed, some trace of this super-celestial kindness is found everywhere throughout the world, because it is said in *Wisdom 1:7 that the holy spirit of wisdom fills the world.*

From this, therefore, one may perceive that **Jah** is the source of all divine kindness; which kindness indeed dwells in the holy spirit of wisdom, which is the **Word of Jah**, existing as the redeemer and Savior of the whole man, inasmuch as without Him, man cannot arise and emerge from the abyss of sin and darkness. And although three principles of life and salvation are enumerated, nevertheless these three are of one and indivisible essence; which is indeed distinguished into three with respect to a triple office which they hold in the fabric of the world. Hence, regarding the ordering and the first emanation into the world, this essence is called the **Father**, as if the first ordainer, speaker, and illuminator. Regarding the relationship of execution and the act of emanation, that same essence is called the **Son**, as if the executor of the ordainer, the Word of the speaker, and the light of the illumination, by whose power the heavens were strengthened and all things were made. But if we look at the effect of the acts of the ordainer and the executor, this same essence is called the **Holy Spirit**, from whom the virtues of created things proceed.

We say, therefore, that three principles of salvation and health are recounted in the sacred scriptures: namely, **Jod**, or God the Father; the **Light of the World**, or the Son or the Word; and the **bright spirit** proceeding from both. These three are nothing but one in essence, though they differ in property, as has been said. Whence, even in the world, different "stations" are attributed to them, most fitting to their operations. For **Jod the Father** distributes life and being to the higher realm, or the Empyrean heaven, and to the angels themselves through the **Word** (which is His power, as the Son), by means of the Spirit. And the **Light of the World**, or the power of **Jod** Himself, in the virtue of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter divine name YHWH.</note> (as in the power of the Father, with the Spirit intervening), kindly bestows life upon the firmament through the **Vau** <note>original: "ו" (V); the third letter of the Divine Name, often associated with the connection between heaven and earth.</note> designated in that great name, and upon the stars arranged within it, and He perpetually reaches out and extends His hand to preserve their lives in that same state of health. But the **Holy Spirit**, proceeding from both through the Word, with **Jod** ordering, confers life upon the lowest heaven—namely, form to the elements and to the three species of things composed of elements: the **Animal**, **Vegetable**, and **Mineral**. And through Him, by means of the Word to which He belongs, the life and health of every species is always preserved to remain forever. And these three species of lives, constituting the first three days of creation by the triple emission of light from the darkness, are referred to the different properties of the most holy Trinity.

But, since all these properties are nothing but the unique essence of the one God, we therefore call Jehovah the general source of all health. He contains within Himself, and in His ineffable essence, the three aforementioned properties of the Deity: for God, His power, and the Spirit of both are one God, in no different a way than the Sun, the light of the Sun, and its heat are called a single Sun. This is because God can no more be called God without His power and His Holy Spirit, than the Sun, if deprived of its light and heat, could henceforth deserve to be called the Sun. Hence Moses said: *Jehovah your God is your life, and the length of your days. Deuteronomy 30.* And Solomon: *God has given life and the number of days. Ecclesiastes 5:17.* <note>original: "Eccles. 5. 17."</note> Yet these properties are also attributed to the world because of the various operations of the rays or light flowing from **Jod** <note>The letter 'Jod' or 'Yod' (י) represents the first point of divine creation.</note>, arising from the different resistance of different matter. We say, therefore, that God is the general principle of life and health.

<margin>"</margin>
*We also say with Saint John, that the Word was with God, and the Word was God, and that Word was in the beginning with God, and that all things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made that was made.* From this it is clear that this was that Wisdom of which the Wise Man <note>Refers to Solomon or the author of Proverbs.</note> says in *Proverbs 3*, *that Jehovah founded the earth by it, established the heavens, and broke open the abyss, etc.* But let us proceed further with the words of Saint John: *In Him was life, and the life was the light of men, and the light shines in the darkness; but the darkness did not comprehend it, etc.* This Word, therefore, is the light of the world, or 그 Wisdom, *which Jehovah possessed at the beginning of His way, before His works, before that time; she who was with Him like a master workman arranging all things. Proverbs 8.* Or, as John intends, the *Word, which was in the beginning with God, this was that unique and simple Spirit of Wisdom; whom the Sage in Wisdom 7 called a breath of the power and strength of God, and a certain pure emanation, or a flow of the clarity of the Almighty God, or the brightness and splendor of eternal light, or a spotless mirror of the majesty of God, and an image of His goodness, which is more beautiful than the Sun, and above every arrangement of the stars; compared to light, she is found to be prior.* This, I say, is 그 light, the fountain of life, and all the lives of things are said to flow from it. Hence it is said, *that the word of God is like a refined fire, which is a shield to those who receive it. Proverbs 30.* That is, it preserves the life and health of those who place themselves under the shadow of its wings, according to that passage in *Psalm 35: You preserve both men and beasts, O Jehovah; how precious is your kindness and mercy; then the sons of men betake themselves to the shadow of your wings, etc.* This wisdom, therefore, is the light of men; and that light is the life of things. Therefore life, being, and light come from the Word or Messiah, who is the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, יהוה (YHWH).</note>, insofar as in Him and through Him all things that exist were made, and without Him nothing, as John testifies. This light, I say, is that life-giving tree situated in the midst of paradise (*Genesis 3:24*), of which the Wise Man says in *Proverbs 3, that it is a tree of life to those who take hold of it.* In this wisdom, therefore, we Christians believe with certain and infallible faith that we are to be saved in soul and body through a complete resurrection, and that through death we shall enjoy that fruitful and eternal life, subject to no disturbances. We believe it was necessary that this wisdom of the Deity, or the Word, should humble itself in the spirit of **Jah** <note>A shortened form of the divine name, often associated with divine presence.</note> and take on human flesh, so that having finally become man (the fruitful Adam), and after reporting victory over death and the Devil, He might by His righteousness abolish the sins of the first Adam, wipe away the lethal stain of the human race, and by His life-giving spirit bring it about,

<margin>"</margin>
*that that which is sown in corruption and dishonor may rise in glory, and that that which is natural and mortal may become supernatural and immortal,* and even so that what was previously dark and corporeal may be made luminous and purely spiritual by the power of that divine man. Moreover, even the Pagans themselves <note>original: "Ethnici"</note> firmly established and believed that such a man would be exalted by a God-like spirit far beyond and above human reason, and that he would be from the lineage of the Gods—one who would exist as the true **Savior** <note>original: "$\sigma\omega\tau\dot{\eta}\rho$" (sōtēr)</note> or creator of the human race. However, while various thinkers felt differently about his person, they wrote with hesitation and uncertainty, as will appear in what follows.

# ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.

By the ancients, this was called Jubilation, the victory and triumph of Apollo, which is named the **Pæan** <note>A 'Pæan' was originally a hymn of thanksgiving or a title for Apollo as a healer.</note>. For this reason, Socrates offered that famous cock in sacrifice to him, as if to Asclepius—that is, to Apollo, the first and incorporeal Sun, the dispenser of eternal life—so that he might return the soul of one dying peacefully with a jubilant shout and a Pæan. For Pæan denotes a brief cessation and rest after liberation. The divine Orpheus also seems to support their opinion, for he sang in his hymns: *Asclepius, master of all, Pæan, come blessed savior, granting a good end to life.* <note>original Greek: "ὁ τῆς πάντων Ἀσκληπιὲ δέσποτα παιὰν ἐλθὲ μάκαρ σωτὴρ βιοτῆς τέλος ἐσθλὸν ἐπάζων"</note> This means: Healer of all, Asclepius; Lord Pæan come, blessed savior, providing a good end to life. And these sentiments of theirs pertain solely to the salvation of the soul.

However, as far as the healing of the body is concerned, the aforementioned Julian <note>Refers to Julian the Apostate (r. 361–363 AD), the Roman Emperor who attempted to revive paganism.</note>, calling Jupiter as his witness, asserts that he knew many who were helped in the greatest dangers; indeed, he confesses that he himself, when suffering grievously, often escaped safely through his healings. Others chose Hercules himself, the son of Alcmene born of Jove, as their redeemer, among whom the Thassians are especially named. They signified this by the inscription on their coinage: *Hercules, Savior of the Thassians* <note>original Greek: "Ἡρακλέους σωτῆρος Θασσίων"</note>. This kind of opinion was common among other nations as well. In Egypt, too, the name **Soter**—that is, *Savior*—was attributed to King Ptolemy.

But among all the others, Apollo, the son of Jupiter, is commonly held by the Pagans as the Savior; insofar as he is the visible light of the world, the dispenser of eternal life, the inventor of medicine, and the healer of bodily diseases. That is, he is considered the restorer of lost bodily health because of his life-giving heat and his vitalizing power. Thus, it is believed that the force of common life, the seeds of particular virtues, and the dispositions of the stars themselves (which are pregnant with seeds), especially the Moon, exist under his power. Indeed, they even assert that the governance of souls in health or sickness is attributed to him, and that souls are received by him and preserved from darkness after their departure from the body.

Furthermore, by this benign operation of his nature, he tends toward the refining of what is opaque and gross, and toward leading back opaque things through dissolution into a transparent body, and earthly things into a spiritual nature. And this is why they made the palace of this divine person the *Sun*, and there they called him *Phœbus*. What else, then, do these fictions of the ancient philosophers intend, other than to introduce and deliver by a kind of poetic frenzy and commentary the truth of that most noble thing, the **Highest Good**? We Christians believe in this with certain and indubitable faith, as we know it to be most true from the doctrine of the Holy Scriptures.

For, if we compare the properties of the true Savior with those of Julian's fictional one, and if we strip away the true attributes from that false, fictional, and invented Redeemer—who was snatched from life by a lightning bolt (as authors have it)—and transfer them to the genuine and truly God-born One, we thereby render the tribute due to the eternal Caesar, led by truth. We say, first of all, that the true Jupiter is *Jehovah* himself, who, in his ideal and formal kingdom, begat from himself not some fictional Asclepius, but his true son, the *Messiah*.

This Messiah, making his way from heaven to earth, uniformly put on a human appearance in the womb of a virgin. Thus, increased even in his external appearance, he stretched out his healing right hand to restore souls that were poorly disposed and bodies that were unwell. Even the cock offered by Socrates to Asclepius can be compared to that cock which crowed to warn Peter of the approaching dawn of the Eternal Sun, who a little later rose from the tomb and from death; thus he was about to come forth as if from the horizon into a dark land, or from night into day. To this true Savior, then, the renewer of both soul and body and of the entire world, Orpheus rightly turns his speech, saying: *Jesus, Savior of all; Lord Pæan; Come, Blessed Savior, granting a good end to life.*

Furthermore, we say that those properties wrongly attributed to Apollo best fit and should be attributed to the Messiah of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, the true Savior. This is because he is the son of Jove or Jehovah, born of the virgin Latona—that is, carried in the womb of the undefiled Spirit before his incarnation. For they say Latona is the circumference or periphery of heaven; who, after the union of the **Jod** <note>The letter Yod, representing the masculine divine spark.</note> with her (for *His Spirit was moved over the waters*, acting upon them as a male upon a female), became pregnant and was, as it were, impregnated by the Power, or his first emanation. And this moist nature produced the love of Cupid and Psyche for the world.

Just as this divine, light-bringing, and life-giving seed—by whose spiritual presence all things that exist in creation were made and received life—was carried from the beginning of the world before its incarnation in the womb of the purest moist matter; so also this same power entered into the womb of pure Matter <note>The author is using a linguistic pun here: 'Materia' (Matter) is contracted to form the name 'Maria' (Mary).</note> (namely, into the womb of the Virgin **Mary**, through the contraction of Matter both by reason of the word itself and its essence into a human mass; for *Materia* is written thus by contraction, *Maria*; and the subtle material element through contraction creates a dense body, albeit a pure one, such as that of Mary). There he joined himself with fleshy nature and finally put on humanity, so that he might restore the most excellent creature—created in the beginning but fallen into a state of disobedience against the creator immediately after creation—to its original state of happiness through the death of his humanity and his resurrection from death, and thus liberate it from the captivity of darkness. This Spirit, instilled into the opaque body, had such great divine force and power that even by touch alone, or indeed by breath alone, and the utterance of a word—even over a long distance when the afflicted person was absent—he could cure diseases and, what is a wonder to say and hear, even the **Cacodemons** <note>Evil spirits or demons.</note> themselves, and spirits...

### CHAPTER III.

### On the action of the Word, or the power of the Tetragrammaton, in the first and foremost kind of health, which is called Sal-
->vation.<-

The Word, the Wisdom of Jehovah, and its first emanation in the production and creation of light, introduced *Jah* <note>original: "Jah" — a shortened form of the Hebrew name for God, often associated with his initial creative power.</note> as the first name of God into the world through its operation. In this name, He exercises kindness toward the creatures of the first *He* (ה) or heaven, which is joined with *Jod* (י): And from this, the Prophet David says: *If you, Lord Jah, should mark iniquities, who can stand? With you is forgiveness, so that you may be reverently worshiped: He himself redeemed Israel from all its iniquities:* <margin>Psalm 130.</margin> With Jehovah there is kindness, and with Him is plenteous redemption, as seen in Psalm 130. Hence also Wisdom is called a sweet, human, and kind Spirit, insofar as it acts in a spirit that is thin, flexible, sweet, tender, and most obedient to its actions. From this and in this heaven and its most simple and pure elements, He made living creatures subject to no sickness or passion of contrariety—namely, the angelic intelligences who always rejoice in God and obey Him eternally. In this heaven, therefore, Wisdom rejoices and is moved by inexplicable joy: <margin>Proverbs 9.</margin> Hence in Proverbs 9: *I, Wisdom, stand by Him as an apprentice, arranging all things; since I was being brought up with Him, I was in delights daily, rejoicing and playing before Him at all times.* <note>The author is quoting a Latin version of Proverbs 8:30, though the margin notes Chapter 9.</note> From this, He also began to have the will to have delights and pleasures likewise with the sons of men, who most closely approach the angelic nature, and to rejoice and play similarly in the habitable world, as is held in that same chapter. <margin>Psalm 33:5.</margin> And this is the reason the Prophet says in Psalm 33:5: *The earth is full of the kindness of Jehovah.*

Next, this most holy emanation of the Tetragrammaton <term>Tetragrammaton: The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</term> extends itself more deeply, namely to the region of *Vau* (ו), and immersing itself into the darkness of that region (the Firmament), it produces *Jeho* (יהו); this is the seal situated in the center of the world, by which the Word marked the forms of life persisting in a more hard and rebellious spirit. And in this heaven, the power of the Tetragrammaton or the emanation of almighty clarity acts, though not as sweetly as in the Empyrean <note>The Empyrean is the highest, most spiritual part of the heavens, composed of pure light or fire.</note> spirit, because it resists His actions and the impressions of Jehovah’s seal more strongly. And yet, because this Spirit is of a middle nature between the subtle and thick waters, even the slightest resistance is made obedient to receive the vital rays of eternal light. Therefore, because of its obedience, the divine light acts mercifully with it, imbuing it with immortality and incorruptibility, and establishes it as the ethereal and vital tabernacle of the World Soul, moving in a sphere of equality. Thus, the divine power satisfies the appetite of that Spirit. So, with a notable moderation, like a middle point between the starting point and the destination, He separated one extremity from the other—namely, the upper *He* (ה) from the lower *He* (ה), which is to say, the waters from the waters, or the subtle from the thick.

Finally, this power and authority of Jehovah, penetrating from the region of *Vau* (ו) all the way to the center of the earth, outlines the lowest region of the world, symbolically described by the final *He* (ה) of the Tetragrammaton. But, because this region includes all the dark spirits reflected back from the higher heavens, the spi-
»rits of this region are rebellious, hard, cold, and of great resistance. Thus it happens that divine strength,
»stronger than all other strength—whose nature it is to subject every hard and perverse power to its own dominion—
»breaks apart the ranks of darkness, and with a great and thundering voice repels them into the center of the abyss so that
»they cannot rise again to this very day. <margin>Proverbs 3.</margin> Thus the feuding elements are distinguished and separated from one another by the bonds of peace and harmony. Thus the earth was founded, and thus the heavens were made. And indeed, all these things were fulfilled by Wisdom, according to that saying of Solomon in Proverbs 3: *Jehovah by Wisdom founded the earth, established the heavens by understanding, by which the depths were broken open, etc.*

<margin>ε. s. 1.</margin> But here it must be observed that these lowest spirits, because of their density and rebellious nature against the disposition of the acting light, and because of their participation with the darkness from which they came—by which they are more opposed to the God-like light—are always subject to sedition. Hence, because of their resistance and rebellion against the actions of the Word, the simple elements are subject to changes and alterations, and their compounds are subject to sickness and death. And yet, the effort of the Spirit of Wisdom, even in this corruptible region of the world, is to save things subject to death, to heal the diseased, to restore the wasting away, and to raise even men extinguished and lifeless by disease through a double resurrection—and this is done through purification, thinning, the separation of darkness, and the illumination of opaque things. <margin>Daniel 6.</margin> For *Jod* (י) produced the Word *Vau* (ו) through the highest *He* (ה); and the lowest *He* (ה) shall be led back in the circuit of time into *Jod* (י), the starting point, through *Vau* (ו), or the power of the Tetragrammaton, or the Messiah; when, according to <margin>Daniel 6.</margin> *the Ancient of Days, coming in majesty, shall give power, honor, and a kingdom to the Son of Man.* <note>The text cites Daniel 6, but this prophecy of the Ancient of Days is found in Daniel 7.</note>

<center>ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES</center>

For it will be necessary—since the letters of the Tetragrammaton <note>original: "Tetragrammati" — the four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note> are all circular in their nature—that the last letter *He* <note>original: "He" — the letter ה, often associated with the material world or the "lower" presence of God.</note> of the name Jehovah should return from the nature of a dense and rebellious spirit into the disposition of the higher *He*, namely into a mild, humble, kind, thin, and immortal state, according to that passage in *Revelation 21: I saw the new city Jerusalem descending from heaven, etc.*

For Eternal Virtue is always the same; however, the difference in its actions occurs by reason of the matter and the subject upon which it acts. And in this way, heaven and earth, which constitute the world according to that hieroglyphic and symbolic model of the ineffable name Jehovah, are produced by a wondrous creation, through the power of the Word and the Wisdom of the Founder. In the dimensions of this world, the origin of both health and salvation, as well as sickness and death, is found. But such is the kindness of the Tetragrammaton that it far exceeds His indignation. Hence, His first *He* (the Empyrean heaven <note>The highest, most spiritual part of the universe, traditionally thought to be filled with pure fire or light.</note>) is full of divine grace, and is thus a sanctuary of salvation, redemption, resurrection, and eternal life. Furthermore, from His *Vau* <note>original: "Vau" — the letter ו, representing the "ethereal heaven" or the bridge between the highest spirit and the lower world.</note>—the ethereal heaven where the fountain and tree of life dwell in its solar sanctuary—a benevolent and universal medicine descends, which is called the "fifth essence" <note>original: "quinta essentia" — also known as the quintessence, a pure substance thought to compose the celestial bodies and hold the power to heal and harmonize the lower elements.</note>. By its presence, the rebellious elements (which are free from their native ethereal bond and already beginning to conflict) are rendered obedient. Through the power of that common bond and wondrous "glue," they are perceived to agree with one another in a right symphony; so that we may see the greater portion of the world-spirit filled with grace, life, and the kind spirit of the Almighty. Conversely, we observe the smaller part—and especially the lowest, elemental part—to be subject to change, morbid imbalance, and death itself, as we shall show below. It remains now for us to declare what that power of the Tetragrammaton is, by which so many and such great kinds of kindness are exercised toward creatures, both lower and higher.

# CHAPTER IV.

### Concerning the author’s Kabbalistic discovery, by which he seems to prove through numbers the mixing of divinity with the natural spirit; likewise concerning the supreme divinity of the number five, both in numbers and in Hebrew letters.

The dispute and debate regarding the essence of the Deity immersing and expanding itself into the material world is most difficult, both among common theologians and the scholastics. For theologians altogether deny that God is Nature itself. Hence, they wish to impose the name of "heretics" upon those who confuse God and nature, saying that *Naturalists* <note>A term used here to describe those who believe God and the physical world are one and the same (pantheists).</note> so venerate nature that, being ignorant of God himself, they accept Nature as God. But (if I may say so with their permission) those people are entangled in a more difficult labyrinth of ignorance who think they will arrive at the true knowledge of God while ignoring nature. It is impossible to reach from one extreme to the other without a middle point, or to climb Jacob's ladder without steps, or to contemplate and meditate upon the highest peak of the "fifty gates of understanding" <note>A Kabbalistic concept referring to the levels of wisdom a soul must pass through to understand the Divine.</note> of the wise, unless we begin from what is behind us and, according to the order of creation, tend toward higher things step by step through speculation. 

How, I ask, is it possible for us to reach from the earth to the third heaven—where *Ehieh* or *Jah* <note>original: "Ehieh vel Jah" — names of God in Hebrew; "Ehieh" means "I Am."</note> is found—unless we gradually refine our senses through the stages of the elements according to the disposition of the higher levels? And then, how shall we ascend through the spheres of the ethereal heaven, full of the "fifth essence," in whose region the very marrow of all nature resides, and where God himself is clothed in the "garment of the moist nature of the firmament"? Thus, we finally reach the Empyrean place, where God—Jehovah or *Jah*—is adorned with the simple garment of the intellectual Spirit. Moses reached the knowledge of this, although he could not see Him as He was in the "simple *Jod*" <note>original: "Jod" — the letter י, the smallest Hebrew letter, symbolizing the point of origin or the pure, unmanifested essence of God.</note>, stripped of every material garment. Hence, it was the opinion of the Kabbalists that God is clothed in many garments within nature. And I indeed, by a speculation not to be despised or rejected, have found the multiplicity of those garments in this manner:

<margin>1. 2. 3.</margin> In the Archetypal World <note>The world of divine blueprints or ideas.</note>, through the progress of one property of the Holy Trinity to another, we have observed a triple order from the digits of simple numbers—namely, three times three making nine. The first of these was 1, 2, and 3, which is the radical order and the simplest of all. Hence it denotes how unity flowed out into a "radical line," which is formed from the points of the first order. And so, this order designates the linear and simple nature of the outflow of the first worldly heaven, whose unity is *Jod*. The first hierarchy is attributed to 1, the second to 2, and the third to 3. This therefore denotes that *Jod* puts on a simple and linear garment in this heaven, namely: י. It is as if 1 were to put on 2 and 3, which make five; which is the number of *He* <note>In Hebrew numerology (Gematria), the letter He (ה) equals 5.</note>, according to the disposition of the first order in the Archetypal world. <margin>4. 5. 6.</margin> The second order of emanation, proceeding from the first in a grouping of three, is 4, 5, 6, denoting an imperfect surface—namely, three times two, or twice three. Hence the final number, 6, indicates *Vau* <note>The letter ו (Vau) equals 6.</note>; and the five in the middle declares the *He* hidden in the belly or center of *Vau*. From these things, it is clear that this second order in the formal world [proceeds] from the first...

Having previously discussed the letters Jod and He, the author now focuses on numerical symbolism (specifically the sequences 4-5-6 and 7-8-9) to explain the structure of the middle and lower heavens, the nature of the "Fifth Essence," and the creation of the angelic hierarchies.</meta>

SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK II.

This emanation is a type of the middle heaven or firmament. And since an odd number (five) is found in the middle between 4 and 6, it denotes that the perfection of that heaven is clothed in a double portion of matter. For an even number denotes matter, and an odd number denotes form. Similarly, 4 denotes the square of duality, or the surface of a line; and thus the number 5 establishes its tabernacle in the middle, between 4—that is, the upper part of the ether or firmament—and 6, which is the lower and thicker part of the middle heaven; namely, in the Sun, which is called the "heart of heaven." Hence it can be said that this heaven, because of the position of the formal number five <note>The "quinary" number.</note> in its center, is the **Fifth Essence** <note>original: "Quinta essentia" — the "quintessence" or ether, a refined substance distinct from the four earthly elements.</note>. 

Therefore, in this second order of the Archetype <note>The divine "blueprint" or original model of the universe.</note> (4, 5, 6), the starry heaven, the sphere of Saturn, and the sphere of Jupiter are given the number 4. The sphere of Mars, the sphere of the soul or of equality passing through the center of the Sun, and the Solar sphere itself are assigned to the number 5. The spheres of Venus, Mercury, and the Moon are assigned to the number 6. 

Certainly, the reason is obvious why the two extremes are even and imperfect—the first being of a lesser order and the last of a greater. Namely, the higher number, 4, is the spirit of that connection with *He* or the Empyrean spirit, which is the subtler part of matter. Thus, a lesser "evenness" <note>Parity or duality.</note> is continued with it because it approaches more closely to a simple odd number. The lower number, 6, is joined with the gross and lowest spirit of *He*. Hence, it exceeds the upper even number by two, denoting by this very fact that the further down the emanation of *Jod* <note>The first letter of the Tetragrammaton (י), representing the divine seed or point of light.</note> tends, the more it immerses itself in imperfect matter and proceeds deeper into multiplicity. 

And although we attribute to the divine majesty dwelling in the world only three "garments" according to the diversity of the matter of the three heavens (which are manifest), God nevertheless puts on as many different garments in the world as there are units in the multitude of matter. From this arises the distinction between things: of genera from one another, of species within those genera, and of individuals within those species. 

But to proceed to the final symbolic order of the formal world, which is 7, 8, 9: just as in the supreme *He* <note>The first "He" (ה) of the divine name, linked to the highest spiritual realm.</note> or the first emanation (1, 2, 3) we found an even number between two imperfect and odd characters—namely, 2—so also in the lowest realm where matter is multiplied, or in the final progression of divine numbers (7, 8, 9), we find 8 as the even number between two perfect odds. Therefore, the number 2, the center of the supreme order, when multiplied by itself as a root, produces 4 (the square) in the second heaven; and that in turn produces 8 in the lowest realm, which is the cube of the whole. 

Thus we see how God is clothed in matter in the world. For every odd figure of these fingers <note>A term sometimes used in medieval mathematics for the single digits 1-9.</note> or divine numbers is a symbol of divinity. Hence it is written that "God delights in an odd number" <note>A reference to Virgil’s Eclogues: "Numero deus impare gaudet."</note>, namely because of its perfection; for nothing is perfection or perfect except God alone, insofar as nothing is absolutely good except God alone. 

In the supreme heaven, therefore, or the image of the name Tetragrammaton, *Jod* (unity) is clothed by *He* (spirit) on one side; and perfection, signified in 3, is like a bond or clasp <note>original: "fibula" — a brooch or fastener.</note> perfecting a wonderful composition from this simple spirit or garment of *Jod*, from which the angels were produced. For the first *Jod* entered into *He*. And 3 was in both—or the Spirit that "hovered over the waters"—providing the power of composition to this garment of God, and producing the choirs of angels. Indeed, as the third person <note>In this context, the third number or manifestation in the sequence.</note> is a multitude in respect to unity, so also it produced not identity, but "otherness" <note>original: "alteritatem" — a philosophical term for the state of being different or distinct from the One.</note> or diversity. For as God is identity, so the angel is otherness, produced from spirit and light—that is, from God Himself or a ray of God—and from created spirit. And hence it is that angels, according to the order of the third person, are divided into three hierarchies, and each of those again into three orders.

By a similar logic, the number 3 is clothed from the upper part by the number 2 (or the spirit/Empyrean) and from the lower part by the number 4 (the upper part of the firmament). And so God is found in the middle of these two spirits, which are bound to each other by a natural—or rather, a supernatural—bond. This is done first so that a symphony <note>A harmonious arrangement.</note> might be established in place of discord, and secondly so that a vacuum is not permitted in the nature of things. 

This is the reason why, in living things, air is so bound to fire that fire cannot ascend without air, nor air without water, nor water without earth, nor the Fifth Essence without fire, nor the Empyrean spirit (or sixth essence) without the Fifth Essence or ethereal spirit. This spirit of wisdom, therefore, is the bond and ligament of the parts of the world to one another; indeed, it even joins the parts of the elements in the composition of creatures with symphonic consent. Let there be peace in their Economy <note>The management or structural order of the universe.</note>, and let it be continued as long as that sacred bond performs its duty in every thing. 

For first, it is the bond by which God (*Jod*) joins Himself with the moist matter of the first *He*. Then He disposes the elements or grades of that heaven and binds them to one another—namely, the moist and the hot—so that from these two, in the subtle moist matter, He may produce pure Intelligences in that heaven. Then, further binding the intellectual spirit of the highest heaven with the vital spirit of the middle heaven by His bond, He joins the formal spirit of the higher realm with the middle, and thus brings in the **Soul of the World** <note>original: "anima mundi."</note>. Next, gluing together the elements of darkness of that same heaven to one another and purging them from pollution, He assigns a portion of that same Soul of the World to each thing so composed on the second day, and they become fixed stars in the number four; and then finally, after the third day, the entire substance of the Soul of the World is contracted into the Sun in the sphere of the number five. By the "glue" of this spirit, every orb of the ethereal heaven is fixed in its place, and nature corresponds to natures with symphonic respect.

Afterward, that divine triple number passes to five, thus: 3, 4, 5. And there, unity is clothed in a garment corresponding to the proportion of "quinary" matter <note>Matter associated with the number 5.</note> in the number three, and three in five;

Therefore, the Deity is signified by odd numbers, as if God were receding from the place of his unity and multiplying himself all the way to *Jod* <note>The Hebrew letter י, which equals 10.</note>, or the number ten; through which, in his world by a typical reasoning, he described the formal steps in the material descent. And the even numbers indicate the degrees of the impression of divinity into the world, or the "garments" of any process of divinity from unity. Therefore, 2 is the garment of unity, and 1 is the clothed light, or the bond tying duality—or the higher spirit—together with God, or the source of light remaining in the eternal world. So, 4 is the garment covering the divine ternary (3); and 3 is the bond of light, connecting the quaternary number itself—or the square—to 2, its root. Hence, the square is said to have its form and being from its informed root, since that is the root and origin of its own square, no less than a line is to a surface. There is, therefore, a divine emanation interposed as act and life, by which the procession happens from unity to the root and from the root to the square, etc. 

Consequently, the odd number, attributed to divinity and essential form, is the act and life of every even number, compared to matter and spirit; it is interposed between them as if it were a support and pillar by which a thing is sustained in its being. And in this world, one has a relation to the other. Thus the quinary (5) is a garment to itself; hence it is a symbol of *Jod* itself; for five and five make 10, the Hebrew character for which is *Jod*. From this we see how God is the wonderful center of spiritual things—that is, sitting on a fiery throne in the middle of the waters. And this is verified by his appearance in every heaven; namely, he sits in the Sun as if in the center of the ethereal waters, and in the cloud of the lower heaven—namely, in the midpoint of the air—just as he appeared to Moses on Mount Sinai. 

Next, 6 is the garment of the number 7, and 8 of the number 9, so that we find five modes of appearance by which God exhibited and opened himself in this world; namely 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9, in which he was essentially present, just as he is; yet because of the five garments by which he was covered, his face (which is also called his "fore-parts") could not be seen. Thus his first clothing was the thinnest spirit in his first emanation, like 2 to 1, or Aleph א; the second was the mixture of the base of the higher spirit with the apex of the ether, like 4 to 3, or Gimel ג; the third was the ethereal spirit, like 6 to 5, or He ה; the fourth was the elementary spirit, like 8 to 7; and the fifth was the composite number, like 10 to 9, which is the final extension of units, beyond which there is no progress. 

Hence, where the matter of the world is measured, we use composite numbers—namely, the tens, hundreds, and thousands; but where formal progressions of numbers occur, we attribute movement into the matter of the world to simple and divine numbers, according to their dignity and holiness. And so we see that God, as Unity, multiplies himself in the world through simple numbers; and at last, he returns by a circular progress to his prince, *Jod*. By these things we are taught that, just as all things proceed from unity to the quinary (5) through the composition of many elements—as if from non-beings to beings—so in the point, and from the point or center of the quinary, all things that exist receive life from the Word, filled with divine light and the power and seal of the Tetragrammaton <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>. And again, from this point of life, through the dissolution of the composite (which we wrongly call "death"), they hasten back to *Jod*,
