# ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.

In the *Yetzirah* of Abraham <note>Referring to the *Sepher Yetzirah* or Book of Formation, a foundational text of Jewish mysticism attributed to the patriarch Abraham</note> we read these things: *Ten Sephiroth <note>The ten emanations or attributes in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note> beyond the ineffable, a number of 10 fingers, namely five against five; and the supreme covenant of the One directed in the middle; in the interpretation of the tongue and of circumcision, ten Sephiroth without the ineffable.* Accordingly, we have striven to order or arrange the 10 fingers through the Hebrew letters in such a way that five are against five; so that the supreme covenant of the One might be established in the middle. Therefore, in the first demonstration preceding, I placed five letters, namely א ח ו מ נ <note>Aleph, Heth, Vav, Mem, Nun</note> against מ ח ו ז י <note>Mem, Heth, Vav, Zayin, Yod</note>; yet in such a way that the covenant of unity was found in the middle. Thus, I arranged them as described previously, namely א <note>Aleph</note> and א as if in the hidden world and the world endowed with eternity; denoting by this very thing how God, before creation, was the Alpha and the Omega. Hence א, the Unity looking back toward Nothing, is called "Nothing" or "Non-Being," and "without end" <note>original: "non finis," likely referring to the *Ein Sof* or the Infinite</note> as far as we are concerned, although it contains All things in itself. And so it stood in respect to our understanding, before He decreed within Himself to shine back into the potential world; by another name, as the Kabbalists wish, it is called *Choshek* <note>original: חושך</note> or darkness. But when He wished to change His form, and to look upon the world submerged in darkness with His splendid and luminous face, it was called the "bright" א <note>Aleph</note>. Whence it is written 
<margin>,,</margin> of Him: *Even as the darkness, so also is its light.* <note>Psalm 139:12</note> This was also left to us, handed down in open words by Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with a syncretic blend of Greek and Egyptian philosophy and magic</note>, 
<margin>,,</margin> saying: *When he had said these things, he changed form, and suddenly revealed all things; for I perceived a certain immense spectacle; namely, all things converted into light, etc.* And a little after: *A horrendous shadow slipped underneath with an oblique revolution, etc.* Then, in alphabetical order, I placed ב <note>Beth</note> after א, insofar as it is the mark of Wisdom; it also denotes, in its grammatical significance, a house or habitation; symbolically it also designates ב the Son, insofar as he is the first emanation from א, and so on for the others. Similarly, we have placed י <note>Jod</note> in the same way in the center of the numbers, or in the place of the five <note>the quinary</note>; however, because we found that grammatical and common arrangement not so fit for finding the mystery of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter divine name, YHWH</note>, we therefore arranged those letters in this manner: so that א stands in the center, and on the right side א looks back with its own light; moreover, י <note>Jod</note> looks out from the left from the unique center, which we said was above the number five; for that number is a double center, as was demonstrated before; namely, either of the formal fingers 1, 3, (5), 7, 9, or the material ones 2, 4, (5), 6, 8. Now indeed it was said above that the "dark" א is taken for God as the principle and formal unity without respect to matter; and י <note>Jod</note> is the unity, or the "bright" א <note>Aleph</note>, and it looks toward matter. Whence י <note>Jod</note>, being always unity, is joined with a cipher for its own existence; just as in *Jehova* <note>The Tetragrammaton</note> it is joined with ה <note>He</note>, which denotes the first entry into matter; or the "bright" א illuminates the spirit ה nearest to itself. And as א <note>Aleph</note> is the first letter, which is the principle of the divine essence אהיה *Ehieh* <note>I AM THAT I AM</note>, who is the Father and the first origin of all, or like a point in a body, so the first heaven is dedicated to Him, namely ה; looking into which with His shining face He is called the "bright" א; which is the same as the י <note>Jod</note> in the Tetragrammaton. Whence א <note>Aleph</note> is called the principal—namely, unity and the one—or the final, specifically for the end of the tens. ## CHAPTER V.

->*A still clearer demonstration of the divinity existing everywhere in the spirit of the world; where it is also proved that the Messiah is the power or act of the Tetragrammaton, for the universal salvation of things, and their liberation and redemption from darkness and the marks of death, and for the healing and restoration to former health of bodies and souls existing outside the limits of health.*<-

<margin>Messiah</margin> What that power of the Tetragrammaton is—which we, with the Kabbalists (hardly differing from the Holy Scriptures), call the Messiah—although we have openly declared it in the preceding chapter in the manner of the Kabbalists, we shall here explain it with a demonstration more familiar to the common people. <margin>world soul</margin> The Kabbalists seem to distribute the world into as many powers of God as there are worlds or heavens: therefore they maintain that the world, which is animated, is illuminated by that mind which they call *Metattron* <note>Metatron, an archangel often described as the celestial scribe or the 'lesser YHWH' in mystical literature</note>; but they believe that the supreme or angelic world is ruled by the soul of the Messiah (which they call the 'ideated idea' of all lives), and that the light of the soul of the Messiah, which is *Elhai* (that is, the Living God), governs the eternal world. They therefore make *Metattron*, whom they call the active intellect of the first mover, communicate with the Messiah; that is, the soul of the world with the soul of the Messiah, or the nature of the Empyrean Spirit with that of the ethereal. They also teach that the soul of the Messiah and the light of *Elhai* are not distant from each other; but they call *Elhai* the fountain of living waters, and the soul of the Messiah the spring or stream of life; and they assert that this supreme world of *En-soph* is that essence of the Deity which the Seraphim celebrated by saying, *Holy, Holy, Holy, Tetragrammaton*, that is, God himself naked in his purest essence without any respect to matter. # ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.

...which we have called the luminous *Aleph* <note>original: "Aleph lucidum"</note>. But, as it seems to me (with all due respect to others), they have spoken concerning the variety of the operation of the one God in the multitude, or of the indivisible and uncreated form within the created world spirit <term>World Spirit: Or *spiritus mundanus*, a Neo-Platonic concept of a vital force that permeates the universe</term>. For, as we have said before, the act is always the same, but the difference in the spiritual matter—whether in obedience or obstinacy, that is, in thinness or coarseness and density—creates and brings about the entire difference in worldly actions. For an act always occurs according to the logic of resistance; because the act, which is divine virtue and power, overcomes all things. Whence, toward the soft, the kind, the humble, and the obedient, it acts kindly, softly, and sweetly; but toward the hard, the proud, the obstinate, and the perverse, it proceeds heavily and violently. 

And from this it happens that, although God is always good and His power tends toward goodness, nevertheless, the resistance of a person refusing this goodness of action is the cause of it being called "evil." This is so much the case that divine action is always good, even if, in respect to the effect of rebellion and resistance in that suffering subject upon which it acts, it is called "evil" among men; for indeed, it is not found to be evil before God, but only before men. And from this arises the fact that God’s act toward men sounds like "justice" and "kindness" to them, or "punishment" and "reward" and "joy"; and yet justice and kindness are one and the same before God. So we also see in fire both benefit and harm; namely, it is observed to cherish cold limbs with its heat; and yet the same nature of fire, unchanged, burns and destroys. Therefore, the rebellion of the subject brings it about, or is the cause, that the action of God is called "wrath"; and likewise, on the opposite side, the subject's obedience causes it to be called "grace," "salvation," and "life." But of these things, more will be said at length below. 

From these points, therefore, we conclude that the power of the *Tetragrammaton* <term>Tetragrammaton: The four-letter Hebrew name of God, יהוה (YHWH), considered ineffable and the source of all power</term> is the same throughout the universal world spirit, although the effect differs according to the spirit’s thinness and density. For thus we see that the heat of this power, looking down from the Solar body, is hotter and more effective in the air during the summer time because of the air's density, as it is thickened by vapors raised up from springs, rivers, and ponds. 

For this reason we also see that the Kabbalists <note>original: "Cabalæ"</note>, in their method of distinguishing the action of each heaven, have dedicated the lower and visible parts of the world to *Metattron* <note>Metattron is often described in mystical texts as the "Prince of the Countenance" or the mediator between the divine and the mundane</note>, but the higher, invisible, and angelic parts to the Soul of the Messiah, and the eternal world of *Ensoph* <term>Ensoph: From the Hebrew *Ein Sof*, meaning "The Infinite," the unknowable divine origin</term>—or the Deity and the light of the Trinity—to *Elhai* <note>original: "Elhai", likely a variation of *El Hai*, the "Living God"</note> or the *Tetragrammaton*. For they seem to confess that the fountain of living waters—that is, of uncreated fiery spirits—is the kingdom of the *Tetragrammaton Ensoph*, from which the *Jod* (י) looks downward; and that the Soul of the Messiah is the stream gushing forth from that fountain. The sea into which that stream or emanation discharges itself, or flows, they make to be the angelic or Empyrean heaven <term>Empyrean: The highest heaven, filled with pure light and fire</term>, or according to the letter *He* (ה) of the *Tetragrammaton*. And yet elsewhere they acknowledge that this soul is the idealized "Idea" of all lives, to which all vitality—whether individual, specific, or general—is referred. 

We also confess that this power of the *Tetragrammaton*, dwelling in the Empyrean heaven in this world, is the fountain and highest genus among created things of all lives, emanating from the most general genus—that is, from the Transcendent Being. But truly, that a genus could exist without its species, or a species without its individuals, we utterly deny. Therefore, the power of the *Tetragrammaton* in the Soul of the Messiah in the Empyrean heaven is like a genus of "making-alive," and is compared by the Kabbalists themselves to the trunk of a root, whose roots are in the *Ensoph*. Then this genus in the ethereal heaven divides itself into species—or the trunk there spreads out its branches, which are the stars. Finally, those species transmit other sub-species downward into the elements, just as the branches of a tree send out their tips and leaves; and at last, the fruits of the sub-species in the elements communicate the fruits of life to individuals: namely, to animals, vegetables, and minerals.

<margin>Abel's Hand writing</margin>

From these things, therefore, we see that just as the effect of the root in a tree is the trunk (which retains in itself all the power of life it received from the root, and then pours out that same force of life into a multitude of branches, and the branches again into other subdivided twigs, and those finally into a multitude of fruits); or just as a genus is divided into its species, and those species are subdivided into sub-species, and they at last into individuals—so also it stands in the emanation of the glittering river of life from the fountain of living waters existing in the super-celestial paradise. That river, flowing down into the Empyrean sea as a genus, divides itself into branches, through which it fills all the luminous fountains of the ethereal heaven. From the fullness of these, other gushing rivulets carry down and infuse the act of life and the waves of the vital spirit into individuals, each destined and subjected to them by God from the beginning. 

We see, therefore, that the power of the trunk is the same as the power of the root, and the power of the branches is the same as the power of the trunk; and likewise, further on, the same power that is in the branches descends into the fruit. By the likeness of this thing, it will be very easy to gather and discern that the same power of the *Tetragrammaton* is everywhere throughout the universal world spirit, according to that saying of the Evangelist in Matthew 5:35: *Heaven is His throne and the earth the footstool of His feet*; and Wisdom 1:7: *The holy spirit of wisdom has filled the world.* I do indeed acknowledge that from the angelic heaven, as if from a nursery, all life is drawn out, as branches from a trunk or a trunk from roots; but it does not follow from this that the trunk is not of the same essence as the root, or the branches with the trunk, or the fruit with all of these.

<margin>Metattron, World Soul, Soul of the Messiah, Light of Elhai</margin>

Accordingly, it is manifest that the soul *Metattron*, or the World Soul, is of the same essence as the Soul of the Messiah, and that the Soul of the Messiah is also the same as the light of *Elhai* or His Father; just as the water of a river and the water of the streams departing from it are of the same nature, and in no way differ from the water of the fountain from which that river had its origin. ### SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK II.

...[general] question: namely, whether the Messiah is God, or the angel Metatron <term>Metatron: In Jewish mysticism, the highest of the archangels who serves as the celestial scribe and the mediator between God and the world</term>, or nature itself? Certainly, he is the Messiah, the Angel, and universal nature; but understood in different ways. Christ the Messiah is called—both by sacred scripture and Kabbalistic doctrine—the beginning, the middle, and the end of all creatures, and consequently the beginning, middle, and end of the divine outpourings communicated to created things. Indeed, Saint John <note>Latin: D. Joannes</note> teaches that he is the beginning itself, and that this beginning is God himself, and that this beginning was with God, indicating that he went forth from the palace or kingdom of the *Ensoph* <term>Ensoph: From the Hebrew "Ein Sof," meaning "the Infinite," referring to God as He is in Himself before any manifestation</term> into this world. Therefore, insofar as he is the beginning in the world, the most worthy place of the world and the first thing created by him is attributed to him.

That he is the "middle" is witnessed by the beauty of the Sun, in which he placed his tabernacle; hence the Sun is also called the dispenser of life and light, since it received its life-giving power from the Word, in which was the light that was the life of all. For this reason, he is also called the Tree of Life placed in the middle of the garden of Paradise in Genesis 2:9. For his seat was in the middle of the created universal Paradise—namely, in the heart of the world or the heavens, or in the center of the universal dark cloud. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus 24:

->I, Wisdom, like a channel led out from a river, and like an aqueduct, have gone forth into Paradise, and I said: I will water my garden most abundantly.<-

Now that river or fountain, from which this most holy and shining power or wisdom went forth, was the Tetragrammaton <term>Tetragrammaton: The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH, often translated as "LORD"</term> itself, according to that verse in Psalm 87: "All my fountains of life are from God." And Ecclesiastes 9:17: "God gave the number of life and days." And certainly, it first began to flow into lower things from the composition of the Macrocosm <term>Macrocosm: The "great world" or the universe as a whole, viewed as a large-scale reflection of the human being</term>, from the middle of which the Sun <note>original: "Phoebus"</note> is said to be the origin of life; and then afterward through the structure of the Microcosm <term>Microcosm: The "little world" or the human being, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe</term>, in whose center or middle region the heart, the fountain of life, is found. This indicates that the procession of spiritual life and the fountain of lives is that "middle" through which all things are made alive. 

But likewise, he exists as a mediator between the most miserable condition of the region of darkness and that excellent and splendid palace of the fountain of light, in which *Jah* <note>A shortened form of the divine name Jehovah/Yahweh</note>, full of mercy and kindness, reigns forever and ever; so that by his mediation, health is conferred from the holy heaven upon the sick and weak, and salvation and redemption from the high heavens are sent to things destined for eternal death. Finally, he is called the "end," because just as his shining beginning was like a small *Aleph*, so his end was the great *Aleph*; for he returns to the point from which he began, and thus into infinity. Hence he is called by Saint John in Revelation 1: "the Alpha and the Omega." The Messiah is therefore the beginning from which all things proceed, and into which they return.

And indeed this power—insofar as it is viewed in and through itself simply, without any consideration of the matter in whose liquid it swims—is the true and absolute essence of God, and consequently God himself. Hence Saint John says: "And this Word was with God, and that Word was God himself." But insofar as it is regarded in the mixture of the world—that is, insofar as this power is mixed with the moist nature of the world—it is called an "angel." For the name is then given not from simplicity and identity (that is, from the Deity), but from simple composition and "otherness"; since an angel is created from the purest created spirit and the uncreated light that creates that spirit. Hence the name is derived from the created and formed part, and not from the uncreated light. Understanding this concerning the Messiah, Jacob said to his sons in his final testament in Genesis 48:16:

->That God, before whose sight my fathers walked continually; that God, who has fed me until this day; the Angel, who rescued me from all evils, bless these boys; and let my name be invoked upon them, and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and let them grow into a multitude upon the earth.<-

Since, therefore, in this passage Jacob asks the same things from the Angel that he asks from God himself, and since he deems him worthy of equal honor, this Angel cannot be understood as anyone else but the Messiah, and as God clothed in a created spiritual garment. Hence also, he who is called Jehovah in Exodus 13:21 in those words:

->Jehovah going before them by day in a column of cloud<-

is said of him in chapter 14:19:

->Then the angel of God himself, who went before the camp, moved...<-

To those [the Egyptians] it was a cloud and darkness, but to these [the Israelites] it illuminated the night itself. From these things, it is clear that Jehovah is here called an "angel" insofar as his power was joined with a moist nature or clothed in the covering of a cloud. Hence, because this was a "composition of the first kind" or "otherness"—namely, of fire (which is the simple essence of God) and of water (which was the covering of that essence, for both cloud and fire appeared)—therefore in one place he is named "angel" from the fiery form or essence, which is the power of Jehovah, and is thus called Jehovah; but in another place, he is named from the form of created matter, namely from the water or cloud, and is called an "angel." And again, that angel is called Jehovah in the same book, chapter 24, in those words:

->When Jehovah looked toward the camp of Egypt in the column of fire and cloud...<-

From these things one may also recognize that when Jehovah is called an angel, the name of the "cloud" is placed before the name of the "fire," arguing that the speech concerns a creature (namely, an angel) according to the disposition of created matter, such that the word "cloud" and its order precedes the name "fire." But where in the final passage Jehovah is taken for or placed as an angel, there the name of the formal essence—namely, "fire"—is placed before the material word or the "cloud." Thus, by "Angel" in this place (as interpreters have not ineptly suggested), the Messiah and Christ are understood. Indeed, by this same formula of speaking, mention is made of him in Exodus 23:25 in these words:

->Behold, I send an angel before you; beware of his face... because my name is in him.<-

From these things, therefore, we conclude that the entire Tetragrammaton Y-H-V-H <note>original Hebrew: יהוה</note> is found in the name of the Messiah, as it is in his power that he operates. For the Messiah is the very power of the Tetragrammaton. My reasoning is that, through a Kabbalistic transformation, YHWH <note>יהוה</note> becomes Yeheshuah <note>Hebrew: יהשוה; the author is arguing that by adding the letter *Shin* (representing the fire of the Holy Spirit) to the four letters of God's name, it becomes the name of Jesus/the Messiah</note>, which is to say, the Messiah. There are, however, some Kabbalists who say that this angel was Michael, because in his name "Jah" <note>Hebrew: יה</note> is found. But this same thing can also be said of Raphael, Gabriel, Zab-

...Michael, Uriel, and the others; in whom we can observe that in the "otherness" <note>Latin: *alteritas*; a philosophical term referring to the state of being "other" or distinct from the absolute unity of God</note> of the Angels, God himself appears in some way, or his essential power. Indeed, they held this world soul to be that sacrosanct wisdom which Ecclesiasticus 1 <note>The Book of Sirach</note> says was created before all things, and that the understanding of prudence has been from eternity; whose fountain, he wrote, is the word of God on high. They said this was that angel in whom the name of God is found; for in him the name Shaddai <term>Shaddai: A Hebrew name for God meaning "Almighty"</term> is found, included through a numerical value equal to both expressions <note>The author refers to gematria, where the Hebrew letters for "Metatron" and "Shaddai" both sum to 314</note>.

Nevertheless, these opinions of theirs do not please me, because according to our discovery—established by secure contemplation and certain foundations—we have found that this angel was the Messiah himself, or the power of the Tetragrammaton <term>Tetragrammaton: The four-letter name of God, YHWH, often considered too sacred to pronounce</term>, containing in itself the complete name of the Tetragrammaton. Hence, not without unique cause, this angel is sometimes called Jehovah—namely in respect to the power and the name itself placed within him—and sometimes an angel, namely in respect to his angelic nature, in which those living and eternal characters of the Tetragrammaton are expressed. The ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton is the most high God himself, universally dispersing the essence of this name of his through the world spirit. But where that angelic spiritual nature exists, there this fiery, complete name of the Tetragrammaton is found. And yet the name of the Tetragrammaton extends itself everywhere and in all places; therefore, likewise, this angel—who is the spirit of wisdom, filling all things and leaving nothing empty—mixes himself through the universal world spirit, informs all things through the name and power of the Tetragrammaton, and preserves them once they are formed.

<margin>How the universal spirit received the characters of the tetragrammaton within itself.</margin>
How, however, this created spirit received within itself all the characters of the letters of the Tetragrammaton—by which it, and with it the whole world, was formed—we have demonstrated in the preceding parts: namely, Jod <term>Jod: The first letter (י), representing the seed or point of origin</term>, the root at the summit of the "machine" <note>The *machina mundi* or the structural framework of the universe</note>, illuminated the upper waters—or the Empyrean spirit—through its spirit, He <term>He: The second letter (ה), representing divine breath or manifestation</term>; and Vau <term>Vau: The third letter (ו), acting as a connecting hook or pillar</term> illuminated and informed the ethereal kingdom of the stars, and from the power of the final He, it acquired its elementary heaven. Thus, in the head of this angel is Jah <note>The first two letters, Jod and He (יה)</note>; in the chest and middle, where his heart is, Vau resides in the Sun; and the final He, carrying with it the spirit of divinity, prepared the lower world, informed it as beautiful and cleansed of darkness, and distinguished the elements.

Hence the universal spirit is called the World <note>Latin: *Mundus*, which also means 'clean' or 'neat'</note> from its cleansing and washing from foul darkness; which was indeed done by the power and presence of the name Jehovah. Nor let anyone say that if the universal spirit becomes a material part of one angel, there can be no other angels, because one angel would have filled the whole world.

<margin>What created and uncreated Wisdom is in respect to its clothing.</margin>
For we respond that, just as God the Tetragrammaton is outside all things and yet contains all things in himself, so also his power—which is of the same essence as himself—contains all other angels, and indeed any other creature, like an infinite king subjecting all things to his will. This power is therefore within all composite things, by whose beneficial property they live; it is also outside all composite things in the elements, and the universal spirit receives soul and action in it and through it. Hence the spirit in which it dwells is its clothing; and this deific power itself informs its clothing in different ways according to greater or lesser thinness or density, and imposes a name upon it according to the condition of the body or matter thus created. This, therefore, is that Wisdom (Ecclesiasticus 1) created before all things in respect to its "clothing"; but truly uncreated if we consider that its power is of the nature and essence of Jehovah himself. Of this the Wise Man speaks in Proverbs 3: "Jehovah by wisdom founded the earth, and established the heavens by understanding." And Proverbs 8:22: "Jehovah possessed Wisdom in the beginning of his way, before his works, before any time; before the ages I was anointed," etc. Here, then, we see that Wisdom—the greatest angel and prince of angels, the soul of the universal world, the power of the Tetragrammaton—is said to be created insofar as the name and power of Jehovah is inscribed upon it. But, all consideration of matter being removed, there remains only the most formal and ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton, by which, in which, and through which all things were made. And this, if I am not mistaken, Saint John <note>Latin: D. Joannes</note> understands in chapter 1, saying: "The true light was in the world, and the world was made through it," etc. Surely by "true light" he signifies the true essence of God and the power of the Tetragrammaton, and by "world" he denotes the garment or universal spirit of that light, which was made and created by the said light according to the will of the Creator. Finally, Malachi speaks of this angel in chapter 3:1, saying: "Behold, I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face," etc. Finally, this power (insofar as it is held to be the essential form of the elements, by which some things are attached to others in their spheres and places destined through creation as if by divine glue, and by which all things are simultaneously coupled and connected in peace and obedience) is accepted and held by Philosophers as the very nature of things. And in this way you see, Readers—perhaps eager for novelty—how the same divine power tends to have various names in different composite things: namely, in respect to the most pure and divine light in the abstract, it is taken for God alone, and the Messiah, and Christ—that is, for identity and charity, which is the life-giving spirit of the Almighty; in the concrete form of the first composition, namely from two parts, it is taken for the angel, which is "otherness" or a creature of the first order; and in the concrete form of the third composition, as in the elements themselves and things made of elements, it is taken for the very nature of things.

SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK II.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*On the nature of the benevolent action of the power of the Tetragrammaton regarding life and health: And how this same power, leading to life and health, acquires various names in the world according to the diversity of its garments.*<-

Through the preceding points, it is explained more clearly than the midday sun (as I believe) even to someone overwhelmed by great foolishness and the darkness of ignorance, why the name of God Jehovah is used in natural things, since He, by Himself, is outside and beyond all things, and is said to reign in His secret and hidden heaven without any regard for matter. Certainly, His name is used there where the power and virtue of that name, clothed in the Spirit, is understood, insofar as it dominates in all things. And again, it is called an "Angel" insofar as the spiritual matter of the angel—which the name of Jehovah produced by its presence—is denoted; and thus it is also called a "Messenger" <note>original: "Nuncius"</note>, according to that passage in Malachi 3: *Behold, I send my messenger/angel, etc.* <note>Malachi 3:1. The Latin *angelus* means both a celestial being and a messenger.</note> That is, the power of my name, which is in the angelic spirit and moves it to carry out the will of its creator. In this context, by "angel," His Word is understood, according to Psalm 40:9: *Behold, I come; In the head of the book it is written of me, that I should do your will.* For every action comes from God, but every "passion" <note>The state of being acted upon or receiving influence; the passive side of existence.</note> comes from the created spirit. And hence it happens that the designation of "angel" arises from the passive and created part, such as when the word "cloud" is placed before the word "fire." For this reason, David in Psalm 104:4 called the angels winds, or spirits, regarding their created nature. But joining the created part with the uncreated denotes action within the passive; hence in the same place he calls them ministers, and a flaming fire—that is, luminous creatures created from the Spirit that was illuminated on the first day.

The Messiah, however, is the luminous power of the very letter of the ineffable name, insofar as he is considered in nature, clothed with the life-giving Spirit of the *He* <gloss>the Hebrew letter ה</gloss>—the first letter in the name of Jehovah <note>While *He* is the second letter of YHVH, it is the first of the "breath" letters often associated with the creation of the spirit.</note>—according to whose pattern the Empyrean <term>Empyrean: The highest, most refined part of heaven, composed of pure light and fire</term> Spirit was created. Therefore, the "Being" of the Word is in the Tetragrammaton and its spirit *He* (ה). The "Being" of the Angel is in the Word, or the power flowing from *Yod* <gloss>the Hebrew letter י</gloss>, which the Tetragrammaton signifies. And the "Being" of Nature is in the soul of the angel Metatron and the double lower spirit; but the "Being" of all composite things is in the soul of nature. All these differences are understood in respect to the diversity of the matter in which the power of the Tetragrammaton works, insofar as all multiplicity exists in matter; while conversely, the power and virtue of the Tetragrammaton, which is the Messiah himself, is one and the same through all things. But the diversity of matter, resisting the divine in different ways, makes the acts of this active power seem diverse to us, though they are not so in respect to the divinity; for there, all acts are the same and weighed in the same scales of supreme justice. This power, therefore, bearing the presence of God Jehovah before it, when it immersed itself in the first created spirit, took its name from the nature of that Spirit: hence it is called an "angel." Descending into the lower world, where it puts on a manifold garment, it is called "Nature." Entering into any thing, whether simple or composite, it is called "Life." And from this arose the opinions of the Pagan philosophers, asserting that *all things are full of Gods.* Hence also Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Apollo, Venus, Mercury, and Diana were treated with divine worship as Gods because of their abundant reception of this power. God, stripped of all substance, is *Aleph* <gloss>the Hebrew letter א</gloss>; the root of all created things is *Yod* (י); whose power, emanating from the "Holy, Holy, Holy" heavens into *He* (ה), is the Messiah. Whence *Jah* <note>A shortened form of the Tetragrammaton, associated here with the attribute of Mercy or Kindness.</note> is referred to kindness, and kindness is attributed to the Son. And this power in the first created Spirit is the mind or intelligence; and intelligence is the angel, who, putting on the middle spirit, is called Metatron; and the power of the Messiah in its center is called the Soul of the World; and then the angel, putting on an elementary garment, is called Nature, which retains all higher things within itself.

Therefore, in the benevolent presence of this divine power, life and health are present; but disease follows its partial absence, and death follows its total absence. Thus, in the higher spirit, the Messiah gives life that is invisibly luminous, without any darkness; whence the angels are said to always stand before the face of Jehovah. In the middle, he gives life that is partly visibly and partly invisibly luminous, participating moderately in darkness; whence that spirit is said to participate in both extremes. In this heaven, therefore, because of the increase of matter, free will begins, since its nature is to adhere sometimes to the higher and sometimes to the lower. Here, then, matter mixes itself equally with the divine nature; and this is the reason why Fate is said to dwell in this place. Furthermore, in the last and lowest spirit, he encloses the luminous life emanating from both higher levels into a cubic and opaque body; where, because of the narrowness of the enclosed light, it is oppressed unless the power of Jehovah constantly assists it—not indeed in respect to the light itself, as it does not suffer, but in respect to the passive and created spirit, by which it is said to be clothed as if in various garments and covered from human understanding. And from this it follows that the super-celestial life is that immortal one, by whose power man shall be free from the death of the lower spirit according to the divine promise, and believes with certain and undoubting faith that he shall rise again. From this, therefore, will arise that salvation and redemption which the human race

Therefore, the elementary life leads to the good disposition of the body, and is chiefly occupied with the natural faculty or power existing therein according to the laws of nature: Its primary duty is to nourish through addition, union, and assimilation; to increase in length, width, and depth; and to generate through the transformative power, which draws forth the seed, and the formative power, which shapes the drawn seed. Its secondary duty is to attract through straight fibers, to retain and digest through oblique fibers, and to expel through transverse fibers. <note>The author is using the medical language of the time to describe how the body functions like a machine with "fibers" that pull, hold, and push nutrition through the system.</note> Indeed, through a defect in these duties, the diseases of the body or of the man are generated and brought on; but its perfection is the cause of health and the obedience of the elements. These two extremes usually happen either because the God-like power, by turning its face away, leaves the rebellious elements the freedom to fight each other, or because, by turning its face toward some hard, raw, rebellious, and preternatural humor dwelling in the body, it excites an imbalance of natural action through its preternatural resistance, and consequently changes it into putrefaction; hence come fevers and putrid diseases. But if it should gradually turn away its "face of life," darkness usually creeps in little by little, and cold, "stupid" <note>original: "stupidi"; in this context, it refers to diseases causing numbness, stupor, or lack of sensation.</note>, raw, and frigid diseases are brought on, as we shall demonstrate below.

### CHAPTER VII.

->On the nature of the second life and its eternity; likewise on salvation and redemption.<-

Just as in the name of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note> we find a double <term>ה</term> <note>The OCR text shows a "י" (Yod), but the context of "double" and the subsequent "He" clearly refers to the letter *He* (ה), which appears twice in Y-H-V-H.</note>, namely one near and joined to the divinity of the *Yod*, and the other more remote and further immersed in the multitude of matter—insofar as the lowest waters are as far as possible from the throne of <term>Alpha</term> or <term>Jah</term>, and closest to the center of darkness; yet the first *He* is found in the waters above the firmament, where the characters of *Jah* are traced in a mystical way. Here also we see the first waters adorned with a greater grace of the *Yod* and with essential light. Whence in those waters is found the fountain and origin of eternal life, but in these lower waters there is only the food and succession of temporal life, descending from that supreme fountain. Therefore, because of the defect of the waters of life and the multitude of matter, that matter always hungers for a new form; and once the prior form is taken away, it suffers corruption and death so that it may immediately put on a new succeeding form. Hence we read that God proposed two cups to men: *one of ruin and destruction, assigned to the wicked; the other of salvation and health, prepared for the just.* For in *Psalm 11:5–6*, we find it written: *The Lord tests the righteous, but the wicked and the lover of violence his soul hates. Upon the wicked he shall rain coals, fire, and sulfur; and a wind joined with various storms shall be the portion of their cup.* And in *Psalm 23:5*, He proposes the health-giving cup to the righteous: *You have prepared a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you have anointed my head with oil; my cup overflows. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I shall rest in the house of the Lord for as long as time shall be.* Similarly, in *Psalm 116:13*: *I will take the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord.* Furthermore, we are taught in many places of the Holy Scriptures that the fountain of life is from God; for in *Psalm 36:9*, these words are held: *They are abundantly filled with the fatness of your house, and you give them to drink from the river of your delights. For with you is the fountain of life, and in your light shall we see light.* Therefore, all life flows from God sitting in the highest heavens; and this life was with the Father, and this life was in the light of the Father, which is the Word of the Father, His first emanation, and <term>Jah</term>, or God in the benevolent <term>Empyrean</term> <note>The highest part of heaven, associated with pure fire and light.</note> spirit, or the Son of the dark Alpha, and the luminous Alpha itself. This emanation is eternal life, or <term>Christ</term> and the <term>Messiah</term>, from whom is the life of all things, according to that in the *1st Epistle of St. John, chapter 1*: *The life was with the Father, and appeared to us.* Eternal life is promised to us: *Ibid. chapter 2.* Life is from Christ: *Ibid. chapter 4. God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.* From this eternal life or light, insofar as its nature and power are considered in the supreme *He*—where it is covered by a single, most subtle, thin, and benevolent garment—proceeds that most powerful and ineffable act of rising from the dead; the effect of which is called the "second life." Concerning which, in *Revelation 21*: *In the second life there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor pain anymore; in this second life they shall thirst no more, nor hunger, nor shall the Sun fall upon them, nor any heat, because the Lamb is in the midst of the throne, and rules them, and shall lead them to the living fountains of waters, and God shall wipe away every tear from their eyes, as it is held in Revelation 7:16.* And these things agree with that passage in *Isaiah 30:26*: *And the light of the Moon shall be as the light of the Sun, and the light of the Sun shall be sevenfold, like the light of seven days;* by which it is signified that the uncreated light of the world shall descend into the midst of the throne, that is, into the place of the Sun, and shall take upon itself the office of the Sun, and shall make the New <term>Jerusalem</term> descend upon the earth, etc. For that light is that <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Sapientia"; often personified in this tradition as the feminine aspect of God or the Logos.</note> which is the splendor of eternal light and the emanation of the brightness of the Almighty...

## CHAPTER VI.

### On the nature of the benevolent action of the power of the Tetragrammaton regarding life and health: And how this same power, leading to life and health, acquires various names in the world according to the diversity of its garments.

Through the preceding arguments, it is explained more clearly than the noonday sun (as I believe) even to anyone overwhelmed by the darkness of great foolishness and ignorance, why the name of the God <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The author uses "Jehovah" as the vocalization of the Tetragrammaton (YHWH), representing the active presence of God in the world.</note> is used in natural things, since He Himself exists outside and beyond all things, and is said to reign in His secret and hidden heaven without any regard for matter. Truly, His name is used there where the authority and power of that name, clothed in Spirit, is understood, insofar as it dominates in all things. Furthermore, it is called an "Angel" insofar as the spiritual matter of the angel—which the presence of the name of Jehovah produced—is denoted; and thus it is also called a "Messenger," according to that passage in Malachi 3: *Behold, I send my angel,* etc. That is to say, the power of my name, which is in the angelic spirit, moves it to fulfill the will of its creator; where by "angel" His Word is understood, according to that passage in Psalm 40:9: *Behold, I come; in the volume of the book it is written of me, that I should do thy will.* For all action is from God; but passion <note>In this context, "passion" refers to the capacity to be acted upon or to receive an influence, rather than an emotion.</note> is from the created spirit. And hence it happens that the naming of an angel comes from the passive and created part, just as the word "cloud" is placed before the word "fire." For this reason, David in Psalm 104:4 called the angels "winds" or "spirits," looking to their created nature; yet joining the created part with the uncreated, he denotes action within the passive. Whence in the same place he calls them "ministers" and "flaming fire"; that is, bright creatures created from the Spirit, illuminated on the first day.

Moreover, the <term>Messiah</term> <note>In this Hermetic-Kabbalistic context, the "Messiah" is viewed as a cosmic principle of light and mediation, rather than strictly a historical figure.</note> is the light-filled power of the very letter of the ineffable name, insofar as it is considered in nature clothed with the life-giving Spirit of the first letter in the name of Jehovah (<term>Jod</term>), according to whose pattern the Empyrean Spirit was created. Therefore, the "being" of the Word is in the Tetragrammaton and its spirit; the "being" of the Angel is in the Word, or the power flowing forth from *Jod*, which the Tetragrammaton signifies; and the "being" of nature is in the soul of the angel <term>Metattron</term> and the dual inferior spirit; finally, the "being" of all composite things is in the soul of nature. And all these differences are accepted in respect to the diversity of the matter in which the power of the Tetragrammaton works; insofar as all multiplicity is in matter; while conversely, the potency and power of the Tetragrammaton, which is the Messiah himself, is one and the same through all things. Indeed, the diversity of matter resisting in different ways makes the acts of the active power seem diverse to us, though they are not so in respect to the divinity; inasmuch as there, all acts are the same, and weighed in the same scales of highest justice. Therefore this power, carrying before it the presence of God Jehovah, when it immersed itself into the first created spirit, received its name from the nature of the Spirit: hence it is called an "Angel." Descending into the lower world, where it puts on a manifold garment, it is called "Nature"; entering into any thing, whether simple or composite, it is called "Life." And from here arose the opinions of the Ethnic <note>The "Ethnic" or Heathen philosophers, referring to the Greeks and Romans.</note> philosophers, affirming that "all things are full of Gods": hence also Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Apollo, Venus, Mercury, and Diana were treated with divine worship as Gods because of their copious reception of this power. God is stripped of all substance; the root of all created things is *Jod*; whose power, emanating from the "Holy, Holy, Holy" heavens into *He* <note>The author is tracing the descent of divine power through the Hebrew letters of God's name, Y-H-V-H.</note>, is the Messiah; whence <term>Jah</term> is referred to kindness, and kindness is attributed to the son. And this power in the first created Spirit is the mind or intelligence; moreover, the intelligence is the angel, who, putting on the middle spirit, is called Metattron; and the power of the Messiah in its center is called the <term>anima mundi</term> <note>Latin: "Soul of the World."</note>; and finally, the angel putting on an elementary garment is called Nature, which retains all higher things within itself.

Therefore, by the benevolent presence of this divine power, life and health are present; but its particular absence is followed by disease, and its total absence by death. Thus, in the higher spirit, the Messiah gives an invisibly bright life without any obscurity; whence angels are said to stand always before the face of Jehovah. In the middle, he gives a life partly visibly and partly invisibly bright, participating moderately in darkness; whence also the spirit is said to participate in both extremes. In this heaven, therefore, free will begins because of the increase of matter; since its nature is to adhere now to the higher, now to the lower. Here, therefore, matter mixes itself equally with the divine nature: and this is the reason why Fate is said to dwell in this place. Furthermore, in the last and lowest spirit, he includes the bright life emanating from both higher levels into a cubic and opaque body; where, because of the narrowness of the enclosed light, unless the power of Jehovah constantly assists it, it is oppressed—not indeed in respect to itself, as it does not suffer; but in respect to the passive and created spirit, by which it is said to be clothed as if in various garments and covered as far as human understanding goes. And from here it is that the super-celestial life is that immortal one, by whose power man shall be free from the death of the inferior spirit according to the divine promise, and believes with a certain and indubitable faith that he will rise again: from here, therefore, will arise that salvation and redemption, which the human race...

...the hand awaits through the arrival and descent of that power from St. Paul’s "third heaven." <note>In 2 Corinthians 12:2, Paul describes being caught up to the "third heaven," which this author views as the source of divine vital power.</note> Heavenly life is that which serves the days of man existing upon the earth; yet it is often afflicted by the restlessness of <term>Metattron</term> <note>Metattron (or Metatron) is a high archangel in Kabbalistic tradition, often interpreted by Renaissance philosophers as the "Soul of the World" that mediates between the divine and the physical.</note> due to a lack of the soul's power. Its primary duty is to nourish through "apposition, union, and assimilation" <note>This refers to the three stages of nutrition: bringing food to the tissue, joining it, and transforming it into the body's own substance.</note>; to increase in length, breadth, and depth; and to generate through the "transforming power" (which produces the seed) and the "formative power" (which shapes the produced seed). Its secondary duty is to attract through straight fibers, to retain and "concoct" <note>A term for digestion or the ripening of bodily fluids.</note> through oblique fibers, and to expel through transverse fibers. <note>The author is using a 17th-century anatomical theory where different types of muscle or tissue fibers were thought to perform specific mechanical tasks in the organs.</note> Truly, through a defect in these duties, the diseases of the body—or the "external man"—are generated and brought on; but their perfection is the cause of health and the obedience of the elements. These two extremes usually happen either because the Deiform power <note>The God-like power within nature.</note>, by turning its face away, leaves the rebellious elements the freedom to attack one another; or because, by turning its face toward some harsh, raw, rebellious, and unnatural humor dwelling in the body, it excites an imbalance of natural action through its unnatural resistance, and consequently turns it into putrefaction. From this come fevers and putrid diseases. But if it should gradually turn its "face of life" away, darkness is accustomed to creep in by degrees, and cold, numbing, raw, and frigid diseases are brought on, as we shall demonstrate below.

### CHAPTER VII.

->*On the second life, and the nature of its eternity; likewise on*<-
->*salvation and redemption.*<-

Just as in the name of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH (Yahweh or Jehovah).</note> we find a double <note>original: "ה"</note> [He]—namely one close and joined to the divinity of <note>original: "Jod"</note> [Jod], and the other more remote and immersed more deeply in the multitude of matter, insofar as the lowest waters are as far as possible from the throne of <note>original: "Alpha vel Jah"</note> [Alpha or Jah] and as close as possible to the center of darkness—so also we see that the first "He" is found in the waters above the firmament, where the characters of <note>original: "Jah"</note> [Jah] are sketched in a mystical way. Thus we also see the first waters adorned with a greater [Jod] of grace and essential light. For this reason, the fountain and origin of eternal life is found in those waters; but in these [lower waters], there is nothing but the food and succession of temporal life, descending from that supreme fountain. Therefore, because of a lack of the "waters of life" and because of the density of matter, that matter always hungers for a new form; and once the prior form is taken away, it suffers corruption and death so that it may immediately put on a new succeeding form. Hence we read that God proposed two cups to men: one of ruin and destruction, assigned to the wicked; the other of salvation and health, prepared for the righteous. For in *Psalm 11:5-6* we find it written: *Jehovah examines the righteous, but his soul hates the wicked and the lover of violence. He rains coals, fire, and sulfur upon the wicked; and a wind joined with a diverse storm shall be the portion of their cup.* And in *Psalm 23:5*: *He offers the cup of salvation to the righteous; You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you refresh my head with oil; my cup overflows; surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I shall rest in the house of Jehovah as long as time endures.* Similarly, in *Psalm 116:13*: *I will take the cup of salvation and proclaim the name of Jehovah.* Furthermore, we are taught in many places of the Holy Scriptures that the fountain of life is from God; for in *Psalm 36:9* these words are held:

> *They are most abundantly filled with the fatness of your house, and you give them drink from the torrent of your delights. For with you is the fountain of life, and in your light we shall enjoy light.*

All life, therefore, flows from God sitting in the highest heavens; and this life was with the Father, and this life was in the light of the Father, which is the Word of the Father, His first emanation, and <note>original: "Jah"</note> [Jah], or God in the benevolent <term>Empyrean</term> <note>The highest heaven, characterized by pure light and fire.</note> spirit, or the Son of the dark Alpha, and the luminous Alpha itself. This emanation is eternal life, or Christ and the Messiah, from whom is the life of all things, according to that passage in the *First Epistle of St. John, Chapter 1*: *The life was with the Father and appeared to us.* Eternal life is promised to us in the *same, Chapter 2*. Life is from Christ: *the same, Chapter 4*: *God gave us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.* From this eternal life or light—insofar as its nature and power are considered in the supreme [He], where it is covered by a single garment that is most subtle, thin, and benevolent—proceeds that most powerful and ineffable act of rising from the dead. The effect of this is called the "second life." Concerning this, in *Revelation 21*: *In the second life there shall be no more death, nor sadness, nor pain any longer; in this second life they shall thirst no more, nor hunger, nor shall the sun fall upon them, nor any heat, because the Lamb is in the midst of the throne and rules them, and will lead them to the living fountains of waters; and God shall wipe away every tear from their eyes,* as is found in *Revelation 7:16*. And these things agree with that passage in *Isaiah 30:26*: *And the light of the moon itself shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, like the light of seven days.* By this it is signified that the uncreated light of the world shall descend into the midst of the throne—that is, into the place of the sun—and shall take upon itself the office of the sun, and shall make the New Jerusalem descend upon the earth, etc. For that light is that Wisdom, which is the brightness of eternal light and the emanation of the glory of the Almighty.

...more precious than the sun, and above every disposition; compared to the Moon, it is found to be prior, as it is written in the *Book of Wisdom, chapter 7.* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 7:29: "For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of stars: being compared with the light, she is found before it."</note> This uncreated wisdom, therefore, flows from <term>Jod</term> <note>The letter 'Y', the first letter of the Hebrew name of God, representing the primordial point of creation.</note> into a spirit that is obedient, refined, kind, and humble; in which the Messiah first exercised his kindness of life. Hence this Deity is called <term>Jah</term> <note>A shortened, poetic form of the name of God (Yah), often associated with divine breath and life.</note>, as if it were kindness, grace, life, and a benevolent light: which kindness God exercises toward the living as well as the dead, according to *Ruth 2:20.* For God does not only follow His people with His kindness and salvation in this life (*Psalm 106:4*), but He also works the fulfillment of the "second life." Therefore, God's kindness is better than life itself, as the Psalmist testifies in *Psalm 63*, because it not only produces the life of this world, but also raises the dead to the perfection of the second and incorruptible life. Hence it is written of Him in *Psalm 57:11*: *The kindness of God is great even unto the heavens, and His truth even unto the higher clouds.* <note>original: "Benignitas Dei magna est usque ad cœlos, & veritas ejus usque ad nubes superiores."</note> This kindness, this light of the face of <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, this God-shaped wisdom, this infinite grace, this power of the Tetragrammaton—this Messiah is the extraordinary Savior in this life and in the second life, insofar as he is adorned with the simple power of the <term>Empyrean spirit</term> <note>The highest, most refined level of the heavens, composed of pure light or fire.</note>, in which he exercises the greatest grace and kindness. Therefore, in this life, the power of <term>Aleph</term> <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, symbolizing the divine unity and the beginning of spiritual work.</note>, clothed in a simple, shining garment, effects regeneration: and hence David says in *Psalm 51:12*: *Create in me a clean soul, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me: Cast me not away from Thy face, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me: Restore to me the joy of Thy salvation, and uphold me with a noble spirit.* Here the Prophet seems to suggest that the joy of salvation is the illumination of the mind, according to that which we cited above: *In Thy light we shall see light.*

And this first appearance of divine power works upon the divine mind; since it looks only upon the light nearest to its own nature and delights in regenerating it. Hence Wisdom says: *My delights or pleasures are with the sons of men* (*Proverbs 8:31*).

Through the presence of this divine kindness, ordinary men are turned into Prophets; they cannot be such without the breath of the divine Spirit, as we can gather from *Numbers 11:25–30*. Nor can anyone be skilled in any art without the spirit of wisdom: For in *Psalm 143*, God teaches by *His good spirit.* Similarly, the *holy spirit of discipline* is the Teacher of true knowledge, as *Exodus 28:3, 31:3, and 35:30* teach us.

From these things it is manifest that the life and kindness of Jehovah, clothed only in the letter <term>He</term> <note>The second and fourth letters of the name YHWH, often linked to the soul's ability to receive divine life.</note>, vivifies and illuminates only the mind. By this illumination, the whole man is regenerated according to that passage in *Wisdom 9* so often repeated: *The body that is corrupted weighs down the soul, and the earthly dwelling oppresses the mind that ponders many things; and we estimate with difficulty the things that are on earth, and we find with labor the things that are before our eyes: but who shall track out the things that are in the heavens? And who shall know Your mind, unless You give wisdom and send Your spirit from the highest?* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 9:15-17.</note> <term>Hermes Trismegistus</term> <note>A legendary figure representing the synthesis of Greek and Egyptian wisdom, central to Renaissance philosophy.</note> seems to have dealt with this power of the Tetragrammaton in the *Pimander, Book 4*, saying: *Whoever is supported by this nature of God, though considered mortal by comparison of their works, are held to be immortal; by their intelligence they embrace all things that are on the earth, and in the sea, and if there is anything beyond them above the heaven, and they raise themselves up to contemplate the Good itself; and when they behold it, they consider the life we feed upon here to be a kind of misery, etc.*

By these words, the wise man seems to argue for a twofold life: namely, the super-heavenly and intellectual life, which is poured into the mind and brings about regeneration in this age and resurrection in the age to come; and the heavenly or ethereal life, which the body uses in this age and upon whose assistance we feed, of which we will treat in the following chapter. Hence, therefore, Hermes Trismegistus in the *Pimander, Book 12* called the spirit of wisdom the "Mind," which is born from the Essence itself (if such is its essence); he asserts that this essence is by no means divided from God Himself, but rather joined to Him in the same way that light is joined to the body of the sun. And in the same discourse he says: *The Mind is the prince of all things, and the soul of God can accomplish whatever it wishes*; that is, the Soul of <term>Jah</term>, which is the emanation or power of Jod, or the Tetragrammaton. And again he says that the *Mind of the soul of God dominates all things, including the law and all else; and that nothing pertaining to salvation is impossible for the mind, and therefore the human mind is superior to fate.* And all this he understood as being about the divine power adorned with its first worldly clothing, which looks only upon its likeness in man and illuminates it. David speaks of this light in these words in *Psalm 18:28*: *For You light my lamp, Jehovah my God, making my darkness shine.* <note>original: "Situ illustras lucernam meam Iehova Deus meus, splendentes efficit tenebras meas." Latin verse numbering varies from English Bibles.</note> Here "lamp" is taken for life and light, of which the human mind is king. Hence *Proverbs 13:9*: *The light of the righteous shall be bright; but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.* And *Psalm 84:11*: *Jehovah God is a sun, giving grace and glory.* Hermes Trismegistus, speaking of this regeneration in the *Pimander, Book 13*, says that the body, sensible by nature, differs greatly from essential regeneration; for one is dissoluble, the other indissoluble; the former mortal, the latter immortal. *Are you unaware that God and one son are born?* By these words he seems to confirm that just as the vital soul, born from heaven and ethereal, vivifies man’s visible part (namely the body), so also the Mind vivifies his airy part and imbues it with immortality before it is separated from the body through death. And this is that outer part of the internal man which is illuminated by the rays of the divine mind, and by the preceding illumination is regenerated through the happiness of the indwelling mind. Moreover, the way of acquiring regeneration, according to Hermes Trismegistus in the *Pimander, Book 13*, is obtained in this manner: *Return,* he says, *into yourself; purge the senses of the body, and free yourself from the irrational avengers of matter itself. For these avengers are not few within you, but horrible and many. For this one is the avenger: ignorance; the second, sadness; the third, inconstancy; the fourth, greed; the fifth, injustice; the sixth, luxury; the seventh, deception; the eighth...*

...envy, the ninth is fraud, the tenth is anger, the eleventh is rashness, and the twelfth is malice. These are indeed twelve in number, and under them many others are contained, which, through the prison of the body, force the imprisoned and sorrowful man to suffer in his senses. However, these are absent from him who relies upon the mercy of God. But all these avenging vices are expelled solely by the divine infusion of the <term>Spirit of Wisdom</term> <note>In this context, Wisdom is viewed as a cleansing, divine force that renovates the human mind.</note> into the region of the human mind; and consequently, a complete regeneration is then achieved. For, by the sending of Wisdom from the Holy Heavens, the "knowledge of God" descends into us (to use the words of <term>Hermes Trismegistus</term> <note>original: "Mercur: Trismeg:". A legendary Hellenistic figure regarded as the author of the Hermetic Corpus, which explores the relationship between the divine and the material.</note>); whence, upon its arrival, ignorance is driven away. Next, with the knowledge of God, the "knowledge of joy" descends into us; and while this is present, sorrow flees entirely, turning instead toward those who are prepared to receive it. Afterward, I call upon the power of "constancy" which leads to joy, by whose strength inconstancy is expelled. In the fourth place, "continence" enters with the Spirit of Wisdom, which drives out the victorious lusts; and this step is the foundation of justice, by whose presence injustice is thrust away. This same virtue also prevails against excess and luxury. "Truth" also removes deception, since Wisdom and Christ are the sole and very Truth itself. The "good of truth" expels envy; and so it is with the rest. For this Spirit, proceeding from <term>Jod</term> <note>The Hebrew letter 'Yod', symbolizing the primordial point of God's creative power.</note>, is a strength stronger than all other strengths; hence it is necessary that the madness of the avengers and demons give way to it. 

But since this same power of the Spirit of regeneration is proposed everywhere in the Holy Scriptures, we shall therefore proceed to the logic of the resurrection. Just as this most noble virtue of <term>Jehovah</term>—namely, the light and splendor emanating immediately from *Jod*—was the occasion for regeneration in this life (a splendor of regeneration which was fully and perfectly present in Adam before his Fall, insofar as he always had this divine ray joined to himself in the Paradise of Pleasure); but after his expulsion from the Paradise of Pleasure due to disobedience, it receded from him, and is now occasionally infused into the minds of some of his successors by the operation of divine grace; seeing that what was then a gift of creation granted to Adam is now a gift of grace flowing into man through the Messiah, or the power of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God (YHWH), used here as a source of restorative power.</note>, endowed in the first life. As I say, just as this virtue was the reason for regeneration in this life after the Fall of Adam, or the restoration of Adam’s fallen nature; so also in the second life, it will be the true occasion for the resurrection after death. For it belongs to the supreme life to re-enliven that which is lowest, subject to fate, and cast down into bodily corruption; and thus, through the resurrection, the body shall be recalled from death into life. 

Therefore, with the life-giving Spirit leading the way, Christ rising from the dead no longer dies (as the resolution of the theologians holds), and by His resurrection, He destroyed our double death—namely, of the body and the soul—which are darkened because of sin. And hence, according to *St. Paul in 1 Corinthians 15*, *Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep*, that is, He rose first in time and in dignity. Whence, by His resurrection, He is said to have conquered death first of all. For, as the first Adam introduced death into the world by his Fall, so also Christ, the Last Adam, has liberated the successors of the first Adam from both corporal and spiritual death by the radiant power of the most holy Spirit of Wisdom. For this Spirit is so pure and subtle, and that Word of Jehovah is so polished and clean (which stood out like *refined silver in a furnace, purified seven times: Psalm 12:7*), that by its presence, that body which is sown in corruption is raised in incorruption; that which is buried in dishonor rises in glory; that which is cast into the earth in weakness is raised in power; that which is naturally committed to oblivion and the bowels of the earth is supernaturally exalted; and from a coarse body subject to death and change, there arises thereafter a spiritual, most pure, and immortal body. St. Paul seems to indicate all these things in *1 Corinthians 15, verse 40*, for he also teaches us that, as the first man Adam was made a living soul, so also the last Adam was made a life-giving Spirit. Therefore, the natural was first, and the second was spiritual; that man made of the earth was earthly, while this one, existing from God, was made super-celestial.

Concerning this place, Jacob also spoke in Genesis 28: *This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven:* And rising in the morning, Jacob took that stone, and so forth. Does not Ecclesiasticus 24:33 <note>original: "Ecclesiast. 24. a. 33." This refers to the Book of Sirach in the Vulgate Bible.</note> most excellently describe this place of pleasure with a discourse of this kind: *The Lord Almighty is God alone, and there is no other Savior besides Him, who fills all things like the Pishon with His wisdom, and like the Tigris in the days of new fruits; who fills like the Euphrates with understanding, and like the Jordan in the days of harvest; who shows instruction like the light, and like the Gihon in the days of the yellowing harvest:* <note>The author uses the four rivers of Paradise to represent different aspects of divine wisdom flowing into the world.</note> I, Wisdom, am like a ditch led from a river; and like an aqueduct, I have gone forth into paradise: I said, I will water my excellent garden, and I will soak my righteous flowerbed, and so forth. From these things, it is clear who the Savior is—namely, Jehovah—and how He works—namely, through His wisdom; in whose right hand is life and length of days. From this, therefore, one may see how immense is the power of <term>Jah</term> <note>original: "Jah". A shortened form of the Hebrew divine name YHWH, often associated with divine breath or praise.</note>, or the power of <term>Yod in He</term> <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton (Y-H-W-H). In this mystical system, the "Yod" represents the masculine seed of light and "He" the feminine vessel or breath.</note> in the salvation and redemption of men; how, according to Psalm 41:3, Jehovah is the restorer of life, by what means the illumination of the human mind and the regeneration of the internal man through Christ occurs, and finally, by what means the resurrection from the dead to the second life is to be expected; namely, by the splendor and clarity proceeding immediately from Yod into He, or from God into the thin and intellectual worldly spirit. There, the same uncreated power, plunging itself into the first spirit, joins the formal and <term>supersubstantial</term> <note>Referring to a reality that exists above or beyond physical substance.</note> character of "Yod" with the spiritual character of the mass of darkness into which "Yod" is imprinted. In other words, the power of Yod puts on its "first garment"; without this medium, it could not have plunged itself more deeply into the lower darkness. And from this, it receives its name, partly from the material character and partly from the formal, indicating by this very fact that God joined Himself with the matter to be created; and thus the "upper waters" were created. That is to say, the creature is named after the matter; because it is distinguished by the name of "form," it is said that on the first day "light" was created—that is, the purest, illuminated, and informed waters, which receive that name because of the dominion of light within them. Thus, therefore, the first part of the name <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, "Jah," was produced, which is a symbol of kindness and grace, since by its power men, overwhelmed and laboring under ignorance and sin, are redeemed and saved—first by regeneration, and then by the resurrection into the second life. Indeed, we could compose an infinite volume on this hidden work because of the vastness of the field; but, since the subject of this treatise constrains us and keeps us within methodical boundaries, we shall hasten toward the nature of that very power which puts on a double garment.

## CHAPTER VIII.

->*That temporal life, which we enjoy here, proceeds from the Messiah or Jehovah by action and power, covered and overshadowed by a double garment: And that the Sun is the seat of life.*<-

<term>Hermes Trismegistus</term> in the *Pimander*, book 12, making mention of this power of the Tetragrammaton, calls it "Mind" <note>original: "Mentem".</note>, and he seems to distribute it in many ways according to the diversity of its garments. For he establishes that the Mind first exists adorned with a spiritual garment of the essence of God (if there be any essence of God); yet in such a way that it is by no means divided from the essence of God. And he attributes a portion of this Mind to humans alone because of its excellence. Therefore, he affirms that some among the number of men are "Gods," and says that through this, their humanity is nearest to divinity. From this, he seems to understand that power or emanation of God which flowed most closely and immediately from God into the <term>Empyrean Spirit</term> <note>The highest part of the heavens, believed by ancient philosophers to be composed of pure fire or light.</note> on the first day of creation. Again, concerning the "second mind," he uses this kind of discourse: *In irrational animals, that mind is Nature.* These are his words: *Mind (he says) is twofold; the lower and the first. The lower is an image of the mind or a certain footprint, following after the exact determination of the first mind; it associates itself with individual animals; but in irrational ones, the mind is Nature, while in humans, it is reason.* And David in Psalm 63 seems to make a difference between the "superior," which he calls kindness, and the "kindly spirit" in Wisdom 1, and the "inferior," which he calls life. These are his words: *The kindness of God is better than life.* And yet, elsewhere he seems to take "kindness" itself to mean "life": whence in Psalm 30:6, *Life is present in the benevolence of Jehovah.* And Saint John says that life is the light of the world; and elsewhere in Chapter 1, he declares life to be in the Word; and again elsewhere, that life is with the Father. And Deuteronomy 30:15: *Jehovah God Himself is your life, and the multitude of your days.* And in the first Epistle of Saint John: *Life is from Christ.* Just as Jehovah and the Word are called "life," so indeed that life is called "eternal," which we mentioned before. And thus "kindness" is said to be better than the life we enjoy. But insofar as life is said to be from Christ, and in the Word, to that extent it is understood or accepted as the common life of any creature. Thus John wrote that *all things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made that was made.* From these things, it is argued that there is a superior life, which, adorned with its simple garment, gives immortality; and it is the most holy wisdom in the thin spirit, the first emanation of light, which is the act giving life to all things. Concerning which Hermes Trismegistus speaks thus: *The Mind, the soul of God, dominates all things—even the law, as well as all other things. Indeed, Jah is the fountain of all life.*
