The second letter of the Tetragrammaton, often associated with the divine breath or the first manifestation of spirit.</note> the covering <term>Vau</term> <note>original: ו (Vau). The third letter of the Tetragrammaton, symbolizing the connection between the upper and lower worlds.</note>; so that on account of the thickness of its outer garment, its rays are constricted, and because of the resistance of the spirit, they are perceived to act more harshly than when clothed in the simple Empyrean spirit. From this, the Messiah has marked its light with life—once the triple heap of darkness was stretched out—and thus every creature of the two lower regions was formed and gifted with life. This, therefore, is the **Soul of the World**, the ray constituting nature, a secondary emanation of wisdom sent downward from Jah; which in its essence of nature is continuous with Jah, but in its action differs from Jah because of the multitude of spiritual matter enclosing it. And from this it follows that it produces life, not eternal, but secular and determined: For ethereal matter (which, because of its hundredfold multitude, is prone to rebellion), when joined together with the elementary or cubic body, is rendered subject to changes and alterations by participating with it. From this follow diseases, intemperance, and other such things contrary to the laws of nature.

Therefore, just as the uncreated virtue—whether the Messiah, or the fiery spirit—proceeding immediately from <term>Yod</term> <note>original: י (Yod). The first letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the point of origin or the seed of creation.</note> from the supersubstantial kingdom, is the simplest soul of the simple <term>He</term>; so also Jah himself, or the divine virtue and soul with <term>He</term> (that is, the intellectual spirit together with its mind), is the soul of the ethereal spirit. And thus the angel **Metattron** <note>Metatron is a high-ranking angel in Jewish mystical tradition, often described as the celestial scribe or the "Prince of the Countenance."</note> is procreated; whose material being is the universal moist nature, constituting the visible world beneath the intellectual heaven; but its soul is Jah. And here Metattron is called the soul of the visible world, or the simple and fiery nature, from whose rays or sparks the essences of all elements or elemental things are derived, for it is by these that they are said to exist and live in peace. And so we see that in the production of the creatures of the first composition, the very virtue of the Tetragrammaton—or the act of God, or the ray <term>Aleph</term> <note>original: א (Aleph). The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, signifying unity and the breath of the Creator.</note>, or the Word emanating immediately from the mouth of the Lord, or the kindness of Jehovah, or the wisdom of the Omnipotent, or the origin of life—is the soul; and thus we have the inanimate soul in its simplicity, and such a virginal spirit, which never knew any other besides that Cupid <note>The author uses "Cupid" here in the classical sense of "desire" or "divine love" that drives creation.</note>. Next, the rivulets of that blessed and fiery fountain of life, tending further downward, expel the darkness from the ether, informing it and animating it with life: And this soul of the firmament is not called the simple virtue of the Tetragrammaton, but is composed of the uncreated splendor of **Yod**, and the spirit **He**, or the Empyrean; and thus this is the **Soul of the World**, inasmuch as its body is the spirit of the visible world, and its heart is the Sun itself, or the tabernacle of the Messiah: Whence, on account of the equality of the uncomposed soul in the nature of **Yod** and **He**, it is called the *sphere of equality*.

Furthermore, the **Vau** in the name of **Jehovah** denotes the soul of the firmament: For, as **Vau**, denoting 6, consists of 5 and 1, or **He** and **Yod**; so it denotes that the soul of this place is partly from **He** and **Yod**; which is the same in composition as **Aleph** without regard for matter: Whence, from the nature of the middle letter **Vau** between **He** and **Yod**, we gather that the Soul of the World is **Jah**; which name of God proves the first entry of God into the world. And so we see that, although the Messiah is not in such simplicity with respect to the outer garment in this heaven as he was in the higher one, it is nevertheless clearly evident that his virtue, both in the heavens and on earth, does everything, and acts through himself, and that without him there is no act in this world: But he acts by degrees. For first, he moves according to his will the obedient moist nature of the spirit **He**, whether intellectual or Empyrean; and he again, moved by his internal principle, like a secondary soul or the light created on the first day, impels the ethereal spirit to execute the vital faculty, and continually excites it for the common benefit. To perform this better, the Messiah—or the virtue of Jehovah—dispersed in this region to drive away the darkness, finally on the fourth day of creation (or the fourth emanation of wisdom) gathered it from the darkness into the solar mass; and thus the **Sun** was made in the visible world as the tabernacle of that Deiform virtue, rejoicing in the higher **He**. Hence the deeper Philosophers, looking more closely into the matter, said that all celestial bodies receive light and life from the Sun, as the king of the Planets holding the scepter and empire in all the heavens; and that it is given to him to govern the world through the angel **Michael**, or, as the Kabbalists prefer, **Metattron**: But we, with others, attribute to his ministry the angel **Raphael**, that is, the *Medicine of God* <note>original: "Medicina Dei". The name Raphael is derived from the Hebrew root for "healing."</note>, insofar as he heals all things, restores those fallen into sickness, and preserves health. This, then, is the chief seat of the Word in the visible world; the foundation of which palace Jehovah made an **angular Carbuncle** <note>A "carbuncle" is a glowing red gemstone; here used as a metaphor for the sun as a cornerstone or radiant center of the universe.</note> cast forth from his mouth, so that he might appear visibly to the visible world to illuminate all things: Wherefore Plato and other wise men not ineptly called the Sun the **visible son of the invisible God**. And the Apostle Matthew seems to confirm this same thing, though not in express words, when he says through the mouth of Christ: *Your Father makes His sun to rise*, etc. <note>Matthew 5:45.</note> Surely by the sun he seems to understand comfort and kindness: By "His sun," he understands the luminous nature proceeding from Him; by the name of the Father, he denotes the Father of both His sun and of man, whose fleshly substance that Deiform Solar Spirit put on, according to that of Genesis 1:15: *He placed the greater light over the day, and to illuminate the visible world;* He created it also to separate the darkness of the night from the light of the day. This same thing the Messiah does in invisible things and the invisible world: And again, Psalm 136: *Who made the sun to obtain dominion by day; for His mercy is forever:* <note>Psalm 136:8.</note> Nothing, however, except the Messiah alone, who is the true light, has dominion over the darkness. Therefore, the Deiform virtue in the Empyrean heaven is the ray of **Yod**; in the ethereal heaven it is the light of the Sun, and in the lowest elemen-

->### CHAPTER IX.<-

->*On the composition of the life of creatures, and on its nature both*<-
->*passive as well as active.*<-

**B**y the reasons previously alleged, it is declared that the virtue or ray of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH (יהוה).</note> is the unity and root of created things, and God himself. Thus "otherness," made from <term>Jod</term> <note>original: י (Jod). The first letter of the Divine Name, representing the point of origin or the Father.</note> and <term>He</term> <note>original: ה (He). The second letter, representing the first manifestation or the Mother/Spirit.</note>, is an angelic composition or duality which, when joined with a third nature—namely, mixing itself with the thicker spirit of the firmament—produces a higher and simple nature from which the vital soul is accustomed to spring.

We see, therefore, that the life of the intellectual heaven <term>Jah</term> <note>original: יה (Jah). A shortened form of the divine name.</note> is the supersubstantial act of Jod, which belongs to divinity; in composition it is the root and becomes *Jah*. And the life of the ethereal spirit is Jod and He—that is, uncreated light in the first created spirit—and it becomes Jod, He, and <term>Vau</term> <note>original: ו (Vau). The third letter, representing the "Son" or the connecting link between heaven and earth.</note> <note>original: יהו (Jahu/Jeho).</note>, which is to say: uncreated light, the first created spirit, and the second created spirit. This is a double *He* and *Vau*, or unity; and this is the **seal**, by whose impressions all elemental creatures are marked with the impressions of life—which seal is indeed called **Nature** itself.

Then a fourth nature, namely the final <term>He</term> <note>original: ה (He). The fourth letter of the Name, associated with the physical world and the "Kingdom" (Malkuth).</note>, joined with those three, brings forth the airy or elementary spirit, producing a dense elementary spirit which we call "weak Nature" and "less simple." By its action, the composite body or "palace"—whether mineral, vegetable, or animal—is built up. In this manner, the world is completed in the image of the Tetragrammaton.

Therefore, the Mind or the Messiah is the soul and life of the angels; the Sun or *Jah* in the ethereal spirit is the soul and life of the stars (distributed into three kinds of composition); and the igneous element (in whose womb the Messiah is sometimes seen to appear from the outside, covered by a dense cloud and a dark veil both during and after creation) is the restorer of the body and of elemental things—provided it is capable of receiving the higher appearances of the Messiah in his simple or folded garments.

Wherefore we see that the uncreated virtue or Igneous Spirit of Jehovah is the general life or soul of all things, but operating diversely in the world according to the diversity of its covering or garment. When existing by itself, it is called the **Word**; in the Empyrean spirit it is called the **Mind** or "acting intellect," and its spirit is called the "passive intellect" or **Reason**; in the ethereal spirit it is called the **Soul**, and its spirit is called the "vital spirit"; in the elementary spirit it is called the "elemental form"; and in the creature itself, it is called **Life**.

Hence, Mercurius Trismegistus did not speak poorly when he said: *The Word is in the mind, the mind in reason, reason in the soul, and the soul in the spirit, and finally the spirit with all these is in the body.* <note>original: "Verbum in mente, mens in ratione, ratio in anima, & anima in spiritu, atque tandem spiritus cum his omnibus in corpore."</note> From these things it is manifest that for the life of higher creatures, both a moist and an igneous nature are required—namely, divine light in an obedient and subtle spirit. But since the spiritual part of life in this heaven is very obedient to the uncreated light, which abounds in it superexcellently, this life is therefore immortal and shall never perish.

Looking again toward the middle region, we find that its life also consists of a middle spirit, and an Empyrean spirit adorned and animated by light. From this it is clear that just as the form of the Empyrean heaven is the purest divinity and a mere ray of Jod, so the form informing the middle spirit is composite—namely, an informed Empyrean nature. Consequently, its form is not as effective as the higher one, because it contains within itself a spirit with a soul enclosed in that spirit. And by consequence, it is declared that the species of the "middle life" are subject to alterations because of the multitude of spiritual matter that concurs in its composition. From this it follows that this species of life, by which the body is quickened, is not durable; according to *Psalm 9:4*: *If a thousand years pass, they are in your eyes as yesterday.* <note>original: "Mille anni si præterit, sunt in oculis tuis, ut dies hesternus." Usually cited as Psalm 90 (or 89 in the Vulgate).</note> And *Psalm 39:6*: *Behold, you have made my days a few spans long, and my time is as nothing before you.* <note>original: "Ecce palmares disposuisti dies meos, & tempus meum ut nihil est coram te."</note> And *Job 7*: *Is there not a set time for mortal man on earth? Like the days of a hired hand are his days.* <note>original: "Nonne præfinitum est tempus mortali in terra? ut dies mercenarij, sic dies ejus."</note>

Similarly, this same point is signified in many places, where the cause of this brevity of life seems to be explained: namely, the multitude of spirit joined with the Empyrean ray. Hence it is said in *Psalm 109*: *I am forced to depart like a shadow when it declines.* <note>original: "Ut umbra cum declinat abire cogor."</note> And again in *Job 7:7*: *My life is wind*, etc. And *Job 14:2*: *Man born of woman is short-lived and full of trouble; like a flower, as soon as he comes forth, he is cut down, and he flees like a shadow...* <note>original: "Homo natus de muliere brevis ætate & satur comotione, ut flos simul ac egressus est, succiditur, & fugit velut umbra..."</note>

...consists. Furthermore, in **Wisdom 2:4**: *Our life is transitory like the trace of a cloud, and is dispersed like a mist, struck by the rays of the Sun and driven harder by its heat; for our time is as the passing of a shadow.* By these words, it is first declared that this "middle life" in man and other animal creatures is not eternal like the supercelestial life. Secondly, the cause of this is linked by comparing life to wind, a shadow, a cloud, and a mist; for all these are composed of a multitude of spirits. It is as if it were hinted that the material of life—which is shadowy, dense, windy, or airy and misty due to its thickness—behaves in the animal body just as a shadow, wind, cloud, or mist does; that is, it appears for a moment and then vanishes again. This happens because the supercelestial bond is not sufficient to perpetually hold together and join so many parts of the dense <term>radical moisture</term> <note>The "radical moisture" (*humidum radicale*) was believed by early modern physicians to be the vital fluid or "oil" of the lamp of life, which is gradually consumed.</note>. For by the weight of matter, we are alienated from God; and the further the smoke is from His face, the further we are from length of life, because Jehovah Himself is life. *Hence it is written in* **1 Chronicles 19:15**: *We are strangers before you; our days on earth are like a shadow, which does not remain.* Therefore, for a long life, divine benevolence is required—that is, the multiplication of the portion of the <term>Empyrean substance</term> <note>The Empyrean refers to the highest, most refined heaven of pure fire or light.</note>, wherein the fountain of kindness, wisdom, and life, and its Tree, are found. This the Psalmist also seems to prove in **Psalm 90:14**: *Life's prolongation is the kindness of God;* and in verse 17: *Let the pleasantness of Jehovah be upon us.* Similarly, in the same **Psalm, verse 10**: *The span of a man's life is miserable without God's kindness.* From this, we see that the increase of the vital soul is the kindness and Wisdom of God. For in **Proverbs 9:12**, it is found that *through Wisdom, days are multiplied, and years of life are added to a man.* And **Proverbs 3**: *Length of days is in the right hand of Wisdom.* Furthermore, **Psalm 18:29**: *If you light my lamp, Jehovah my God makes my darkness shine;* that is, He brings both the spark of life and the illumination of reason. For the lucid wisdom of Jehovah serves as much to increase the spark of life as it does to exalt the mind through regeneration.

From these stated reasons, we see that every life consists of a spirit and a spark of a supercelestial ray enclosed within it; that is, from the radical moisture and the warm virtue of the <term>Word</term> <note>The "Word" or *Verbum* refers to the Logos or the creative power of God.</note> and the Messiah infused into it. Hence, in respect to its lucid and uncreated nature, life is called "light" in **John 1**: *And the life was the light of men.* And **Mercurius Trismegistus** in *Pimander, 1*: *The Father of all, the Mind, is life; and being radiance, He procreated man like unto Himself.* And again: *Light and life bestowed the soul.* And elsewhere: *Life and light is God.* And again in *Pimander, 12.* Similarly, we find in **Proverbs 13:9**: *The light of the righteous shall rejoice, but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.* And **Job 30:20**: *To me, hoping for light, came darkness—that is, to me, hoping for life, came death.* And **Job 18:5**: *Indeed, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine.* And **Psalm 80:4**: *By the light of the face of Jehovah shall we be saved.* So also, in this same respect, it is called a "Lamp." Hence **Job 21:17**: *How often is the lamp of the wicked put out, and their destruction comes upon them.*

And as we said before, the entire essence of the world is fashioned from God and the spirit created or illuminated by His presence. When, in that same primary composition, respect is had for the "supersubstantial form," it is called the "composition of Jehovah"—as was said of the angel preceding the Israelites in the desert. Thus, **Exodus 3**: *And Jehovah appeared to him in a flame of fire, etc.*—that is, in the spirit gleaming by His presence. But when it refers to the created spirit, it is called an "Angel," which is a creature. So also here, life, in respect to the Messiah informing its spirit, is called light, a spark, a lamp, a ray of Jehovah's face, and so on; and commonly, the mind, the act, or the soul, as was demonstrated before. But indeed, having respect to its relation with the radical spirit, it is called life, wind (**Job 7:7**), *the spirit in the nostrils* (**Job 26:3**), *the breath of life* (**Genesis 2**), and it is compared to a shadow (**Job 14**), a cloud (**Job 30:15**), a mist (**Wisdom 2:4**), and so forth.

Therefore, we believe it has now been sufficiently declared how life is called "spirit"—namely, in respect to the passive part of life, which is the radical and ethereal moisture—and how it is likewise called "light" in respect to the soul—namely, in respect to the active part, which is the Empyrean or fiery spirit. With these things established, let us proceed further for the present to the principle of health and wellness.

# CHAPTER X.

## On the method of restoring and recovering lost health and wellness.

Just as it is certain from the preceding that life is the daughter of the benevolent uncreated light in spiritual matter (or darkness), so also its prolongation and happy progress proceed from the continuous succession of that same Messiah or ray of Wisdom. For the diminishing of the lucid act of the <term>Soul of the World</term> <note>The *Anima Mundi* or Soul of the World was viewed as a divine vital force that permeated all of nature.</note>—which is the very splendid essence of Jehovah, clothed in a double created garment, namely the sixth (or Empyrean) and the fifth (or ethereal) essence—brings about disease. But the increase of the same induces a happy life, according to the text:
> *When God gives, the creatures gather; when He opens His hand, they are filled with good; but when He hides His face, they are troubled; when He takes away their spirit, they expire. Psalm 104.*

By these words of the Prophet, it is explained that both disease (which he understands by "trouble") and death (which he denotes by the "expiration of the spirit"), as well as health (which he signifies by "good"), proceed from the very power of Jehovah. For health is the continuation of the life given by God for the complete wellness of man in that same perfection; that is, the successive flow of the <term>quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth essence" or quintessence was the pure, celestial substance from which the heavens were made, thought to be the most potent medicine.</note> of nature, pregnant with the solar life or the Messiah, clothed in a double garment.

...or the benevolent regard of the face of Jehovah’s power toward the life of a living creature. For without the light of the face or the power of Jehovah descending from heaven, the airy part of life in its own sphere will not be moved with a motion suitable for life; rather, it will seem to rest in the manner and nature of darkness due to the lack of an active mover. But truly life—which is the symphonic motion of light within the spirit—is the opposite of rest, just as death and deprivation (which are the companions of rest and darkness) are opposed to life (which is the daughter of motion and light). Therefore, for the existence of life, both action and passion are required. Consequently, the divine light acts as the *actor* upon the double spirit, which is *passive*. For the uncreated light first acts upon the luminous spirit, or created light, and procreates eternal life; this, in turn, is moved by the impulse of that internal principle and becomes **Jah** <note>original: "Jah." A shortened form of the Hebrew divine name, often used in mystical texts to represent the active, masculine principle of divinity acting upon the world.</note>, acting upon the ethereal spirit, which is the passive element of temporal and worldly life. And here again, this spirit is driven by its internal **Jah**, or luminous soul, into local motion. By this motion, the air—which is the final part of the internal animal—is moved to fulfill its vital function. We can also understand this from the fact that, just as life occurs in the **Macrocosm** <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "large world" or the universe as a whole.</note>, it must necessarily be perfected in the same way in the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "small world," referring to man as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note>. We find such things regarding the operation of the World Soul upon its airy passive element:

<margin>*Ecclesiastes 1:5-6*</margin>
> *The Sun rises, and after the Sun has set, it pants again toward its place where it may rise: it hurries toward the South, and circles toward the North; circling in its path, the air hurries on, and according to its circuits, the air returns.* <note>The author uses this biblical passage to show that the movement of the "World Soul" (linked to the Sun) physically drives the movement of the atmosphere.</note>

By these words, the Wise Man [Solomon] seems to imply that the visible Spirit of the world (represented by the air) is moved by the motion of the World Soul, which the Sages have placed in the Sun. In plainly the same way, the airy Spirit [in man] is moved by the solar life—which is the **quintessence**, or the ethereal light, or the ray or lamp of the World Soul. Thus, the airy spirit performs its natural function by moving the blood without ceasing. Likewise, **Jah** himself excites the ethereal spirit through the arteries to fulfill the vital faculty by an involuntary and continuous motion. Meanwhile, **Jah** himself, dwelling in the highest region of man [the head], operates in his animal power according to his will, moving all lower things at his command. So also **Jod** in **He** <note>original: "Jod in He." The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton (YHWH). In this context, it represents the Mind (Jod) acting upon the Soul (He).</note>—that is, the Mind and intellect—acting upon the rational or intellectual spirit, performs its voluntary motion with reason and intelligence.

From these things, we conclude that if the ethereal force does not sufficiently impel the airy Spirit (just as the Sun impels the air, according to the aforementioned words of the Wise Man), then the natural spirits become sluggish in their motion and induce torpor and weariness in the whole body. Consequently, the nutritive faculty and the augmentative [growth] faculty are weakened and cannot perform their duties of placement, assimilation, and union. From this follows either **Atrophy**, or **Anasarca** <term>Anasarca</term> <note>A medical term for severe, generalized swelling or edema in the body.</note>, or another disease of this kind. Furthermore, the sluggishness of the motion of the blood and natural spirits—which usually happens due to a lack of **innate heat** <note>The vital heat believed to be born with every creature, centered in the heart.</note> and a cooling of the liver—is accustomed to induce all those diseases. This is because an inclination toward rest denotes a diminution of heat and light, whose nature it is to move things naturally. For rest belongs to the nature of darkness, whose child is coldness; by its congealing power, coldness fixes and mortifies, and in this way causes mobile things to come to rest.

Conversely, if light extends itself toward the natural faculty beyond the laws of nature, it causes the air enclosed in the veins to move too rapidly, and thus very quickly absorbs the **radical moisture** <note>The vital fluid or "oil" that sustains the flame of life.</note>. This happens when **Jehovah**, being angry, looks upon a man or another animal, as we shall say below. Similarly, if the light of **Jah**, or the soul of the middle heaven, is diminished, **Melancholy, sadness, despair**, and other such affections of darkness will follow. If Jehovah looks in wrath, he induces fevers of the spirits, the plague, and other such diseases, due to the conversion of the moist nature of the ether into poison. Finally, if **Jah** does not show his benevolent rays in the highest region, he allows **Apoplexy, Paralysis, Epilepsy, Carus** <term>Carus</term> <note>A state of profound stupor or deep unconsciousness, more severe than lethargy.</note>, and other such affections of darkness to predominate. But if he looks out from his sphere in his wrath, the reason is disturbed by **phrenitis** [delirium], **leucathropia** <note>Likely a variant or error for lycanthropy (wolf-madness) or another form of mania, given the context of "fury."</note>, **mania, fury, delirium**, and the most burning pains.

On the contrary, health is that disposition of life which consists in moderation; in which, while God looks benevolently upon the spirit found in man (whether it be airy, ethereal, or empyrean), the splendor of that benevolent look relates to the spirit either by proper weight or at least by justice. Thus, the spirit is neither moved too quickly by its light (since nothing violent is long-lasting or perpetual) nor does it proceed too slowly or sluggishly in its channels, and in that way, it remains far from disease and darkness. The nature of life consists in the middle and, as it were, in the center (as we see in the position of the Sun). Therefore, the motion of the spirits must consist in a moderate condition so that it may lead to the health of life. For this is that true, beneficial power of God, which is said by Physicists to consist in the "middle," just as the moral virtues do. This is indeed what we can gather from many testimonies of the Holy Scriptures; for in **Psalm 30:6**, it is read: *Life is in the benevolence of Jehovah.*

This life is healthy when Jehovah is not found in the extremes—namely, when he does not look upon the spirit of man in wrath, according to **Psalm 6:2** and **38:2**: *The wrath of Jehovah is his heat.* And **Psalm 2:12**: *The wrath of God burned against the wicked, and he did not turn his face from them;* according to **Psalm 104:28**: *When he hides his face, the creatures are troubled; when he takes away their spirit, they die, etc.* But it is healthy when he looks upon it in a benign middle-way, according to the peaceful appetite of the spirit, etc. Hence **Psalm 27:1**: *The light is the salvation of the just, and the strength of my life.* And **Psalm 106**: *He whom God has visited with his salvation shall enjoy the good and happiness of his elect.* And **Psalm 63**: *The kindness of God is better than life;* that is, better than a life that is as much diseased as it is healthy; for kindness and wisdom hold salvation and length of days in their right hand. Therefore, by the benevolent light of Jehovah (as we have in **Psalm 80:4**), *we shall be saved.*

In the preceding sections, we have clearly dealt with the ineffable root of the world and all its creatures, **Jod**, the first member of the Tetragrammaton; and then likewise concerning **Jah** <note>original: "יה"</note>, the second; or the first stage, emanation, or aspect of the Tetragrammaton into this world, by which a most simple and pure composition is made from two things: namely, from uncreated light and a most pure and obedient spirit. 

Afterward, **Jeho** <note>original: "יהו"</note>, the third member, immersing itself in the second stage into the darkness of the region of the firmament, produced the middle composition in the world; specifically, from the spirit of **Jah** <note>original: "יה"</note> and with the emanation of **Jod** descending with **He** into **Vau**. 

And the essential emanation of the Creator, putting on a double created garment, is called the **Seal of God** <note>original: "sigillum Dei"</note> by the **Cabalists** <term>Cabalists</term> <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism. Here, the author uses it to describe how divine letters act as the "blueprint" of the universe.</note>, because by its eternal impression—like the character of the uncreated Word—all corporeal things, both celestial and elemental, are marked with the life by which they live and exist. 

But because the material clothing of this seal flows from a bright source into a multitude, that life, especially in elemental things, is not eternal, but transitory. For just as life was produced through **Jod** into **He** and **Vau** to the final **He**, so also by proceeding in a circle (for all the letters of **יהוה** are circular, as has been told), the final **He**—through a putative or imaginary death by the power of **Jod** itself (which is the power of the Tetragrammaton, or the **Messiah**, or **Jesus**, or **Christ**)—will return from the final stage of multiplicity, or the dense and dark cube, into **Vau**. 

And afterward, from **Vau**, stripping off the ethereal garment, it returns into **Jah**, namely into the angelic nature; and finally, those to whom the divine mind was given will pass from "otherness" into that very identity of **Jod** in Christ, through Christ, and with Christ. For it is certain that eternal life is from Christ descending into the first **He**; but the temporal life, which we consume here, is from Christ with his first vehicle into **Vau**. 

Both of these lives are bestowed upon man through Christ; and with the former indeed he possesses a mind, but with the second he lives in the manner of other animals. From this it is clear that man alone among other animals is found to live a double life: namely, the immortal and the mortal. Other animals, however, receive the nourishment of life from **Vau** alone, and have received the essence of animal reason from the spirit of the first heaven enclosed in darkness. From the reasons alleged above, it appears that the ineffable name of the Tetragrammaton <note>The "four-letter name" of God: YHWH</note> extends from the summit of its root, Jod, sitting fixed and permanently in the incomparable heaven of eternity, all the way to the center of the created spherical machine <note>original: "machinæ sphæricæ" (a Renaissance term for the physical universe or cosmos)</note>, filling every intermediate place of the same through the fiery power of each letter of his name. But, as we see, just as every spring, the further it is removed from its source, the more slowly and weakly it moves; and just as a ray, the more or further it is away from the flame of a candle, the less power of illumination it has; and just as the Sun likewise, the further it is distant from us, the less it warms; so also, the further the letters of the ineffable Tetragrammaton are distant from their root Jod, the less effective is the life-giving condition of Jod. Not indeed that the Messiah, who is the power of Jod, is not equally in one place as in another; but because he is accustomed to put on diverse and varied garments <note>In this context, "garments" (Latin: vestimenta) refer to the material forms or densities that veil the pure divine light as it descends into the physical world.</note>, which cause the one and the same action to differ because of the diverse respect to the matter of the garments. Therefore, the same action produces different effects: namely, sweet and life-giving in a thin and obedient spirit, and hard and harsh because of rebellion and strong resistance in a denser and more opaque spirit. For however strong a spirit may be in its resistance, it is nonetheless necessary that it be overcome by uncreated power, insofar as that is a strength stronger than all strength; which indeed is accustomed to produce truly tremendous and stupendous actions in darkness and a dense spirit; just as this ineffable power shone back terribly upon the rocky mountain of Sinai from a dense and dark cloud, and gave forth its voice: *And all the people perceived those sounds, and the lightnings, and the sound of the trumpet, and that mountain smoking; and perceiving them, they were moved from their place, and stood afar off, and said to Moses: Speak thou with us, and we will hear, but let not God speak with us, lest we die.* Exodus 20:2 <note>This citation follows the Vulgate numbering; in modern Bibles, this text appears in Exodus 20:18-19.</note>. From which it is clear that the resistance first of the subject or thick spirit—which exerts force against the powers of the unconquered spirit—and then the very fogs and darkness of the dense spirit, opposing themselves to the incomparable light of the face of Jehovah, were the cause why the Actor and Victor appeared from the cloud with such terror to men. Thus we see that the same fire or Sun cherishes by heating, and nourishes, brings to life, and causes to multiply; and yet that same Sun causes others to faint, brings headaches to them, burns them, and induces many injuries. In the same way, we even call the planets **Saturn** and **Mars** "evil," although they are just as good and healthy as the others. But the reason for the harm lies in the **subject** <note>In this philosophical context, the "subject" is the person or thing receiving an action or influence.</note> that receives their influences poorly, as we have clearly explained in our *Mundane Music* <note>original: "Musica nostra mundana" (likely referring to the author's previous work on the harmony of the spheres and the elements).</note>. So also there is no wrath, nor heat, nor consuming fire, nor arrows of affliction, nor fury, nor anything else of this kind truly in the nature of Jehovah, but rather in the object that receives His act poorly, unjustly, disobediently, and with hardness. Thus *Exodus 7:22: And Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had commanded.* Indeed, the Lord cannot, because of His own inherent goodness, destroy a man unless He has first hardened his heart; that is, unless He has rendered his spirit rebellious and close to the darkness, so that in this way He might destroy him because of the resistance of that hard spirit. And hence in *Exodus 14:8* it is read: *And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh; and he pursued the children of Israel into the Red Sea.* Similarly, *Exodus 33:3: I will not go up with you, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I perhaps destroy you on the way. And certainly, unless God hid His face (whose essence is to purify all things and to test them as gold) from us sinners and from the elements themselves behind His veil of waters, what, I ask, could stand before it? Yet that glow was nothing but a certain image of the glow of Jehovah, covered by a veil. Who is he, therefore, who can look upon the face of God as it is, without dying instantly and suddenly, since even the hardest rocks cannot endure before it without being melted like wax?

But this is indeed a remarkable sign of mercy: that God does not do that which He is able to do, but reflects and contracts His power within Himself, so that only with His modest and moderately veiled gaze toward justice does He look so benevolently upon us and all creatures, ensuring His life-giving power does not exceed the capacity of matter. <meta>This page continues the discussion of the divine name and how God's presence interacts with the material world. It specifically addresses how the "last He" (the material realm) is tempered by the "supreme He" (the highest heaven) through the mediation of the Messiah, preventing the destruction of the imperfect physical world by divine purity.</meta>

# OF SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.

It should be understood that, just as Jehovah, extending himself from the heavens, is accustomed to dwell in the center of the elements—according to that passage:
> *Psalm 144: Jehovah, bow thy heavens and descend; touch those mountains and they shall smoke* <note>original: "Jehova inclina cœlos tuos & descende; tange istos montes & fumigabunt"</note>—
so also he brings down from his highest heavens a great portion of that same benign spirit, so that the hardness and disobedience of the earth and the elements may be tempered according to justice. In this way, they become more obedient to God’s will and are raised from the darkness toward the regions of light. Thus, the immediate acts of Jehovah produce kinder and milder effects. By the mediation of the **Messiah**, the lowest region of the world (or the final **He** [ה]) is tempered by the humble and obedient nature of the **Empyrean heaven** <note>The highest, most spiritual part of the universe, often associated with pure fire or light</note> (or the supreme **He** [ה]), where **Jah** <note>A shortened form of the divine name</note> or the benign God reigns forever and ever. Hence the Psalmist says in *Psalm 33:5: The earth is full of mercy or benignity.* And in *Psalm 36:5-6: Thy mercy, O Jehovah, is in the heavens; thy faithfulness reaches unto the higher clouds; thy righteousness is like the greatest mountains; thy judgments are like a great abyss.* And in *Psalm 85:10-12: Mercy and faithfulness meet together; righteousness and peace kiss each other; Faith shall spring out of the earth, and righteousness shall look down from the heavens; Yea, Jehovah shall give that which is good, etc.*

By these things it is explained why all these things in the lowest region—since they are impure, submerged in darkness, subject to density and hardness, and prone to rebellion—can nevertheless persist before the face of Jehovah, which punishes all impurity, subdues rebellion, and separates all **dross** <note>original: "scoria" (the waste matter or impurities left after smelting metal)</note> from pure silver through an ineffable trial. This is possible because of the mercy and benignity of Jehovah. Although he could examine and dismantle all things in the blink of an eye, he is moved by clemency to partly restrain the heat of his face and reflect it back into his Paradise; and partly, by the spirit of wisdom, he bends hard spirits and makes them moderately obedient to his actions. Therefore, an abundance of the benign spirit of life is the method for maintaining health; its defect or reduction is the occasion of disease; and its total loss is the bringing on of death. This, I say, is the cause of changes and alterations in generation and corruption in this lower region of the world; this is the infallible origin of life, sickness, and death. How Jehovah is also called the author and procurer of good and evil, health, life, and death, we shall declare in the following chapter.

## CHAPTER III.

->*How, according to the opinion of the Kabbalists, the ineffable name<-
->of the Tetragrammaton, and the titles of God which are used regarding<-
->the works produced by him, denote both severity and punishment in Jehovah,<-
->as well as benignity and<-
->clemency.*<-

The **Kabbalists** <note>Followers of Jewish mystical tradition</note> called the ten **Sephirot** <note>term: Sephirot (The ten emanations or attributes through which God reveals Himself and creates the universe)</note> (the divine numerations and measures) the "garments" of divinity. Hence the Psalmist says in *Psalm 104: Clothed with light as with a garment;* that is, in the first illuminated **Or** <note>Hebrew for "Light" (אור)</note>, which is called Light. To each of these Sephirot they attribute one of the divine names, some of which seem to denote the benignity of God, and others his severity. Those that indicate mercy are: First, **Ehyeh** (I Am), which is assigned to the first numeration, namely **Keter** or the Crown. Second, **Jehovah** or **Jod** and **Jah**, assigned to the second, which is called **Chokhmah** or Wisdom. To the third numeration, namely **Binah** or Prudence and Understanding, **Elohim** is referred. To the fourth, **Chesed** (that is, Clemency), the name **El** is appropriated. To the fifth, **Tiferet** (that is, Grace and Beauty), the name **Eloah** is given. To the sixth, **Yesod** (the Basis or Foundation), **El Chai** or **Shaddai** is attributed.

The first of these names attributed to the Sephirot denotes paternal mercy—the mercy of him insofar as the father is the unity, basis, and foundation of the whole; indeed, it is called the "Crown of Benignity." We see here, therefore, the **Jod** (י) and **Jah** (יה) from the letters of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, signifying Jah, who is the father of mercy. The second is Jehovah himself, where the Jod carries the same meaning as the entire Tetragrammaton; because Jod, signifying the number 10, contains 1, 2, 3, and 4 within itself, which are the image of the four letters of the Tetragrammaton. Within this name the **Messiah** is contained, by whose benignity all things are to be saved; he is also the distributor of life and of the being of every thing. The third, **Elohim**, insofar as its numeration flows through the orders of the **Thrones** <note>An order of angels associated with God's justice and judgment</note> into the sphere of Saturn, denotes (according to the opinion of the Kabbalists) repentance and the remission of sins. The fourth, **El**, by the meaning of its numeration, indicates clemency, goodness, grace, and mercy. The fifth, **Eloah**, insofar as its garment is grace, beauty, decorum, and delights, is not far from benignity. Similarly, the sixth, **Shaddai** or **El Chai**, by reason of its Sephirah, declares redemption and rest. 

From these we see that God's greater property is concerned with clemency and benignity. So also we see that the two upper heavens abound in the richness of clemency; for the higher gives eternal life and resurrection from the dead, while the middle gives temporal life and health. Likewise, the names of God which argue for severity are **Elohim**, whose Sephirah **Gevurah** denotes power,

**SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I: BOOK III.**

...force, severity, judgment, punishment; and <term>אדני</term> <note>Adonai, meaning Lord</note>, whose numbering is <term>Malchut</term> <note>the "Kingdom," the tenth and lowest emanation on the Tree of Life</note>—dominion, empire, etc. And according to the **Cabalists**, under this numbering is denoted the "cutting off" of the kingdom and the removal of the tree of life because of Adam’s sin. From these things, it is clear that few of **Jehovah’s** properties lead to punishment, while most lead to mercy. It also denotes the mystery of the law given by mouth; hence it also implies severity. And since all these divine names, taken from the works of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> in this world, are contained in that one ineffable name (which is the unique name of God and is called "separated" because, according to **Rabbi Moses the Egyptian** <note>The philosopher Maimonides</note>, it signifies the substance of the Creator in a pure sense, in which there is no participation of other things), namely in <term>יהוה</term> **Jehovah**; therefore, we shall perceive through diligent and proper inquiry that the parts of mercy belong to the preceding or first letters of Jehovah, which designate the higher heavens—the <term>י</term> [Jod], <term>ה</term> [He], and <term>ו</term> [Vau].

Insofar as the first <term>Sephiroth</term> <note>Divine emanations or "numberings"</note>; **Cheter** <note>Kether, the Crown</note>, flows through the orders of the **Seraphim** into the *Primum Mobile* <note>the "First Moved" sphere of the universe</note> and from there to all things to which it gives being. The second, **Hochma** <note>Chokmah, Wisdom</note>, is the confirmation of all things; hence it is said that God perfected all things by his word and wisdom. The third, **Binach** <note>Binah, Prudence or Understanding</note>, descends through the orders of the **Thrones** into the sphere of **Saturn**. The fifth, **Chesed** <note>Mercy or Kindness</note>, penetrates through the order of the **Dominations** to the sphere of **Jupiter**; the sixth through the order of the **Virtues** into the sphere of the **Sun**, etc. From this, we should observe that the two higher heavens are infused with the primary and secondary flows of mercy. 

But indeed, that emanation which passes through the order of the **Powers** into the sphere of **Mars** denotes that, just as God is the Lord God strong and full of judgment, so he also exercises severity against the rebellious, the hardened, and those attacking his dominion. For, as Mars is a fiery planet, so Jehovah, the Lord of hosts, carries out his war with a *consuming fire, with burning coals, glowing arrows, heat, fury, and wrath* <note>original: "igne consumente, prunis ignitis, sagittis ardentibus, æstu, furore, ira &c."</note>.

So also **Malchut** denotes the tree of life in the earthly Paradise. Hence, because of the "cutting off" of that tree—by which it is denied to the children of Adam—it argues for punishment and misery because of disobedience. But leaving these things aside, we come to the observation of the ineffable name of the **Tetragrammaton** itself, since we are dealing with its mystery in this place. Therefore, with proper contemplation having been made, we see first, according to the pattern of the letters of the name **Tetragrammaton**, that the immortal and the mortal are included within it. The immortal is seen in the first <term>י</term> [Jod], which receives the beauty of the Jod and is signified by **Ehieh** <note>the divine name meaning "I Am"</note>; for it is the crown and root of the whole world.

Through this <term>י</term> [Jod], therefore, the mind and the intellect, including wisdom and prudence, are understood; and so it designates the most noble soul of man and the head of the world. Therefore, the mind and intellect descending from this place are immortal. But indeed, the lowest <term>ה</term> [He] indicates the body made of the four elements, which is delivered over to death and subjection. Indeed, even the **Savior** of the world himself, immersing himself into this <term>ה</term> and putting on flesh or an elementary body, was not free or exempt from death. And indeed, through the bond of nature, which was not foreign to him, his superior **Jod**, or <term>י</term>, was joined with that inferior letter; and thus **Christ** was made God and man. 

And as a double <term>ה</term> [He] is found in **Jehovah**; and one <term>ה</term> (or the number five) multiplied by the other <term>ה</term> produces 25; so, if that number is doubled again by the number of the double <term>ה</term>, it constitutes **50**. This number is the symbol of the **Great Jubilee**, or the celestial week, or the **Sabbath of rest**, and the **Sabbath of Sabbaths**, in which all pure human souls, having cast off their stain, will finally return free to the inheritance of the Fathers, and will enter into our truly proper possession, which we have acquired and retain through the soul of the **Messiah**. For the superior <term>י</term> [Jod], whose soul is the Messiah himself (or the power of Jod), entering into the lowest <term>ה</term> [He] and the **Cubic body**, after death made that lowest part incorruptible, and raised it to the summit of the **50 gates of intelligence**. Moses was never able to reach this in this life, nor in the second, except through the mediation of the Messiah or the Son, who alone is the one through whom we can see and know the essence of the Father. 

We see, therefore, that just as the supreme <term>י</term> [Jod] is life, essence, and most full of kindness, so also that lowest letter, conversely, is weak and subject to infinite changes. And this is the reason, as I believe, that the **Cabalists** divided <term>יהוה</term> [Jehovah] into <term>יה</term> [Jah]—the **Being**—and <term>וה</term> [Vau-He]—**Himself**—but with the letters inverted. This is the ideal, spiritual, and immortal Being, and "Himself" as the example formed in its image, but open to changes. These two extremes, by the power of the one **Messiah**, are led back to the same point of the **Crown** or **Jod**. And this is the reason why **Jehovah** carries, in a silent way, **Jesus Christ**.

Furthermore, we also notice three progressions in Jehovah: namely, <term>יה</term> **Jah**, <term>יהו</term> **Jeho**, and <term>יהוה</term> **Jehovah**. The Jod in **Jah** denotes **Ehieh**, which is the highest operation of the Tetragrammaton; hence **Jah** is the sign of paternal mercy. But **Jeho** is the symbol of **Ehieh** itself; for it is the seal of God, with which **Ehieh** sealed the world, and it is called <term>אמת</term> [Emeth], which is **Truth**.

What the nature of this seal is, the hidden meaning of the letters teaches us: for first, **Aleph** [<term>א</term>] argues for the same thing as **Jod**, that is, the first and simplest essence of **Ehieh**. **Mem** [<term>מ</term>] is the symbol of fire and the fiery spirit, denoting by this very thing the created light, which is nothing other than the purest illuminated spirit. And **Tau** [<term>ת</term>] is the simple spirit in its own nature. Therefore, God (the uncreated light), and the created light in the middle participating in the spirit and pure uncreated light, and the spirit itself, make up the seal of the **Tetragrammaton**, by which all things obtain the impression of their life and existence. And **Jehovah** is the perfection of all things—all things both mortal and immortal, both perfect and imperfect, both good and evil...

### ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES

...evils, life and death; health and disease, heaven and earth, light and darkness, day and night, encompassing both the Deity and the Devil himself within Himself, and embracing them with His immense arms. For can anything exist without the presence of Him who is everything that is, and without whom there is nothing? Do we not have this confirmed by many testimonies of the Holy Scriptures? For in *Ecclesiasticus 11:14* <note>original: "Ecclesiast. 11.14." This refers to the Book of Sirach</note> it is written: *Good things and evil, life and death, poverty and riches, are from God.* And in *Ecclesiastes 7:14: Consider the works of God, that no man can correct him whom He hath despised. <meta>This page continues the philosophical exploration of the dual nature of the Tetragrammaton, specifically how the One God manifests as both a life-giving "Apollo" and a destructive "Dionysus" through the numerical interplay of the ternary (3) and the quaternary (4).</meta>

SECT. I. PORT. I. PART. I. LIB. III.

...assembling again that which had been torn apart and cut off. By this they seem to hint that from an even number—namely 4, to which the material spirit is referred—and an odd number—namely 3, to which light and form are attributed, as if to a patient and an agent, or a female and a male—all things are generated and composed in the <term>septenary number</term><note>The number seven, formed by the union of 3 (spirit/form) and 4 (matter).</note>; and likewise, by the same logic, all things are corrupted and dissolved. For generation comes from heaven and is life, which is to say, it is super-celestial light and a life-giving force as if from **Apollo**; but corruption comes from darkness and the underworld; that is, from the "tearing night." And this is the reason why they assigned to the night **Dionysus** the Tearer, as the bringer of evils; but to the day they assigned the harmonious **Apollo**, as the driver-away of evils. For this reason the Athenians called Apollo *Alexiacon* <note>original: "Alexiacon," meaning "Averter of evil"</note>, that is, the putter to flight of evil; and **Homer** called him *Ulion* <note>original: "Vlion," likely from the Greek *Oulios*, meaning "Destroyer" or "Healer," here translated by the author as "author of health"</note>, that is, the author of health; for he makes all things harmonious, perfect, and in consonance.

But we shall show how these things are accustomed to happen through the <term>septenary number</term> mentioned before. Truly, this number is forged from 3 and 4, of which the former is an odd number and the origin of all perfect numbers, insofar as it contains within itself a beginning, a middle, and an end. Therefore, it presents a most simple form and a specimen of the divine essence, which is the "acting act" and the actor of all things, or the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter Name of God, YHWH</note> itself. And just as the <term>ternary number</term><note>The number three</note> is the origin of all perfect or odd numbers, so also the <term>quaternary</term><note>The number four</note> is the principle of imperfect and even numbers; for according to the doctrine of the **Pythagoreans**, the number two is not called a number, but a "confusion of unities."

The <term>quaternary number</term>, therefore, signifies matter to be formed; which, once finally formed—that is, united with form and the <term>ternary number</term>—constitutes the creation of the entire world. And thus it is like the <term>septenary number</term>, which is forged from 3 and 4. Here, 3 is the symbol of the properties in the most Holy Trinity, and 4 is the sign of matter or spirit appearing out of the vast darkness. Here, then, we see that **Jehovah God**, who is "all in all," is called that super-celestial **Apollo** in respect to the ternary and luminous number—He who is the life of all, the father of generation, the restorer of health, and the re-collector of parts separated in corruption. But in respect to the <term>quaternary number</term>, the offspring of darkness, He is called **Dionysus**, corrupting all things according to His good pleasure, destroying what is composed, and "tearing apart" and dividing things into their similar parts. From this we see that God, in respect to His supersubstantial essence, is always kind, benevolent, and merciful to His creatures; but in respect to the "created garment" drawn out from the blackness of **Chaos**, He is said to tear apart and corrupt the composition into pieces. For matter—whose very being is God Himself—is never content; by greedily seeking new forms, it is the cause of destruction, corruption, death, diseases, and all perturbations. But on the contrary, light or form vivifies, cherishes, restores, and produces every good. Whence it is truly said that *nothing is made good except God alone* <note>original: "nihil præter solum Deum fit bonum"</note>; since other creatures are called good only by participation—namely, insofar as they participate in the divine goodness, according to what is found in *Genesis 1*: *And He saw that it was good, etc.*

From these things it is manifest that malice and corruption are not in God the "Agent," who in His property is a perfect ternary, but in the "Patient," which is always found fit to participate in the malice of the darkness from which it arose. Therefore, **Dionysus** is God "clothed in darkness," who is accustomed to tear apart the darkness in which He exists and with which He is mixed, insofar as things are in every way contrary to His nature. Thus we also see that the letter *Yod* <note>The first letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the divine spark</note> in the "upper square" is said to be clothed in light, according to *Psalm 104:2*: *Light is the covering or garment of God*; but in the "lower square," He is clothed in darkness. In the upper, therefore, He is the Spiritual Apollo and Mind; in the middle, the visible Apollo; in the lowest (though in Himself He is always the same in clemency and goodness), He is **Dionysus**. Insofar as He appears in a thick cloud and dense night, He is accustomed to tear apart mountains, to set rocks on fire by the heat of His countenance, and to bring upon creatures in infinite ways those infinite things which we call "evils." These things, although produced by the action of God, are nevertheless the effects of rebellious, impure, and dark matter; as it is poorly disposed to receive divine actions, it produces events that are bad and most wicked as far as our senses are concerned. Yet those very events, considered in themselves and intellectually, are ordained by God for the best end; so much so that, just as that which seems good to men is often displeasing to God, so also that which appears evil to them is always held as good by the Actor, namely God.

And in this way we see how God is called the Lord of clemency and kindness, and how He is the Lord of severity and punishment; likewise, why He Himself is the author of good and evil, health and sickness, life and death. That **Jehovah** is the God of mercy and severity is concluded by the following testimony drawn from the Holy Scriptures, *Exodus 34:6*: *And Jehovah, passing before him, cried out: Jehovah, Jehovah, the strong, the merciful, the gracious, slow to anger, and full of mercy and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, and taking away iniquity and transgression and sin, and who by no means clears the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children's children, unto the third and fourth generation.* Here, therefore, it is clearly taught that **Jehovah**, in His first and principal progress, is gracious and merciful; but in the latter, He is severe and punishing even unto the third or fourth generation. Furthermore, we see the manner through which He extends His mercy: namely, through the brightness of His face...

<meta>This page continues the philosophical exploration of the dual nature of the Divine, specifically how the Tetragrammaton (the four-letter name of God) acts as both a life-giving force, represented by the Greek god Apollo, and a destructive force, represented by Dionysus, depending on how the "matter" of the world receives the Divine light.</meta>

# ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES #

...by taking away iniquity, transgression, and sin—that is, by illuminating men and, through that illumination, removing all darkness, according to that passage of the Psalmist previously cited from *Psalm 18:28*: 

> *If you light my lamp, Jehovah my God, you make my darkness shining.* <note>The author uses "Jehovah" for the Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter name of God.</note>

And *Psalm 80:3*: *By the light of your face, Jehovah, we shall be saved.* And in this sense, **Apollo** is imagined by the Heathens <note>original: "Ethnicis," referring to non-Christian or classical Greek/Roman thinkers</note> as gracious, life-giving, and healing all things; and likewise **Dionysus** is spoken of by them in relation to the night, inasmuch as he is said to tear all things apart in that condition. For in the darkness, God turns his face away, so that by his absence all things are corrupted and dissolved into their elements; because it is the presence of God that causes all things to exist, without which all things perish and are, as it were, torn asunder. 

And yet again, when **Apollo**—or the splendor of the face of Jehovah—is present, there occurs a recollection, union, and vivification <note>the restoration of life</note> of the scattered parts of the composite body. Thus, the total turning away of the face of Jehovah, or the splendor of the **Messiah**, from a creature brings about death and corruption; but its diminution and decrease breeds diseases and disturbances. Likewise, by his presence in justice and his kind countenance, we enjoy life and the health of life. Does not King David confirm this very thing in *Psalm 104:28-29* with words of this sort?

> *When God gives to the creatures, they gather; when he opens his hand, they are satisfied with good; by the absence of his face, they are troubled; when he takes back their spirit, they expire.*

By these words the Prophet instructs us primarily that all things which exist are in God, from God, and through God; and that the life or Spirit of every creature is in the power of God, and that every disturbance, disease, and imbalance <note>original: "intemperies," a lack of proper mixing of the bodily humors</note> of the creature depends upon God. For he says that by the absence of the divine face, creatures are troubled, meaning by this that without God's mercy, life is afflicted by diseases so that it is most unhappy; according to *Psalm 90:10*: *The span of life is miserable without the kindness of God.* Hence he also says in *Psalm 91:16*: *With length of days I will satisfy the just man, and finally I will cause him to enjoy my salvation.* 

Therefore, just as Jehovah is imagined to be the true, benevolent **Apollo**, so his benevolence is described in this manner by the Psalmist in *Psalm 84:1*:

> *Lord, you have blessed your land; you have forgiven the iniquity of your people; you have covered all their sins. You have mitigated all your wrath; you have turned away from the wrath of your indignation. Convert us, O God of our salvation, and turn away your wrath from us. You, O God, being turned toward us, will quicken us, and your people shall rejoice in you. Show us, O Lord, your mercy, and grant us your salvation.*

Where in those words, *Turn away your wrath, etc.* and *You, O God, being turned, etc.*, he denotes and seems to hint, by the word "wrath," at a change of form from the nature of the severe **Dionysus** to the nature of the mild and kindly **Apollo**. But insofar as he is imagined to be Dionysus, it is said that we are consumed by his wrath and troubled by his heat. And in *Deuteronomy 28:21*:

> *Jehovah will make the pestilence cling to you until you are consumed; Jehovah will strike you with a hot wasting disease, and with the burning ulcer of Egypt, and with hemorrhoids, and with the scab and the itch, from which you cannot be healed.*

And in *Leviticus 26:16*:

> *I will cause terror to rule over you, with wasting disease and with burning fever, that shall consume the eyes and cause the soul to suffer.*

And in *Job 33*, Jehovah rebukes through pain upon the bed, and makes all his bones waste away, etc.

> *His soul shall draw near to corruption, and his life to death, etc.*

From these things, therefore, it clearly appears how Jehovah, acting both in commiseration and in punishment, is said to be the cause of life and death. Of life, certainly, in the benevolence of the life-giving action of his essence, which is simply to act toward eternal salvation; but of death and sickness in respect to **matter**, which—on account of its bad disposition—receives his benevolent actions poorly, so that they tend not toward life, but conversely toward destruction. 

Thus we also see that the sight of the **Sun** accelerates corruption and death for some; while conversely it brings life, health, recreation, and multiplication to others, and leads to generation. We see also that the life-giving and good solar heat, mixing itself with thick and ill-disposed air, very often makes it putrid, corrupt, and pestilential during the summer time. Whence the plague is observed to arise not only in living animals, but even in the plants and vegetables themselves. And yet the fault is not in the action or the agent <note>the Sun</note>, but in the thing suffering poorly, receiving the celestial actions perversely and unjustly. For the action of light always tends toward purification and refinement; but since, because of the resistance of the **malignant Spirit**, this cannot happen without corruption, it is necessary that that spirit—whether packed into a composite body or free in the air, water, or earth—be corrupted, so that after corruption it may become more obedient to the acts of the power of the **Tetragrammaton**.

Is, I ask, the cause of pestilential diseases from the depraved disposition of the air in the eastern place called **Sanderon** <note>Likely a reference to a specific region known for "bad air" or a corrupted form of a place name like Santorini or a specific wind</note>, or from the Sun, which by its health-giving action is accustomed to lift up the mists daily for the sake of purifying them? Surely he who is wise will assert that the malignant condition of the place proceeds not from the rays of the sun, but from the poisonous vapor of the place; for the Sun constantly attempts to remove and purge that impurity with its heat. 

By a similar reasoning (if indeed it is permitted to compare created things with the Creator), the acts of Jehovah always act benevolently in themselves; and where his acts are received humbly and obediently, there the grace, glory, and benevolence of God are said to abound. But where, conversely, his acts are resisted harshly, obstinately, and disobediently, or where the matter is not fit to receive such noble actions—insofar as impure hearts and "vessels" are not suitable for receiving divine influences—there indeed, on account of the malice of the subject upon which he acts, Jehovah is said to act in wrath, heat, and fury. And thus he is said to bring in corruption and death, ruin, diseases, and all other species of unhappiness, even though he himself is always remaining in himself, always stable, and constant in his actions. But matter, as it differs in multitude and proportion, produces infinite and mutually different effects, which are called either good or evil in consideration of the state of this life; although (as it seems to me) all things may be called good in respect to the uniform action of God, but in respect to...

<summary>This page explains that God's nature is constant and benevolent, but it is perceived as either life-giving (Apollo) or destructive (Dionysus) based on the "matter" or spiritual receptivity of the person or thing receiving His light. The author uses the analogy of the Sun, which provides life to healthy things but causes rot in foul air, to explain how a single Divine cause can result in both health and pestilence.</summary>

### SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK III. ###

However, in the case of matter—which is entirely evil in itself—things behave differently, so that this specific "something" can be rightfully called nothingness or evil. But we must consider here that, although the action of God in nature is always the same and always constant in itself (as is apparent in fire or the Sun), it nevertheless makes one thing healthier and another weaker, depending on whether there is a greater portion of Him in one than in the other. Therefore, where Jehovah is present with the abundant gaze of his benevolence, there the shadows—the daughters of evil—are expelled, diseases are driven away, and health is always present. In such a state, **Dionysus** <note>Dionysus is used here to represent the "destructive" or "tearing" aspect of divine power, contrasted with the solar, healing power of Apollo mentioned on the previous page.</note>—or the power of God clothed in darkness and sorrow—does not appear. Thus, we enjoy the presence of a good and luminous angel and are not troubled by the society or familiarity of the evil one. 

For even in the Devil himself, we know that the uncreated light is good in itself; but because he is burdened and clothed with darkness, night, and sorrow, as well as the malice of gloomy matter, he is called the "devastator," "slayer," or "murderer" and "striker" in many places of the Holy Bible. Indeed, sometimes "Jehovah" is used in place of the "destroying angel," for the same reason we mentioned above: namely, that Jehovah is taken as the *act*, and the devastator as the *dark spirit* of the malignant angel in whom there is malice or punishment. This is just as in earlier passages, where the "angel" received its name in respect to the matter of the cloud, and "Jehovah" was named by reason of the pillar of fire. 

Hence, *Exodus 12:12*: *I will pass through the land of Egypt on that night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast, etc.* Here, Jehovah makes mention of himself, arguing that he himself is his own avenger. Thus, in *verse 13*: *And I will see the blood and pass over you, and there shall be no destroying plague among you when I strike the land of Egypt.* And again in *verse 23*: *For the Lord will pass through to strike the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the lintel, he will pass over the door of the house and will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike.*

Therefore, here, when it says that *he will not allow the destroyer to enter the houses*, it refers to the nature of **Dionysus**—that is, the tearing disposition of his dark garment—in which Jehovah, acting in his usual way, causes that malice to immediately execute His will. For the "striker" is no more divided from the "one who strikes" than a sword is from the hand of the man striking. For Jehovah’s instrument is "sorrowful matter," through which He is seen to act by death, or disease, or ruin, or destruction. Hence it is said in a certain place: *The hand of Jehovah struck with death*; and elsewhere: *A punishing hand and an outstretched arm*; and elsewhere: *The sword of Jehovah or of the angel, etc.* 

But the fact that the "striker" or "sword" was joined with Him who actually gave power to the striker is proved by the following words in *verse 29*: *And it came to pass at midnight that the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt.* From this, it is clear that Jehovah was both the striker and the act of striking; here he is taken as God together with his "garment" or "sword." So also in *Exodus 14:19*, it is said: *The angel of Jehovah went before the Israelites, etc.*, insofar as created matter is signified. Just as it says there: *He will not allow the destroyer to enter, etc.* and afterward it is said: *Jehovah himself went before the Israelites, etc.* So also here: *The Lord struck every firstborn, etc.* Similarly in *3 Kings 24:15* <note>original: "3. Reg. 24. 15." In the author's timeframe, the "Books of Kings" included what we now call Samuel. This refers to the plague in 2 Samuel 24.</note>: *And the Lord sent a pestilence upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of the people died. But afterward, when the angel of the Lord stretched out his hand over Jerusalem to destroy it, etc.*

Thus, the creature sometimes takes the name of the one in whom Jehovah operates, and sometimes the action is attributed to the actor himself, namely Jehovah. 

But now let us descend for a moment to a more exact declaration of the name **Jehovah** <note>original: "יהוה" - the Tetragrammaton</note>, in which the mysteries of the whole universe and the internal moving principle of all things seem to lie hidden. First, therefore, we shall contemplate its mystical arrangement according to the names found in it following the order of the letters, namely in **YHWH** <note>original: "יהוה"</note>; and then we shall consider its "surnames," as it were, which are joined to it for the explanation of His works here in the world. 

Regarding the names or significant syllables contained within it, it must be noted that the principle of Jehovah is **Ehieh** <note>original: "Ehieh," meaning "I Am."</note>, which is denoted by the letter **Yod** <note>original: "י"</note>. According to the Kabbalists, this sounds the same as four letters; for **Yod** denotes 10, and ten comprehends the characters of the four numbers joined together (1, 2, 3, 4), which make 10. <note>This refers to the Pythagorean "Tetractys," where 1+2+3+4 = 10, a concept adopted by Christian Kabbalists to explain the power of the ten-valued letter Yod.</note> And just as all other characters are formed from the **Yod**, as lines from a point, surfaces from lines, and a body from surfaces; so also from **Yod** (the first letter of the ineffable Tetragrammaton) is formed **He** <note>original: "ה"</note>, and from **He** comes the illumination **Vau** <note>original: "ו"</note>, and from the illuminated **Vau**, the final **He** <note>original: "ה"</note> is formed and illuminated. 

From this, it is clear that **Ehieh** or **Yod** is the entry—or the attempt at entering—of the Tetragrammaton itself into the nature of things. Again, **Jah** <note>original: "יה"</note> denotes the essence of God in merits. Furthermore, in respect to the incomparable ideal and archetypal world, **El** <note>original: "אל"</note> (beginning with **Aleph** <note>original: "א"</note>) denotes the beginning, but **Jah** <note>original: "יה"</note> indicates the end, insofar as the progress begins from **Aleph** toward **Yod**, which is the end of the uncreated world without end; since in it, a new created world begins where the uncreated seems to finish. 

We have, therefore:
*   **Yod**: which signifies the first emanation and descent of the Tetragrammaton into the Spirit of the abyss.
*   **Jah**: the name of the essence in the work of merit and retribution, designating the kindness of Jehovah.
*   **YHW** <note>original: "יהו"</note>: the symbol of the seal of **Ehieh** itself, with which **Ehieh** sealed the visible world and its creatures with the impression of life; it is called **Emet** <note>original: "אמת"</note>, that is, "Truth," as discussed above. Conversely, **YHW** is like "Let it be" <note>original: "Esto"</note>, or the voice of God, by whose sound all dense spirits were formed. Or it is **Truth** itself, as if to say: "He himself on earth as in heaven."
*   Finally, the whole name of the **Tetragrammaton** (**YHWH**) denotes God everywhere, and everything that is. 

As for the names of God joined to the Tetragrammaton, it should be known that those names are sometimes placed before the name of Jehovah, and sometimes after it. For the same surnames, placed before or after, cause the ineffable name to differ in its properties. First, therefore, **Elohim** <note>original: "אלהים"</note> is found placed both before and after the name of the Tetragrammaton.

# OF SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES #

<page-num>81</page-num>

...set. Genesis 2: *Behold, when the Four-Lettered Elohim <note>original: "Elohim Tetragrammatus." The author refers to the combination of the names Jehovah and Elohim.</note>, King of Kings and Lord of Lords, went forth; and it was said then for the first time: "These are the generations of the heaven and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the Four-Lettered Elohim made the heaven and the earth."* In this context, when these names are joined, the Clemency of God is understood alongside His Justice. For wherever in the Holy Bible the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH, often rendered as Jehovah.</note> joins itself to *Elohim*, there we find the quality of both Clemency and Justice. It is also sometimes joined with *Adonai* <note>Hebrew for "Lord."</note>, as in the prayer of Habakkuk: *The Four-Lettered Adonai is my strength.* The Kabbalists <note>Jewish mystics whose traditions were often adapted by Christian scholars like the author of this text.</note> understand by such a connection that the power of the Tetragrammaton descends to the spoken name *Adonai* itself. Furthermore, it is found in the inverse order: *Adonai the Four-Lettered.* For in Genesis 15, it is held thus: *Adonai the Four-Lettered, what will you give me?* In this position, we understand the divine qualities as ascending from the lower to the higher, apprehending the supreme light. Sometimes the Tetragrammaton is also joined with *El*, as in Psalm 118: *El the Four-Lettered has shone upon us.* By the connection of these two, Clemency is signified. And it sometimes happens that *Elohim* is added to *El* and *Jehovah*, as in Psalm 50: *El Elohim Jehovah has spoken, and called the earth.* With these additions, the ineffable name indicates grace joined with, or clothed in, severity. In a clearly similar way, we find among the Prophets the title *Sabaoth* <note>Hebrew for "of Hosts" or "of Armies."</note> placed after *Jehovah* or the Tetragrammaton, as in Psalm 46: *The Tetragrammaton (or Jehovah) of Sabaoth is with us, our taker-up, the God of Jacob.* This form suggests the quality of judgment and punishment; therefore, the Prophets used this formula when rebuking with severity. Through these additions, we are taught that the same four-lettered name is used both for goodness, mercy, life, kindness, and clemency (in which way the Ancient Sages understood it under the name of the benevolent **Apollo** <note>The Greek god of light and healing.</note>) as well as for severity, punishment, affliction, and disturbance.
