We conclude, therefore, that the cause of sickness, weaknesses, and diseases—indeed, even death itself—as well as the power to restore health and well-being, and life itself, kindness, happiness, and beauty of both soul and body, proceeds from יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton: Y-H-W-H.</note> and exists in the letter *He* (ה). Of this name, the first part, *Jah* (יה), is kindness itself and eternal life. But the last part, the *Vau* (ו), is the offspring of darkness, and consequently capable of diseases and disturbances. The letter *Yod* (י) in the first *He* (ה) is the daytime **Apollo**, merciful, gracious, life-giving, and eternal. However, *Jah* in the *Vau*, and the *Vau* in the final *He* (ה)—that is, plunging itself into the darkness—is that **Dionysus** <note>Dionysus is used here to represent the "nocturnal" or "wrathful" aspect of God that breaks things down to purify them.</note> of the ancients, the angry and nocturnal one, who punishes, tears apart, and abounds in severity. This is because, clothed in garments contrary to his nature, he contends with the darkness and attempts to purify density by refining it, to make the unclean clean, to illuminate the dark, and to perform other such duties of perfection. But because of the impurity of matter in this heaven and its foul disposition, he cannot lead these things to a conclusion without the corruption and dissolution of the thing itself, which is tainted by the vice of the darkness of impurity and sin. Therefore, he strives to renew things defiled by darkness and rebellious with foul hardness and coldness by bringing about dissolution and the separation of parts, so that he may tame that which is polluted and rebellious in its actions and render it obedient.

It happens, moreover, that some men are humbled by his rebuke and by the affliction instituted through diseases; for these people, **Dionysus** is turned back into **Apollo**, so that they are healed. This is manifest in Hezekiah, whom Jehovah first commanded to prepare for death by threatening him with it; yet finally, by turning the quality of His severity into mercy, He granted him life and length of days.

Others, however, who are perverse and rebellious, persisting in the hardness of their hearts and not yielding to moderate chastisement for their own humiliation, are taken from the number of the living by an untimely death. Thus, they are torn apart and exterminated by the nocturnal **Dionysus**—that is, by death. This does not happen because of the action of the Tetragrammaton’s power, which is always the same, permanent, and complete, but because of the perverse disposition of the matter receiving it. Indeed, unless God turned His face away from our iniquities, who could stand before Him? As it says in Wisdom 11:

> *You have mercy on all, because you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of men so that they may repent. For you love all things that exist, and hate nothing of those things you have made. For you would not have fashioned anything if you had hated it. And how would anything have endured, unless you had willed it? Or been preserved, if you had not called it? But you spare all things because they are yours, O Lord, lover of souls.* So also in Wisdom 1:14: *God did not make death, nor does he delight in the destruction of the living; for he created all things that they might exist, and he made the nations of the world healthful, etc. But the acquisition of death is injustice. The ungodly, however, have summoned it with their hands and words; and thinking it a friend, they have wasted away and consumed themselves, for they have made a covenant with it, because they are worthy of death who belong to its company.* And in Wisdom 2: *God created man for an incorruptible state, and made him in the image of his own likeness; but by the envy of the Devil, death entered into the world.*

Thus we see from these things that death and diseases, which are its messengers or precursors, belong to the side of darkness and matter, and are by no means from the simple act of the divine essence itself.

# SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK III. #

->*Epilogue, or a recapitulation of this entire portion: Wherein the seat of Paradise, both heavenly and earthly, is demonstrated, and at the same time the logic of health, disease, and resurrection is briefly explained according to the meager and slender capacity of the author.*<-

In the hieroglyphic demonstration of the world and its regions through the characters of the Miraculous Name <note>The "Miraculous Name" refers to the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note>, we have clearly explained with arguments not lacking in reason how the power of the Tetragrammaton—which is the Messiah, or the emanation from the letter *Jod* <note>The first letter of the Name, י (Yod), representing the father or the source.</note>—reaches through the letters *He* and *He* <note>The second and fourth letters, ה (He), often associated with the spirit and the physical world.</note> all the way to the center of the world’s machinery. Accordingly, although that most holy power of the Tetragrammaton acts everywhere and seems to be present everywhere (not unlike the light of the sun in the world), it does not usually go out "personally"—that is, in its entire essence—beyond the regions of the two *Hes*, any more than the sun’s brilliance leaves the solar body, or God Himself leaves Paradise. 

From this it follows that just as this holy power, or the Messiah, is God (that is, the Word and Wisdom of the Tetragrammaton) who does not depart from His Paradise or garden of pleasure, so too the Messiah does not exceed the immense limits of the double *He* and the *Vau* <note>The third letter, ו (Vau), which connects the upper and lower worlds.</note>; although He scatters the rays of His life-giving spirit everywhere through the world and the creatures of the world. By His presence, all things enjoy the benefit of life or the "character of existence," and without Him, they cannot live or subsist even for the blink or moment of an eye. For these uncreated characters, or life-giving hieroglyphics, move through the regions of the world in no other way than the Sun itself; except that the Sun is led around in twenty-four hours by a regular motion established by God (which is to say, an involuntary motion). However, the motion of the miraculous characters of the Tetragrammaton itself is voluntary and not at all forced; it is accustomed to appear everywhere at its own choice and good pleasure in its Paradise—both the super-celestial and the lowest elemental one. From this Paradise, God sometimes speaks to all men, according to that passage in Psalm 18:19 <note>In modern Bibles, this is Psalm 19:3-4.</note>:
> *There is no speech nor word whose voice is not heard; their sound has gone out into all the earth, and His word to the ends of the world.* 

And yet the voice of God is despised by the foolish and is not understood, according to Proverbs 1:
> *Supreme Wisdom sings out abroad, she raises her voice in the streets, she cries out at the head of the crowds, in the city she utters her words: "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simplicity, and the foolish hate knowledge?"* 

But truly, she is listened to with reverence and fear by the wise, and her sound is received with joy and gladness; by which very thing they are finally exalted, according to Psalm 18:31 <note>Modern Psalm 18:30.</note>: *The Word or speech of God is most pure, existing as a shield to all who take refuge in Him.* This Word or power, therefore, was breathed out from the letter *Jod* within the Tetragrammaton itself. The Psalmist also testifies to this in Psalm 56:11: *In Jehovah <note>original: "Iehova."</note> I will praise the Word.* Consequently, the power of the Messiah is contained within the characters *He* and *He*. Therefore, the Messiah was in the center of *Jod* when He was outside of all things—that is, before anything was created. Solomon also seems to confirm this in Proverbs 8:22 with these words: *Jehovah possessed Wisdom in the beginning of His way, before His works, before any time.* And in Wisdom 9:9 <note>The original text mistakenly cites Wisdom 19:9.</note>: *Wisdom is with God, she who knows His works, etc.* 

Next, entering into the *hyle* <note>A Greek term for "prime matter," the raw substance of the universe.</note>, He made His dwelling in the "Upper He" (*He* superiori), or the Empyrean spirit <note>The highest, most fiery part of heaven.</note>. And so it is said in Wisdom 7:
> *A pure emanation or flow of the clarity of Almighty God; and the brightness or splendor of eternal light, and the mirror without spot of the majesty of God, and the image of His goodness.* 

And in the same place (chapter 9): *Wisdom was present when God made the world.* And in verse 10: *God sends Wisdom from the holy heavens; from the throne, I say, of His glory, etc.* And Psalm 68:33 <note>Original cites Ps 69:22.</note>: *Behold, God utters His voice, whose strength is in the clouds above, etc.* Here, then, is the place, or the Garden of Paradise, in which God is clothed in the thinnest garment of luminous spirit, and appears peacefully and benevolently to His angels as He is. From the living waters of this Paradise and the fruit of the Tree of Life, the "second life" (which is permanent) is promised to the world and to man, who is the image of the world. Through the fruit of this super-celestial Paradise, therefore, we await the resurrection to eternal life.

Then, in the *Vau* (ו), or the spirit of the sun, He placed His tabernacle; where the Carbuncle <note>A legendary red gemstone, here symbolizing the life-force or the spiritual heart of the solar system.</note> of the life by which we live is placed as a foundation. And in this globe of life, we see the glow and the seat of the celestial Paradise. For the guarding of this place, there is no need for a Cherub—or for Julianus de Campis <note>A pseudonym for a Rosicrucian author, often identified as Julius Sperber, who wrote about the restoration of ancient wisdom.</note> with a flaming and two-edged sword—lest the descendants of Adam obtain the wood of the Tree of Life; for this Paradise is too high, such that the progeny of man cannot ascend into it to remove or repair the damage of our first parent. There is, therefore, yet another Paradise, which is called "earthly," in which Jehovah, or His Wisdom, or the Messiah, or the Word is said to dwell. And this is the one said to dwell on Mount Zion, or the Elysian Field, or the "Lower He" (infimo ה).

It appears, then, that Jehovah shows Himself in the "Upper He" (His super-celestial Paradise) to His angels and intelligences; and Jehovah also reveals Himself in the Paradise of the "Vau" to the celestial stars and the spirits <note>original: "Dæmonibus," used here in the neutral sense of guiding spirits or intelligences.</note> inhabiting their spheres, from which He also constantly illuminates the entire world with His light. Finally, He occasionally shows Himself to men and other creatures in the "Lower He," or the elemental Paradise. From there, as if from the peak of a high place, He sometimes cries out and utters His voice by the way in the place where many paths meet, as we read in Proverbs 8: *Here Wisdom remains in delights, daily, rejoicing and playing before Jehovah at all times in the habitable world, and having her delights with the sons of men.*

### ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES ###

<margin>Proverbs 8; Song of Solomon 3</margin> Here comes the bridegroom, leaping over the rolling mountains and hills like goats and young stags. <margin>Wisdom 9, 10</margin> This is that seat of pleasure in which dwells that holy <term>Wisdom</term> <note>Latin: *Sapientia*; often personified in this tradition as the feminine aspect of God or the Divine Architect.</note> which God sent to man from the holy heavens, so that she might be present and work with him in his labor, as seen in *Wisdom 9:10.* This is the most holy dwelling-place of that divine word which, as David testifies in <margin>Psalm 68:11</margin> *Psalm 68:11, Jehovah is accustomed to give to those who preach the good news.* This is the most delightful garden of that Blessed Wisdom, which (according to the Wise Man in <margin>Proverbs 3:14</margin> *Proverbs 3:14*) is more precious than carbuncles; to which all the delights of men cannot be compared; in whose right hand is length of days, and in her left hand, riches and honor; whose ways are the paths of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace; who is a tree of life to those who take hold of her, and whoever has acquired her is blessed. And if you wish to know her by an even more brilliant description, she is indeed, by the testimony of Solomon in <margin>Wisdom 7</margin> *Wisdom 7, more precious than the Sun, and above every arrangement of the stars; compared to light, she is found to be prior; for night and darkness succeed the light, but no evil prevails over Wisdom.*

From these things we see that <term>Jehovah</term> <note>The personal name of God, used here to represent the fullness of divine presence.</note> fills every paradise of the world with his presence. And although he is always the same in his own luminous and <term>supersubstantial</term> <note>Meaning "above all substance" or "beyond physical matter."</note> nature—a bath of his own love in whose virgin waves one may swim with ineffable joy, delighting oneself as if in the purest liquid of eternity and purity—he is accustomed to refresh himself with the most chaste <term>Psyche</term> <note>The Soul.</note> or untouched spirit in great joy, like the bridegroom with the bride in the Song of Solomon. This spirit is that sweetest <term>Zephyrian breeze</term> <note>Referring to Zephyrus, the gentle West Wind of spring.</note>, by whose life-giving breath every paradise is filled, so that by his spirit, diffused through the world from the creator's inspiration, the world is illuminated with life and all things receive the breath of essence. Meanwhile, this Blessed breeze remains in its own region, not departing further out of it than the spiritual mass of the Sun departs out of its own sphere. 

However, because this spirit is "clothed" in different garments of purity and impurity, or thinness and density, according to the nature of the region of the world where the Paradise (or the place and garden of God) is located, the same Jehovah appears to creatures in different ways from that same spirit. Thus we see that one and the same common fire (which is nothing other than the act of Jehovah in a coarse and impure spirit) acts mildly and sweetly in the open air, but with hissing and crackling in water, and with the greatest violence and destruction in a combustible thing which its nature can overcome. Likewise, the very power of Jehovah in the higher <term>Yah</term> <note>original: יה (Yah), the first two letters of the Name of God, representing the higher, more spiritual realm.</note> is most kind; in the sun it is moderately kind, but sometimes heating beyond measure, and from there it passes into its lower paradise. 

<margin>Exodus and 1 Kings 19</margin> Moses testifies in *Exodus and 1 Kings 19* with how much terror He spoke to the Israelites on Mount Sinai and to Elijah on Mount Horeb. And yet Adam, while he lived within the limits of the lower Paradise of <term>Yah</term> <note>original: יה</note>, is said to have heard the voice of Jehovah walking, not indeed in a cloud with horror and stupor, but *at the breeze after noon.* Elijah also heard the first voice of Jehovah with great fear, which was followed by *a great and strong spirit, overturning mountains and shattering rocks before the Lord; and an earthquake* (or a commotion of mountains) *and a miraculous fire.* But *after the whistling of the breeze* which he heard, he stood firm, laying aside all fear, and received the voices and speech of Jehovah. 

And this is why Jehovah addressed him twice and in two ways with the same words: in the first, those things appeared out of the malice of darkness which were not real (just as Moses' rod, when thrown on the ground, appeared as a terrible serpent); but in the latter, things appeared as they truly were because of the presence of the Lord, who is mild and sweet. Thus, also, the rod in Moses’ hand appeared as a rod, as it truly was, and not as a deceptive serpent. So Moses says: *I call heaven and earth to witness that I have set before you life and death; Choose life, that you may live with your posterity.* Such is the Mosaic law; such is the law of Christ. 

Therefore, the true Paradise is where the true, sweet, constant, and mild breeze of <term>Yah</term> <note>original: יה</note> is found. Adam, having been cast out beyond the limits of the lower <term>Yah</term>, immediately and without any delay tasted the affliction, changes, and inconstancy of the worldly or elemental spirit—he who, while living in the paradise of <term>Yah</term>, was free and immune from all passions of both body and soul. For the voice of God in a thick cloud was one thing, and another in the thin, constant, and sweet breeze in which God is accustomed to appear to some of the elect as he truly is. 

For just as it would seem more excellent to us to dwell in the royal palace of the sun than in the land of the dead, so also it would be desirable beyond imagination to stay in the thin, healthy, divine, knowledgeable kingdom filled with joy and gladness (the breeze of paradise), rather than in the coarse, foul, raw, morbid air subject to constant changes, where honey is mixed with bitterness, prosperity with adversity, good with evil, life with infirmity, and where good fortune seems to be infected and defiled by misfortune. Nor is there indeed any good or health in earth, water, or air, except that which they have received from the breath of this Paradise. Therefore, when God gives good to creatures from his paradise, they receive life and happiness; but when he denies the benefit of his breath, plague and other grave diseases, famine and war, and every evil happens and rushes upon the world, <margin>Psalm 104:28-29</margin> according to that in *Psalm 104:28-29: When God gives to them, they gather it up; when he opens his hand, all things are filled with goodness; but when he turns away his face, they are troubled; he takes away their spirit, so that they fail.* 

From these things, therefore, it appears that every good thing is from Paradise, insofar as it proceeds from God, who alone is goodness, and who indeed inhabits Paradise both in the heavens and on the earth. Therefore, as his presence is considered in the higher <term>Yah</term> or breeze, or intellectual spirit, David said: <margin>Psalm 68:33</margin> *Psalm 68:33, God sits upon the heaven of heavens of old, etc.* (For the Empyrean heaven was created first.) <margin>Psalm 113:5</margin> And *Psalm 113:5, Jehovah God dwells most high, who looks down upon the lowest things in the heavens and on the earth.* <margin>Psalm 115:3</margin> And *Psalm 115:3, God is in the heavens themselves: he does whatever pleases him.* <margin>Job 22:12</margin> And *Job 22:12, God is higher than heaven, and is exalted above the height of the stars.* 

As he is also in the lowest paradise, the Royal Psalmist speaks of him in <margin>Psalm 104:3-4</margin> *Psalm 104:3-4* in these words: *God makes the clouds his vehicle, or his chariot, who walks upon the wings of the wind, who makes his angels winds, and his ministers a flaming fire.* Moreover, the Prophet argues in <margin>Psalm 144:5</margin> *Psalm 144:5* that Jehovah God descends from the upper <term>Yah</term> to the lowest.

### SECTION I. PORTION I. PART I. BOOK III. ###

*Jehovah, bow your heavens and descend; touch these mountains, and they shall smoke:* <note>Psalm 144:5</note> Although here, even with a small word, I would wish everyone to be carefully reminded that the difference between the heavens is not always considered in terms of distance, or the height or depth of places in the sense of physical space, but rather in the sublimation of dignity and the exaltation of goodness and purity. Thus it is said that *God, or the Holy Spirit, does not usually dwell in an impure or unclean heart*; and yet in truth, *where God dwells, there is paradise; and where paradise is, there we say heaven is*; For heaven is on earth, and vice versa, earth is in the heavens, according to that saying of *Hermes* <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy.</note> in his *Emerald Tablet: That which is above is like that which is below, and conversely*; <note>Latin: *Quod est superius, est sicut illud, quod est inferius*</note> that is, the subtle is the thick, and the thick is the subtle. For water is thin earth, and air is thin water, and fire is thin air; therefore, by condensation, fire becomes air, and by the same reasoning air becomes water, and water becomes earth. On the other hand, through <term>subtiliation</term> <note>The process of making a substance more refined, spiritual, or airy.</note> earth becomes water, and water becomes air, and this air is called "heaven." Hence it is said in *Deuteronomy 11:17: Jehovah will shut up the heavens, so that there be no rain etc.* And in *Genesis 1:30: The birds of heaven etc.* From this it is also written that the heavens are the throne of Jehovah, and the earth is his footstool.

Neither should it be believed that the final **ה** <note>The letter 'He', the fourth letter of the divine name יהוה (YHVH).</note> of the name **יהוה** <note>The Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter Name of God.</note> is less pure in its uncreated nature than the first **ה**, which is closer to the **י** <note>The letter 'Iod'.</note>; But nevertheless, because of the malice of the matter in which it exists, or which has surrounded it, it usually produces worse effects outside of itself—with the Messiah moving within it—just as one may gather and see from many places in the holy scriptures. Moses says in *Genesis 3* that Jehovah was walking in the midday, or after the midday; indeed, Jehovah is a sufficient light unto himself, exalted above all solar brightness; for he is the Sun, granting grace and glory to whom he wills. In his characters impressed upon the world and immersed in the mundane spirit, the **י** (Iod) is the <term>Zenith</term> or vertical point, in which, as if at midday, the splendor and clarity of the glory and majesty of Jehovah is exalted. At his voluntary movement, the other members of the incomparable Name in the world are likewise moved toward the regions to be produced through the Word; so that, where the lower paradise is present, there the super-celestial paradise also stands above it, so much so that God Jehovah is always seen to be consistent with himself and to dwell in his own homes.

But we find this difference between each **ה** (He): that the upper **ה** is kindly surrounded and protected by Seraphim and Cherubim, so that any understanding soul is permitted to taste of the living waters and the tree of life; while in the meantime, conversely, entry into the lower garden of pleasure is forbidden and denied to men. The gate leading into it is guarded and defended by Cherubim with a fiery or flaming and two-edged sword, lest anyone from the progeny of Adam enter into it, and by reaching out his hand to the tree of life, take of its fruit and live forever. Here, therefore, I believe, remains that *Julianus de Campo* <note>A pseudonym used in early Rosicrucian writings, likely referring to a "Brother of the Rose Cross."</note> of the **F.R.C.** with his flaming sword, threatening death to those who approach; Wherefore one must "hasten slowly," and wait sagaciously and patiently *in the fear of Jehovah, which is the beginning of wisdom*; since all rashness and haste is from the Devil. But concerning the location, nature, and condition of this paradise, we shall produce some testimonies from the holy scriptures, so that we may make you more certain against the vain opinion of men, and teach you that even to this day there is such a place in this lowest region of the world, from which health, riches, and glory in this life—with divine benevolence leading the way—can be sought and acquired as if from the hand of Jehovah. We shall therefore attempt to demonstrate two things regarding the subject of Paradise from the Holy Bible: the first is that there is such a place upon the earth, related to and familiar with the peaks of mountains; then, we shall show that this place is the apothecary and sanctuary of health and the balsam of life. We must note above all things that, just as Jehovah is in his hiding place of this kind—or tabernacle, or land of the living, or island of pleasure, or seat surrounded by a glassy and icy sea (according to *Revelation 4: And in the sight of the seat, as it were a sea of glass, like crystal*) which is that throne of Jehovah signified by the last character of his name; so it is said by the holy scriptures in *Job 9:5: he moves the mountains and shakes the earth; And Psalm 47:3: Jehovah is a great King over all the earth; And Psalm 76:3: God’s tabernacle or hut is in Salem, and his dwelling place in Zion; And Psalm 94:2: God is the judge of the earth; And Psalm 97: at the presence of God the mountains melt like wax; And Psalm 104:3: God makes the clouds his vehicle or his chariot, who walks upon the wings of the wind etc. And in the same place verse 32: When God touches the mountains, they smoke; And Psalm 107:17: Jehovah breaks the gates of brass, and cuts the bars of iron asunder; he delivers the just from darkness and those bound in the shadow of death, from affliction and iron etc. And Psalm 114:3: At the presence of God the sea fled, Jordan turned back, the mountains skipped like rams, and the little hills like lambs; And Psalm 139:7: God is in hell, in the furthest parts of the sea, in the night, and in the darkness; And Psalm 144:5: Jehovah, bow your heavens and descend: touch these mountains, and they shall smoke: Cast forth lightning and scatter them: Shoot out your arrows and consume them; And in Psalm 148:13* the Prophet teaches us that the power of the name of Jehovah is as much in the heavens as on the earth: namely, that the power of God is in the upper character **ה** (He) as much as in the lower; His words are these: *Let them praise the name of the Lord Jehovah, for his name alone is exalted, and his glory is above the earth and heaven. ### ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES ###

With respect to the spiritual garment, he is called an angel; but with respect to the internal, luminous, uncreated principle, he is called Jehovah. Just as Christ is called both God and man, so Jehovah is called both God and angel, as has been indicated elsewhere. From these things, therefore, it is clear that the God Jehovah exists as much in the lowest **He** (ה)—namely, the elementary heaven, which is the type or symbol of the earthly Paradise in which God is said to dwell—as in the highest **He**, which is the pattern of the celestial garden of pleasure, or the sanctuary and shrine of Jehovah himself or the soul of the Messiah. 

But on the contrary, just as the God Jehovah is said to be in the super-celestial Paradise—namely, in the **He** (ה) closest to the sacrosanct **Jod** (י) (which is the type of the entire <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God: YHWH.</note>)—so it is said by the sacred scriptures: *Jehovah's throne is in the heavens* <note>Psalm 11:4</note>; that is, in the Empyrean **He** (ה) and the ethereal **Vau** (ו). And in *Psalm 68:34: God sits upon the heaven of heavens.* And in *Deuteronomy 33:26: He who sits upon the heavens for your help, and in his magnificence upon the clouds above.* And in *Psalm 75:4: God illuminating wonderfully from the eternal mountains etc.* And in *Psalm 93:2: God’s throne and seat are stable; before time, before the age, you reign.* And in *Psalm 113:5: The God Jehovah dwells on high, who looks down upon the lowest things in the heavens and the earth etc.* And in *Psalm 115:3 & 122:1: God and his seat are in the heavens themselves etc.* This means that Jehovah reigns in every heaven; namely, **Jod** (י) in the uncreated and supersubstantial heaven; the first **He** (ה) in the first-created Empyrean heaven; **Vau** (ו) in the ethereal heaven; and the final **He** (ה) in the elementary heaven. And in *1 Kings 22:19: I saw Jehovah sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him etc.* 

The manner, however, in which he descends from one Paradise into another is explained by the Royal Prophet <note>King David</note> in *Psalm 144:5: Jehovah, bow your heavens and descend; touch those mountains and they shall smoke.* Similarly, in *Matthew 5:35*, it is said that heaven is the throne of God, and the earth is his footstool; and *Deuteronomy 10:14: The heaven of heavens belong to the God of Gods.* Thus, it is proven by this very fact that by the presence of Jehovah, every heaven exists in its own being and state.

From these things, it is clear that the power of **Jod** itself (which is the symbol of the whole Jehovah)—namely, the Messiah, or the Wisdom of God (which exists in the name of Jehovah just as the light of the Sun exists in the Sun)—is in every heaven in the same nature and being. This is true despite the variety of garments (for in every heaven he puts on a new and different garment); his uniform action produces various and different effects. 

Thus, in the supersubstantial heaven, the Deity is naked: the Messiah, the power of Jehovah, or the divine essence, is to be seen in its simplest form, stripped of every garment. God utterly denied this vision even to Moses himself, indicating that no mortal could gaze upon it with their eyes in that supreme state without sudden death. Then, immersing himself in the first degree of the waters of dark <term>hyle</term> <note>Primary matter or the fundamental substance of the universe.</note>—namely, descending into the **He** (ה)—it is recorded in *Psalm 104:2* that *he is clothed with light as with a garment.* In respect to this clothing, Jehovah is said in *Psalm 93:1* to *reign clothed in majesty and highness.* 

Afterward, as he descends into the **Vau** (ו) (which is the ethereal Paradise), it is said in *Psalm 104:2* that *the heaven is like the curtain of God’s house*; that is, the ethereal spirit is like a veil for the house of **Vau**, or **He**, in which unity dwells. Or rather, the garment and veil are thin, through which the Messiah, clothed in the prior garment of light, is covered; by its thickness and condensation, the light—as the garment of Jehovah or the Messiah—is made visible. And so it is said that *he placed his tabernacle in the Sun.* 

But here it must also be noted in passing that the luminous garment of God is nothing other than the appearance of invisible light in the world-spirit; which spirit, so illuminated, is called "light." And because it receives the power of **Jod** in its spirit or uncreated throne (the first **He**), it is therefore called the house or garment of God on his throne; although that light, considered in itself without the spirit, is nothing other than the very essence or emanation of God sitting in the **He**, whose garment or vehicle is the first-created spirit.

Finally, the same divine essence, with its first and second garments, descends into its lowest kingdom, the final **He** (ה). Entering there into an elementary covering—or entering an aerial hiding place, or a watery and transparent tabernacle—it is said according to *Job 26:9* to *bind the face of his throne, and spread his cloud over it.* And in *Job 22:12: Thick clouds are a hiding place for him*; that is, over his throne **He** (ה); in respect to which the aerial heaven was made on the third day of creation. 

But, to reveal what I truly conclude regarding his paradise or the earth of his throne with its spirit or seat: I believe, indeed, that Jehovah establishes his position mostly upon mountains and the higher places of the earth, and especially in the mountains in the northern parts facing us; from which the golden light of Jehovah is often accustomed to come to us and to all in wonderful ways. 

Finally, by immersing itself even more deeply, this Deific power—namely, into the darkness and the perfectly mixed dark body—also puts on, over all its worldly garments, the opaque body of the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>Man, viewed as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note>, or makes the human body its dwelling place. Hence it is said in *Deuteronomy 32:9: The Lord’s portion is his people, Jacob is the cord of his inheritance.* And St. Paul says in *1 Corinthians 3:16: Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the spirit of God dwells in you?* The temple of God is holy, which you are. And in *1 Corinthians 6:19: Or do you not know that your members are a temple of the Holy Spirit, who is in you?* Furthermore, we read everywhere, and we establish by faith, that the Deity or Messiah put on a human body, since Christ is both God and man.

From this, it is clearly explained how it was said by the Royal Prophet in *Psalm 144:5* that God is in the night and in the darkness. And St. John 1: *That light was in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.* But now, to come at last to the site and name of the location or seat of the earthly Paradise, we elicit the following from the testimony of the sacred scriptures: and first, this sentiment of King David in *Psalms 3, 5, and 15*: first, *Jehovah answers me from the mountain of his holiness*

<margin>Psalm 24:3</margin> Therefore his seat or throne, namely the **lowest He** (ה), **is a mountain**. <note>The author uses the letter He (ה) to represent the final part of the Divine Name, often associated in Kabbalistic thought with the physical world or the "Shekhinah" (the Indwelling Presence).</note> Thus it is said that he appeared to Moses on Mount Sinai; and he spoke to Elijah on Mount Horeb, that is, the mountain of God. <margin>Psalm 18:7</margin> *Who shall dwell in your tent? <margin>Song of Solomon 4:12</margin> —the Lord <note>original: "Iah"</note>. This very gate, through which the Righteous enter to Jehovah, was similarly described by Solomon, the son of David, in his mystical wisdom—which he inherited as king—in the **Song of Solomon 4:12**: *O fountain of the gardens, a well of living waters, which flow from Lebanon; Awake, O North wind, and come, O South wind; blow through my garden.* Furthermore, the **Wise Man says in Ecclesiasticus 24:28** <note>Though cited as "Eccl. 24," this is Sirach 24 in the Apocrypha.</note>: *The Lord Almighty is God alone, and there is no other Savior besides him, who fills all things with his wisdom like the Pishon, and like the Tigris in the days of new fruits; who overflows like the Euphrates with understanding, and like the Jordan in the time of harvest, etc. Who makes instruction shine forth like light, and like the Gihon in the days of the harvest etc. I, Wisdom, like a canal led out from a river and like an aqueduct, have come into Paradise. For I make instruction shine like the morning dawn, and I display it even to far-off places; for I pour forth doctrine and prophecy, which I shall leave to eternal generations.* 

And also in **Genesis 3:23**: *Therefore Jehovah God sent him out of the garden of Eden to till the earth from which he was taken, etc.* And in **Genesis 3:24**: *He placed before the paradise of pleasure Cherubim and a flaming, turning sword to guard the way to the tree of life, etc.* It is as if he were saying that the Lord makes the entrance into Paradise—that is, into heaven—appear nearly impossible and very dangerous because of the opposition of the fiery element; except for those to whom it is granted by Him to penetrate into the interior of that garden. Such were Enoch, Abraham, Jacob, Moses, Elijah, Christ, and others. To some of these it was permitted to taste the fruit of the tree of life; to others, it was denied by Jehovah either because of sins or for the sake of human salvation. 

Paradise also appeared to be in **Bethel**, that is, the house of God, in which He showed himself through the vision of the ladder of ascending and descending angels. *For this place (said Jacob) is none other than the house and place of God, and the gate of heaven; and I did not know it (Genesis 28).* Furthermore, in **Exodus 3**, when he had come to the mountain of God, Horeb, the angel appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush, etc.

When Jehovah saw that he turned aside to look, God called to him from the midst of that bush, saying: *Moses, Moses, do not come near; take off your sandals from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy ground.* And in **Exodus 19:12-13**: *Set limits for this people all around, saying: Watch yourselves, that you do not go up into this mountain or touch its border; whoever touches this mountain shall surely be put to death.* Similarly: *O flee from the land of the North, for I have scattered you to the four winds of heaven; O Zion, flee, etc. (Zechariah 2:6).* And in the same book (4:7): *Who are you, O great mountain, before Zerubbabel? You shall become a plain. And he shall bring forth the capstone, and make its grace equal, etc.* Similarly in **Psalm 48:1-2** <note>Original says Psalm 47.</note>: *Great is Jehovah, and greatly to be praised in the city of God, on his holy mountain. Finally, Paradise is called the **land of the living** because of its stability; whence it is said: *When I shall have given glory in the land of the living (Ezekiel 26)*; in which the tree of life is planted, and the throne of God is placed, as John witnesses in **Revelation 4**. We could produce infinite other passages from the most holy scriptures as testimony to this matter, but we believe it would be too long and tedious to review them all in this treatise. Therefore, we shall move on to the second part of our intent, in which we shall strive to prove, by infallible arguments drawn from the divine fountain, that **Paradise is the seat of health**. 

First, therefore, we read in **Psalm 14:7**: *Oh, that someone would give salvation out of Zion for Israel!*—that is, from the dwelling place of God. And in **Psalm 20:2** <note>Original says Psalm 18.</note>: *May God send you help from the Sanctuary, and protect you out of Zion.* And in **Psalm 36:8-9** <note>Original says Psalm 39:9.</note>: *They are most abundantly filled with the fatness of your house, and you give the children of men to drink from the torrent of your delights and pleasure, for with you is the fountain of life.* And in **Psalm 46:3-4**: *The waters roared and were troubled, the mountains were shaken by his strength: the rush of the river gladdens the city of God, etc.* And in **Psalm 63:1-3**: *O mighty God, I seek you early; my soul thirsts, my flesh faints for you, to see your power and your glory, just as I saw you in the holy place: for your lovingkindness is better than life.* And in **Ezekiel 26 and Revelation**, this place is called the **land of the living**. And in **Matthew 16:28** and **Mark 9:1**: *There are some standing here who shall not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.* 

Furthermore, concerning **Wisdom**—whose house is the very **He** (ה) in the garden of Paradise—Solomon speaks thus in **Proverbs 3**: *She is more precious than jewels, etc. Length of days is in her right hand, in her left hand are riches and honor. Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace. She is a Tree of Life to those who lay hold of her, and finally, everyone who holds her fast is blessed.* Through this sacrosanct wisdom of Jehovah was built that high city of God, or that earthly Paradise, from which health is received, according to **Proverbs 9:1**: *Wisdom has built her house with her seven hewn columns,* through which...

The author uses extensive biblical citations to link Zion, Eden, and the Temple with the concept of a "land of the living" where death is overcome.</summary>

# ON SUPERSUBSTANTIAL PRINCIPLES.

...how much (*as the Wise Man says in the same place, verse 12*) your days are multiplied, and the years of your life are added to you. <note>original: "quàm multiplicantur dies tui..." citing Proverbs 9:11</note> *And in Ecclesiasticus 24:3: I, Wisdom, came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth like a mist; I had my tent in high places, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud; alone I encompassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the depths of the abyss, etc.* I could bring forth infinite other testimonies in this place regarding the healthy arrangement of Paradise; but, because a more pressing necessity constrains me, and other matters necessary to this business call me away, I now say by way of conclusion that health and length of days proceed from the beneficial fountain of life and health—from the throne of the Almighty through the power of Wisdom—like a blessed dew; that is, by distilling from the life-giving liquid of the Paradise of pleasure. I say also that this *Wisdom, whose delights are with the sons of men (Proverbs 8),* is the director of the just man, his governor, his teacher of medicine, and the mediator between Jehovah the Father and man who is subject to change. She mercifully removes the disease-ridden decay and stains of the body, washing and wiping away the spirit of the soul defiled by sin with the balm of her kindness. Then, at last, she causes his whole being—following a complete preparation or purification—to be sublimated on high and transfigured into a celestial and spiritual nature in a true resurrection.

Therefore, in the beginning, Jehovah God the Craftsman acted through Wisdom—which is the Messiah or his Power—for the creation of the world and its creatures. And so, out of nothing—that is, out of a dark and unformed mass—He produced something; this was indeed the first testimony of His kindness. Because of this, He was first called <term>Jod</term> י <note>The first letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the starting point of creation</note>, or the point, or the center without dimension (that is, without regard to the finished work). Then, after the beginning of the work, He was called <term>Jah</term> יה <note>A shortened form of the Divine Name</note>, which is a name of kindness and power. Afterward, He was called יהו <note>Jahu</note>, which denotes the seal of the existence of all things, by which the "open letters" of the lives of all creatures are sealed or protected, from the command "LET IT BE" <note>Latin: FIAT</note> until the final "LET IT PERISH." And finally, He was called יהוה <note>The full Tetragrammaton: Jehovah or Yahweh</note>, which completed the entire miraculous work. This name is the beginning and the end of all things, inside and outside of everything: God by nature, and God beyond nature; the circumference and yet the center of all things; the <term>archetype</term> <note>The original pattern or model from which all things are made</note> and also the created world. He is everything in all things, and outside of everything that exists; the sole act, the king and commander, the effector, the ruler, the bond, the harmony, heaven and earth, substance, quantity, and quality. Yet He is none of these things individually, because He is a Transcendent Being, and nonetheless He is each of them.

Here, I say, He is called "everything," as these things are His garments, and His presence gives them a degree of existence; and yet He is none of these things insofar as He is the simplest and <term>supersubstantial</term> <note>Beyond or above the nature of physical substance</note> essence. He is the created light, or the <term>Empyrean</term> <note>The highest heaven, composed of pure light or fire</note>, ethereal, and elemental spirits which He puts on as clothing; and yet He is none of these, since they are created. He is the angel, He is nature, He is the sun, He is man; their bodies serve as His temple and sanctuary. He gives them that "being" by which they exist as what they are. Thus, He was called the Angel in the bush, and the Sun giving grace and glory, and Christ the God-Man; yet He Himself, as He is Unity, is neither the angel (who is "Otherness"), nor the Sun (which is compounded of three things), nor man (who is compounded of many).

He is therefore the life and center of all things by which they exist, as well as their form and the "first act" that gives them a name and being. Thus, a creature is sometimes called Jehovah solely in respect to the uncreated light which it receives and by which it lives; but in respect to the created, passive matter, it takes a name according to the condition of its substance—namely, that of a "creature." Oh, how ineffable and unexplainable these things are! How admirable and found to be placed far beyond the grasp of human intellect is the attempt to investigate the reason for this astounding matter through any inquiry.

But if the One is all things, it follows necessarily, conversely, that all things are one. Thus, in the beginning, the miraculous name יהוה expanded itself from the center <term>Jod</term> י into the circumference, and so He made the material world in His own image. For He extended Himself from a point to a line, and from a line to a surface, and from a surface to a solid body; or, speaking mathematically, from unity to the root, from the root to the square, and from that finally to the cube. So also in the end, He will reduce this entire circular or rounded work by contracting it back to its center. And whatever in the world is impure and defiled by sin will be devoured and absorbed by the eternal oblivion, deformity, and perpetual darkness of <term>hyle</term> <note>A Greek term for primordial matter, here representing the void or chaos lacking divine light</note>, which is destitute of all grace and light.

However, that which remains of the pure, simple, and undefiled spirit shall be, for ages of ages, the unique palace and tabernacle of the uncreated Unity. There, there shall be no death, no pain, no hunger, no contention or passion, because the One can neither die nor suffer, since it does not contain opposites within itself. This most holy Unity, leaning upon its miraculous characters as if upon the wings of the creator's winds and descending into the world, divided it into three regions or stations according to the number of its characters. Because of the simplicity and sincerity of its essence, it was unwilling to endure or put on the "raw" garment of the world directly. Instead, from each of its characters—surrounded on all sides by these said characters and looking out as if from its uncreated throne—it shone upon each region of the world. It brought into "act" those things that were submerged in darkness, utterly lifeless, formless, and plainly non-existent; and in that act, it began to inhabit the various dwellings of the world. We have depicted here with a vivid demonstration how this Unity, <term>Jod</term>, is naked upon its throne, and then later puts on a different garment in each heaven.

## CHAPTER I.

*Concerning the three natural characters, which are the symbols of the three physical principles.*

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial V containing floral patterns and a central face.</image-desc>

JUST AS the Metaphysical characters, contained within the wondrous name <note>The Hebrew letters יהו (Yod, He, Waw), representing the first three letters of the Tetragrammaton, or Jehovah.</note>—namely YHW—are the Fathers, bringing all things into being; so their last two letters, in respect to divine properties, are referred to the Son begotten by the Father, and to the Holy Spirit proceeding from both. But truly, insofar as all these properties—namely Unity, Father, Wisdom (or the Word), the Son, and the Holy Spirit (or Fire)—are co-helpers in the work of the macrocosm <term>macrocosm|The "great world" or the universe as a whole, as opposed to the "microcosm" of the human being.</term>; (for by the Word of Jehovah the heavens were made firm, and by the breath of his mouth all their host <note>original: "spiritu oris ejus omnis virtus eorum." Citing Psalm 33:6.</note>) to that extent, in respect to created things, we call them Fathers or primary ministers, according to that passage in Proverbs 8: *I, Wisdom, was with him as a foster-child, or the one composing all things.* <note>original: "Ego Sapientia eram apud eum veluti alumnus, seu cuncta componens." See Proverbs 8:30.</note> But, since the supernatural properties or "Fathers" (YHW) require portions to be created for the creation of the world—into which they may act, according to the respect of each of their properties, just as fathers act upon mothers, or males upon females for procreation—therefore the wiser of the Hebrew nation (among whom I specifically name Abraham in the *Yetzirah* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* or "Book of Formation," an ancient Jewish mystical text attributed to the patriarch Abraham, which describes the creation of the world through Hebrew letters.</note>) named three "Mothers" at the instant of creation; which by [their] action...

<meta>This page continues the discussion from the introduction of Part II, moving from the metaphysical "Fathers" (the divine letters YHW) to the physical "Mothers" (Aleph, Mem, Shin). These represent the fundamental building blocks of the material world—Darkness/Earth, Water/Spirit, and Fire/Light—according to Fludd’s interpretation of the Sefer Yetzirah (The Book of Formation).</meta>

<page-num>56</page-num>
<header>SECTION I. PORTION I. PART II.</header>

...of the three uncreated Fathers, into light and being, the first of all things in the world were produced, namely Darkness, Water, and Light. For Moses made mention of Darkness and Waters before he arrived at Light: *And darkness was over the face of the abyss; and the spirit of the Lord moved over the waters: And he said, Let there be Light.* <note>Fludd is citing the opening verses of Genesis 1:2-3.</note> From these things it is clear that Darkness was first, and then the Waters; which, by the power of the fiery spirit emanating from the luminous Aleph, or Jod, now rising and revealing itself in the center of the dark abyss (inasmuch as it previously lay hidden and was called dark), were created into the form of waters; and finally, the first composite creature was made, namely from the mixing of the rays of uncreated light with the created spirit or waters. This, in respect to the created spiritual body which it informed, is called created light; although it is nothing other than the mixture of uncreated light with created spirit, by which that spirit is formed and animated by eternal life. The Kabbalists and Abraham the Jew, in the book previously cited <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah*, traditionally attributed to the patriarch Abraham.</note>, made these characters for these "mothers": namely א for Darkness, מ for Waters, and ש for created light. The meanings of these mothers, according to Kabbalistic doctrine, are as follows:

**א (Aleph)**, since it is retracted and immanent within the abyss of darkness, and idle—or, as they say, looking toward nothing—it is therefore called *Ain* <note>original: "אין" (Ayin-Yod-Nun). In Kabbalah, *Ayin* represents the primordial Nothingness from which all being emerges.</note>, which is to say "Non-Being" or "Without End." This is because we, being punished by such poverty of intellect in divine matters, judge those things which do not appear in the same way as those things which do not exist. But when it shows itself in such a way that it is "something" and truly subsists, then the dark Aleph is converted into the luminous Aleph; and it is then called the Great Aleph, when it desires to emerge from the darkness and appears as the cause of all things through **נ (Nun)**, which is the symbol of the Son and of Wisdom. Hence it is called *An* <note>original: "אן" (Aleph-Nun), interpreted here as "Father of all generation."</note>, the father of all generation. It is evident, therefore, that when Aleph is contracted and hidden in the belly of the abyss of darkness, darkness appears in its own state. Thus, א is that mother ascribed to darkness; and by consequence, it also denotes the element of Earth, which is a mass of shadows reflected toward the center of the [world] machine. It also signifies the West, which is why it is assigned to night; and furthermore to Autumn; from which it denotes melancholy, which is the darkest of the humors. <note>In the theory of the Four Humors, melancholy was associated with the element of earth, the season of autumn, and a cold, dry, dark temperament.</note> Therefore, just as the simplest א, in and of itself and without any respect to creation, was the first principle of the Archetypal world, so too here, by its hiding, it makes darkness the first principle in creation; from whose womb the second principle is drawn, namely **מ (Mem)**.

**מ (Mem)** is the second mother, responding to the waters and the spirit, born from the womb of the first mother. According to Kabbalistic doctrine, it is the hieroglyphic of the Waters; hence "water" in Hebrew is written with a double מ, thus: *Mayim* <note>original: "מים".</note>. And just as א made darkness act as a father, so מ made **י (Yod)** manifest as a son. For this reason, מ is attributed by the Kabbalists to the Son, or the Word <note>original: "Verbum".</note>, proceeding from the voice of the luminous **ל (Lamed)** or **ו (Waw)**. And here we must note that the Hebrews reckon a double character for this Mem: the first is called the common **מ**, and the second is the final **ם**. The first **מ** indicates the waters illuminated and open, as when Jehovah spoke from the cloud; thus it is open at its base. The other denotes the closed waters and indicates thick darkness, and is a symbol of silence. This mystery is not hidden from the wise: it suffices here to testify that מ is the character of the Waters, and the second mother in creation.

**ש (Shin)** is the last mother, which is referred to fire and created light; hence fire in the Hebrew language is called *Esh* <note>original: "אש" (Aleph-Shin).</note>; wherein all things are testimonies of light; namely the presence of the father of light (the luminous א) and ש itself, which is the symbol of created light and is referred to the Holy Spirit in its property. Therefore it has three points on its crown, indicating by this very fact the properties of the Trinity gathered into one. Here, then, it must be noted that just as the dark Aleph, by means of the divine spirit, gave being to the Waters (or מ), so on the contrary, the luminous Aleph, through its rays, gave being to ש itself, which is the fullness of things and the opposite of void or emptiness.

->As for the less significant Elements; understand them thus:<-

**ב (Bet)** is the symbol of the house or habitation, of life, the son, wisdom, and the beginning of the Law.
**ג (Gimel)** indicates retribution, peace, strong angels, etc.
**ד (Dalet)** denotes a door, gates, or an entrance; the third intelligences, and wisdom.
**ה (He)** signifies weapons, the spirits of the blessed; the sense of smell, etc.
**ו (Waw)** is the character of terror, of speech, also denoting angels of the seventh order.
**ז (Zayin)** is the sign of inclination, and the Cherubim.
**ח (Het)** imports the palm of the hand, the *Primum Mobile* <term>Primum Mobile|The "First Moved," the outermost sphere in the Ptolemaic model of the universe which carries all other spheres in its daily rotation.</term>, the fixed stars, and wealth.
**ט (Tet)** denotes doctrine, the sphere of Saturn, and business.
**י (Yod)** indicates the son, the grandson, the sun, and pathways.
**כ (Kaf)** is the sign of apposition: it denotes the spirit; that is, *Ruach* <note>original: "רוח" (Ruach), meaning breath, wind, or spirit.</note>.
**ל (Lamed)** signifies the left eye, the Moon, and laughter.
**נ (Nun)** is the character of the mouth, the intellectual soul, and the animal spirit.
**ס (Samekh)** signifies the matter of the heavens and the elements, and imports suspicion; and the final **ץ (Tsade)** signifies the forms of the elements.
**ע (Ayin)** indicates revolution and circuit; it is the symbol of inanimate things, minerals, and those things called "mixed elements"; it also indicates sleep.
**פ (Pe)** is the sign of poverty and want; and in creatures, it signifies all vegetables and fruits; likewise, it indicates grace, fertility, and inheritance.

# CHAPTER II.

## *A Kabbalistic explanation of the three secondary Physical Principles, which proceed immediately from those three Theosophical ones.*

Having finally completed the treatise on the three supernatural and primary principles—namely, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit—that is, on the three properties of the one Deity signified symbolically and in a Hieroglyphic manner by the Kabbalists under the great and ineffable four-letter name of God <note>The *Tetragrammaton*, YHWH.</note>, and on those characters alone among others endowed with spherical perfection, namely Y-H-W <note>original: יהו</note> in the composition and ordering of the world and the heavens, through the divine and unique wisdom of Jehovah, the Messiah, or the power residing in them as if upon three thrones of distinct property; it remains that in this small book we should briefly discuss the created principles, which flow immediately from those primary ones, in a manner as much Kabbalistic as it is open and common, yet nonetheless Theo-philosophical. 

Therefore, just as we have perceived through our speculation and observation according to the doctrine of the Kabbalists that the three different spherical letters of the name Y-H-W <note>original: יהו</note> were the characters and symbols of the uncreated principles—namely, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit (whom we indeed call the "primary fathers" in creation)—so also, according to the opinions of the remaining Kabbalists, those three "mothers" cited by Abraham in the *Yetzirah* <term>Ietzera: The *Sefer Yetzirah* or "Book of Formation," an ancient Jewish mystical text</term> are the secondary principles. Into these mothers, as if into females, the father-characters are said to have entered for the creation of the world. The three mothers are called by Abraham *Aleph* א, *Mem* מ, and *Shin* ש. 

And although Aleph (א) is the sign of the uncreated God and of His sacred unity within the Trinity, it is nevertheless necessarily expressed here among the secondary principles, insofar as nothing could exist without its presence. And, as was declared in the preceding pages, just as in the second place a cipher (which we compared to the formless spirit) usually denotes nothing without the presence of unity, so also that spirit or water could not be named unless its mother, from whose womb or vitals it was brought forth, were named first. Hence Moses, in Genesis 1, makes mention of Darkness before the Waters; nor indeed could the Darkness have had its name unless Aleph had shone back out of them. From this, in respect to their opposition to the light, they are called Darkness. 

It should therefore be noted from these things that just as Jod <note>The letter *Yod* (י), which has the numerical value of 10, often representing a manifestation of the Unity (1/Aleph).</note> follows Aleph and is, as it were, the conversion of the dark Aleph into the luminous Aleph—that is, the flowing of the light-form from its hidden center to the manifest circumference of the world—so also did the darkness precede the luminous spirit. These darknesses, heavy and pregnant with spirit by the hand of the Daemogorgon <note>In Renaissance mythology, a primordial creator deity or the personification of the mysterious forces of nature.</note> (that is, by the light of Aleph already made manifest), gave birth to Pan <note>The original Latin uses *Panem* (bread), but Fludd is playing on the name of the god *Pan*, representing the "All" or universal nature.</note>, or the universal moist nature, or water, or the spirit of the world. Thus, as the mother precedes the son, so also the Darkness precedes the Waters; and consequently Aleph, which was dark, is taken for the darkness itself to which it gave a name. 

So also Jod, which is the second progression from unity (for unity receives itself into the number ten), gave a name to the higher waters; hence they were called the Light created on the first day. From this, therefore, by the witness of Abraham, Aleph in natural things denotes the element of earth, which was made from the collection and heap of darkness into a single place or the center of the universe. Furthermore, we shall perceive that this word "earth" was used by Moses for the universal darkness before it was driven back to the center, if we carefully consider his words, which are these: <margin>Genesis 1.</margin> *And the earth was void and empty, and darkness was over the face of the abyss.* Therefore, the High Priest <note>Referring to Moses as the author of Genesis.</note> does not seem to speak of the earth created on the third day, since that was not empty and void, insofar as it was fruitful and fertile, adorned with herbs producing seed (as is explained in the same chapter), but of the darkness dispersed universally. In this state, it existed in potentiality toward the earth that rested in its destined place on the third day. Indeed, we are drawn to this even more because the waters had not yet been named at that time—those extracted from the vitals of the empty earth—nor had any spark of light been revealed. 

But since the fulfillment of all things is made by God (א), and truly that Aleph was still dark—that is, contracting the rays of its light into itself—for that reason the earth or darkness was called void and empty, from the conglomeration of which into the center of the world-machine the earth was made. For the cause of fullness is fertility; and again, the cause of fertility is the rays of multiplying light which, revealed from the face of Aleph, or Jod (which is Aleph with a cipher, or formless spirit), flowed forth. And this indeed can be confirmed by these words: <margin>Job 26:7.</margin> *God stretches out the North over the empty and void place* (that is, he made the heaven to rotate where the earth was empty and void) *and hangs the whole earth over nothing* (that is, he gathered and congregated that emptiness and void, the space of which the heaven already filled in creation, into one mass, which is called earth, and it is suspended over nothing).

Hence it is that the ancients feigned that Saturn was the father of the Gods; that is, the dark Aleph, clothed in a Saturnine garment; from whose expanded splendor Jupiter (that is, Jehovah) comes, and from Jupiter comes Apollo,

And although Aleph-God is everywhere in the spirit of the world under the character of Jod <note>original: י</note>, he nevertheless lies hidden in the darkness—indeed, in the very center of the earth, or the mass of darkness—just as was declared through the cone of the formal pyramid according to our invention. For there we made the cone of the formal or "lucid" pyramid penetrate all the way to the center of the base of the material pyramid opposite to it. From this, we argue that just as God, symbolically signified by Aleph <note>original: א</note>, is unity, and all lines of a pyramid usually meet at an angle (that is, in a point or unity), so also does the God Aleph, or unity itself, usually dwell in the center of darkness. In its hidden state, it takes the place of the central Sun, just as in its visible manifestation it is the celestial Sun, and in its invisible manifestation it is the solar Jod <note>original: י</note>, giving spiritual grace and glory, as is found in the Royal Prophet <note>King David, referring to the Psalms</note>. Indeed, as the Wise Man says on this matter in Ecclesiasticus 24:

> *I have walked in the depths of the abyss,* says Wisdom, *I have circled the circuit of the heavens, and in the whole earth, etc.* <note>original: "In abyssorum profunditate ambulavi... rotunditatem cœlorum circuivi, & in tota terra &c."</note>

And in Psalm 139:11:

And in John 1:

> *The Light of the Word shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it;* <note>original: "Lux Verbum in tenebris lucet, & tenebræ non comprehenderunt illam"</note>

And in Job 22:14:

> *Thick clouds are a hiding place for him, so that he does not see, etc.* <note>original: "Densa nubes sunt latibulum ei, ut non aspiciat &c."</note>

And according to Hermes Trismegistus in the *Pimander*, book 1: But indeed, insofar as Aleph <note>original: א</note> is placed in this position as its covering or garment, it is taken to represent the darkness and the "void earth," which is the first mother of things to be created. Her daughter is Mem <note>original: מ</note>, who is the universal water. This daughter, eventually mixing with her "Cupid" or universal rays emanating from Jod <note>original: י</note>, produces the third mother: namely Shin <note>original: ש</note>, which is fire, or created light. Therefore, the second mother of things to be created is called by Abraham <note>Referring to the patriarch Abraham, traditional author of the *Sefer Yetzirah*</note> Mem <note>original: מ</note>, or universal water, from which all things were created in terms of substance, according to 2 Peter 3:5:

> For it is hidden from them that the heavens were of old, and the earth consisting of water and through water by the word of God. <note>original: "Latet enim eos, quod cœli erant prius, & terra de aqua, & per aquam consistens Dei verbo"</note>

Indeed, this symbol of water denotes that entire space of the universal spirit or the world which is transparent and clear between the highest seat of light and the infernal dwelling of darkness. It is divided into three regions, which are called the heavens, so that this transparent medium is like a middle ground between two extremes that differ from each other in nature and quality (of which we shall make broader mention below).

And here, in passing, I wished to inform the readers of the reason why the mothers Aleph <note>original: א</note> and Mem <note>original: מ</note> are called elements or secondary principles. For just as from the simple 1 there is a composition of the first order, 10, and from that proceeds the vigor of the second composition (and this always through the presence of unity), so also the obscure Aleph produced one mother, from whom the second mother, coming forth, established the first composition of unity—namely Jod <note>original: י</note>, or the number ten. This is by the presence of the paternal Aleph with Mem <note>original: מ</note>, without which Mem (or water) would no more exist than a zero (0) without a one (1).

From this, I have gathered that among the Hebrews, the meaning of a word agrees perfectly with the nature of the characters. For *Yam* <note>original: ים</note> properly signifies "the sea," that is, universal water; here Jod <note>original: י</note> is joined with Mem <note>original: מ</note>, signifying by this very fact that unless the presence of God were there, the sea or water could not exist. Furthermore, it is sometimes written with a double Mem, in this way: *Mayim* <note>original: מים - "Waters"</note>. From this one argues hieroglyphically that the universal Mem, or universal waters over which the spirit moved, were divided and separated into two regions by the mediation of the firmament. This is also argued through Genesis 1, where one reads *Mayim* <note>original: מים</note>; that is, "The Seas" <note>Note: The author interprets the plural 'Mayim' as 'Maria' (Seas) to show the division of upper and lower waters</note>. Thus, the superior and inferior waters can be signified. The first Jod indicates God in the supersubstantial heaven, looking into the world to be fabricated; and the second Jod is that unity above the He <note>original: ה</note> in the Vav <note>original: ו</note>, by which the preceding Jod is joined with the following, not unlike how in the mystical name <note>The name Eheyeh, "I AM"</note> the superior He was bound with the inferior Mem through the unity above the He in the Jod.

And just as in *Mayim* <note>original: מים</note> the Jod is found in the middle between the double Mem, so in *Eheyeh* <note>original: אהיה</note> the Jod is placed between the double He, and Aleph placed in the first position denotes the principle of all that follows. For the darkness which was, and is, the created hiding place of the He <note>original: ה</note>, was the origin of the He. As before creation Aleph in Jod (that is, the luminous) produced He; and as after creation Shin <note>original: ש</note> succeeded Mem <note>original: מ</note>, so also before creation Vav <note>original: ו</note> succeeded He <note>original: ה</note>. And as Shin is the symbol of fire and light, or the illuminated spirit, composed of the purer part of darkness and the identity of divine light, so also there arises from Vav—which is composed from the spirit of He and the unity by which Vav exceeds He—a disposition placed in the world’s sphere of equality. We can also note the hidden nature of the Hebrew word which signifies water or waters, namely *Mayim* <note>original: מים</note>, where Jod is also placed between two waters for the reason mentioned above; and being hidden in the first Jod and signified by the vowel *Chirek*, it denotes Aleph hidden by darkness, now shining outwardly for the production of spirits from the waters.

We have, therefore, two simple characters from the Mothers: namely, Aleph <note>original: א</note> as simple darkness without any other respect, and Mem <note>original: מ</note> as simple water without any other consideration. But indeed, the third, namely Shin <note>original: ש</note>, is the nature produced by both: namely, from the daughter of darkness (water), which is the passive part, and from the clarity or lucid emanation of the manifest or lucid Aleph (which is Jod), which is the active agent and takes the place of Cupid or the husband. From this it happens that some attribute Aleph to the Father, Mem to the Son, and Shin to the Holy Spirit. This can also be understood by considering Aleph in its obscure and hidden nature in the darkness, by whose power the waters were produced; and again, from the light of the manifest Aleph and the dark spirit, as if from both, Shin <note>original: ש</note> or the nature of the heavens arises.

INTRODUCTION. 79

Shin <note>original: "Shin"; the Hebrew letter ש</note> is so named; from this first order of composition, the heavens were made on the first day of creation, as we shall explain more clearly in the following chapter.

From these things, therefore, we can consider that the divine characters are mostly of the order of "digits" <note>In early mathematics, "digits" referred to the single numbers 1 through 9</note>, as will be shown later. Specifically:
* **א** <note>Aleph</note> denotes the Father and unity.
* **ב** <note>Beth</note> denotes the Son, life, wisdom, and duality.
* **ג** <note>Gimel</note> denotes peace, retribution, kindness, and the number three.
* **ד** <note>Daleth</note> denotes the house, the gates and doors of heaven, the order of angels, and the number four.
* **ה** <note>He</note> denotes the spirit or hand of Jehovah, the Holy Spirit, the symbol of the waters, and the number five.
* **ו** <note>Vav</note> denotes the symbol of the Word in spirit, the center of Jehovah, the soul of the world, and the number six.
* **ז** <note>Zayin</note> denotes the arms, weapons, or darts of Jehovah, the spirit of the blessed, and the number seven.
* **ח** <note>Het</note> denotes the terror proceeding from the throne of Jehovah when He speaks and is accustomed to rebuke in anger; it also denotes speech, which arose first and before all things from the spirit of Jehovah, and the number eight.
* **ט** <note>Tet</note> denotes the "inclining" or bowing down of the heavens, by which Jehovah descends and touches the mountains, according to **Psalm 144:5**: *Jehovah, bow thy heavens, etc.* Likewise, it denotes the Cherubim, upon whom Jehovah sits as if upon the winds when descending (**2 Samuel 6:2**).
* Finally, the number nine <note>The author likely means the letter Jod, **י**, which represents ten, but follows the sequence of nine digits</note> signifies Jehovah God himself, the divine essence, and the number ten, or the principle in composition; by His presence, something is made from nothing, just as by the presence of unity, a cipher <note>the number zero</note> is transformed from a "nothing-namer" into an essential number of the first composition.

From this it is clear that these letters, or simple numbers (the 9 digits before the letter Jod), denote things concerning God in the *metaphysical* world. In the same way, proceeding from Jod <note>**י**</note>—which is the principle of the second composition, or the "simple articles" <note>In historical arithmetic, "articles" referred to multiples of ten (10, 20, 30...)</note>—they designate things in the *physical* world as the secondary order of tens. Therefore, by mixing the letters of the first order with one or more of the second, the mixture of God himself into worldly things is proven. Thus, in one respect, there is a relation to God and He may be called "creature"; in another respect, there is a relation to the creature, and the creature may be called "God." 

For this reason, God is called **אלהים** <note>Elohim</note> throughout the whole of creation, as if from **אל** <note>El</note> or **אלה** <note>Eloah</note>—meaning "Strong God"—and **ים** <note>Yam</note>, either from "the sea" <note>Hebrew: ימים, yamim</note> or "the waters" <note>Hebrew: מים, mayim</note> by transposing one **י** <note>Jod</note> before the **ה** <note>He</note>. It is as if one were saying: "The Strong God of the Waters." This is not to be understood as God in the plural number, as almost everyone else has wrongly twisted the sense. I am led to this view even more because "Elohim" is used 32 times in the creation story, which took place in the waters, through the waters, and from the waters, as we have declared elsewhere. Hence it is said, *that the Spirit of Elohim hovered over the face of the waters, etc.* And yet, Elohim is sometimes called an "angel." Therefore, on one side we have **מ** <note>Mem</note>, or water, which is the medium between eternal light and shapeless darkness; it sometimes receives gloom from the earth on one side, and clarity and transparency from the other side from Jod <note>**י**</note>, or the shining Aleph <note>**א**</note>. Just as **מ** is capable of clarity, so **מ** is transformed.

Finally, the last Mother, which is **מ** <note>Mem</note>, is found in the second order of tens. Consequently, it denotes the second composition from the preceding principles: namely, from the light **א** <note>Aleph</note>, which is the simplest letter and first among the digits. This letter is the first "Mother" in respect to the darkness that was its hiding place, although in respect to itself, it is the Father of all. In its place, because of the entry of Jod into the composition, we have not unwisely placed Jod itself (which precedes the character of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>) as the uncreated Father.

Next, **ש** <note>Shin</note> of the first ten <note>The author notes it is found as the 13th Hebrew letter in this order</note> is the second Mother. Finally, **מ** <note>Mem</note> (which is made from the first and simple **א** and the **מ** of the second order) of the secondary order (being the 21st letter) is the third and final Mother. These Mothers are called "symbols" and are like hieroglyphs of the three universal principles or elements that constitute the entire nature of the world-machine: namely, Darkness (which is listed first of all in creation), Water (the daughter of Darkness), and Created Light, which we shall treat copiously in this place.
