SECTION I. PORTION I. PART II.

Therefore, in the series, the most simple exists, namely <term>Jehovah Ehieh</term> <note>original: "יהוה אהיה"; these are the two primary names of God in the Hebrew Bible, meaning "The Existing One" and "I Am."</note>; yet of these characters, some are absolute, simple, and joined to the supersubstantial essence; some of these are primary, and acting as the principal acts, and are called "fathers," namely **א** <note>Aleph</note> and **Jod** <note>י</note>; while others are secondary, arising from the primary; and therefore they are more passive in respect to their properties, namely **ו** <note>Vav</note> and **ה** <note>He</note>: Thus the son is said to be obedient to the father, and ready to perform his will, and the spirit of wisdom is modest, patient, etc. And yet these letters constitute one and the same essence of the Deity: For as **א** <note>Aleph</note> is in <term>Ehieh</term> <note>אהיה</note>, so is **י** <note>Jod</note> in <term>Jehovah</term> <note>יהוה</note>; where also the unity hidden in the belly of the **Vau** <note>ו</note> signifies this same thing, as the **י** <note>Jod</note> in the middle between **א** <note>Aleph</note> and **ה** <note>He</note> in <term>Ehieh</term>. Again, of these essential and superexcellent letters, some are absolute and central, and others are respective and comparative: For **א** <note>Aleph</note>, which is unity, is the point and center absolutely speaking, since from it the other lines or letters have gone forth: Hence the Son is said to go forth from the center of the Father, and the Holy Spirit from the center of both: Whence it came about, as we demonstrated a little above, that **א** <note>Aleph</note> contains within itself in a hidden way the whole name <term>Jehovah</term> <note>יהוה</note>: Therefore **א** <note>Aleph</note> is the absolutely central letter; in whose character, in a mystical way, all things are contained; which were, are, and shall be; insofar as it contains within itself the whole <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, both **יהוה** <note>Jehovah</note> and **אהיה** <note>Ehieh</note>: Therefore the three remaining letters, which belong most greatly to the essence of this, are called spherical, namely **ו** <note>Vav</note>, **ה** <note>He</note>, and **י** <note>Jod</note>, as was declared in the preceding parts: therefore [Aleph] was the center of uncreated things, and indeed of the darkness itself; and so also, by comparison, **Jod** <note>י</note> can be called the center of all created things; because **Jod** is the same in creation as **א** <note>Aleph</note> was before creation; for when **א** <note>Aleph</note>, residing within itself in the center of the darkness or the immense and murky cloud, began to dilate and illuminate the immense moist shadow into a periphery, then it was not the dark Aleph, persisting by itself in the deformed chaos, but the bright Aleph—that is, mixed with the waters, or with the digit 1 and the cipher 0 <note>This refers to the number 10, which is the numerical value of the letter Jod</note>; which bright Aleph is nothing other than **Jod**, or the number ten; Which letter **Jod** is therefore formally called "spherical," because its light illuminates the whole periphery of the world, and was carried over the waters in a circular motion; Furthermore, it is also called the center of created things, insofar as the creating unity, or **Jod** in the spirit, is said to sit upon the throne of **Vau** <note>ו</note> in the Sun or the center of the world: Therefore **ו** <note>Vav</note> is a spherical character with respect to **א** <note>Aleph</note>, and is the center within **Vau** with respect to **ה** <note>He</note>. These four letters, then, are the simplest of all, and most proper to the nature of God existing in His supersubstantial essence: Which letters, if they are mixed in a word with others of the digital series, always signify some mystery in their true meaning; For example, **נא** <note>Na</note> denotes the father of all generation; For **א** <note>Aleph</note> proves the son; and consequently, joined with the father **נ** <note>Nun</note>, it denotes fruitfulness: Thus **אה** <note>Ah</note>, "Ah," or "where," is the affection of desiring, as one who would be exalted according to his vow to the highest good: Whence by the wings, as it were, of the God **א** <note>Aleph</note>, and **ה** <note>He</note> is seen to be elevated to the place of rest: And in truth, in these divine or simple letters of the order of digits, something like the Soul, the spirit, and the body are found: For **א** <note>Aleph</note> is like the simple soul without a spiritual garment; and **ה** <note>He</note> is like the simple spirit, and **Vau** <note>ו</note> is like the Soul in the spirit of life: But the remaining letters refer more to spiritual bodies, namely **ח ז ד ג ב** <note>Het, Zayin, Daleth, Gimel, Beth</note>: Where therefore the holy letters run together by themselves and alone, it is to be understood that God is signified in His simple nature: For example, **אה** <note>Ah</note> signifies "Where," denoting by this very fact that God is to be found nowhere, or is infinite; again it is taken for an "island"; which island in an occult sense is taken for the land of the living, and the cornerstone, which is the Messiah, surrounded by the sea or the abyss; and yet it is used in the common sense: Thus **הו** <note>Ho</note> denotes God as kind and clothed with strength, etc.

But if these essential letters are joined with the less essential letters of the same order, they denote a more corporeal thing, such as **אב** <note>Ab</note>, "father"; **אד** <note>Ad</note>, "to the Excellent," "exalted," etc. Which attributes pertain to the creature exalted by divine goodness: **אה** <note>He-Aleph</note>; "This, that"; as if one were to say, a thing demonstrable in the light of God: So also **זה** <note>Zeh</note>, "That one, this"; And **יד** <note>Yad</note> denotes the hand and power; for **יד** <note>Yad</note> had its force from **י** <note>Jod</note>, and so in the others. We say therefore, that **יד** <note>Yad</note> makes all things through **א** <note>Aleph</note>; and so it denotes in its simple nature substantial things, pertaining to that order of Angels which is called <term>Ophaim</term> <note>original: "Ophaim"; Hebrew for "Wheels," referring to the angelic beings described in the vision of Ezekiel</note>, that is, wheels or forms: **ד** <note>Daleth</note> denotes life, wisdom, the house of God, and the rest: **ג** <note>Gimel</note> proves kindness, retribution, strong and robust angels, peace, and the rest; and so in the others. But if the sacred letters mix themselves still more deeply with letters, they have a significance even deeper in worldly matter: Thus, as <term>Chen</term> <note>original: "חן"; Grace</note> was God being kind, so **אל** <term>El</term> <note>original: "אל"; God</note> is the strong and robust God, proving justice: It is also the spirit of discipline; For **ל** <note>Lamed</note> denotes discipline; And so, extending itself outside the Empyrean heaven, it mixes itself with the sphere of <term>Saturn</term>, and immerses itself into the middle heaven: And in the name <term>Elohim</term> <note>original: "אלהים"; a common name for God in the Bible, often associated with His role as Creator and Judge</note> the divine power **א** <note>Aleph</note> and **ה** <note>He</note> mix themselves through **ל** <note>Lamed</note> and **ם** <note>Mem</note>; that is, through heaven and earth; For **א** <note>Aleph</note> in the darkness proved the earth, and **ל** <note>Lamed</note> the sphere of Saturn, whose character it almost has; which Saturn rules over the earths: and **ם** <note>Mem</note> is the symbol of the waters or the heavens, which **י** <note>Jod</note> illuminates: And so God is said to be in heaven, and is called the "bright Aleph," or <term>Apollo</term> the preserver: He is also said to be on earth, and so is called the "dark Aleph"; and <term>Dionysus</term> the tearer-apart: May you be a son of light, and not those perceiving the dark Aleph. Furthermore, it is also because of this mixing of the Deity with worldly matter that <term>Jehovah</term> is said to be this same thing, which in another respect is a creature: For the angel, who went before the Israelites, was called an "angel" in respect to the column of the dark cloud, and <term>Jehovah</term> in respect to the column of divine fire: So also the fire, which <term>Moses</term> saw in the bush under Mount <term>Horeb</term>, by the same reasoning, is at one moment called an "Angel," insofar as the "otherness" of the flame is considered, and at another moment <term>Jehovah</term>, in respect to the simplicity of the light that was present. Moreover, the reason for this thing is best declared in the word <term>Elohim</term> <note>original: "אלהים"</note>—

These refer to Psalm 8:5 and Psalm 138:1.</note> Finally, from these most holy letters, the letters of the second order, which are called the "mothers," are animated; for example, **Mem** (**מ**) denoting water and darkness, through **Aleph** (**א**) whose shapeless house they were before creation; and **Shin** (**ש**), which is a third thing springing forth from these, through the luminous **Aleph**, or **Jod**, to which **Shin** refers, and through the spirit **He** (**ה**), to which water refers, and through the dark **Aleph**, to which darkness and gloom are attributed: For where **Jehovah**, that is, the hidden **Aleph**, does not shine forth but reflects its rays back into itself, there it is necessary that darkness results and predominates, and consequently, that the waters are left dense, shapeless, and like horrendous shadows. But where He manifests His form, *there the horrendous shadow, by an oblique revolution, is accustomed to slip away at the presence of His luminous face, as <term>Hermes Trismegistus</term> <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure said to be the author of the Hermetic Corpus, a series of texts on philosophy, magic, and alchemy.</note> testifies.* And then, in the meditation after the mystical appearance of **Aleph** or **Jehovah**, **Beth** (**ב**) follows, and the Word is brought forth; and then **Beth** is called "father," because **Beth** is His son or primary emanation, appearing in the humid nature: Thus it becomes **Zayin** (**ז**); in which a fiery spirit floating produces a creature adorned with a triple crown, signifying by this very fact that this creature was created in the likeness of the <term>Trinity</term> from divine rays and humid nature, like the Holy Spirit from **Jod** and **Vau** in the wonderful uncreated name. Therefore, from the mixture of these elements, things are created in the world that are more worthy the more they receive essential letters in their Hebrew names: For this was the method by which **Adam**, the first man, assigned to every creature a naming proper to its nature.

For example: we see that in the word **Bereshit** <note>original: "ראשית"; the Hebrew word for "In the beginning," the start of Genesis.</note> "In the beginning," there are two extremities: **Resh** (**ר**) indeed denoting poverty or need—the first boundary toward the act of fertility—and **Tav** (**ת**) of inheritance, grace, and succession; and **Tav** which is an indication of solitude, whence is placed before it <term>Tohu</term> (**תהו**) "solitude" and <term>Bohu</term> (**בהו**) "<term>Chaos</term>," <note>original: "Chaos, sive materia informis & inanis"; the void or formless matter before creation.</note> or formless and empty matter. Here the difference between <term>hyle</term> <note>The Greek term for "matter" or "stuff," often used in philosophy to describe the raw potential of the physical world.</note> and Chaos can be discerned: For in **Tohu**, emptiness is found at the beginning, middle, and end, because neither **Aleph**, **Beth**, nor **Shin** is found there. But nevertheless, because **He** (**ה**) is found there, it denotes the power of being brought into action through the luminous **Jod** or **Aleph**. But in the Chaos of **Bohu**, the **Vav** (**ו**) is found there; that is, **Vav** in place of one **He** in the word **Tohu**: Whence *hyle* is converted into Chaos, where there is nonetheless no peace, but discord; because **Vav** is not in the interior, but outside the middle **He**. Whence in **He**, or the Spirit of the elements, **Mem** (**מ**) or the earth, and the end, wage war with **Vav** or the light in the middle of **He**, which is heaven. But by the transposition and mediation of **Jod** between **Mem** and **Aleph**, peace and concord will be made between heaven and earth: Whence **Tav** (**ת**) denotes to mark, to designate, to describe, to circumscribe, and to define, as if one were to say: God bound the litigious and all irregular and quarrelsome things in concordant places with the bond of peace, which is **Vav**, and restricted, circumscribed, and defined all elements within their own proper limit. For **Tav** in this place is the "Great **Aleph**" or the **Omega** (**Ω**), which is as much a symbol of God as **Aleph**: But **Tav** denotes the dark **Aleph**. For the Great **Aleph** is a symbol of the number 1,000, indicating by this the entry of **Aleph**, or God, into the depths of matter or cubic multiplicity. So also **AA** is taken for the form, where **Aleph** is read as **Aleph** in pronunciation. 

But returning to the matter, we see that in the beginning the whole act or luminosity of the divinity, **Aleph** and **Shin**, is covered as if by a dense and dark cloud, namely **Mem** and **Tav**; where **Mem** is dark, and **Aleph** is luminous, and **Shin** is the effect, which is to be produced into action by both through the mediation of the humid gloom for the completion of the world. And so the Creator of all things delineated them ideally in his <term>Archetype</term> <note>The original model or divine blueprint of all things existing in the mind of God.</note> by his secret counsel, before he broke out from the cloud of darkness and, by extending the humid nature like a curtain, established the heavens through the Word. This, therefore, is that "Beginning" in whose center **Aleph** and **Shin** were hiding; by which later water, the heavens, and the earth emerged clearly and lightly from darkness into light through the revelation of divine majesty: Hence the waters are called in the Hebrew speech and character **Mayim** (**מים**) according to the uncreated exemplar of the name **Jehovah** (**יהוה**) or the name **Ehieh** (**אהיה**); so that the lower waters (the first **Mem**) and the upper waters (the final **Mem**) are illuminated by the rays of the uncreated Sun, **Jod**, in the middle and as if in the center of the entire watery mass. Similarly, heaven is described in Hebrew characters as **Shamayim** (**שמים**); where **Shin** denotes fire or created light, and the first **Mem** the waters above the firmament, and the second **Mem** the waters beneath the firmament, joined together by **Jod**, whose symbol is **Vav**, or unity in **He**; so that **Shamayim** is said as if it were "fiery waters" or "illuminated waters," which are nothing other than the heavens: Whence the highest heaven is called <term>Empyrean</term>, as if a fiery spirit; and <term>ethereal</term>, that is, fiery air, etc. 

Similarly, the earth or mass of darkness is explained by these characters among the Hebrews: **Artzah** (**ארצה**) as if "cultivated earth"; where because of the presence of **Aleph** it is called cultivated earth, just as because of its absence it is called **Tohu** (solitude or empty earth) and **Tehom** (the abyss). In the characters of the earth, namely **Adamah** (**אדמה**), we see the reason why it is dark; namely, because **Aleph** by its luminous presence is found on the outside, but in the interior it lies hidden; and no luminous letter is found there. Whence that it is the seat of darkness is clearly explained, since **Dam** (**דמ**) are dark waters in it; and **Resh** (**ר**) argues that it is a gate or door through which **Aleph** enters into the dark waters of **Mem**, and hides itself in its cottage, or goes out through **Resh**, and illuminates the **Mem** of the other extremity. But if **Aleph** should look out from the dark waters of **Mem** in the degree of **Jod**, then its aspect is terrible: Whence **Adam** in the Hebrew language is the same as "formidable" and "terrible" in the Latin language. But also **Tzad** and **Aleph** (**צא**) are characters proving the earth; where **Aleph** is also on the outside in the manifest, but in the center it hides itself: Whence **Ratz** (**רץ**) is as if one were to say, a lack or defect of the presence of divine light; for **Resh** denotes poverty and want, but **Tzade** symbolizes with matter...

Therefore, this **Resh** (**ר**) is here and everywhere else in the place of the body or the medium that captures and receives divine influences from **Aleph** (**א**): And thus light was created; namely, the **Resh** (**ר**), the body of light, was adorned—that is, a portion of the higher spirit—and not the **Yod** (**י**) or **Aleph** (**א**), which are the essential characters of the divine and supersubstantial name; in which respect created light itself can be called **Jehovah**: For in such a manner **Jehovah** is called a *consuming fire*. <note>original: "ignis consumens"</note> By these things we are also reminded how noble and divine a thing light is, toward which so many characters or signs of the uncreated essence converge: Oh, how wonderful and pleasant is this contemplation! I confess indeed that while I think and write these things, I seem to myself to be snatched up in a certain ecstasy of divine pleasure, and with my mind exalted, I reach even to the palace of <term>Ehyeh</term> <note>Hebrew for "I Am," the name of God revealed to Moses.</note> itself.

Furthermore, in the examination of the nature of the day, we find that **Or** (**אור**), the day, <note>In Genesis, God called the Light (Or) Day.</note> has within itself a double proportion of uncreated light, namely **Vav** (**ו**) and **Aleph** (**א**), to a single proportion of the water, **Resh** (**ר**): Hence it is said; *And He called the light Day:* And, just as the light of the first day proceeded from the Fathers into the created things of the world—namely **Aleph** (**א**) and **Vav** (**ו**)—so also the Sun, a creature and a greater light, was produced from the mothers: Hence **Shemesh** (**שמש**), the Sun, has two signs and testimonies of created light through the repetition of the mother **Shin** (**ש**), which is the symbol of fire and created light; between these two **Shins** is placed **Mem** (**מ**), or the body and dense matter of the substance of the Sun, which is hidden and, as it were, submerged in the center of the double light or luminescence—or, to speak properly, **Shin** (**ש**): For the light produced on the first day has only a simple spiritual body; but in the Sun there is a double spiritual body, namely the higher **Shin** (**ש**) here, and **Vav** (**ו**) within **Vav** (**ו**). Hence the **Vav** (**ו**) of the hidden: created light is the soul of the mother **Shin** (**ש**); just as that is the <term>Anima Mundi</term> <note>The "Soul of the World," a concept where the universe is a living being with an underlying soul.</note> and the life of the Sun: The soul of created light is the Messiah himself, and light is the soul of **Shin** (**ש**), which is <term>Metattron</term> <note>A high-ranking angel in Jewish mystical tradition, often described as the celestial scribe or the mediator between God and man.</note>, or the soul of the visible world. The characters of the Moon also, the lesser light, are **Yareach** (**ירח**); where matter is strongly proven; namely, **Resh** (**ר**) the dense body, and **Heith** (**ח**) the stubborn and cloudy spirit; these two are illuminated by the virtue of **Yod** (**י**): Therefore, just as there were two testimonies of light in the Sun, and one of the spirit condensed in the center; so here, conversely, there are two dense and dark spirits as witnesses, and only a single part of light: From this also the reason can be gathered why the Sun is the father of life and the cause of multiplication; namely, that **Shin** (**ש**), the fire or the male, acting upon **Mem** (**מ**), the water or the female, and with her, in the manner of a cock and a hen, joining continually and incessantly, causes both the agent and the patient to disperse their life-giving seeds everywhere into the earth: Hence it is that among the Hebrews, **Shemesh** (**שמש**) signifies both to join together and to minister.

But, to arrive at the investigation of the nature of man, we perceive that in **Adam** (**אדם**), the soul of honor is God Himself, the **Aleph** (**א**); his spirit is **Daleth** (**ד**), and his body is **Mem** (**ם**); so that it is also argued from this that in the **Mem** (**ם**) is the door; or the gate and entry-way through which God enters into man, or His temple, by means of **Daleth** (**ד**), signifying wisdom, and **Aleph** (**א**), signifying His kind and peaceful spirit; which two are mystically included in **Aleph** (**א**), the father: Man is therefore sustained on one side by the spirit **Heith** (**ח**); by whose attraction and expiration, through the presence of God **Aleph** (**א**) in his right part, he lives and is established in this world: Thus, therefore, man was made a <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World," meaning man is a miniature reflection of the entire universe.</note> according to the pattern of the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World," the universe as a whole.</note>; and thus the world, both the greater and the lesser, was made and formed in the image of the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>: **Aleph** (**א**) gives life, **Mem** (**מ**) receives and is the vehicle of the same; and both finally—namely the light **Aleph** (**א**) through the spirit **Mem** (**מ**) — are introduced into the body **Heith** (**ח**): We could indeed insert infinite things of this kind into this treatise; but we shall certainly not do so, since other things of another nature call us away.

Here, however, we conclude with the concluding Hebrew letters, that those final two which exceed twenty are the complement of the whole mystery of creation: For, just as **Tsadi** (**ץ**) denotes solitude, emptiness, and depletion as well as the abyss, and consequently is a symbol of the darkness by which the world is bounded (for "the beginning" <note>original: "Reshith"</note> ends emptiness and solitude; and "emptiness" <note>original: "Bohu"</note> begins, and likewise "the abyss" <note>original: "Tehom"</note> and "chaos" <note>original: "Tohu"</note>), so conversely **Tav** (**ת**) is fullness and the removal of the vacuum through the presence of God's rays everywhere in the Spirit; And as **Tav** (**ת**) terminates the letters in nothingness and in an imperfect number—that is, the spherical world is terminated everywhere with darkness or the vacuum—so its being begins from unity: Wherefore **Tav** (**ת**) is not a letter, but a certain seal of the final limit of the letters: Thus in Cain there was the seal of disgrace, and in created things, there is the seal of the limits of the world, and of the entry into the margins of the empty and deformed matter: Whence the number of Hebrew letters is found in this way in the perfect sevenfold number, namely in the sevenfold multiplied three times, which is 21, according to the <term>Cabalistic</term> <note>Relating to the Kabbalah, a mystical Jewish tradition.</note> numbering of the effect of the divine name **Ehyeh** (**אהיה**), which denotes the essence in all things: For 10 and twice five and one constitute the gathering and addition of 21. ### SECTION I.

## Book I.
->*Concerning*<-
# THE PRIMARY ELEMENTS OF NATURE.
### CHAPTER I.

> *Whether (as some wrongly think) my opinions and the foundations of my doctrine are recent and, as it were, new?*

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'Q' set in a square frame with floral motifs and foliage.</image-desc>

BECAUSE a significant error has arisen among men, as some suppose my opinions to be recent and the foundations of my philosophy new and not at all ancient, I have deemed it worthwhile to demonstrate to those looking with the eyes of justice that if my foundations are ancient and my opinions are established both by philosophical reasoning and by living demonstration, then they are undoubtedly not new, and consequently not so dangerous—insofar as the argument of my opponents is framed solely in this way: that my opinions are dangerous because they are new. That my **Macrocosmic** <note>Relating to the "Macrocosm" or the great world/universe, as opposed to the "Microcosm" or the human being.</note> principles or foundations are drawn from the deepest depths <note>original: "visceribus"; literally "bowels" or "entrails," implying the innermost parts.</note> of antiquity can be proved and confirmed not only by the authority of the ancient philosophers but also by the testimony of the Holy Scriptures; for from those very principles the world and all things in it took their origin. 

Had this doctrine of mine been founded upon **Aristotelian** bases or principles—namely, upon **Matter**, **Form**, and **Privation** <note>Aristotle’s three principles of change: Matter is the substance, Form is the specific nature it takes, and Privation is the absence of a form that is yet to be realized.</note>—it would certainly, and without any hesitation, be regarded as ancient by those men driven by excessive curiosity, and it would be shared with the public without any opposition from them. But these "new" principles (as they call them)—namely, **Darkness**, **Water**, and **Light**—must not be accepted because they are supposedly recent, as if they were newly invented and unheard of before now. 

Does it not seem a gross and palpable sign of ignorance in Christian men to so greedily embrace the assertions of the pagan **Aristotle**, defending them with the most vehement insults and arguments, and even for their sake to repudiate, neglect, and hold in derision the truest principles of the Prophet **Moses** <note>original: "Antistitis Moysis"; Fludd uses "Antistes" (leader or high priest) to elevate Moses's status over secular philosophers.</note>—on whose authority we nevertheless place the foundations of our faith? Does not our Moses seem to assert that darkness was a hindrance to form and essence, by saying that the earth was void and darkness was upon the face of the deep <note>original: "abyssi"; the primordial abyss or "tehom" mentioned in Genesis 1:2.</note>? Does he not make darkness itself the receptacle of the unformed earth and, as it were, a shapeless veil? This matter, which is scarcely imaginable, he calls the "abyss." <header>CONCERNING THE PRIMARY ELEMENTS OF NATURE.</header>

...sis: **And the Spirit of the Lord was moved over the waters** <note>original: "Spiritus Domini ferebatur super aquas"; quoting Genesis 1:2.</note>, from which, as Saint Peter bears witness, the world and all things in it were made. Finally, was not light created on the first day as that formal principle and "first act," through which—as an immediate emanation of the fountain of all light into the purest Spirit of the water—all things were thereafter established? Do we not, therefore, perceive here from the Mosaic doctrine those three principles or foundations by which the heaven and earth were established through creation? Furthermore, if we are denied the faculty and freedom to follow the only and truest <term>Theosophy</term> <note>Divine wisdom or knowledge of God.</note> as well as Philosophy of the Holy Bible, such that we are forbidden the clearest light of the sacred letters and forced to wander like the blind in the filthy and muddy obscurity of the Heathens and infidels, then indeed against that unjust opinion of men (if such exists) we may fittingly allege in our defense and excuse that argument of the Prophet Baruch, chapter 3, which a just man should by no means reject:

> It is not fitting to desert the fountain of all wisdom, and to seek art, science, and intellect in foreign regions, as did the <term>Agarenes</term> <note>A biblical term often used in this period to refer to "outsiders" or those lacking the true faith.</note> and those who were in Teman, who indeed never recognized the way of true wisdom.

By which we are clearly taught to embrace the Holy Scripture as the fountain of all wisdom, and to leave behind the Heathen and foreign doctrine or writing, as it is something in which no true science or divine wisdom is found.

But what will these censors of mine say if I prove—with solid and irrefutable arguments—that even the ancient and famous philosophers of the Heathens, by traveling through Egypt, Arabia, Assyria, and especially Judea, stealthily snatched the foundations and principles of their entire Philosophical doctrine from the sacred fountain of mysteries, and from the Biblical treasury <note>original: "myrothecio"; literally a "perfume cabinet" or "receptacle for ointments," used here metaphorically for a storehouse of precious truths.</note> of the Word of God, and injuriously attributed them to themselves?

Indeed, setting aside all further dispute and proof, we shall perceive this very thing even with our own eyes if we leaf through the mystical writings of Plato, Hermes Trismegistus, Orpheus, Hesiod, Ovid, and the divine Philosophers, both poets and others.

And if all these things are not enough even for the most meticulous followers of Aristotle, let us descend to an inquiry into the principles of Aristotle himself; for thus we shall at last most easily realize that he was a disciple and imitator of the High Priest Moses—or rather, a plunderer of Mosaic principles, falsely attributing them to himself.

For what else (I ask you) is that **"First Matter"** of Aristotle—which he says is clearly nothing in "act," but merely a kind of imagination, or, as his teacher Plato would have it, an image appearing in a dream? Hence Aristotle called this "something in potentiality"; and yet it is called "nothing" because it is formless, since form alone gives a thing its name and its Being.

Is not that scarcely imaginable matter the **"Darkness"** of Moses, which was over the face of the abyss, which Synesius and others, along with Aristotle himself, called <term>Hyle</term> <note>A Greek term for primordial, unformed matter.</note>?

Next, what is that "Secondary Matter" of Aristotle except for *Hyle* or First Matter led into "act"? Or rather, the dark and deformed abyss of Moses now informed by the presence of the light and the "uncreated act," and distinguished by the name of **"Waters,"** which were the universal matter of all things in creation? Thus, that **"Void"** <note>original: "Inane."</note> of Moses, or this "quasi-nothing" of Aristotle, is led into act—that is, it is created—by the splendor of the uncreated light.

Hence Moses said, **"The Spirit of the Lord was moved over the waters,"** that is, by the presence of the informing Spirit, they are now named "Waters" and are produced in act, which before did not exist, or were not so named.

What, then, was that "Essential Form" of Aristotle, by the sight of which this matter in potentiality was reduced into act? Was it not that **Light** created on the first day, which was the first and immediate emanation from the living God into the moist matter?

Did he not, therefore, call that essential form the "first act," or the first "informer" of material things?

Finally, what did Aristotle understand by **"Privation"** <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, "privation" is the absence of a form that a thing should naturally possess.</note> except for the darkness and deformity which the matter in potentiality cast off at the very point of its informing or creation?

Which darkness, nonetheless, was not "privation" before the creation of things, because no positioning of matter preceded it; a fact which Aristotle seemed to be ignorant of, because he (differing in this from his teacher Plato) thought the world was eternal and not created.

But this darkness, with creation preceding it, can be called "privation" insofar as it is said to possess matter at that instant which exists between the point of corruption and generation.

What, then, do you think now of these "new" opinions? Are they so recent and new, when their foundations are found to be so ancient and venerable? Or, because I—as a Christian perhaps excelling more in the use of Mosaic doctrine than in that of Aristotle—attribute to my teacher Moses what is his by just measure, and in this I seem to differ from Aristotle (who, hiding the marrow and sense of Mosaic discipline behind a foreign veil of words, arrogantly and falsely ascribed to himself those principles of creation which Moses himself received from the mouth, instinct, and as if by the hand of the living God Jehovah the Creator, and converted them to his own Heathen sense); because (I say) I recognize the divine doctrine and true philosophy of my divine Master, am I therefore to be blamed?

Are not the Holy Bibles the fountain and origin of all wisdom and science? And shall we leave or desert them, so that we may follow the inconstant doctrine of the Agarenes and those in Teman—that is, of infidels and Heathens—who never knew true wisdom or certain science, but built a Philosophy for others relying on vain opinion and fragile imagination upon those foundations which were secretly stolen from the Jewish mysteries? And thus, by leaving behind life and the true science of the soul, we would knowingly and willingly bring death upon ourselves.

### CHAPTER I.

*Whether my opinions and the foundations of my doctrine are recent and, as it were, new—as some wrongly believe?*

SINCE no small error has arisen among men, while some think that my opinions are recent, and that the foundations of my Philosophy are new and by no means ancient, I have considered it worth the effort to demonstrate to those looking with eyes of justice that if my foundations are ancient, and my opinions are established both by Philosophical reasons and by living demonstration, then beyond doubt they are not new, and consequently not so dangerous—at least insofar as the argument of my opponents is formed solely on the basis that my opinions are dangerous because they are new. That my <term>Macrocosmic</term> <note>Relating to the "great world" or the universe as a whole, as opposed to the "microcosm" of the human being.</note> principles or foundations are drawn from the deepest bowels of antiquity, we can prove and confirm not only by the authority of ancient Philosophers, but even by the testimony of the holy scriptures; for from these very principles the world and all things that are in the world had their origin. If this doctrine of mine had been founded upon Aristotelian bases or principles—namely, upon Matter, Form, and <term>Privation</term> <note>In Aristotelian thought, "Privation" is the absence of a form that a substance is capable of having.</note>—it would certainly be held as ancient by these men driven by excessive curiosity, and would be published abroad without any of their contradiction. Yet these "new" principles (as they call them)—namely, Darkness, Water, and Light <note>original: "Tenebræ nempe, Aqua, & Lux"</note>—are not to be admitted, because they are recent and, as it were, newly invented and unheard of before this time. But does this not seem a gross and palpable argument of ignorance in Christian men, to so greedily embrace the assertions of the Heathen Aristotle and defend them with the most vehement arguments of insult, even to the point of repudiating, neglecting, and holding in derision the most true principles of the High Priest Moses for their sake? Nevertheless, it is upon his authority that we place the foundations of our faith. Does not our Moses seem to assert that darkness was the impediment to form and essence, by saying that the earth was empty, and darkness was over the face of the abyss? Does he not make darkness itself the receptacle and, as it were, the deformed veil of the unformed earth? Indeed, he calls this matter—which is scarcely imaginable—the "Abyss." Did not the Spirit of the Lord, by the power of his uncreated light, give form to that "almost nothing" (or the deformity of darkness and <term>hyle</term> <note>A Greek term for primordial matter.</note>), so that he reduced the abyss into the form and being of the waters? ...scriptures: "And the Spirit of the Lord was moved over the waters," <note>original: "Spiritus Domini ferebatur super aquas"</note> from which waters—as St. Peter testifies—the world and all things within it were made. If all these things are still not enough for the most meticulous followers of Aristotle, let us descend to an inquiry into the principles of Aristotle himself: for in this way we shall finally and most easily perceive that he was a disciple and imitator of the leader Moses—or rather, a thief of the Mosaic principles, falsely attributing them to himself. Is this scarcely imaginable matter not the "Darkness" of Moses, which was "upon the face of the abyss"? This is what Synesius and others, along with Aristotle himself, called **Hyle**. <note>A Greek term for "matter" or "raw material."</note> 

Next, what is that "Second Matter" of Aristotle except the **Hyle** or First Matter led into "act"? This means that by the presence of the informing Spirit, they are now named "Waters" and are produced in act, whereas before they did not exist or were not so named. 

What, then, was that "Essential Form" of Aristotle, by whose aspect this matter "in potential" was reduced to "act"? Was it not that Light created on the first day, which was the first and immediate emanation from the living God into the moist matter? Did he not, therefore, call that essential form the "first act," or the first thing informing material objects?

Nevertheless, this darkness before the creation of things was not "privation," as no positioning of matter preceded it; this is something Aristotle seemed to ignore because he, differing from his teacher Plato in this, thought the world was eternal and not created. But this darkness, following creation, can be called "privation" insofar as it is said to possess matter in that instant between the point of corruption and generation. 

What, then, do you now think of these "new" opinions? Are they so recent and new, when their foundations are found to be so ancient and venerable? Or, because I—as a Christian perhaps more proficient in the use of Mosaic doctrine than that of Aristotle—attribute to my teacher Moses what is his by just measure, and in this I seem to differ from Aristotle (who, hiding the marrow and sense of the Mosaic discipline behind a foreign veil of words, arrogantly and falsely ascribed to himself those principles of creation which Moses himself received from the mouth, instinct, and as if from the very hand of the living God Jehovah the Creator, and converted them to his own Pagan sense); because, I say, I recognize the divine doctrine and true philosophy of my Divine Master, am I therefore to be blamed? Are not the Holy Bibles the source and origin of all wisdom and science? Thus, by abandoning life and the true science of the soul, we would knowingly and willingly bring death upon ourselves.

### CHAPTER II.

->On Darkness and its Varieties.<-

<margin>Wisdom 11:18.</margin> That darkness existed before all things—into which the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH, representing the divine creative power.</note> acted during the creation of the world to lead them into a lucid nature or act—is taught to us by that most wise Solomon. His words are as follows: *God made the world out of unformed matter*; or, as Hieronymus <note>Saint Jerome, the 4th-century scholar and Bible translator.</note> interprets it, *from invisible matter*. This refers to the spirit or the waters, which were empty and void—that is, filled with no lucid form or grace, nor brought into being in any specific way. From this it follows that, since light is in every way opposed to darkness, darkness and gloom necessarily follow wherever light is absent. Hence it is said in <margin>Wisdom 7:22.</margin> *Wisdom is clearer and more lucid than the Sun or the Stars, which night succeeds*; that is, darkness and gloom follow the absence or the lack of the presence of the divine spirit. These words of Solomon seem to be perfectly confirmed by <margin>Job 12:22.</margin> Job. Indeed, from his express words, we can best extract three species of darkness: *He reveals (he says) the foundations out of darkness, and brings the lethal shadow into the light.* By the word "Darkness," therefore, he understands the mother of all darkness, namely the most obscure <term>Hyle</term> <note>original: "hylam." A term for prime matter or the raw substance of the universe before it is given form.</note>, in which there is no trace of light. And although the <term>Aleph</term> <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, here symbolizing the hidden divine spark or unity.</note> was hidden within it from eternity before the world was brought forth into light, it was nevertheless called entirely "dark" in a relative sense, even if in itself it is absolutely lucid; for it did not wish to emit rays toward the circumference (that is, into multiplicity), but contracted them within its own center and unity. <margin>Hermes Trismegistus</margin> Hence Hermes Trismegistus says: *The Monad generates the monad, and reflected its own heat back into itself.* This was the reason that the universal moist spirit, destitute of all divine grace, was covered and veiled by immense darkness and absolute gloom, to the extent that not even a spark of light was present in it. From this, it was clearly considered as nothing, and nothing seemed to exist; but all that which was—if indeed it was anything at all—was called "nothing," insofar as it was nothing else but darkness. Such darkness utterly resists the one who gives it a name and form of existence, and it strongly struggles against any divided act; for it is in the very nature and disposition of darkness never to move, but on the contrary, to rest forever in its own connatural place. These, then, are those general darknesses, or the *hyle*, from whose womb or entrails—as the *Aleph* operates from the center toward the circumference—the depths (that is, the abyss of waters) are revealed. And the "lethal shadow" (which <margin>Hermes Trismegistus</margin> Hermes Trismegistus calls *horrible*) which was everywhere still upon the face of the abyss, was that dark Chaos in which the holy splendor was present, but in a confused and irregular manner. From the eventual gathering of this splendor into the center of the created machine, the earth or dry dust was produced. Concerning each of these, we shall discourse in methodical order in this book; but before we descend into that public field, we shall provide a brief and succinct discourse on the consideration of the sacred characters, by which the natures and dispositions of each of the aforementioned species are explained as if by living hieroglyphs.

### CHAPTER III.

->On the examination of the sacred characters, by which the aforementioned species are explained in the Holy Language according to their exact nature and condition.<-

IN the preceding sections, we have clearly enough declared that every thing has its own name according to the property of its disposition, so that the characters of a name are like symbols and hieroglyphs of the condition of the named thing itself. It was in this respect that God brought to Adam all the beasts of the earth and all the birds of the air, so that he might give them names suitable to their natures—that is, so that he might assign characters to each name which would best declare their internal nature through "formal" and "essential" letters (in proportion to their life in heat and moisture), and explain the measure and number of the body's mass in its elementary composition through more "material" and "opaque" letters. From this it happened that to every creature was attributed a name composed of living letters, in every way consistent and suitable to its disposition. Nor indeed (as I believe) is there anything in the nature of things expressed by the Word of God in golden characters whose nature and essence is not clearly, albeit mystically, explained in those same characters. Thus, if the mysteries of the sacred letters or living characters were fully revealed to men, I truly believe it would not be impossible for them to behold the exact form and even the physical composition of any thing as if in a mirror; since even in a rough manner, and through external consideration alone, we are accustomed to uncovering significant things and rendering judgments that are not absurd, though perhaps not absolute. For example, in our current subject (for we now prepare ourselves for our task), <margin>Gen. 1.</margin> when mention is made of general darkness, according to Genesis 1, there is placed first <term>Tohu va-bohu</term> <note>original Hebrew: תהו ובהו</note>, which means *solitude, emptiness, deformity* (or lacking all form), and *vastness*. Thus Moses says, *the earth was such before creation*; and by "earth" he understood those empty darknesses from which, eventually, the earth was made, once it was filled with light and enriched with fertility after the darkness was driven back to the center. And "the earth was emptiness or solitude"; that is, the substance of the earth, now visible and sensible to us, was at that time a vast and empty darkness without any form or spark of light; as its matter before creation was the substance of the *hyle*, in which there was no light...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the primary elements of nature, specifically focusing on the linguistic and mystical nature of darkness. <header>ON THE PRIMARY ELEMENTS OF NATURE</header>

...the testimony of the one who gives form: For the first letter *Tav* [ת] is a sign of privation <note>original: "privationis." In Aristotelian philosophy, privation is the absence of a quality that should naturally be present.</note>. Indeed, it is said that Cain was marked with it, to prove that he was excluded from the divine presence. Furthermore, it is the final letter, by which the world terminates the boundaries of its light and ends with the darkness of *hyle* <note>original: "hylæ." From the Greek 'hyle', meaning primordial, unformed matter.</note>. But because this final letter is placed at the beginning [of the word *Tohu*], it denotes that before the start of the world, there existed something like the world’s limits, which are adjacent to *hyle*. Furthermore, both *Bohu* [בהו] and *Tohu* [תהו] are the characters of the waters—or of the spirit and the waters, or of subtle and coarse waters—existing only in potentiality toward that being which they now possess, because they lack every act of divine light. For neither *Bet* [ב], nor *He* [ה], nor *Vav* [ו] are present in them; only *Tav* [ת], which is a passive or feminine letter, is found there without any accompanying masculine letter. Therefore, just as a female without a male remains empty, sterile, and useless for procreation or for bringing anything into action, so also is *Tohu* overshadowed by its own dark veil, without divine action. Yet this action is, in and of itself, full of both types of fertility, as *Hermes Trismegistus* <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with a body of mystical and alchemical writings.</note> testifies. *Tohu* is therefore plainly nothing, because it is Darkness and empty *hyle*. Indeed, it is *hyle* insofar as it is destitute of all presence of light, and consequently, it is the highest, most extreme, and most general "genus" of darkness, from which its subordinate types are derived: namely, gloom and the abyss. These are all those dense waters appearing from the womb of *hyle* which are not yet purified by light, but exist as almost—though not entirely—unformed and empty. This we can also perceive from the names of the characters themselves or their Hebrew root: For *Bohu* [בהו] does not differ much from *Tohu* [תהו], except for the letter *Bet* [ב], because the offspring or mixture of *hyle* now begins to reveal itself so that it appears to be water. Hence it is concluded with a "closed" *Bet* [ב], which denotes dark waters; for an "open" *Bet* [ב] <note>The author is likely referring to the visual shape or the mystical "opening" of the letter to let in the light of the first letter, *Aleph*.</note> argues for the sight of the lucid *Aleph* [א], or the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> outside the abyss, by which the dark waters are illuminated. Thus it happens that the abyss is the second degree, or the "second son" of darkness. The third degree, however, is that gloom which is the lowest contraction of the darkness of any heaven during the second spiritual day, or the gathering of horrific shadows into the lowest place. In its womb the divine fire is enclosed, and the rays of light are sown; that is, in the center of the abyss, light is held back by the spirit covered in darkness and gloom, and the divine presence seems to exult with the angels. This is also taught to us by the characters of its name, which are arranged thus: *Choshech* [חושך], Darkness or Chaos. Here, the luminous character of fire and light, *Shin* [ש], is enclosed by two dark and material letters, *Chet* [ח] and *Kaph* [ך]; it is as if the solar light were obstructed and surrounded on all sides by a dense and gloomy cloud, so that nothing but darkness and gloom could be seen. This is similar to the "palpable darkness" of Egypt, or when God wished to cover and hide his face, as in the pillar of cloud, and when at the time of the Lord’s passion there was darkness over the face of the earth from the sixth to the ninth hour. Finally, the last species of darkness is the earth itself, whose interposition between the Sun and the hemisphere of the world's machine causes night to fall daily. But indeed, that this is the lightest of all species of darkness is shown to us by the three characters from which it is composed, namely *Eretz* [ארץ]; here light is not entirely enclosed, as in *Choshech* [חושך], but flashes out from one side of the dark characters through *Aleph* [א]. This proves that the solar light, or the visible presence of God, is always manifested in one hemisphere of the earth (or the final heap of darkness). By this reasoning, this species of darkness, which was previously an empty, void, and solitary earth, is now a fertile land, filled with the roots of minerals and plants having their own nurseries, adorned everywhere with fruit-bearing trees, and a little later inhabited by animals of every kind. How these three words agree with one another in nature, take it thus: *Tohu* by interpretation is emptiness, the void, the unformed thing, solitude, etc. *Bohu* is the Abyss; which abysses, as *Psalm 77:17* testifies, *feared the presence of the Lord and were troubled*; arguing from this that they were contrary to the splendor of God, and consequently covered in gloom. And *Genesis 1*: *Darkness was upon the face of the abyss.* And *Hermes Trismegistus, Pimander 1*: *Darkness and shadow were moved by the ineffable face of light, and they glided away in an oblique revolution.* And *Pimander 3*: *There were infinite shadows in the abyss, etc.* *Choshech* in the Latin tongue is Darkness, obscuring, gloom, obscurity, etc. *Eretz* is the earth, which in *Job 17:12* seems to be called darkness and hell; and whose dark places the Psalmist says in *Psalm 74:20* are *full of the cruel and the violent, etc.* But we shall make mention of those things particularly and distinctly in this place.

## CHAPTER IV.

->*On the first and highest kingdom of darkness, or the most general genus, which is called* תהו [Tohu] *by the Hebrews, and* χάη [Chaos] *by the Greeks, and solitude, darkness, and emptiness by the Latins.*<-

*Tohu* [תהו] among the Hebrews and *Chaos* [χάη] among the Greeks is the same as solitude, gloom, and empty darkness among the Latins. The Latins also frequently use this Greek word *Hyla* for the primary material principle—that is, for the most remote matter—although some use this term for every species of darkness. Hence *Synesius* <note>A 4th-century philosopher-bishop.</note> says in his second Hymn:

> The ether covered the back
> Of the fluctuating Hyle,
> With fire sitting upon the summit.

But we truly accept it as the primordial material principle of all things; which is the most remote matter, formless, and existing only in potentiality. Regarding this, Augustine speaks thus: *When I conceive of something formless, I first understand nothing better than I understood before; because, just as shadows are seen by seeing nothing, so silence is heard by hearing nothing.* From which it follows that *Hyle* is that which is perceived between something and nothing. Therefore, just as it is not called "something," so it must be held by us as "nothing" insofar as it is not informed—that is, it is not illuminated by creation. Consequently, God created all things out of nothing; that is, He produced all things into being not from a pre-existing or informed act, but from nothing or from a formless thing. For Augustine acknowledges that *Hyle* is not "something," and in respect to that, it is as if nothing; not otherwise than what the Cabalists call the "dark Aleph" <note>The letter Aleph (א) is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In mystical thought, it represents the infinite source before manifestation.</note> when it does not shine for others. For what can that be or be considered in the nature of things which is called empty, void, and dark; that is, which is said to be destitute of every luminous form? 

Hence, when God willed to create the world, it was necessary to set aside that "emptiness and void" <note>original: "inane & vacuum"; referring to the Latin Vulgate translation of Genesis 1:2.</note>, since while they were present, nothing could arise or be created in actual existence. Hence Job 26:7 says: *God extends the North over the empty and void* (that is, He made the heavens revolve over the North pole; he established the beautiful, informed spirit in place of the nothingness or the void and empty) *and he hangs the earth upon nothing;* that is, the primordial darkness of *Hyle*, or the dark spirits driven downward, are now filled with rays of formal light and have left behind the name of "void and emptiness." Insofar as all things are richly furnished and abundant through the divine presence, they are said to be "suspended upon nothing" on an earth well-cultivated by God; that is, established in the place of the void by the power of the Word.

From these things we can gather that the "empty and void," which was nothing other than *hyle* and primordial darkness, existed before the heavens or the world were created and brought into the light. And hence in Genesis 1 it is said that the earth was "void or empty." This earth is indeed taken for the first darkness; for these were in potentiality toward the earth, which flows with the abundance of the divine act. And this earth was named "formless and empty" before any creature was brought forth into the world or issued into the light. 

This "empty earth," then, or universal darkness, or horrendous shadows, embraced the "deep spirit" hiding in their womb or abyss—existing as almost mere nothing—with foul arms, sad and lethal to the nature about to be created. This lasted until, by the appearance of the divine presence, it was revealed both what that deep thing hidden in the womb of *hyle* or the primary darkness was, and what the darknesses themselves (so opposed to the life of creatures) were; according to that passage in Job 12:22: *He reveals the deep things out of darkness, and brings out the lethal shadow into light;* that is, He made the spirit or the waters, submerged in the oblivion of deformed shadows, now emerge from them, and by His ineffable light He brought the horrendous darkness and lethal shadows (which are contrary to life, for they are the principles of privation) into the light.

But now with a light leap we shall descend to the second species of darkness, namely to the nature and condition of the Abyss.

# C H A P T E R V.

## *On the scruple of some who rise up against my opinion, in which I establish that hyle is uncreated.*

Since (to deal with it in passing) a scruple of no small importance occupies the minds of some—as if a very great error had crept up on me in this: that I called *Hyle* (the first matter or those Mosaic darknesses) uncreated—just as if by this very thing I had established something co-eternal with God, I therefore also respond to this objection. I am far from such great presumption; I constantly assert, fortified not only by the opinions of the ancient philosophers but also by the authority of the most Reverend Father St. Augustine, that although *hyle*, or first matter, or the unformed abyss—that is, covered in darkness—is something by name, yet it is not anything in reality. From which it follows that it is not undeservedly defined as that which is conceived by the imagination between absolute nothing and this "something" in truth, or a thing informed and created. For this reason, St. Augustine says that this matter is scarcely imaginable, like silence in respect to speech. Just as, therefore, silence is not speech, but is the potential for speech; so also *hyle* or the dark abyss is nothing, but in potentiality for reduction into something in act, that is, creation.

From which it must be gathered that this first matter is something scarcely imaginable, empty, and consequently nothing; for where the act of God is absent, it is impossible for any thing to be able to subsist in act <note>The author uses "act" (actus) in the Aristotelian sense of being "actualized" or made real.</note>, since His presence is that first and supersubstantial act creating all things and informing all things. And yet these darknesses were destitute of all form and divine presence, and therefore it is clear they are held plainly for nothing, in respect to any thing. Furthermore, we do not doubt that the learned understand the creation of all things to be nothing other than the attribution of act, given to nothing or to unformed things, and consequently the induction of form conferred upon imaginary things, which previously were not informed by the actual presence of the spirit of the Lord.

But truly *hyle* or first matter was a thing denoted indeed by the name of the art, but in truth not to be conceived except in a vain and fantastical way through the imagination, insofar as it comes to be considered in potentiality alone, holding itself like a phantom in sleep, or silence to a voice, as was said. This *hyle*, after it was created or brought into act, is called by Aristotle "second matter," <term>materia secunda</term> insofar as it is derived from the first. By Moses it is called by the name of "waters," which flowed out from the dark and deformed abyss, the radiant presence of the Spirit of the Lord intervening, taking on the appearance of waters. By Hermes Trismegistus, however, it is called "moist nature," revealed from the horrendous shadow through the assistance of the divine Word. And St. Peter says, in 2 Peter 3:5 <note>The text incorrectly cites 3.6.</note>, that the heavens were of old and the earth consisting of water and through water by the word of God. And yet it is said that God created all things from nothing.

Are not, therefore, the unformed waters or the abyss understood by "nothing," upon whose face were darknesses which were plainly nothing in act, and yet by the presence of the informing fiery Spirit became Waters? For since it is the condition of the essential form to give name and being, it follows that that thing is nothing from which form is utterly absent; that is, having neither a proper name nor a genuine being. The foundation of the world was, therefore, in potentiality an abyss destitute of form, inasmuch as upon its face were primordial darknesses, by whose presence form is entirely removed and the trophy of nothingness is established. But the foundation of the world in act was water, brought into act from the dark abyss (as if from potentiality and plain nothingness in respect to essence), that is, water made or created in act. Does not Job himself seem to support this thing exactly, when in *chapter 12, verse 22*, he speaks in these words: *He reveals foundations from the darkness, and brings out into the light the shadow of death?* Where by "foundations" he understands (if I am not mistaken) the active and passive principle, namely water which, according to the testimony of Peter in the place cited above, is the material foundation of heaven and earth, and light, which is the fun-

...the formal foundation shining forth from the darkness. Even Job calls the abyss the "shadow of death," <note>original: "umbram lethalem"</note> that is, a darkness that removes form by its presence (from which death follows) no differently than light, by its countenance and appearance, removes the deformity of the abyss. It is said that light brought back that "nothing"—or rather, that "potential something" existing between absolute nothing and something in act—into the "Being" of the waters. Does not that man, as wise as he was patient <note>Referring to Job.</note>, seem to confirm this same thing to us in chapter 26, verse 7, with these most clear words: *God stretches out the North over the empty and the vacuum, and hangs the earth over nothing*? Here, by "the empty and the vacuum," <note>original: "inane & vacuum"</note> he understands the shadow of death, which Moses also called the "empty earth," insofar as the created earth was produced from that shadow—destitute of divine splendor and presence (which is now said to fill all things)—and was filled with the most abundant gifts and seeds of the divine presence through the repercussion of the rays of divine light mixed with shadows toward the center.

All these things seem to be best demonstrated by the Rabbis of the Jews writing in the Cabalistic <term>Cabalistic: Referring to Kabbalah, a tradition of Jewish mysticism that explores the relationship between the eternal, mysterious Infinite and the finite universe.</term> manner, who say: that *Aleph* <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet: א</note> (which they call the Principle), when retracted within the abyss of darkness, immanent and idle, or (as they say) looking toward nothing, is therefore called *An*, <note>original: אן; usually rendered as 'Ayin,' meaning 'Nothing' or 'Non-Being.'</note> that is, "Nothing," or "Non-Being," and "the No-End," <note>original: "non finis"; likely referring to the *Ein Sof* or the Infinite.</note> because we, punished by such poverty of wit in divine matters, judge those things which do not appear no differently than those things which do not exist. But where it shows itself so that it is "something" and truly subsists, there the "Dark *Aleph*" is converted into the "Luminous *Aleph*." 

From this it is explained to us that, although Wisdom (which they call *Aleph* and the Principle) is considered by our thin capacity as "Nothing"—since, hidden in the abyss of darkness, it seems to be like nothing or "Non-Being" insofar as it does not appear in "act"—it follows from there, as if by concession, that the darkness itself is much more regarded as nothing; for indeed, by the deformity and privative appearance of darkness, a "something" is made into "nothing." 

But if these assertions of mine do not yet suffice for you, I certainly do not doubt that I shall satisfy your curiosity with the following reasoning, so that I may at last reconcile and unite your wavering spirits with my own mind: I believe it escapes no one of sound mind that our God, Jehovah, by his secret wisdom and inscrutable counsel, decreed that the world be fabricated out of nothing by weight, measure, and number; and that he first delineated the pattern, matter, and form of this creation in his eternal and supersubstantial Idea or Archetype <term>Archetype: The original model or "blueprint" in the mind of God before physical creation.</term> before it was led into "act" by true creation for human sense. From this, however, it follows that mere and absolute "nothing" was so prepared by this secret decree of the Creator that—although that matter seems unformed to us, and thus scarcely imaginable to the thinness and poverty of our grasp and intellect—it was nevertheless destined by the hidden counsel of God to exist as the matter for creating the world. Suddenly, then, it was so prepared from plain "nothing" that it stood forth as "something in potential." 

Indeed, this "potentiality" or "preparation" was to the Decreer <note>God, as the one who issued the decree of creation.</note> already a sort of most absolute creation, though most hidden and appearing not at all, insofar as it was not yet led into "sensible act." But to conclude this clause of the declaration briefly and as if with a single word—through that which is considered in Scholastic doctrine <term>Scholastic doctrine: The system of theology and philosophy taught in medieval European universities, based on Aristotelian logic and the writings of the Church Fathers.</term> to be in no way inconsistent with the substance of the Divinity—we say that, insofar as God is present at all times, to that extent all things which have had an origin and actual existence in the concept and intellect of men have always been in "objective potentiality" before the eyes of God. Although this potentiality seems like "nothing" to human consideration, yet with respect to the preceding decree of the Creator, it is in a certain way already a "creature in act" before God. 

We conclude, therefore—in order to establish this opinion of ours by producing an even more manifest passage—that it is likely from the very context of the Holy Scriptures that the world, and those things which exist in the world, were composed and produced from matter that was not yet created (that is, destitute of "act") and consequently unformed. For regarding this, the express words of Solomon himself are found in his most complete *Cosmological Magic*, in the Book of Wisdom, chapter 11, verse 28 <note>In modern Bibles, this is Wisdom of Solomon 11:17.</note>; which according to Pagninus’s translation read: *The hand of the Almighty made the world from unformed matter*; or according to Tremellius’s exposition: *Your hand created the world from unformed matter*; or as Jerome renders it: *Your hand created the world from invisible matter*. From these it clearly appears that my aforementioned opinion in no way departs from the object of Truth itself.

## CHAPTER VI.

->*Concerning the second kingdom of darkness, namely the Abyss, and its species.*<-

The Abyss, or *abyssos* <note>original: ἄβυσσος</note> among the Greeks, sounds the same as *Tehom* <note>original: תהום</note> among the Hebrews, and "the deep" <note>original: "profundum"</note> among the Latins. Its holy characters, through which the living nature of the abyss is signified, do not differ from the characters of the *hyle* or the "empty darkness," except that in the final letter the *He* (ה) is changed into a closed *Mem* (ם). For *He* denotes a more secret and hidden spirit, while *Mem* denotes something more open and almost led into "act." Whence it denotes that the waters began to appear from the belly of the *hyle*, but in an obscure way; so that the previously resting dark *He*—now moving intrinsically from the center of the infinite darkness—caused the face of "moist nature" (as yet unformed) to leap out from the universal *hyle*. But it did so in such a way that the *Mem* (which is the symbol of that same obscure appearance) was "closed," and not "open"; for the light had not yet broken out from the belly of the *hyle*. 

Whence it is said in Genesis 1 that "darkness was over the face of the abyss." And these abysses were those depths which Jehovah revealed out of the darkness, and the "shadows of death" which he brought forth into the light, according to that which was previously alleged from Job 12:22. These are those shadows and darkness with ineffable lumi- <note>catchword: lumi- (likely "luminosity" or "light" on the following page)</note>

Hence, *Psalm 77:17: The abysses feared the presence of the Lord and were troubled.* And *Hermes Trismegistus, Pimander, Book 1: The horrific shadow glided beneath with a slanted revolution, agitated then by an ineffable countenance.* And *Genesis 1: The Spirit of the Lord moved over the waters.* For there, the closed *Mem* is opened, and it becomes מ, which is an open *Mem* <note>The Hebrew letter Mem (M) has two forms: open (מ) used at the beginning or middle of words, and closed (ם) used at the end. Indeed, the Spirit of the Lord penetrated into the abyss and revealed the waters, which were hidden, covered over by the darkness in the abyss. For first He moved over the waters, tracing the spherical path of the heavens; and then He penetrated into the depth of the darkened abysses, which were hidden in their shapeless belly and were held as a place of nothingness, and finally, by His presence, they were made manifest. *I alone (says Wisdom) encompassed the circuit of the heavens in the whole earth, and I walked in the depth of the abysses, etc. Ecclesiasticus 24.* From these things, therefore, we see that the abyss, whose face was buried in darkness, stands in the next degree to its mother, the *hyle* <term>hyle: A Greek term used in philosophy to describe "prime matter" or the raw, unformed substance of the universe.</term>, from whose belly and womb it began to appear with a closed countenance, מ, and in the manner of a dispute, by resisting the living actions of the Creator, it finally descended downward from the face of the rays of the pursuing *Jod* ל <note>The letter Jod (י) is often used in Cabalistic thought to represent the first point of divine light or the hand of God.</note>, and fled from its terrors. Yet it could not so avoid the luminous actions of the *Tetragrammaton* <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note> that He, by His wisdom, did not see through its innermost parts with diligent inquiry and bring into act and being things never before revealed. Thus, therefore, all the darkness of the worldly waters was removed by the power of divine Chemistry <note>original: "Chymiæ divinæ." This refers to the alchemical process of God separating and refining the elements of creation.</note>; and its sixth essence was stored in the highest region of the machine <note>The "machine of the world" or the universe.</note>, the fifth essence in the middle heaven, and the fourth essence in the lowest. Finally, into the center of this lowest region, the dregs of darkness were reduced from the moist material of the whole expanse—the universal water—as if from the circumference of a Philosophical Egg <note>The "Philosophical Egg" is a classic alchemical symbol for the vessel in which the transformation of matter occurs, mirroring the creation of the cosmos.</note> to its center and heart; according to that passage in *Job 38:37: Who has numbered the heavens in wisdom, and who has made that which descends from the heavens to rest, when the dust descended into that hardness, and the clods cleaved together?* But concerning these things, we shall speak in their proper place.

We see, therefore, how the abyss is numbered as the second species of darkness, and is, as it were, the daughter of the *hyle*—that most general and infinite darkness, whose vast expansion extends infinitely beyond the margins of the created world. The portion of this matrix from which *Pan* <note>Pan is used here to represent "Universal Nature," derived from the Greek word for "All."</note> or universal nature was finally procreated, was called the Universal Abyss; under whose shadow the universal unformed waters, soon to be produced, were contained. And this is the reason that its final letter is the closed *Mem* (ם), proving, clearly, that the abyss was prepared to produce the shapeless waters by the stretching out of the hand of the *Demogorgon* <note>Demogorgon: A mysterious deity or personification of the primordial creative force, often associated with the underworld or the source of all things.</note> or the *Tetragrammaton*. After these waters were brought forth into the light, they are called ם, where the מ in the middle between the double *Mem* indicates the solar tabernacle, from which the *Jod*, as if from a center, illuminates both the lower waters, signified by the closed ם (because they end with the darkness of the earth), and the open מ, because through it *Jehovah* shone forth into the universal world.

But now we shall speak a few words concerning the subordinate species of abysses which remain in the world to this very day. We know there is another peculiar abyss hidden with *Jehovah*, according to the assertion of the Royal Psalmist in *Psalm 33:7: Jehovah has placed the abysses in treasuries.* Concerning which the Wise Man speaks in *Ecclesiasticus 1:3: Who shall investigate the breadth of the earth, and the height of the heaven, and the abyss, and wisdom?* There are, therefore, superior abysses, and there are inferior abysses. Concerning those superior ones already existing, the wise man speaks in *Proverbs 8: When Jehovah strengthened the superior clouds above, when the fountains of the abyss grew strong, etc. I was wisdom, rejoicing and playing before him at all times.* And *Genesis 7:11: The fountains of the abyss and the floodgates of heaven are opened.* Concerning the inferior ones, the Psalmist speaks in *Psalm 104:6: You covered the earth with the abyss as with a garment; the waters stood above the mountains, and at your rebuke they fled.* Hence the Royal Prophet seems to take the abyss here for clouds, or dense waters. Thus in *Psalm 104: The dense cloud is the vehicle of God or his chariot.* And *Psalm 105: God expanded a cloud for a covering.* And *Job 22:15: A dense cloud is a hiding place for God.* And *Exodus 40:34: A cloud covered the tent of the assembly.* And *1 Chronicles 6:1* and *1 Kings 8:12: Jehovah said he would dwell under thick darkness.* By which it is proved that the abyss is above. Similarly, the cloud is taken for darkness itself. Whence *Joshua 24:7: He placed thick darkness between you and the Egyptians.* Likewise, the dense and dark waters of the sea itself are considered an abyss, according to *Exodus 15:5: The abysses covered them, they descended into the deep like a stone.* And in the same place, verse 8: *The abysses were congealed in the heart of the sea by the blast of your nostrils.* Here he takes the abyss for the grim waves of the swelling sea, and for the obscurity of the waters on account of their density. Hence even a dense cloud can be called an abyss.

We understand from these things, therefore, that the abyss is nothing other than a great heap of dense water, obscure and dark because of its depth. And because from the beginning of the whole mass, the depth of the universal waters was covered with darkness due to the absence of light, it was therefore called the abyss—that is, a huge mass of waters deprived of light. This is also what its primary and living characters signify: *Tehom* (תהום) <note>The Hebrew word for "Abyss" or "Deep" used in Genesis.</note>, as if it were a *Mem* closed by darkness, or shapeless waters. Hence Moses first mentions Darkness, and then the Abyss, before he utters a single word about the Spirit brooding over the waters. And in truth, the remaining portions of the abyss named up to this day are abysses in a relative sense rather than an absolute one, insofar as nothing now exists that can truly be called "empty" or "void" in the world, just as in the beginning there was *Tehom*, where no character or seal of light or luminous form was to be found. Hence it is also taken metaphorically for the depth of the sea, in which no internal light shines, or for an obscure cloud, in which the marks or signs of light or fire are not enclosed.
