# ON THE PRIMARY ELEMENTS OF NATURE.

...terminating its point in the belly of the element of fire; from which it is demonstrated that the proportion of the **material pyramid**, raised from the earth to the fire, is equal to the proportion of the **formal [pyramid]** of the element of fire, which descends from the fire to the earth; and consequently, the action is proportioned to the resistance of the passion <note>In the language of the time, "passion" refers to the capacity of a substance to be acted upon or transformed by an external force, like heat acting on cold.</note>, and the place of the intersection made by those two pyramids is that true place, or the **sphere of elemental equality**, in which **Jehovah** <note>original: "Jehova"</note> is accustomed to manifest himself to us wonderfully in his glory; just as also in the middle intersection, made by two universal pyramids traversing through the entire mass of created water, the sphere of the soul and of mundane equality is said to be carried around, in which **Jehovah** has placed his tabernacle. 

We say, therefore, that the cause of humidity in its proper sphere lying between earth and fire is of this sort: The entire disposition or mass of the earth is divided into three regions, namely, into three spheres of the darkness of the three heavens; any one of which excels the dignity of any other, and has a different respect for resisting the actions of the element of fire. For its superior region (from whose coldness the element of fire, manifested by compression, fled upward) penetrates all the way to the fire; but since the spirit of this dark cold (which is the animal spirit) exists by the dignity of the **Empyrean Spirit** <note>The Empyrean was considered the highest, most refined part of heaven, composed of pure light or fire.</note>, therefore the nature of fire easily disperses and dissipates it, and from that point, it appears almost entirely fiery. 

However, because a portion of the middle darkness penetrates only to the convex surface of the fire, and because its coldness is stronger—since the **vegetable heat** <note>This refers to the life-giving, animating warmth that allows plants and living things to grow.</note> is less—it is therefore accustomed to be congealed in the air; but that dryness in coagulation is resolved by the action of the fiery pyramid and is converted into a middle temperament between heat and coldness. But if the act of the fire is weak, then in the middle region of the air, hail, ice, and snow are generated; which again, by the urging of heat, are reduced into humidity and vapor, or rain and dew. 

Furthermore, the humidity of these two elements <note>Meaning air and water, often grouped together as the "humid" elements.</note> varies and differs in its degree of thinness and density insofar as they are closer to either the lower or the upper boundary. For in the lower place, the humidity is denser and thicker because of the power and dominion of the terrestrial cold over that watery medium; but in the superior place, it is thinner and more subtle because of the property of fiery heat in the disposition of the humid. Moreover, water is also such a coarse humidity, for it is extracted from the dense darkness of the visible and mineral region of the world. 

From these things, therefore, we see that the region or sphere of humidity is all that space which fills this entire gap between fire and earth; and that the essential quality of the illuminated water itself is nothing other than **humidity**. This is called a passive quality because it is made by the action of a hot nature upon a cold nature, by reducing everything into actual humidity which, by the presence and dominion of congealing and astringent cold, was previously only held in potentiality for such an act. Therefore, the congealed spirit, made dry by cold, suffers the act of heat; by whose dissolving virtue the dryness is removed, and the frost is reduced into humor <note>A liquid or fluid state.</note>. And thus, finally, the quality of humidity—or the middle nature between heat and coldness—is procreated. This is the true and natural disposition of "revealed" water; the absence of which, as far as we are concerned, is called **dryness**. Although, as it seems to me, dryness "absolutely stated" is not found in the nature of things, but only comparatively or respectively, as will be clearly declared in the following book. These words of Job 24:19 seem to confirm the elevation of this pyramid of humidity from the earth: *Vapors ascend from the extremity of the earth, etc.* <note>The author provides a variation of the text found in the Vulgate or other contemporary translations to support the idea of rising vapors.</note>

Indeed, we could write a book of immense magnitude concerning the ineffable mystery of the waters, and their condition both hidden and manifest; but, since that does not pertain to the project already committed to our hands, we shall omit it in this place, so that we may at last step forward and arrive at the third and nobler principle, both supernatural and natural, which is light.

# PRIMARY ELEMENTS OF NATURE, AND SPECIFICALLY CONCERNING LIGHT.
### CHAPTER I.

->*Concerning the final mother ש [Shin], and how she proceeds from the first illuminated mother, namely א [Aleph], and from the second non-illuminated mother.*<-

<image-desc>Ornate woodcut initial letter 'Q' decorated with intricate vine and leaf patterns.</image-desc>Just as in the miraculous name, or the supersubstantial elements יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God: Yod-He-Vav-He.</note> the emanation of the most essential character **Jod**, as the second person and the son from the father, passes into the first spirit **א** [Aleph]; so also in the three substantial elements, which are called "mothers," we see that the immediate principles of the world and of natural things are derived from it. For the first dark **א** [Aleph], by looking forth from the darkness of matter <term>hyle <gloss>The primordial, unformed substance of the universe.</gloss></term>, becomes luminous, and thus denotes darkness and concealment by its silence, but by its manifestation it denotes the point, center, and origin of illumination. And since its immense ray illuminated the **ש** [Shin] <note>Likely referring to the fiery spirit or the "waters" in a state of potential.</note> or the waters, and brought them into action out of the nothingness of the abyss, therefore **מ** [Mem] is said to proceed from **א** [Aleph], just as a son from a father; and it is therefore compared to a line, which is the first progression in Geometry from a point. And from this it is accepted by the **Cabalists** <note>Practitioners of Cabala, a form of Jewish mysticism that influenced many Renaissance thinkers.</note> as the divine Word, as the "informed" standing for the "informer." And the **מ** [Mem] when final and closed [ם] denotes the word *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be."</note> not yet spoken, but still enclosed in the womb of the Abyss; hence the closed **מ** is a symbol of silence. But the open **מ** [Mem] indicates the word or speech as open and brought forth, and it is the symbol of the sphere of Jupiter; thereby indicating that the glory of **Jehovah** is revealed to men by the opening of the abyss of waters. We see, therefore, that **Mem**, the second mother, indicates the son, the second person, or the Word; because by the presence of the Word the waters appear as they are; and from them the heavens were created, according to that passage in the Psalms: *By the Word of the Lord were the heavens created, etc.* But now at last let us come to the final mother of natural things (which I have proposed to treat in this booklet), which the Sages have called **ש** [Shin]. She indeed stands in relation to the two preceding ones as a surface stands to a line and a point; for, just as a surface proceeds from a point as the primary principle and a line as the medium, so also **Shin ש** flows from **א** [Aleph] and **מ** [Mem]. Wherefore, just as **מ** proceeded from **א** like a son from a Father, or a second mother from the first, so also **ש** proceeds from **א** and **מ** as a certain third thing, derived as if from the Father and the son, and is likened by the **Cabalists** to the **Holy Spirit**. And it is from this that its character is formed as having the shape of a crown with three peaks; so that it is indicated from there to be a symbol of the Holy Trinity. Furthermore, we say **ש** [Shin] is that which, grammatically, "suffices" or "is enough" <note>A reference to the divine name Shaddai, often interpreted as "He who is sufficient."</note>, insofar as it is a symbol of the Trinity and the completion of the whole machine [of the world], according to that aforementioned saying: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the spirit of his mouth all their power;* where the Lord is **א** [Aleph] the speaker, and the Word is the enacted *Fiat* **מ** [Mem]; and the Spirit from his mouth is **ש** [Shin] from which, as if from a fiery form, all action and power proceed. For **מ** [Mem] is in **Mem**, and the power of both is in **ש** [Shin]. For these three mothers are nothing but one spirit, which is one God, which **Abraham** also supports in the **Yetzirah** <note>The Sefer Yetzirah, or "Book of Formation," traditionally attributed to the patriarch Abraham.</note>: *One God.*

But after its revelation, this one spirit is divided into three properties, which we call the mothers of the world; all of which are said to have migrated into the nature of **ש** [Shin].

### CHAPTER II.

#### Concerning Shin [ש] hidden in darkness, and revealed; and how the property of the word is observed to differ according to the positioning of its character.

IN the preceding sections, it was declared that **Shin ש**, which is the symbol of created fire and light, or of the fiery spirit—the uncreated spirit mixed with the created—is either enclosed and hidden within the dark waters of the abyss, or it is not hidden. In the former case, it denotes the penultimate species of darkness, which signifies **Chaos**, and is thus enclosed by obscure characters as **חש** <note>Hebrew *Chash*, implying silence or the darkness of the "hyle" (primordial matter).</note>; and thus the divine fire went out from the dark cloud on Mount Sinai before the Israelites. But truly, if it is not hidden, it appears to be that terrible and consuming fire passing before the face of Jehovah, of which the Israelites spoke when talking to Moses:

> **Deuteronomy 5:24–25.** <note>Text cites 5.31.</note> We have heard the voice of Jehovah out of the midst of the fire; if God continues to speak with man, shall he live? Now therefore, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us, etc.

And in this case, it is not hidden among obscure characters but is depicted thus: **אש** <note>Hebrew *Esh*, meaning "Fire."</note>, signifying fire; where **Aleph [א]** denotes Jehovah, of whom it is the symbol; and therefore that letter mixed with **ש** [Shin] proves that Jehovah appears from the center of the fire or created light. Hence it is said:

> **Psalm 104:2.** God is clothed with light, extending the heaven like a skin, or a tent-curtain.

Furthermore, the essence of the **Sun** is explained by living characters of this kind: **שמש** <note>Hebrew *Shemesh*, meaning "Sun."</note>, that is, the Sun, so named from the "ministry of light"; where **מ [Mem]**, or water, or the clear spirit and pure substance of the Sun itself, is seen in the center; and the two characters of **Shin [ש]** enclose it on either side, proving that light is seen only in the Sun; and the substantial spirit (which is called by the Philosophers the denser part of its orb) is covered on every side by light and fire. By these things we are clearly taught that this mother letter is the most effective cause of visible light, and that its power emanates from the fathers or living characters of the Ineffable Name; according to whose pattern the mothers of nature are produced, and the parts of the world are delineated.

And hence it is that the primary and spiritual light, which flowed immediately from the face of **Jod [י]**, or the luminous **Aleph [א]**, emanated from the formal characters or elements of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, Yod-He-Vav-He.</note> itself. Whence that most holy word **FIAT** <note>Latin for "Let there be."</note>, surrounded on all sides by the fiery spirit, is expressed in holy letters as **יהי** <note>Hebrew *Yehi*, the first word of creation: "Let there be (light)."</note>. Where, just as in the Sun (**שמש**) the central element is held by a double embrace of the single mother—which is the tabernacle of the Word in the world—so also the **ה [He]**, the central spirit of the most effective Word **FIAT**, is likewise contained by a double embrace of the single **Jod [י]**, the father of light.

Where, in place of the entire miraculous name **יהוה** (Jehovah), we have **יהי** (Jah); and the **י [Jod]** which equals the double **ה [He]**; so that from this it is denoted that the **י [Jod]** fills the triple **יהוה**, that is, the three heavens of the entire universe, and consequently that the **Messiah**, or the power of **יהוה**, is everywhere in the world and through the world; He who was Wisdom itself, and existed before anything was created, with **Jod**; as is found in the sacred text. Therefore, the light shining immediately from His spirit retains in itself the characters of divinity.

Whence it is called in the holy tongue **אור** <note>Hebrew *Or*, meaning "Light."</note>: where **א [Aleph]**, as was said before, is a sign of poverty, vacuum, and emptiness, and consequently can denote the darkness of <term>hyle <gloss>The Greek term for primordial, unformed matter.</gloss></term>; from which the shining **א [Aleph]** renders the middle **ו [Vau]**, just as **Jod** in **He**, or the luminous **Aleph** in **ה [He]**; which together constitute six; the hieroglyph of which number is **Vau ו**. Therefore, it denotes the illuminated divine spirit. For just as **Mem** or illuminated water is called Light, and is noted by **Shin ש** (in which **מ [Mem]** is hidden, as in the Sun **שמש**), so also the Holy Spirit **ה [He]** is hidden in **Vau ו**; for the latter signifies uncreated light, while the former signifies created light. And in **אור** (that is, light), **Vau ו**, being a spherical letter, proves that between **א [Aleph]** (God) and **ר [Resh]** (darkness), the spherical world **ו [Vau]** was placed and illuminated. Whence it also denotes that God is both outside and inside all things.

## CHAPTER III.

### An exposition of the word "Heavens," based on an examination of its living characters.

Just as the three substantial "mothers" of nature are derived from three "fathers" who are beyond substance and are the most primary of all—who are explained through the three characters of the stupendous name **Yod-He-Vav** [יהו] as if through hieroglyphics (for **Yod** [י] is the symbol and, as it were, the soul of the mother **Aleph** [א], while **He** [ה] is the soul of the mother **Mem** [מ], and **Vav** [ו] is the soul of the mother **Shin** [ש])—so too do secondary or more complex principles arise from these primary and most simple natural principles. For the substance of the heavens themselves is composed of **Aleph** [א] and **Shin** [ש]: **Aleph** acting as the material part, and **Shin** as the formal part. Hence, the highest heaven is almost entirely **Shin**, or fiery; for this reason, the **Empyrean** <term>Empyrean: The highest part of heaven, believed by ancient cosmologists to be composed of pure fire or light.</term> is named from *pyr* <note>original: πῦρ</note>, which means "fire." The middle heaven is the **Æthereal**, which is like "fiery air" <note>original: æthaer</note>.

Just as in the first ordering of things, **Shin** [ש] proceeded from the luminous **Aleph** [א] and the spirit or water of **He** [ה] (by whose mixture the air and light, **Avir** [אויר] <note>original: אויר, Hebrew for air/atmosphere</note>, were subsequently created, the hieroglyphic of which is **Shav** [שוא]), so also from this mother thus composed and from **Mem** [מ] were the visible heavens made, which are called the **Firmament**. We can see and perceive this most clearly, as if in a highly polished mirror, from the arrangement and condition of the "living characters" <note>The author treats Hebrew letters not just as symbols, but as active, living forces of creation.</note> of the holy word signifying "Heavens." That word is **Shamaim** [שמים]. Some maintain that this word is composed of *Sham* [ש], meaning "there," and *Maim* [מים], meaning "waters"; as if one were to say, "Behold, the waters are there." For **Shin**, insofar as it is fire, illuminates; and through its light, it points to a place: "there," as if indicating "Behold, See," etc.

However, others—with a more correct understanding, in our opinion—have deduced the composition of the heavens from **Esh** [אש] and **Maim** [מים], that is, from "fire" and "water." Indeed, we draw this very conclusion from the nature of the characters of the word itself. For in the word for fire, **Esh** [אש], we find the **Shin** [ש], the hieroglyphic of fire; and we find **Maim** [מים], which is water. From these, it is argued that heaven is nothing other than a composition of light or fire and water—that is, from the "matter" of water, which is its substance, and from the "essence" of fire or created light, which is the first composition, **Shin** [ש].

Because **Shin**, as has been said, is forged from the luminous **Aleph** [א] and **Mem** [מ] (as if from God and moist nature), that which is now called **Shamaim** [Heavens] was called, before and after creation and unto eternity, **Elohim** [אלהים] <note>The Hebrew name for God.</note>. This is as if one said **Elha** [אלה], God, and **Yam** [ימ] or **Yamim** [ימים], the universal sea. For by placing a **Yod** [י] between the double **Mem**, it becomes **Maim**, meaning "water"—as if one were to say **Elohim**, the "God of the universal sea," or from **El**, the "Strong God," and **Ha-Maim**, "of the waters," as in **Elmaim**.

For **Shin** [ש] exists in the world as an image of the Spirit, **He** [ה], in the Archetype <term>Archetype: The original divine blueprint or world of ideas in the mind of God before physical creation.</term>. Indeed, in the name **Jehovah** [יהוה], it denotes the uncreated spirit, and **Shin** in the world denotes water or spirit. Thus, **Elohim** before creation was the exemplar of **Shamaim** after creation. For just as **Elohim** was the "God of the waters"—that is, the uncreated light illuminating the uncreated waters—so also **Shamaim** is, as it were, the created light illuminating the waters that have now been created!

Hence **Aleph** [א] was the exemplar in the Archetype of **Shin** [ש] itself in the created world. For just as **Aleph** illuminates the Archetypal world, so too does **Shin** illuminate the created world. Therefore, in **Elohim**, **Aleph** is before all things and outside all things, having its action upon the Spirit **He** [ה] of the Archetype, and its power in the **Mem** [מ] of the world to be created. It existed before all things; and thus, before any mention of a creature was expressed by Moses, that name of God was used, which nonetheless had a relation to the creation of the world to be produced. Finally, in the likeness of this name, the heavens, or **Shamaim** [שמים], were made during creation. Therefore, just as **Aleph** or **Jod** held its place in the Archetypal world, so did **Shin** hold its place in the created world. Consequently, **Shin** in creation is like a "natural God" within the created waters (**Maim**), just as **El** is in the uncreated spirit and the waters to be created. **Maim**, which in God is the same as **Shin** in **Maim**, insofar as **Shin** is the uncreated spirit, just as **Shin** is the created spirit. Thus, **Shamaim** in creation has a relationship to **Elohim** the Creator, in whose icon and image the world, forged from the distinct heavens, was made.

## CHAPTER IV.

### Of how many kinds Light may be, or concerning the multiform nature of light.

In the Holy Scriptures, we find light divided in many ways. And although the essence of light is fundamentally one and the same, nevertheless, with respect to its various and different "garments" in this world, we say that it is various. In respect to itself, light is nothing other than identity—one and the same nature. In one place, therefore, we read of "strange fire" before Jehovah (Leviticus 10:1); in another, we are taught that "Jehovah is a consuming fire" (Deuteronomy 4:24 and 9:6). Likewise: "He showed you His great fire to see; for you heard His words from the midst of the fire" (Deuteronomy 4:36). We also read of the "fire of punishment": "The land is burnt up with brimstone and salt" (Deuteronomy 29:23). Similarly, Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed by this kind of fire (Genesis 19:24). We also read of the fire of the messenger shining in the right hand of Jehovah. Furthermore, the scriptures...

# C H A P T E R V.

### *Concerning uncreated invisible light, and how it is compared to the nature of visible fire: Furthermore, it is proved that visible light is a certain reflection of the uncreated and invisible light into the "garments" which it puts on.*

That invisible and uncreated light, from which heaven, earth, and all things both visible and invisible were formed, is that unique, sacrosanct, ineffable, and eternal **Word of God**, or the Messiah, and the true power of the Tetragrammaton <note>Tetragrammaton: The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note>. And this Word was in the beginning with God, and the Word was God. All things were made through this Word, and without Him was nothing made that was made; in Him was life. This is that Word in which all things firmly subsist, and through which God has powerfully and gloriously manifested Himself to His creatures. This is that Word through which God spoke from the mouths of the Prophets and angels, and announced salvation to the human race. This is that Word which powerfully took upon itself the sins of the world and reconciled humanity with God. 

This is that Word which constitutes the Third Person in the sacrosanct Divinity. For God created the heaven and the earth—by which the First Person is noted to us. The Second is noted in that God spoke this Word <term>יהי</term> <note>Hebrew: "Yehi," meaning "Let there be."</note> **FIAT** <note>Latin: "Let it be done."</note>; and the Third in the spirit of His mouth. God Himself explained all these things through those brief words just mentioned, showing that in His divine majesty He is Three in a uniform essence—namely, God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit; and thus Three in persons, but only one God. This Word, **FIAT**, I say, is eternal and divine; the splendor of divine glory, the invisible image of the divine essence, and the light of this world which illuminates every person in this world. Whoever apprehends this light with a humble heart and true desire, it shines before them into eternal life. 

This light is not perceived by human eyes, but is seen by the Spirit, which was implanted in man by God, in this life and the life to come. For since the human body given by God is darkened by flesh and blood so that its eyes are blinded, it is impossible for it to gaze upon this light; nor can a mortal body, before its "clarification" <note>original: "clarificationem," referring to the theological concept of glorification or the transformation of the body into a spiritual state</note>, see that which is immortal. Scripture also testifies that man has neither seen God, nor will he ever see Him in this carnal body, until he is purified, and after this life becomes conformed to the body of Christ through clarification, becoming as if divine. For there he shall see God as He is. 

This is 그 eternal light which first illuminated the formless waters in the identity of the Spirit with the Father. This is that Divine Wisdom which distinguished the three heavens from one another by its power, and by whose sight the light things were established by flying upward, and the heavy things by descending downward. This is that **peaceful knot** <note>original: "nodus pacificus"</note> by which—once the discord and strife of moist matter were removed—a harmony was created through the regions of the entire universe, and a perpetual peace was reconciled between the contentious and litigating elements. This invisible light is the intellectual mind of the higher heaven, the essence of the ethereal heaven, the form of the elements, the life of composite creatures, and the **Soul of the Universal World** <note>original: "mundi universalis anima"</note>. It is, I say, the soul of the universal waters, and the center or point of life in all seeds enclosed in water; and consequently, it is the first, true, and unique "act" <note>In the Aristotelian sense of "actualization" or "driving force"</note> of all creatures. Through it, the earth is suspended in the vast center of the world upon the scales of justice over nothingness. Through it, the mass of the earth rests, and the nurseries contained within it grow and multiply. Through it, minerals daily but slowly grow rich in form, and vegetables...

But the principal thing in fire is that it tolerates no impurity, and it illuminates all things, cherishes them with its heat, transforms them, and even makes them transparent. Scarcely any other art is found besides <term>Alchemy</term> in which so many subtle shortcuts are employed, and so many utilities in medicine and other things are created. He who knows this art will be more fit, capable, and agile for all the remaining arts, provided that discretion is used in this matter, or by handling these things dexterously. Scarcely also is any manual operation found more acceptable, or more pleasing and delightful, than this very one which is dispatched through fire. Furthermore, this is the greatest and most effective operation of fire of all: that by it, the heaven and the earth shall be burned and renewed according to the supersubstantial will.

Yet, truly, insofar as He is in His own essence—naked and revealed without regard for any material clothing or hiding place—He is said to be **outside all things**, since He is not contained by them, but rather encompasses all things in His infinite embrace.

## CHAPTER VI.

### A fuller discourse on the nature of the *Universal Mystic Word, or Uncreated Light, both in the universal moist nature* <term>Mem</term> <note>The Hebrew letter מ (Mem), representing water in the Hermetic and Kabbalistic tradition.</note> *as well as in the fiery nature* <term>Shin</term> <note>The Hebrew letter ש (Shin), representing fire.</note>.

To begin a deeper discourse on the ineffable mystery of the Divine Word, it must be understood that it is a light, invisible in and of itself, and perceivable only by the intellect. And yet, because of the effect of its action, the subject in which it dwells (or the garment which it puts on) is made more colorful and adorned with a certain visible light the more it is worthy and honored in its density—as seen in the Solar body and that most noble spirit <term>ה</term> (He) <note>The Hebrew letter He, often associated with the vital breath or the soul of the world.</note> among us. Hence, visible light is not the immediate act of the eternal and invisible light, but rather its effect, or a reflection upon some worthy, colored body. Therefore, the Divine Word creates both invisible and visible species, both in heaven and on earth: invisible where the spirits (or the garments receiving it) are invisible and thin; but visible by accident where the spirits are dense and visible, for they receive their visible and colored condition from the reflection of the divine light. This light is called **natural** in respect to the garment in which it dwells; but in respect to itself, and without consideration for any natural covering, it is called **supernatural**, insofar as it flows from <term>Jod</term> <note>The Hebrew letter י (Jod), the first letter of the divine name, representing the supersubstantial source or "point" of creation.</note>, the source above all substance. 

To describe what the effects of this divine light are in the universal mass of water (denoted by the hieroglyphic <term>Mem</term>), or what the remarkable properties are in the substance of created light or fire, would indeed be infinite in this place. However, to speak according to the sense of the Holy Scriptures, we find that by the expansion and dilation of this most holy power, all things are rendered living and active, dense and frozen clouds are scattered, the swelling waters of the seas are made proudly mobile, and the entire air becomes warmer. On the contrary, by its contraction, the spirit is frozen and becomes denser; water is condensed into snow, ice, hail, frost, and rime. Similarly, just as heat is stirred up in water by the expansion of the faculty of the primary light, so also cold holds dominion through its hiding and contraction. Furthermore, it is within the power of the Word that while the effect of its light remains in a colored body, the heat can nevertheless be contracted, diminished, or erased, and consequently, cold can predominate, according to that passage:
<margin>Wisdom 16:18.</margin>
*Wisdom 16:18: God softens the fire so that it does not burn; at one time He makes the fire burn in the midst of water;* and 
<margin>Ibid. 22.</margin>
ibid. 22: *Fire exists within snow and ice, yet they do not melt:* for the creature, serving You who made all things, is strained for the punishment of the unjust, and relaxed for the benefit of those who trust in You. 

How water is also condensed by the absence of the "Face of the Word," and dissolved again by its presence, is taught to us by that passage noted by the Royal Psalmist:
<margin>Psalm 147, from verse 16.</margin>
*Psalm 147:16: God sends out snow like wool, and scatters frost like ashes; He casts down His ice like morsels; who can stand before His cold? Sending out His Word, He melts them; as soon as He blows His wind, the waters flow.* From these words, it seems to become known that by the hiding of the warm power of the Word (or Divine Light), cold is permitted to predominate, so that clouds are condensed into snow, hail, and ice; but by the "sending out" of the Word (or the effect of the Word) into the cloud, and by its warm breath, the frozen waters are dissolved and flow away, returning from snow or hail into rain. We read, therefore, that the Word of God brings about or induces the winds, thunders, clouds, exhalations, and sounding storms.
<margin>Psalm 148:8.</margin>
*Psalm 148:8.* From these things, one can see how much power the Word has over the waters, both in their freezing and their dissolving, and consequently in cooling and heating the watery mass—that is, in the production of heat and the introduction of cold...

by its hiding: Similarly, how effective that sacrosanct light is in restraining the powers of manifest and visible fire, and in provoking those same powers to punishment, is declared to us by the Holy Bible—not only in the passage cited above, but in many others as well. For Jehovah, when mitigating his fire, is said to be full of benevolence, mercy, and kindness; and so the light of his face is said to bring the greatest joy to the soul, <note>Psalm 4:7-8 in the author's source; likely Psalm 4:6-7 in modern Bibles.</note> to illuminate the darkness and the candle (or the soul), <note>Psalm 18:28.</note> and to cause us to see good. <note>Psalm 4:6.</note> It is the salvation of the righteous and the strength of life, <note>Psalm 27:1.</note> and in it we shall be saved; <note>Psalm 80:3.</note> likewise, it is the Sun, giving life and glory, <note>Psalm 84:11.</note> and so on in other places. 

But truly, insofar as it is intensified for punishment, to that extent it is called the wrath and the heat of God, as in Psalm 6:1 and 38:1. The wrath of Jehovah is his heat; and Psalm 11:6: *He rains snares upon the wicked*; <note>The Latin 'pruinas' suggests frost or burning coals depending on the translation tradition.</note> and Psalm 21:9 and 83:14: *The wrath of Jehovah is like a consuming fire*; and Psalm 78:21: *The fire of Jehovah was kindled against Jacob, and so it burned against Israel*; and Psalm 78:63: *God consumes the impious with fire*; and Psalm 79:5: *Will you be angry forever? Shall your jealousy burn like fire? Pour out your heat upon the other nations etc. For the consumer has consumed Jacob*; and Psalm 106:18: *A fire kindled in the assembly of the Israelites; a flame burned up the wicked*; and Psalm 106:40: *The fervent wrath of God was kindled.* Similarly in Job 20:26: <note>The text cites Job 2:26, but the quote is from Job 20:26.</note> *A fire not fanned by breath shall consume him*; and so in other places. 

For, according to that aforementioned saying in Wisdom 16:24: *The creature of fire, serving God who made all things, is at one time intensified for punishment against the unjust, and at another time relaxed for beneficence.* First, however, that fire is a creature serving God is denoted by those passages written here: namely, Psalm 104:4 says: *Who makes your angels spirits, and your ministers a burning fire.* And Job 38:35: *Can you send forth lightnings, that they may go and say to you, "Here we are"?* Regarding the angels, who are types of invisible light, it is written thus in Psalm 103:20: *Angels of God, most mighty in strength, performing his word, etc.: ministers doing his pleasure.* 

Thus an angel appeared to Moses in a visible fire from the midst of a certain bush in Exodus 3. and preceded the camps of the Israelites in a pillar of fire and a cloud in Exodus 14:19. Thus an angel ascended in the flame of a burnt offering to heaven before Manoah and his wife in Judges 13:20. <note>The text cites Judges 13:16.</note> Moreover, we read that by divine power fire is intensified for punishment: first, in Leviticus 10:2, where indeed fire coming out from the presence of Jehovah struck the sons of Aaron, and they died. Then, in Numbers 11:1: *The wrath of Jehovah was kindled, and his anger glowing against them consumed those who were at the edge of the camp; but when the people cried out to Moses, Moses prayed to Jehovah, and that fire was suppressed; therefore the name of the place was called Taberah, because the fire of Jehovah had burned against them.* And Numbers 16:35: *A fire went out from Jehovah and consumed those 250 men who had offered incense.* Likewise in Deuteronomy 32:22: *A fire is kindled by my anger, which shall burn to the lowest hell, and shall consume the earth with her increase, and set on fire the foundations of the mountains.* 

By these things we are taught that by the fiery face of Jehovah—that is, by the excitation of the fiery power of Jehovah, which is his Word and eternal light—the soul of the <term>creature fire</term> <note>The "soul of fire" refers to the underlying spiritual force that makes physical fire act.</note> is vivified and provoked to execute the extreme violence and efficacy of its power and nature. For the fiery power of the Word is the most agile and most lively soul of fire. Therefore, when that power is reflected back into the center of the Word (or the unity of the Messiah), the force of the fire is relaxed and mitigated. 

But truly, if that power is released, then it even calls forth the fires enclosed within stones, and attributes force and action to them—they which were working potentially and hiddenly within the stones—not otherwise than we see in a **military engine** <note>original: "tormento bellico"; likely a cannon.</note> loaded with **gunpowder**. Indeed, in such a case, that powder does nothing unless it is ignited by a living fire; but once ignited, it exerts immense force and power in the air. For, just as the Divine Word was the fountain, principle, and origin of light, motion, and every act in created things, so too that act is as if dead and does not appear during the absence of its Prime Mover; but when he is present, it is revivified and once again acquires and recovers its former strength. 

Thus, by the mediation of the Word and the fiery spirit of the Messiah, Lazarus rose from the dead; because the candle of his life, which had been utterly extinguished, was suddenly illuminated again by the presence of the uncreated light, and with no delay, he lived again. And this shall be the reason for the revivification and resurrection in every deceased person on the Last Day. 

But returning to the matter, we say that even fires that are as if dead—resting as it were in stones and wood, and existing only in mere potential—are stirred up and reduced into action by the presence of the divine countenance, and they yearn to suddenly and swiftly perfect and carry out the will of their creator. Thus we read in Judges 6:21 that fire rose up from the rock or stone under the oak by the power and the mere touch of the Angel's staff, rapaciously consuming and effectively devouring the burnt offering of Gideon. Similarly, when Jehovah was present, Mount Sinai burned with fire even unto the highest heaven (Deuteronomy 4). 

And Wisdom 16:18 confirms this best: *God makes fire burn in the midst of water, so that the fruit of the unjust earth might be destroyed.* Furthermore, it is said in 1 Kings 18:38 that the fire of Jehovah, falling from heaven, consumed the burnt offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust itself, and that it even licked up the water that was in the trench. From this we can also judge the immense property and power of the fire that will purify all things on the Last Day. And yet, that consumption of things will be nothing other than their reduction into **prime matter** and simplicity—that is, a transmutation from a visible, impure, and defiled thing into a pure, transparent, and invisible thing. 

Therefore, it is no wonder that fire is intensified for punishment by the power of the Word, since that Word is the *purest consuming fire*, according to Deuteronomy 4:24 and 9:3. It is called "consuming" because it destroys what is impure and preserves what is pure; so that what is called punishment for us is justice and equity for God himself. Yet if he were to exercise this toward all who are impure, who could stand before him? For he turns that wrath against the wicked, but spares those who trust in him, and does not do all that he is able to do.

...according to that passage in Wisdom 11: *You have mercy on all, because you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of men so that they may repent,* etc. *For how could anything have endured unless you had willed it? Or how would that which you had not called forth have been preserved? But you spare all things because they are yours, O Lord, the lover of souls.* <note>Wisdom of Solomon 11:23–26. The author uses the title "God of souls" for the final phrase.</note> And this is what was said above: *The fire is turned back into beneficence.* <note>original: "Remittitur ignis in beneficentiam"</note> For if Jehovah were to show his face to the entire world, it would be necessary for all things to die or be transfigured, since nothing of impurity or pollution can endure before him. Therefore, for the sake of the righteous, God relaxes and restrains the burning heat of the fire—in which the Word is chiefly present—and kindly converts it into a benefit for them. Thus it is said that God led the Israelites by a light of fire throughout the night (Psalm 78:14), where, according to Wisdom 16:18, God mitigates the fire or renders it mild so that it might illuminate and not consume.

And so you see clearly (benevolent readers, and those looking closely at these matters) that the Word or power of Jehovah holds all sovereignty over water and fire. You see that <term>Mem</term> <note>The Hebrew letter representing Water.</note> and <term>Shin</term> <note>The Hebrew letter representing Fire.</note>—the creatures or "primary mothers"—are ministers, most obedient and compliant to the command of the supreme, luminous, eternal spirit, since they were formed according to his exemplar. They are, as it were, his instruments, by which he works in this world in either a fiery or watery manner. These are intensified or relaxed at the will of his soul—which is the Word, the Messiah, or Eternal Wisdom—no differently than the sword of a most expert General, which is used and exercised upon the enemies set before him (and finally subdued) either with severity and violence or with clemency and kindness. 

From these points it is also sufficiently clear that no one suffers anything at all, and nothing is done in the entire world, except that which is perfected by that first Act of all—by that Light, governing all things by its own moderation. Consequently, nothing can move toward good or evil except through the disposition of the Divine Word, whose fertile rays must necessarily dwell in the center of every thing, more or less; for without these rays, we consider it impossible for anything to subsist or remain in action. This was the reason that the Platonists, and indeed the Pythagoreans, maintained that all things are "full of gods," though they referred them all to Jupiter as the single source. Plato also warned everyone not to speak of God without light. Others have said that the more light a thing contains within itself, the more of God it should claim for itself. And St. Augustine, in his work *On Genesis*, acknowledged that light is the noblest and most worthy part of the entire composition of the world. 

Indeed, some have even made gods for themselves out of the Sun, the Moon, and the stars for this very reason. Among these I shall count the unfortunate crowd of Jews, who—impiously and profanely rejecting and wretchedly despising their true, central, and singular God—chose to venerate and adore a superficial and non-essential fire, a thing that is derived and made rather than the Principle and Cause; thus a creature rather than the Creator. For in 2 Kings 21:3, *He built altars for all the host of heaven*; and in 23:5, *Likewise those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, the moon, the planets, and all the host of heaven.* Thus, led by a heavy plague, they accepted the passive and the informed in place of the primary active and the supersubstantial Form; they took the colored, visible, and created body instead of the invisible, eternal, and uncreated Spirit. They failed to heed that command of Jehovah published through Moses in Deuteronomy 4:19: <note>The text cites verse 16, but the content matches verse 19.</note> *Do not look up to the sun, the moon, or the stars, or any of the host of heaven, to be led astray and bow down to them and serve them.* 

And certainly, among other iniquities of idolatry, the abomination of the Heathens came closer to the truth when they passed their children through the fire, proving by this very act that they recognized that the God they ought to adore lies hidden in the heart and secret center of fire. But what need is there for them to adore a ray of God in fire, or the Sun, or any other created thing, when God—the source of all things and the Sun who gives grace, splendor, and glory to both spirit and body—is in his entire essence in his super-existential kingdom? From that kingdom, he pours the rays of the life of things through the Word into worldly creatures, by which they exist. Let us therefore worship Jehovah in himself and through himself, existing outside of all things and in all things. Let us consider the visible creatures, in which he exists as life, to be of less value to us, as we who were made in the exact image of our Creator. Let us worship, I say, God or the Word hidden in the moist nature and its compositions, yet commanding all things from outside of all; and let us contemplate and admire nature itself as the effect of that Word which is to be adored, to whom be praise, honor, and glory forever.

### CHAPTER VII.

->*How the entire mass of created waters is divided into three heavens by means of the Word.*<-

The number of the heavens, or their regions, corresponds to the number of spiritual days—namely, those between the creation of light and the earth—during which God worked upon the world to divide it into distinct regions. Since the entire moist spirit was created in three days (or three appearances of the Spirit), therefore that entire spirit is divided into three heavens. Among these, the work of the first day is more worthy than the work of the second, and the work of the second day is more worthy than the work of the third. St. Paul mentions this number and dignity when he confesses that he was caught up in the spirit into the "third heaven," where he saw stupendous and unspeakable things.

Indeed, we have said that these heavens were created according to the pattern of the characters of the name <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note>; in which name we have proven that the letter <term>ה</term> (He), being closer to <term>י</term> (Jod) itself—as the fountain of perfection—is the type or image of the supreme and more worthy heaven because of its proximity to unity. Thus we also see that the more an object approaches fire, the more effectively the fire acts upon it; and consequently, the gift of its perfection is more freely imparted to it. Therefore, <term>Jod</term> <note>The first letter of the Divine Name, representing the point of origin or divine spark.</note>, from outside all things, wonderfully illuminated and blessed the Empyrean heaven with its glory on the first day; in which a simple composition was made, constituting <term>יה</term> (Jah). 

Afterward, on the second day or illumination, following the example of the letter <term>ו</term> (Vau), the middle or ethereal heaven was formed, in which there is a "middle composition"—namely, from <term>יה</term> (Jah) and <term>ו</term> (Vau). This is <term>יהו</term> (Jaho), or the seal of the life of natural things, and it is called a composition of the middle order. This is because there is a double <term>ה</term> (He) there: specifically, the <term>ה</term> in <term>יה</term>, and another <term>ה</term> or spirit hidden beneath the rays of the unity of <term>ו</term> (Vau); since <term>ה</term> represents five and <term>ו</term> represents six. Hence, just as the first composition <term>יה</term> (Jah) exists in the number ten (for it functions as 10), so <term>יהו</term> is in the hundreds; where the double <term>ה</term> stands for a double cipher <note>The zeros in 100.</note>, and the unity above the <term>ה</term> (five) in the <term>ו</term> (six) stands for <term>Jod</term>, in this manner: 100. Thus, this composition is "squared," insofar as its root is 10; or it is "superficial" <note>Meaning having two dimensions, like a surface or area.</note>, because its line is <term>יה</term>.

Furthermore, the final <term>ה</term> (He) is the icon of the lowest heaven, which is of the final worldly composition, compacted from material elements. Thus, <term>יהוה</term> (Jehovah) with <term>י</term> (Jod) makes the number one thousand (1000), which is the cube of the square 100, or the "body" of the surface <term>יהו</term>. This represents the complete perfection of the world in the likeness of the complete name <term>יהוה</term> (Jehovah). 

From this, it is manifest that there are three heavens, and that the supreme heaven is more worthy than the lower, insofar as it is called the seat and place of Jehovah due to its dignity. Yet indeed, wherever Jehovah is—whether in the heaven relative to us, or in the open air, or in the waters, or on the earth—there also are all these heavens, and He is accustomed to dwell in the more worthy part. Though this may seem ridiculous to some, it is demonstrated by the Holy Scriptures to be so. For in *Proverbs 8:28*, the *heaven and the upper clouds are said to be established from above;* and in *Psalm 89:7*, it says, *Who in the upper cloud is considered equal to the Lord God?* From this it is clear that wherever Jehovah appears to men, He speaks from the midst of a heaven of this kind, as one may also see from the vision in *Ezekiel chapter 1*; similarly in *Isaiah 6:1* and elsewhere. 

Moses also speaks of the multitude of heavens in *Deuteronomy 10:14*: *The heavens of heavens belong to the God of Gods;* by which he understands that Empyrean realm from whose center the glory of Jehovah is accustomed to shine forth and the Word is poured out. And this is that *house of God* spoken of in *Psalm 104:3*, whose "curtain," as it were, is the second heaven or firmament. Regarding these supreme heavens, Nehemiah speaks in *Nehemiah 9:6* with these words: *Jehovah made the heavens of heavens and all their host.* Furthermore, the Psalmist says: *God sits upon the heaven of the ancient heavens;* <note>original: "Deus inſidet cælo cælorum antiquorum"</note> that is, His place is that first and most ancient region of the heavens which was manifested in the world on the first day with the appearance of <term>Jod</term>, and in which God placed His first habitation in this world. 

The second heaven is that transparent one which is called the firmament, or the expanse, or the "clearer air," separating the supreme realm from the dark cloud or the lowest realm, as Moses testifies. There, in the solar center, the Divine Word established His more-than-royal palace; for by this Word the heavens were also strengthened (*Psalm 33:6*), since under the name of Wisdom it was present at the structure of the heavens *as a master craftsman composing all things* (*Proverbs 8:27*). 

Holy Scripture also teaches us that the elementary space existing beneath the Moon is called "heaven," as in *Genesis 1:30*: *The birds of the heaven, etc.* And *Deuteronomy 11:17*: *Jehovah will shut up the heavens so that there be no rain, etc.,* where "heaven" is understood as the air and the entire transparent realm. By these things we are taught that the diversity of the heavens consists in the diversity of the "cloud," and that the individual heavens are like clouds differing from one another in density or subtlety, which are suspended by the admirable power of the Word in a higher or lower place in this world. For there is an admirable binding of things by the Divine Word, by which each of them—according to its dignity or merit—is elevated to a higher place or suppressed to a lower one.

Moreover, that every heaven is a "cloud," moved here and there at the divine will by the breath of the Fiery Spirit, we are taught by these passages of the Holy Bible: *Proverbs 8:28*: *The heaven, the upper clouds strengthened from above;* and *Psalm 89:7*: *The heaven is called a cloud to the one above;* and *Psalm 104:3*: *The upper heavens are covered with waters by God.* But "subtle waters" are nothing other than vapor or cloud; and "subtle clouds" are nothing other than spirits. Indeed, clouds are that "curtain" of the house of God cited before, according to *Psalm 105:39*: *God spread a cloud for a covering;* and *Exodus 40:34*: *A cloud covered the tent of the assembly;* and thick clouds are the vehicle of God or His chariot, which moves upon the wings of the wind (*Psalm 104*). It is to be understood, therefore, that just as there are dense and perceptible clouds, so also there are subtle and imperceptible clouds, most full of the invisible light of eternity; indeed, even the subtle becomes dense, and again the dense becomes subtle. And this occurs by the Word contracting or dilating those things, or by the power of the uncreated light which acts in both the visible and invisible spirit.

We see here, therefore, the reason why the waters—distinct and divided by the emanation from <term>Jod</term>—are separated into various regions called heavens. It also appears that these heavens are nothing other than clouds, thick or subtle, sustained in the vast world by the winds emerging from the treasuries of Jehovah. We can also observe that a greater or lesser act of light is the cause of both imperfection and perfection, of both thickness and thinness, of both visible things...

Therefore, in place of a conclusion for the present, we wish only to remind the kind Reader that we have dealt with the quality of light—namely, its heat, proceeding from the action and motion of light, which is so contrary to coldness because of its harmony with rest—both in <term>Treatise 1, Book 1, On the Macrocosm</term> and elsewhere in this very booklet. And thus, we briefly bring this part to an end.

### CHAPTER I.

*That the primary principles of the Microcosm are the same as those of the Macrocosm: Concerning the spherical letters constituting the ineffable Tetragrammaton; and that they are not common and dead, but fiery and living: Of what nature the hidden influences of the world are.*

<image-desc>Decorative initial letter 'V' showing a landscape with a river, trees, and buildings inside the letter's frame.</image-desc>Just as in the description of the origin of the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note> (previously brought forth by us), we explained in very few but clear words that its primary principles were round or spherical letters (which we called "Fathers" because of their perfection); so also are these the supersubstantial foundations of the essence and existence of the Microcosm <note>The "Little World," referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe.</note>. This is because the human is the image of the world, just as the world itself is called the icon or exemplar of the Archetype <note>The original divine blueprint or the mind of God.</note> itself, insofar as it is like a highly polished mirror in which the most beautiful and most holy likeness of the Tetragrammaton <note>original: "Tetragrammati"; the sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> is perceived.

From this it follows that both of these structures are called children of the Tetragrammaton; for they not only derived their paternal origin from it, but also carry within them its truest likeness. Insofar as they receive the impression of life and being by the power of His Word—or the uncreated seal in which the divine Majesty is imprinted—they exist like perfume-vessels <note>original: "myrothecia"; small containers for precious oils or ointments.</note> or sanctuaries. Within these, that supersubstantial treasure is hidden as if in a perfectly prepared chest, secluded and separated from the abyss of darkness or matter <note>original: "hyle"; the Greek term for the primordial "stuff" or chaos from which the world was formed.</note>. Finally, the universal mass of creation is illuminated, activated, and brought to life by the splendor of His presence, and is ultimately preserved from corruption.

These letters, therefore, containing within themselves the infinite power of the Tetragrammaton, constitute that unique and true ineffable name of God, by which all things—both of the Macrocosm and the Microcosm—were sketched in the ideal or Archetypal world before creation. Indeed, one should not believe that these letters are of the same essence or nature as those common Hebrew letters depicted with ink or human engraving (which are truly dead and artificial). Rather, those letters were the same as those brought forth in the beginning from the dark matter and expressed in golden characters, or composed of the purest fire. By their presence, effect, and motion, the *Word* emanated immediately from the Archetype into the spherical structure of the world. By the action of this Word, as the Psalmist witnesses, *the heavens were made firm, and the spirit full of fiery love was borne upon the waters*. By its influence, all virtues and especially souls were infused first into the world, and then into its creatures.

Of such great weight, I say, and such great efficacy were these formal or fiery and spherical letters of the first order: <term>Yod</term> <note>Hebrew: י</note>, <term>He</term> <note>Hebrew: ה</note>, and <term>Vav</term> <note>Hebrew: ו</note>. They are natures far removed from those common and accidental letters produced by human invention for public use, in which no force or virtue is implanted, except insofar as they are artistic marks or signs <note>original: "stigmata"</note> by which the intention of one person may be understood by another. And yet, the ignorance of common people is so great, and their blindness so extreme, that they refuse to admit any letters except these artificial and dead ones. They are entirely unaware that spiritual letters (as the Apostle witnesses) are written in the inner and more central parts of the creature itself. From the impressions of these spiritual letters the Word comes forth, *in which, according to St. John, is the life of...*

Therefore, that divine name was not trivial or accidental, concerning which, when Moses asked what it was, God Himself replied, *I am who I am* <note>original: "i. h. u. h." or "Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh"</note>, that is, יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton, the sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>; this is my name forever, and this is my memorial from generation to generation. The Tetragrammaton is, therefore, the name of eternity: and consequently, the letters constituting it are living, perpetual, and not artificial or accidental, for such things possess neither life nor duration in themselves. This is because the Word consists of these primordial and purely fiery letters, of which not even one jot <note>original: "jota," referring to the smallest letter, Jod</note> shall ever fall to the earth, but shall remain forever. These letters are therefore the rulers, the only spherical ones, the originals, and as it were the true Fathers of both worlds, applied to the sacrosanct Trinity; since **י** <term>Jod (the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet)</term> is rightly attributed to the Father, **ה** <term>He (the fifth letter)</term> to the Son, and **ו** <term>Vau (the sixth letter)</term> to the Holy Spirit, according to their nature and property. I have not ineptly called these persons "Fathers" in the preceding sections—existing as they did before the world's existence—insofar as each moved a specific action according to its own peculiar office to complete the "machine" of the world. They acted upon the "Mothers," **א** <term>Aleph</term>, **מ** <term>Mem</term>, and **ש** <term>Shin</term> <note>These are the three "Mother Letters" in Kabbalistic tradition, representing the elements</note>, for the production of Darkness (or earth), Water, and Light. Thus, it is not irrelevant to consider that, just as we see in the world that Angels act upon the stars, and stars upon the elements, and elements upon creatures, so also do the Fathers act upon the mothers, and the mothers upon their own elements, and the elements upon the meteors <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning</note>. With their help, they move natural composite bodies toward generation as well as lead them toward corruption. And this was the intention of the more occult Philosophers, who posited a certain invisible Zodiac that exerted its influence upon the visible Zodiac, and this again upon the Planets, by which they asserted fate was dispensed to lower things and all was governed. This was also the intention of the Kabbalists in their inverted tree of the 10 *Sephiroth* <note>The ten emanations or attributes of God in Kabbalah</note>, whose root was *Eheieh* <note>I AM</note> presiding over *Cheter* (the Crown), and whose summit tending downward was *Adonai* (Lord), to whom is subject *Malchath* (the Kingdom). And by these, the levels, numerations, and dimensions by which God works variously in this world seem to become known; of which we shall speak clearly below.

# CHAPTER II.
## Concerning the number and measure of the Tetragrammaton, by which both the Macrocosm and Microcosm are numbered and measured.

IN our book on divine numbers, we explained the reason why the world is divided into 27 parts; namely, for the production of a Cube from the most exact and perfect root of the number 3, which embraces the sacrosanct Trinity. The square of this number was 9, and consequently, it makes a Cube of 27 (that is, 3 times 9). Or, as the Platonists explain it, 9 9 9, in which they include so many mysteries. An exact demonstration of this matter may be seen in Treatise 1, Section 1, Book 1, and Chapter 12 of the *Microcosmic History*. Therefore, we shall explain the mystery of this number in this place, and we shall elicit its rationale from the primordial foundations in this manner. We see, specifically, that the ineffable name consists of three fiery and formal letters, insofar as they include the fountain of all light: 1, 2, 3. These are only spherical, and therefore superexcellent, most eminent, and constituting the primary and simplest number of perfection, namely 3. And hence it is that the Kabbalists maintain that this is that unique name circling the universe and connecting all things: namely, the highest to the highest and the lower to the lower, and the highest to the lower and the lower to the highest. Thus, we find from this that the aforementioned Cubic number 27 is the numbering of that dimension to which the Semidiameter of the world is adapted, measuring from the circumference to the center. For, if we look at the Hebrew numbers, which are expressed only by letters, we will perceive that this Cubic number results from the value of the letters of the name Tetragrammaton. For **ה** <note>He</note> is five, and **ה** <note>He</note> is five, and **י** <note>Jod</note> is ten, and **ו** <note>Vau</note> is six, which together constitute 26; and **א** <note>Aleph</note>, which is always the root of the number ten, or unity, and is never separated from God, constitutes 27.

Hence, therefore, it is said that He is the Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the End: for He who is the beginning of the world is also the end of the same. Wherefore it is also right to observe that God began His work from the small **א** <note>Aleph</note> or unity, and finished it with the great **א** <note>Aleph</note>, which signifies the number one thousand. And this is the reason that in the sublunary region <note>The realm below the moon, i.e., the Earthly sphere</note>, the number one thousand is found in our pyramidal demonstration; and this not ineptly, insofar as it is the cube of the number ten.

From these things, therefore, it is clear enough that the whole name Tetragrammaton is nothing other than **א** <note>Aleph</note>; and everything that exists is included by Aleph or God, who is יהוה <note>YHWH</note>. This name is again Aleph, or the measure between the principal and the final Aleph. From this, it is evidently proved that everything that exists, and every Being, is God Himself, Aleph; who is light and darkness; namely, darkness when hidden in *hyla* <term>hyla (primordial matter)</term>, and light when manifesting Himself. And this is the reason that Aleph is called by the Kabbalists "dark and lucid," just as was clearly explained in the preceding pages. By these things, it is also clearly declared that God is the whole through the whole, and is solely that which exists from the circumference of the "machine" even unto the point of the center; that is, inside and outside everything that is created. Whence, Deuteronomy 10: *Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to the Lord.* And Isaiah 66: *Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.* Because, however, He is in every-

This passage argues that God is in all things and beyond all things, and consequently infinite; *If the heavens and the heavens of heavens cannot contain you, etc. 1 Kings 8.* But this is demonstrated even more clearly by this definition from Hermes Trismegistus <note>original: "Mercurij Trismegisti"</note>, by which he declares the infinite and omnipotent existence of God: *God, he says, is a circle whose center exists everywhere, and whose circumference is nowhere:* This is indeed best represented by these two arithmetic marks, 10, signifying ten, explained among the Hebrews by the letter <term>Jod (the 10th letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often used to symbolize a divine point of origin)</term>, which is the hieroglyphic of <term>Jehovah (the Tetragrammaton YHWH)</term> itself, signifying the same in the number ten, or the first "article," as <term>Aleph (the 1st letter of the Hebrew alphabet)</term> is explained in unity. The first of these marks, representing unity, is like an indivisible point through which the center is found everywhere. For there is no number in which unity is not found, insofar as all numbers arise from it, nor is a number anything other than a collection or gathering of units. Furthermore, the cipher (which is the second mark of the number ten) denotes the circumference in its shape, and is as if non-existent in any one place, insofar as it is worth nothing by itself; therefore, it refers to the <term>Ensoph (Ein Sof, the Infinite God prior to self-manifestation)</term>, infinite in its being.

We see, therefore, through these symbolic demonstrations, how the name <term>Tetragrammaton (the four-letter name of God, YHWH)</term>, by which the dimension of the world is outlined, is included in the single and immensely capacious letter **א** <note>Aleph</note>. This is shown in this way: In the character **א** we find a double **Jod**; one, namely, ascending in the form of a wing, and another descending. It has been very often demonstrated that **Jod** denotes the number ten among the Hebrews. Also, the spear descending in the **Aleph**, in this manner **\**, is the true character of the letter **Vau**, and consequently signifies the number 6. Two tens, therefore, with 6 added, make 26 <note>10+10+6=26, the gematria or numerical value of the name יהוה / YHWH</note>. From this it is clear that **א** is equal in number to the name Tetragrammaton, in which a double **He**, that is, twice five, constitutes 10, and a single **Jod** denotes another 10, and **Vau** 6; from the value of these numbers added together arises 26. And the unity of the **א** itself completes the number 27, which is the cubic number of both the <term>Macrocosm (the great world/universe)</term> and the <term>Microcosm (the little world/man)</term> <note>27 is 3 cubed (3x3x3), representing perfect spatial completion</note>. Thus we find the world divided into three regions, and each of them into nine spheres or intervals; so that the world in its first division refers to the persons of the Trinity, to whom it is compared; but in the second, to the square number, namely the ninefold of the most holy and highest root of perfection, namely the number three; from whose cube the whole Macrocosmic work is forged. Similarly, according to the image of the world, man is distinguished into three regions or sections, corresponding to each heaven of the Macrocosm: the superior of which is again subdivided into three hierarchies; the highest is of the mind, the middle of the intellect, and the lowest of reason, the root of which is the Word. The highest region of both worlds refers to the first person of the Trinity or the Father, who was before the second or third region existed; the second to the Son, who received light and being from the first, as from the Father; and the third to the Holy Spirit, who derived his nature and action from the two superior ones. Thus, even among Philosophers and Physicians, no small dispute has arisen as to whether the first appearance of a human being's generation, or the beginning of his life, was in the brain or the heart. Among them, those who embraced sensory observation made the heart the first living thing; but those who looked more deeply into the matter with intellectual eyes established that the hidden life and movement of a rational creature from the point of vegetative generation is in the brain. For it is certain that the highest heaven received light, life, motion, and action from the <term>Alpha (the beginning/God)</term> before the second or middle heaven. This is proved even more clearly because the first region of the world, or the Empyrean heaven, was living and moving before the second or middle region—namely the Aethereal—appeared in the womb of the world. But, since we have made more abundant mention of the dimension of the name Tetragrammaton in both the Macrocosm and Microcosm in the *Introduction to Section 1, Portion 1, Chapter 2*, where we revealed clear reasons as well as illustrations of this matter, we have decided not to waste much time on that business here.

### CHAPTER III.

->*Concerning the ten Sephiroth, or divine numbers disposing all things in the world, according to our opinion.*<-

Although we have made some mention in the preceding sections of the ten divine numerations, which are called <term>Sephiroth (the ten attributes/emanations in Kabbalah)</term>, nevertheless, for the better explanation of this our work, we think it worthwhile to clarify and explain them more lucidly in this place. Indeed, it will be very difficult to understand them rightly without a clear explanation, because within them lie hidden infinite and plainly stupendous mysteries, if any faith is to be placed in the wiser Kabbalists. For this is (as the Sages themselves have testified) a science of profound speculation, and a certain immense ocean into which all our contemplation is submerged, and having been submerged, is swallowed up as if by a gap. Nevertheless, the Doctors have written many, many things concerning the tree of the ten numerations, and have reduced almost the whole of the sacred Old Testament into these ten numerations, and through them into the ten names of God themselves, and through those again into the one name of the Tetragrammaton. They affirm that the <term>Ensoph (the Infinite)</term> or infinity is the Alpha and Omega, who said "I am the first and I am the last": and that <term>Cheter (Keter, the Crown)</term>, that is, the Crown of the kingdom of all ages, is a fountain without a bottom, etc. We think it should be known first of all that

...that the <term>Sephirot (the ten divine attributes or emanations in Kabbalah)</term> are divine measures and numerations in the dimension of the world, which the Kabbalists call the "cloaks of divinity." Thus it is said in Psalm 104: *Clothed with light as with a garment.* These numerations are therefore various lights descending from a single root, by whose favor all things are created, and once created, are nourished. Hence they are also taken by some to represent the days of the world's construction; and they are sometimes called "Short Days" by the Kabbalists. Through their diversity, various works were made in the creation, and these have been continued and preserved from the creation until the final <note>original: "Peréat" — the ultimate dissolution or end of the world</note>. And without a doubt, these are the various garments of the one God, producing things of different natures in the world through various influences; this occurs because of the variety of resistance in materials of differing density, in which God, the Father of Light, is clothed in the world. And it is from this that <term>Orpheus (the legendary Greek musician and prophet)</term> established a plurality of Gods, all of whom had a relation to these Sephirot. And <term>Democritus (the pre-Socratic philosopher)</term>, Orpheus, and many of the <term>Pythagoreans (followers of the philosopher Pythagoras)</term> said that all things are full of Gods; they referred all of these to the one Jupiter, just as all numbers are referred to unity. For all nine lower Sephirot depend upon and arise from a single root: hence the Sephirot are not inaptly compared to an inverted tree, having a root, a trunk, and branches.

<margin>The names of God are twofold.</margin> These Sephirothic numerations or dimensions are contained within the number ten; for this is the end of all numbers, and consequently the measure of all measures, to which the Decalogue of Moses, the ten spheres of heaven, and the ten categories of the logicians are subject. Of these ten numerations, three are called "supreme" by way of excellence, insofar as their seats are the highest, where sits the *Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of Hosts*; and they represent the persons in the Trinity, and consequently are more principal, just as the remaining seven are less exalted in essence. And although a peculiar name of God is attributed to each Sephirah or numeration, it must be seriously understood that among those ten names, only one is truly appropriated to God: His other names are taken from His works. That one unique name, namely the ineffable <term>Tetragrammaton (the four-letter name of God, YHWH)</term>, attributed chiefly to God, signifies the substance of the Creator in a pure sense, in which there is no participation; but His other glorious names denote the reality with participation, insofar as they are derived from actions or works that have been discovered. For thus the surname of God, *Adonai*, is taken from this man *Adoni*, which means "Lord." Thus it is said: *The man, the Lord of the earth, spoke.*

<margin>The Crown.</margin> Now, *Adonai* is said (as <note>original: "Rabb. Moys. AEgypt." — Rabbi Moses the Egyptian, better known as Maimonides</note> reports) for the reason of glory and honor. And thus Abraham spoke to the angel: *My Lord (Adonai), if I have found favor, etc.* *Adonai* is therefore a surname of the Creator; but all others, such as Judge, Just, Gracious, Pious, *Elohi*, etc., proceed from His works. Of the three principal ones, the first is as it were the root of the entire Sephirothic tree, and is called <term>Kether (כֶּתֶר)</term> by the Kabbalists, which among the Latins is called the *Corona* or "Crown." This Crown is signified hieroglyphically by the letter <term>Shin (ש)</term>; for it is crowned with three eminences and is a symbol of the Trinity. Furthermore, the crown is indicated by the character of the cipher *o*, which we compared above to the circumference of God, which is nowhere, insofar as it is infinite, and consequently outside of all things, and whose center is 1, found throughout; so that when these are joined together, they form the number ten, which encompasses all things. And certainly, if we contemplate the order of the world's creation, we shall find the cipher *o* to be the type of the entire formless and infinite matter; which was <term>hyle (primordial matter)</term>, the cottage of the God who was not yet apparent to the world. But truly, when He appeared in the world through the 1, the *o* was made into something of consequence out of nothing. For the appearance of the central unity drew back the darkness, filling the cavity of the now-created world with the appearance of waters. Whence it was said: *And the Spirit of the Lord moved upon the waters*; which previously were darkness, or the abyss, whose face was veiled by darkness. And thus this Crown of God is forever radiant, for to Him (as the Psalmist testifies), *darkness is as light, and night as the day.* But truly, to formless creatures overwhelmed by darkness, He now arises in sensible beauty, and from nothing (as far as human sense is concerned) He is brought into action by the appearance of unity, reducing that "nothing" into the denary quantity or dimension. And from this infinite Crown, the first emanation flowed into the formless shadows by which they were reformed. Thus the Messiah, or the fiery power, was produced into the bosom of the mass of darkness; by whose power the waters are now revealed, and the divine Majesty of the moist nature is unveiled. Thus the royal Psalmist rightly said: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm*—that is, by the power of the Tetragrammaton the heavens were established—and *by the Spirit from His mouth all their power.*

<margin>Kether.</margin> This *Kether* or Crown is therefore called by the Kabbalists the root of the entire Sephirothic tree, which consists of the number ten, denoting the effect of the character <term>Jod (י)</term>, which is 10, in which the name Tetragrammaton consists; so that this single letter *Jod* signifies the same thing as the Tetragrammaton. Therefore, the Crown, or *Kether*, or the root of the divine tree in the world is the same as *Jod*; and again, *Jod* is the same as 10; and finally, 10 denotes unity, or the fountain of light looking out from its dark hut into the formless world *o*: by whose presence *o*, from nothing, becomes the whole in every action. And from this it follows that to this first Sephirah, *Kether* or the Crown, that name of God is attributed which has the closest relation to the divine essence, and denotes the Father among the persons of the Holy Trinity, from whom the Son and the Holy Spirit are derived. Wherefore it also seems to denote the three times of eternity, and the plurality of persons with the unity of nature; for where the Father is, there the Son is presupposed to be;
