...and where both are, there the outflow of the Holy Spirit from both is recognized. Hence Moses says in Exodus 3: *I am who I am, and I am he who will be.* For <term>Ehieh (the Hebrew name meaning "I Am")</term> is the future tense of the verb <note>original: "Hajahi"</note> "to be," denoting—according to the interpretations of the <term>Talmudists (scholars of Jewish civil and ceremonial law)</term>—the eternity of God; for through the future tense, it implies the present and the past. These three differences of time are reduced into the divinity, which cannot be comprehended, as in Psalm 90: *A thousand years are as one day.* Therefore, in this <term>Tetragrammaton (a four-letter divine name)</term> <note>original: אהיה, "Ehieh"</note>, the letter <note>original: א</note> **Aleph** signifies the Father; **He**, the Spirit or the bond connecting the Father with the letter **Jod**, the Son; and the final **He** brings back the Son, through an indivisible bond or circle, into the **Aleph** or Father from whom he was born. For the letter **Aleph** in the future tense always declares the first person. This is the reason why the name of God, **Ehieh**, is always associated with mercy and love, insofar as it is attributed to the Father, whose nature is always to have mercy on his children and to love his infants (Psalm 103). 

The office of this part of the <term>Sephirotic Tree (the diagram of the ten divine emanations)</term> is to flow through the orders of the <term>Seraphim (the highest order of angels)</term> into the <term>primum mobile (the "First Mover," the outermost sphere of the universe)</term>, and from that to all things to which it gives being. For it must be observed in this place that just as in the creation three heavens were made or fabricated, one after another, so also a triple reception of influences occurs before an effect can be produced in the lower worlds. These are received first from the <term>Sephirot</term> of divine unity, then from the spheres of the middle heaven, and finally from the elements, which pour or infuse them immediately into the bodies adapted to them. 

However, as it seems to me (contrary to the opinions of some <term>Cabalists</term> who place the influences of this radical Sephirah only in the First Mover), **Ehieh**, having dominion in the numbering of <term>Cheter (Kether, the "Crown")</term> insofar as it refers to the divine essence, gives strength and power from its own office to the trunk and branches of its tree, so that from them the influences may finally be sent down and infused into lower things, as the will of God and the necessity of his creatures require. This is no different than how the virtue of a tree's root communicates power to the trunk, the trunk to its branches, and the branches to the fruit and leaves, which afterward nourish the creatures. Yet the immediate cause of nourishment is not attributed to the root of the tree, but to the fruit and leaves; though it is certain that the same nourishing power proceeds originally from the root, without which the tree and its fruit cannot exist. 

Indeed, if we look a little more closely at the nature of the name **Ehieh**, which presides over the root of the tree, we find that it differs in no way in essence from the ineffable name <note>original: יהוה, "Jehovah"</note> **Jehovah**, to which the trunk of the Sephirotic Tree is attributed. For as God before any creation was <note>original: א</note> **Aleph** or unity, so at the moment of creation, he moved from **Aleph** to **Jod** (the number ten), where unity is joined with a cipher. Thus, as **Jod** (10) proceeded from the unity of **Aleph**, so the divine essence moved from the root, over which **Ehieh** presides, to the trunk, over which **Jehovah** dominates. In the Tetragrammaton name **Jehovah**, therefore, is the entire power of the Crown, **Ehieh**, just as the virtue of the root is in the trunk of the tree. The efficacy of **Jehovah** also passes into the lower names, just as the nourishment of the trunk penetrates into the branches and leaves, by which animals are eventually fed and refreshed. From **Ehieh**, therefore, all the intelligences in the <term>hierarchies (the organized ranks of angels)</term> rejoice, moved by the Father. These intelligences, being moved, themselves move the spheres and celestial bodies over which they preside. This is the reason why God is called by <term>Hermes Trismegistus (the legendary father of Hermetic philosophy)</term> *a circle whose center is everywhere and whose circumference is nowhere*, as was said above. From these things, unless I am mistaken, it is clear that the proper office of **Ehieh** is universal, and by no means so particular as some have wished to make it; for if it were, then the lowest numbering, <term>Malchuth (Malkuth, "The Kingdom")</term>, would not influence the Moon (which is the common receptacle of all higher influences), but would have some even lower place for its vessel—which, it seems to me, would be irregular.

Furthermore, since all things were made by Wisdom, which was present as a help to **Ehieh** like a right hand composing all things (as Solomon says), and since that Word and power of the Tetragrammaton **Ehieh**—or the Messiah and universal emanation—flowed forth from that bright fountain in which there was only life and light, by whose power the heavens were established so that he emerged as the soul of the entire world or <term>Metattron (Metatron, the supreme celestial mediator)</term>, it seems likely that the immediate influx into the First Mover comes from him who holds the name of **Jehovah** impressed upon himself, so that from that orb it may thereafter be poured down to all things to which it gives being. This, then, is that ineffable and most holy name presiding over the second Sephirah, which is likened to the trunk of the tree. This Sephirah, or numbering of the second order, is called <term>Hochma (Chokhmah)</term>, that is, **Wisdom**. To it is referred the "first-born" nature, insofar as it immediately succeeds **Cheter** (which is referred to **Ehieh**, the Father). Similarly, it is the primitive Law, insofar as Wisdom was first with the Father and was sent forth as the primary and constant Law through which the world was fabricated from the beginning, according to that of the Royal Prophet in Psalm 136: *The fabric of the heavens is from the Word*, or as the Wise Man says in Proverbs 3:19: *God established the heavens with Wisdom.* To this is also attributed "Being," insofar as according to Ecclesiasticus 1: *Wisdom was created first of all Beings,* and it was the Being of Beings, insofar as all things were made by it, and without it, nothing was made (according to St. John 1). Hence it is also written that nothing is a more ancient principle than Wisdom alone. For **Ehieh** by itself was infinity, when it was retracted in the abyss of darkness and, as it were, idle, or (as they say) looking toward nothing; and for that reason, it is called among the Hebrews <term>Ein (Ayin)</term>, that is, **Nothing**, or Non-Being and "Without End"; because we, being punished with such a thin poverty of intellect in divine matters, judge those things which do not appear in the same way as those things which are not.

Wisdom, therefore, insofar as it was the first emanation from the dark Aleph and the "First Nothing," is said...

And this is the reason why Aleph receives into itself the nearest and most fruitful letter, and is named <note>original: "Ab" אב</note> **Father**, that is, the father of all generation and production: for by joining <note>original: "Beth" ב</note> **Beth**, <note>original: "Aleph" א</note> **Aleph** generates <note>original: "Ben" בן</note> **Son**, which is the first production from unity and the principle of alteration. From this, he is named <note>original: "Reshith" ראשית</note> **Beginning**, even though he is the second emanation from infinity—that is, the second <term>Cabalistic numeration (Sephirah)</term>—through which all things were made. Moreover, the name attributed to this numeration is that ineffable one mentioned above, namely <note>original: "יהוה" (YHWH)</note> **the Tetragrammaton**, in which the single letter <note>original: "Jod" יוד</note> **Jod** signifies as much as all four letters of the name, since it represents the number 10. This contains the number 4 through successive counting (1, 2, 3, 4), which, when added together, produces ten. And, because all Hebrew figures are formed from **Jod**, which is merely a single point—than which nothing is simpler, and consequently more symbolic of the simplicity of the divine essence—we are also taught that all created things are fashioned from a similar little point of divine simplicity. This point is so simple in its essence that it is inwardly indivisible and always the same. The <term>Kabbalists</term> observed that the four letters of the ineffable Tetragrammaton name are not to be pronounced; hence the name is called "ineffable." Although these letters are four in number, only three of them are actually different <note>The letters are Y-H-V-H, so Y, H, and V are the three distinct characters</note>. This triple number, when squared, produces 9, which is the simple number of the moving spheres of the middle heaven, the orders of angels in the highest heaven, and the elementary regions, as has been declared in various places in our history of the **Microcosm**. This square number, 9, when multiplied by its root, produces that <term>Platonic Cube</term> of 9, 9, 9, or 27, by which the semi-diameter of the entire world is measured. From this, one may see that **Wisdom**, residing in the bosom of the Father (in whom the divine and ineffable name of the Father exists), fabricated the world according to that ideal dimension through the characters of the divine and ineffable name, depicted with fiery ink upon <term>hyle</term> <note>The primary, unformed matter of the universe</note> as if upon black paper. For just as <note>original: "Vau" ו</note> **Vau** previously separated the first <note>original: "Jod" יוד</note> **Jod** from the latter <note>original: "He" ה</note> **He** by the will of Jod, so also, at the command of <note>original: "Elohim"</note> **God**, the firmament separated the upper waters from the lower waters. But setting these things aside, since we have dealt with them extensively in the preceding parts of this volume, we say that some Kabbalists have made a double <note>original: "He" ה</note> **He** in the name of **Jehovah** to imitate the dual nature of the **Messiah** himself, which is therefore called the "power of the Tetragrammaton." For they wish the <note>original: "Jod" יוד</note> **Jod** immediately following the Jod (which is the image of the Father) to represent the divine nature of the Redeemer, and the final <note>original: "He" ה</note> **He** the human nature, and that <note>original: "Vau" ו</note> **Vau**, insofar as it is a copulative conjunction, joins these two natures together. Yet truly, this opinion of theirs does not please me, since it is certain that **He**, insofar as it is a sign of inspiration, denotes the **Holy Spirit**, who is the bond of love, joining the Father with the Son in an inviolable bond, and again rejoining the Son with the Father in a spherical union, according to that saying of <term>Hermes Trismegistus</term> <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with hermetic philosophy</note>: *The Monad generates the Monad, and reflected its own heat into itself.* And this is the reason why these letters alone are spherical or circular: which is demonstrated as much by a straight line as by a square and a cube, insofar as their numbers always end in the same digit.

<margin>Jod 100 1000</margin>
Thus <note>original: "Jod" יוד</note> **Jod**, which denotes the number 10 (which is like an extended and stretched out line), if multiplied by itself, produces 100, which is the Square; this multiplied again by the root will bring forth 1000 for the Cube. And so from ten to ten unto infinity.

<margin>He 25 125</margin>
Likewise <note>original: "He" ה</note> **He**, which is the sign of the number 5, will have 25 for its Square and 125 for its Cube <note>Note how the last digit remains 5</note>.

<margin>Vau 36 216</margin>
Furthermore, <note>original: "Vau" ו</note> **Vau**, which is the character of the number 6, becomes 36 by multiplication; this number led back to its root produces the Cube 216 <note>Note how the last digit remains 6</note>.

<insert>NB. The number of the name of the great Creator, from which the circles of the world arise.</insert>

From these things it is evident that these numbers end just as they begin in their root, square, and cube; which other numbers do not do. Therefore, they are not ineptly considered "circular." And this is the reason why **Wisdom**, to whom this Sephirah with the ineffable and spherical name is given, had it as her office to fabricate the heaven and the world round, as being more perfect and capacious, according to the Words of the Wise in Ecclesiasticus 24: *I, Wisdom, alone have compassed the circuit of the heavens, etc.* And Proverbs 8:19: *God established the heavens by his wisdom.* Therefore, God acknowledged in express words that this ineffable name, consisting of spherical letters, was deservedly in this uncreated Angel, saying: *My name is in her.* This Sephirah sends its influences through the orders of the <term>Seraphim</term> (as I believe) to the <term>primum mobile</term> <note>The "First Mover," the outermost sphere of the universe in traditional cosmology</note>, so that from there they may be transmitted to all lower things, whereby it abundantly gives them life and **Being**. For the *primum mobile* received its life from it, inasmuch as it moves all the lower spheres with a most rapid motion from east to west. For it is certain that the world and its natural *primum mobile* received its motion from the first supernatural mover—that is, from the **Son**, the first mover of things, proceeding from the immovable Father. This Son was that divine **Word**, in whom was Life and eternal Wisdom, by which all things were created; for she is the divine Spirit possessing all power, as Solomon testifies in Wisdom 7.

Wherefore, without doubt, all motion and action in the world, since they are powers, emanate from her: For Wisdom, which is a sincere emanation or flow of the brightness of the almighty God, is more mobile than all things that move, and consequently is the origin of the world's motion, as Solomon testifies. This Sephirotic numeration was therefore the first act, and the principle of motion, and the life, as it were, of the world and its creatures; since its form, or luminous soul, is the act and splendor of the divine Majesty, and that true Wisdom...

## Three Principal Sephiroth

The Messiah, or the Power of the <term>Tetragrammaton (the four-letter name of God, YHWH)</term>; which is diffused everywhere from the mouth of Jehovah through the world, by which the world is animated, and its creatures enjoy life—specifically by the power of the name of Jehovah. For (as Archangelus rightly says in his *Dogmas of the Cabalists* <note>Archangelus of Borgonovo was a 16th-century Franciscan who wrote on the Kabbalah.</note>) this name is the unique one, circling the universe and connecting all things: namely, the highest things to the highest, the lower to the lower, and the lower to the highest. There is, therefore, a continuous flow of the power of this <term>Sephirah (divine numeration)</term> and its name, insofar as worldly being flows continually from its source. But truly, that which flows continually must be sustained by something permanent, lest it perish due to a lack of influences; this permanent thing is the Word of God, in which all things were established and move, according to the words of St. Paul: *Upholding all things by the Word of his power*.

But now we shall descend to the third Sephirah, whose name in Hebrew is <note>original: "בינה"</note> **Binah**; which in the Latin language signifies **Prudence** or **Understanding**; and it is the lowest of the three superior or Principal Sephiroth; for this reason, it is attributed to the Holy Spirit. And this is the reason why the name <note>original: "אלהים"</note> **Elohim** is attributed to this numeration, which is most properly assigned to the Holy Spirit among the most holy persons of the Trinity. Hence, because this person is the common bond of the preceding persons in unity, some render **Elohim** by the interpretation "Gods," making a plural number from the singular <note>original: "אל"</note> **El** (God). But, as it seems to me, **Elohim** is rather a singular number, as we have declared elsewhere, compounded from <note>original: "אל"</note> **El** (strong, or strong God) and <note>original: "מים"</note> **Mayim** (waters, or the sea). Or it is from <note>original: "אלה"</note> **Eloh** (God) and as if from <note>original: "מים"</note> **Mayim** (water). Thus, **Elohim** is like "the strong God of the sea and the waters" in <note>original: "אלהים"</note> **Elohim**, or <note>original: "אלהמים"</note> **Elomaym** (the strong God of the waters); where **Elomaym** is contracted into **Elohim**.

From this also the heavens are called <note>original: "השמים"</note> **Hashamaym**, insofar as they were made spiritual heavens from the waters through the Spirit. For this must be known above all: that all fluid things in the world belong by office to the third person of the most holy Trinity. And hence it is said that the *Spirit of the Lord moved over the waters*. In **Elohim**, therefore, as in a single common Spirit, the Trinity seems to be included. Hence "the strong God of the waters" is explained as the strong God of the world through whom the world lives and exists. For the Spirit of the Tetragrammaton moved over the waters, imparting a fiery force to them, and dividing the universe into three regions corresponding by office and property to each person of the Trinity. These three are nothing but the unique God, the Tetragrammaton, containing within itself the <term>י</term> (Yod) and <term>ה</term> (He), representing the characters of the three distinct persons.

For this reason, just as the preceding Sephirah, **Chokhmah**, signifies Wisdom, the Messiah, and the Word or second person; so this one denotes prudence, understanding, the divine Spirit, and the Holy Spirit of discipline. Thus it is said in *Deuteronomy* 34:9 that Joshua the son of Nun was full of the Spirit of Wisdom when Moses had laid his hands upon him; and in *Numbers* 11:25, that the enjoyment of the Spirit of Jehovah makes Prophets; and that He attributed understanding to the 70 Elders, so that they might govern the people with Moses. And in *Genesis* 41:39, it is said to Joseph: *There is no one so understanding as you*; and in verse 38 of the same chapter, the reason is given: *Can we find a man like this, in whom the Spirit of the Gods is?* We can produce many other examples from the sacred scriptures by which it is very easy to prove that the Sephirah **Binah** (that is, Prudence and Understanding) belongs to the third person of the most holy Trinity, whose property it is to give understanding and to imbue minds with prudence.

Indeed, this Sephirah makes its influences descend through the order of the <term>Cherubim</term> into the eighth sphere or the starry heaven, which the belt of the Zodiac surrounds with its golden characters. And since the principal virtues of the stars consist in this heaven, and truly the Holy Spirit is the dispenser of all virtues, therefore this sphere is attributed to the Holy Spirit. And hence it is said that *this divine Spirit brooded over the face of the waters*; or, as Pagninus <note>Santes Pagnino was a famous 16th-century Hebraist and Bible translator.</note> interprets it, *moved itself upon the surface of the waters*; that is, it was carried and moved in the first heaven over the face of the watery heaven, in whose convexity are the fixed stars, imbuing them with fiery virtue; by the mediation of which every inferior virtue arose and existed as a derivative. And hence the Royal Psalmist says: *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the Spirit of his mouth all their virtue.* Concerning these stars, it is said in *Psalm* 147:4: *God tells the multitude of the stars and numbers them, and as many as there are, he calls by their names; great is our Lord and of many virtues, whose understanding is infinite, etc.*

Where, by the "imposition of names" made to the stars, he understands the attribution of virtues; since each of them received a name according to its nature and property. For by this same sign, Adam gave names to the beasts of the field and the birds of the heaven, as is read in *Genesis*. And this is the last of the three Sephiroth of the higher degree, which prove the traces of the Trinity; from which, finally, all virtues are infused abundantly and liberally from the Zodiac first to the Planets, and then from them to all inferior things. This is therefore the reason why the Planets have the virtue of the signs of the Zodiac and of the other fixed stars located outside the Zodiac. Thus we say that Saturn has the nature of Capricorn within the Zodiac; but of the belly and tail of the Whale <note>The constellation Cetus.</note>, and the beak of the Raven <note>The constellation Corvus.</note> outside it; Jupiter has the nature of Pisces within the Zodiac and, outside it, of the bright Hydra; and so on for the rest. Thus also one sign is called the house of this or that Planet, or its exaltation or triplicity, and in all properties it is necessary that the wandering stars <note>The planets.</note> agree with the fixed ones. And for this reason, we have thought that the fixed stars were created before the wandering stars, specifically regarding the causes and origin of their actions: For, as the Zodiac and its entire sphere received its virtue from the influence of the Sephirah Binah, as if from a fountain, and that by act and...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the Sephiroth, moving from the higher intellectual realms (Binah) into the emanations that govern the physical cosmos, planetary influences, and the moral order. by the power of the name **Elohim** <note>One of the primary names of God in the Hebrew Bible, often associated with justice and the natural order.</note>; so also the Planets receive their general impressions from those living hieroglyphics of the eighth heaven <note>The sphere of the fixed stars, situated above the planetary spheres.</note>, and their particular impressions from the lower **Sephiroth**, and then afterwards they pour those virtues, having flowed from the Zodiac, into lower things. From this it follows that <term>Cichus Esculanus</term> <note>Cecco d’Ascoli (1257–1327), an Italian encyclopedist and astrologer.</note>, an author or writer on the spheres, says not ineptly that each of the twelve signs received its particular name from the nature and property of some animal, or rather, vice versa, that every animal receives its name from its own celestial star, insofar as it is seen to symbolize one nature with another. And <term>Moyses Arabicus</term> <note>Moses Maimonides (1138–1204), the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher.</note> says that all animate things have a star from heaven flowing into them to guard and preserve their essence; and this by divine command and will; so that the stars constituting the sign of Aries in the Zodiac govern and have regard for the terrestrial Ram, and the celestial Taurus for the terrestrial Bull, and the higher Whale for this lower one, and so on for the rest. And this is what Ptolemy teaches in the *Centiloquium* <note>A collection of 100 astrological aphorisms traditionally attributed to Ptolemy.</note>: namely, that lower things are ruled by higher things, and the lower world is contiguous with the superior bodies. We conclude, therefore, that the forms of the fixed stars are like those lucid outpourings from the <term>Sephirah Binah</term> (Understanding): which forms, operating occultly, are called by some "intelligences," "daemons," and "Gods." Hence <term>Mercurius Trismegistus</term> <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the Hermetic writings are attributed.</note> said in *Pymander*, Book 3: *The Gods were conceived within the ideas of the stars along with the signs* <note>original: "Dij in astrorum ideis cum signis concipiebantur"</note>. The stars were numbered according to those Gods who inhabited them. For by "Gods" he seems to mean the formal influences which each name of God rains down from its own Sephirah.

<margin>The fourth: Clemency</margin>
The fourth numeration or Sephirah, which is the first of the less principal ones, is called by the Hebrews **Chesed**; which in Latin signifies **Clemency**, goodness, or grace. To this numeration is attributed the name of God **אל EL**; which flows from this, its tabernacle, through the order of Thrones <note>A high-ranking choir of angels in Christian angelology, often associated with God's justice and chariot.</note> into the sphere of Saturn; although the opinion of others is that its influence is into the sphere of Jupiter, insofar as Jupiter is a friend and benevolent to the human race. But we, led by another consideration, grant it to Saturn rather than Jupiter; specifically because it denotes the **Sabbath**, which according to the Cabalists is the mystery of the living God and the symbol of the higher world—that is, the Jubilee of eternity, where all labor ceases. Hence they say its use is found in two ways in the Holy Scriptures: namely, insofar as it refers to external actions according to the condition of the lower world; and of this use it is said in *Deuteronomy 5: Observe the Sabbath day*. Or, insofar as it regards internal actions with respect to the higher world. Whence it is read in *Exodus 20: Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy*, namely by joining the powers of the soul to the mind for the progress of contemplation according to the higher world. From this it follows that God wished to reveal the law through these two words: **observe** and **remember**. Hence the Sages made two Sabbaths, according to that passage in Exodus, a matter which Ezekiel 20 also seems to support: *I gave them my Sabbaths*. But in truth, through this gift of the Sabbath, God gave that most perfect gift of clemency which is called the **Jubilee** <note>original: "Joboleus," referring to the Hebrew Yovel, the year of release occurring every 50 years.</note>, to be embraced always with a mindful spirit; which indeed is the supernal week called the Jubilee, from which all remission, propitiation, and infusion of grace descends. And this is the Sabbath of rest, or the Sabbath of Sabbaths, in which all pure human souls, having cast off their stain, will recover the paternal inheritance which we acquired through the Messiah. This is indeed that true Sabbath of the Cabalists to be sanctified at all times, in which we follow the will not of the flesh, but of the soul, and contemplate divine things, thinking nothing contrary to the Divine Majesty; and this stands as a law for all nations, insofar as it sprouted from nature itself. And therefore, if I am not mistaken, the day of the Sabbath is attributed by God to this planet (as the Jews themselves assertively say), which they have observed so exactly and strictly according to the will of their God. It may be for this reason that, although this planet is called "unlucky" by astrologers because of its slowness and the dull qualities arising from it, it nevertheless denotes fixity, cessation from labor, and a tabernacle of rest—even if its efflux is mostly adverse to animate things here in the lower realms due to the mutability and alteration of their nature. There are even some who seem to interpret the power of the Sabbath proposed by Moses as consisting in this: because the star of Saturn is unlucky and malevolent to lower things, Moses in his wisdom did not wish for any business to be performed or attempted on that day; but he wanted not only men, but even other animals, to rest and be free on that day for divine service, because Saturn presides over the first hour of the day of Saturn (Saturday), which begins late at night, just as Mars (who is the "lesser misfortune" and a most pernicious planet) governs the last hour. Wherefore some Cabalists believe that evil spirits have more power to inflict every kind of evil on the fourth and seventh nights, over which these two planets preside, than at other times of the week. Hence they maintain this was instituted in the Decalogue: *Remember to sanctify the Sabbath day*. But truly, this reason for why the day of Saturn is the Sabbath is more external than pertaining to the internal Sabbath.

<margin>Gheburah <unclear>the fifth</unclear></margin>
The fifth numeration is called **גבורה Gheburah**, which signifies power, might, severity, judgment, and punishment, yet nonetheless with clemency. The name fitting for this is **Elohim**; where *El* mixes peace and sweetness with the rebellious disposition of the **Maym** <note>Hebrew for "waters."</note> or waters; for their rebellion and resistance is the cause of evil, and is not of God. This numeration flows through the Dominations <note>Another rank of angels, the Dominions.</note> into the sphere of Jupiter. Hence Jupiter is held as the first Lord among the Gods, terrible and to be feared. Whence he is depicted with a lightning bolt in his hand and is called the "Thunderer," sparing whom he wishes to spare, and sometimes punishing according to merit. Thus in his left hand he holds clemency while rebuking, as in his right he holds the spear of severity.

->### CONCERNING THE PRIMARY PRINCIPLES OF THE MICROCOSM<-

...presides by the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note> **Eloah** <note>original: אלוה; a singular form of the divine name Elohim.</note>. This influence flows through the order of **Powers** into the sphere of **Mars**, who is a powerful leader. The seventh **Sephiroth** is called **Netzach** <note>original: נצח; meaning "Victory" or "Eternity."</note>, Triumph, or Victory; and the name governing it is **Jehovah Sabaoth**, the God of Hosts. This emanation projects and pours out its influences through the orders of **Virtues** into the sphere of the **Sun**: from which it is filled with vital power and abounds affluently, which it flows liberally into lower things. And its angel **Michael** or **Metatron** is the leader of the army of God, who triumphed and gained victory in the spiritual battle over the prince of darkness. The eighth emanation is named **Hod** <note>original: הוד; meaning "Glory" or "Splendor."</note>; that is, Honor or Beauty. Its divine name is **Elohim Sabaoth** <note>original: אלהים צבאות</note>, God of Hosts, not for war and vigor, but for piety and concord: this influence occurs through the order of **Principalities** into the sphere of **Venus**. The ninth is called **Yesod** <note>original: יסוד</note>, that is, the base, foundation, redemption, or rest; its name is **El Chai** <note>original: אל חי</note>, the Living God, or **Shaddai** <note>original: שדי</note>, the Almighty, or rather, He who is self-sufficient, without any external thing. Its influence is through the Order of **Archangels** into the sphere of **Mercury**: for peace was announced to the earth through a messenger or Archangel. The tenth and last **Sephiroth** is called **Malkuth** <note>original: מלכות</note>, Kingdom, Empire, or the Temple of God. Its name is **Adonai** <note>original: אדני</note>, Lord; and it sends its influences through the order of **Angels** into the sphere of the **Moon**. And this is partly our opinion, so that I may defend the opinion of the Archangel <note>Likely referring to Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, who held the title Count of Concordia and wrote extensively on the "Archangelic" Kabbalistic dogmas.</note> in his *Commentary on the Dogmas of the Kabbalists*, who absolutely placed the influence of **Malkuth** through the order of Angels into the region of the Moon; although **Reuchlin** <note>Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a key German humanist and scholar of Hebrew/Kabbalah.</note> himself and some others say the influences of **Malkuth** pass through the order of blessed souls into rational creatures. Nor indeed can we entirely reject the opinions of those who make ten spheres or orders of the Empyrean heaven.

<margin>#</margin> But we have only made a progression in the number nine, and treated the **Sephiroth** according to that measure. According to their opinion, then, **Kether** <note>The "Crown," the first Sephiroth.</note> or the first **Sephiroth** flows through the orders of **Seraphim** into the "first mobile" <note>Primum Mobile, the outermost moving sphere in the geocentric model.</note>, and from that to all lower things, to which it gives being. I will by no means contradict this opinion of theirs, considering that just as the divine name **Ehieh** <note>original: אהיה, "I Am."</note>, related to the divine essence, represents the first person of the Trinity, namely the Father, and consequently claims the first act for itself in the superior and supernatural world; so also the first mobile behaves in the natural world, insofar as it is like the father and immediate origin of the movement of all lower spheres. But in truth, because the Word or Wisdom, namely **Chokhmah**, was the first mover in the world; for that reason, I said its influences were adapted to the first mobile. But both are granted, and neither will be denied by me. They say **Chokhmah**, the second emanation, flows through the **Cherubim** into the eighth or starry sphere. Nor will I entirely deny this either, insofar as the Zodiac of this starry heaven is called <term>Zoon</term> <note>original: ζῶον, Greek for "living being" or "animal."</note>, that is, an animal. But in the **Word** was life, which it pours into that belt of life <note>The Zodiac.</note>, so that from there, by the mediation of the Planets, it may be carried and flow to lower things. Nevertheless, our opinion seems not to differ much from the truth, wishing that **Binah** or the **Sephiroth** attributed to the Holy Spirit pours its influences into this sphere. They also say that the third **Sephiroth**, **Binah**, flows through the order of **Thrones** into the sphere of <margin>3. Seph. Binah</margin> **Saturn**: whence they call **Binah** the "supramundane Saturn" of the intelligible world, noting by this very thing the repentance and remission of sins, which took place at the end of the multiplication of the square of the number seven <note>Refers to the 49-year cycle leading to the Jubilee.</note>: thus also is drawn the great **Jubilee of Jubilees** of the future age. Afterwards, they wish in the fourth <margin>4. Seph.</margin> place that the emanation **Chesed** flows through the order of **Dominions** into the sphere of **Jupiter**. And insofar as he is a friend of the human race and the life of things, we admit it, wishing that it has its influences from **Chesed** or the supercelestial Jupiter, or ♃, always denoting Clemency, grace, and the mercy of the life of things. They say also that **Gevurah**, the fifth **Sephiroth**, flows through the order of **Powers** into the sphere of **Mars**: <margin>5. Seph. Geburah</margin> nor indeed do I say that I entirely deny this, insofar as **Gevurah**, the superior and spiritual Mars, is power, severity, judgment, and punishment; of which same condition is the celestial Mars, as one who threatens wars, desolations, and spoils. They make the influences of the sixth emanation, **Tiferet**, penetrate <margin>6. Seph. Thiph.</margin> through the order of **Virtues** into the sphere of the **Sun**, attributing to it clarity, light, and life, which descend from the sphere of the Sun to produce all minerals, of which **gold** is the head—like the Sun among celestial things, bread and wine among vegetables, and man among animals. Nor do I think this wanders much from the truth, insofar as **Tiferet** denotes grace, beauty, and ornament; all of which are observed to exist in abundance in the Sun. In the seventh order, it may be that **Netzach** flows <margin>7. Seph. Netzeth</margin> through the order of **Principalities** into the sphere of **Venus**: and those influences descending from Venus produce the love of justice, and finally bring forth trees, plants, herbs, and other vegetables in the elementary world. In the eighth place, that **Hod** sends its influences through the **Archangels** to the sphere of <margin>8. Seph. Hod</margin> **Mercury**, which afterwards descending produces animals. Afterwards, that **Yesod** of the ninth series pours its flows through the "sieve" of the order of **Angels** into the sphere of the **Moon**; from whose region thereafter the increase and decrease of things descends. And in the final arrangement of the **Sephiroth**, that **Malkuth** flows through the order of blessed souls into rational creatures, <margin>9. Seph. Jesod</margin> conferring knowledge of things, science, and industry. Let it be assumed, I say, that all these things are granted as certain, <margin>NB</margin> provided that the sphere of blessed souls (as some theologians claim) is included in the Empyrean heaven; yet, if our reasoning is well considered, which is concerning the measure of the number nine, you will perceive that the greatest force and no small probability lies in my order of the **Sephiroth**, and concerning...

SECTION I. PORTION II. PART I.

...description. Indeed, it does not seem fitting that the influence from **Malchut** <note>The tenth Sephiroth, meaning "Kingdom," representing the physical world and the manifest presence of God.</note>—passing through the sphere of blessed souls (if such a sphere exists) from the highest heaven through the middle—should fall upon the earth out of proportion with other influences, or that it should grant knowledge and reason by a profound leap to humans dwelling in the center of the world-machine. For it seems that such knowledge is instead infused by the influence of the super-celestial Mercury, who according to the Kabbalists is **Jod** <note>The tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often associated with the point of creation.</note>, and according to our calculation is **Jesod** <note>Yesod, the ninth Sephiroth, meaning "Foundation."</note>, rather than by the influences of **Malchut**, which, on account of Adam's sin, is more a cause of ignorance and darkness than of knowledge. Furthermore, **Binah** <note>The third Sephiroth, "Understanding."</note> also grants knowledge and intelligence; for its divine name, related to the Holy Spirit, is the fountain and origin of sciences and doctrine, as is explained in many places of the Holy Scriptures in the clearest words. But, because I do not wish to seem obstinate in my opinion, I shall set it aside and adapt myself, my mind, and the entire thread of this subject to the doctrine of the aforementioned Sages:

### CHAPTER IV.

### *Why the Sephiroth, or numerations, are in man or the Microcosm, since he contains God and His lights within himself no differently than the world does—as man is the son of the world, just as the world is the son of God.*

The Platonists <note>Followers of the philosopher Plato who viewed the universe as a living, rational being.</note> called the world *Zoon* <note>original: "Zoon"; Greek for "living being" or "animal."</note> not without reason: and **Hermes Trismegistus** in the *Pimander* <note>A foundational text of Hermeticism, a philosophical and religious tradition based on writings attributed to Hermes Trismegistus.</note> says that the "Great World" is the first animal, composed of a certain material and intelligible nature (and hence the Psalmist says that the heavens and elements praise the Lord, and exult and rejoice in the name of His presence); and similarly, man, or the "Small World" <note>The "Microcosm."</note>, is the second animal. Hence elsewhere he calls the world the "Son of God," just as man is the "Son of the World"; for, as the world includes nothing in its essence except what it received from God, so too has Man derived all parts of his composition—both internal and external—from the world. Thus, he is not ineptly called the "Image of the World," which is itself the "Son" or "Image of God"; and consequently, Moses rightly says that man was made in the image of his Creator. On this, Hermes Trismegistus speaks profoundly in the eighth sermon of the *Pimander*: *“I know that the world exists from God and in God, but man exists from the world and in the world; however, the principle, comprehension, and constitution of all things is God.”* And in the same sermon he says again: *“The first God, according to God, made the world in His own image as the first animal; the third God, Man, He made as the second animal.”* These words will become even clearer to those who read that entire eighth sermon accurately, where they distinguish these "Gods" thus: *“The first God is eternal among all, immovable, unbegotten, the author of all; the second is the world, made in His image, begotten by the first God, and by Him preserved, nourished, and gifted with immortality; finally, Man is the third God, terrestrial, but subject to mortality.”*

From these things it seems clear enough that if the world, which is the Son of God, is governed by the ten divine **Sephiroth** <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself.</note> or numerations along with the holy names presiding over them, then by similar reason those same numerations exercise their force and power in the Microcosmic spheres. This is because the Microcosm is fashioned from a portion of every region of the world. Consequently, the Sephirothic Tree acts as effectively in man as in the world; for in man there is both heaven and earth. His "heaven" is both the seat of the Divine Word from the root **Ehieh** <note>original: אהיה; the divine name meaning "I Am."</note> and the temple of the Spirit **Elohim**, who was carried over the waters—a truth which St. Paul also teaches us in various places. And this is what Hermes Trismegistus seems to understand in Sermon 13, where he says that the *“number Ten is the parent of the soul; for Life and Light are united there, where the units of the number itself are born of the Spirit.”* Therefore, unity according to reason encompasses the ten, and conversely, the ten encompasses unity. 

Indeed, he does not speak outside the sense of the Holy Scriptures, which acknowledge that all names of God refer back to the unique **Tetragrammaton**, namely **יהוה** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, which is the most polished mirror of the divine essence, in which all names and surnames of God shine; just as all the gods of **Orpheus** <note>The legendary Greek musician/prophet; the author is comparing Greek polytheism's hidden unity to the Jewish names of God.</note> are contracted into a single Jupiter or Monad. By "Life," therefore, that priest Hermes understands the acts of the Sephirothic light, according to that saying of **John the Evangelist**: *“In Him, who was the light of the world, or in the Word, was life, or life shines forth from the Word of God,”* as that from the Father or **Ehieh**. By the "number ten," he undoubtedly understood the ten Sephiroth or divine numerations. Since these flowed from one root or **Ehieh** (the Father), he calls that ten the "Parent." Hence he said that the units of the number itself are born of the Spirit: which unity indeed embraces the ten, as the Ten embraces unity. For **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing the number 1.</note> is the same as **Jod** <note>The tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing the number 10.</note>, and vice versa, Jod is the same as Aleph, and both Aleph and Jod are nothing but unity. For 10 is the same as 1, insofar as 0 is nothing by itself; but what it has, it possesses entirely from the 1. And 1 is the same as 10, since 1 is not exalted by 0, but conversely, the cipher is given form by the 1. 

From these things, therefore, we see that since the soul is in man—indeed, is the very heaven of the Microcosm—and since the number ten is the parent of the soul (for the soul's essence proceeds from the influence of all the Sephiroth, of which the lowest is **Malchuth**, which is the receptacle of the power of all higher influences—since, as we said in many places in the first volume of *The Microcosm*, the Mind in its descent received the powers of all the orders of angels), it is necessary that the force and virtue of all the Sephiroth operate in the Microcosm just as in the Macrocosm. This is also confirmed by the most learned Kabbalists,

ON THE PRIMARY PRINCIPLES OF THE MICROCOSM.

...those who assertively say that Magic is the science of the celestial world, which contains within itself ten spheres, which are the instruments and modes through which it acts upon us; namely, the nine moving spheres and the tenth immobile one called the Empyrean <note>The highest part of heaven, thought by ancient cosmologists to be composed of pure fire or light.</note>. And to prove this proposition of theirs, they insert these two proofs, by which they attempt to show the divine acts of the **Sephiroth** <note>In Kabbalah, the ten emanations or attributes of God through which the universe is created.</note> in the heavens and throughout all: *Behold, Lord, the heaven is thine, and the heaven of heaven* (Deuteronomy 10). And: *If the heavens, and the heavens of heavens cannot contain thee* (3 Kings 8) <note>This refers to 1 Kings 8 in modern Bibles.</note>. Where they ascend in a demonstration of the power and potency of God from the Elements and the spheres, into which the influences of the Sephiroth occur—namely from the heavens to the Sephiroth themselves, which are numbered in the heaven of heavens, that is, in the supernatural heavens, insofar as the Sephiroth are divine and super-essential, beyond which the root of **Ehieh** <note>Hebrew: אֶהְיֶה‎, "I AM," the divine name associated with the first Sephiroth, Kether (The Crown).</note> itself nevertheless penetrates infinitely into **hyla** <note>term: hyla (original Greek: ὕλη), meaning primordial matter or the basic substance of the universe.</note>.

### CHAPTER V.

->On the duties of the divine enumerations in man, and on their wonderful mystery in the exaltation of human nature:<-

Who can doubt that this divine number of ten is contained as much in man as in the angels themselves, through whose orders their radiations pass? Since, as Psalm 8 testifies, *he made man a little lower than the angels, and crowned him with glory and honor; for with his own hands he made him, and put all things under his feet.* Through the Sephiroth, therefore, God breathed into man the breath of life, according to Genesis 2. Through them, he looks down from the heavens upon the sons of men thus created—that is, from the root of the tree **Ehieh**—to see if there be any that understand, according to Psalm 52. And he watches over him (Job 7:20) and visits him in the morning hours, that he might test him every moment (Job 7:18). By the virtue of these, he brought him out of his mother’s womb, according to Psalm 22:11. *He fashioned him like clay, and poured him out like milk, and curdled him like cheese; he clothed him with skin and flesh, and fenced him with bones and sinews;* <note>original: "Sicut argillam fabricavit... ossibus & nervis texuit eum"</note> And all these things occur through the superior influences descending into **Malchut** <note>The tenth Sephiroth, "Kingdom," representing the physical world.</note>; *with the kindness of life he exercised him, and his visitation preserved his spirit,* according to Job 11. Through the power of the influence of the second and third Sephiroth, and of **Tephireth** <note>Tiphareth, the sixth Sephiroth, meaning "Beauty" or "Harmony," often associated with the heart or the sun.</note> itself; through these, all the works of man, and his thoughts, and his imaginations, and his movements, and his entire life are known by Him; indeed, he has beset him behind and before, according to Psalm 139:2. *Whither shall a man go from the Spirit of the Lord? or whither shall he flee from his face? If he should climb the heavens, he is there; or if he should make his bed in the grave, behold, he is present; if he should take the wings of the morning and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea, even there his hand shall lead him; if he should say: Surely the darkness like the twilight shall cover me, and the night shall be about him, even the darkness cannot so obscure him that he does not see, but the night shines to him as the day, for the darkness is to him as the light itself. (Psalm 139:7).* From these things, therefore, it is clear that **Ehieh**, from the root **Cheter** <note>Kether, "The Crown," the highest Sephiroth.</note> or the Crown, looks upon man through all the Sephiroth. This same point was signified even more clearly by the text of Job, where it is said that there is a Spirit in man, but the inspiration of the Almighty gives him understanding. From which it may be perceived that the succession of intelligence comes from God the Father, **Ehieh**, through **Hochma** <note>Chokmah, "Wisdom."</note>, Wisdom, his son or the **Word**, by means of **Binah** <note>Understanding, associated here with the Holy Spirit.</note>, intelligence, or the Holy Spirit; and so through the whole trunk of the tree, which is the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God.</note>, **יהוה** <note>note: the Hebrew letters for YHWH (Jehovah).</note> Jehovah, and the branches springing from it. This action or plenary influence does not occur in any sublunary creature except in man alone, to whom a portion of the intellectual heaven is granted. This indeed **Synesius** <note>Synesius of Cyrene (c. 373–414 AD), a Neoplatonist philosopher and bishop.</note> (Hymn 1) seems to acknowledge with these words:

> The Mind, an immortal offspring of divine parents, having slipped down into matter; a small thing indeed, yet the whole of them, and this island, being entirely one within the whole, turns the vast cavity of the heavens, and preserving this universe, is present distributed into various forms; part of it is the course of the stars, part the assembly of angels, and part even has obtained an earthly form through a heavy bond, and being separated from its parents, has drunk dark oblivion through blind anxieties, wondering at the pleasant earth.

From these things, therefore, we see that the origin of the human mind is from the root **Ehieh**, and that its movement occurs through the universal divine Sephiroth, insofar as it passes through the assemblies of angels, which it informs, and through the spheres, which it animates. And consequently, this universal Mind is the Spirit of the enumeration **Hochma** or Wisdom itself, which is the power of **Ehieh** and the Tetragrammaton itself, and the Messiah, or the Word preserving all things. Hence it also happens that this divine Mind, dwelling in an opaque body, has a relation to the superior and more simple enumerations. Which indeed **Mercurius Trismegistus** <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure Hermes Trismegistus, supposed author of the Hermetic Corpus.</note> (Pimander 3) clearly declares in a discourse of this kind:

> The human soul (he says), veiled by the shadow of the flesh to undertake the discourse of the celestial Gods, to the works of God and the progress of nature, to signs of good things, to the knowledge of divine power; a certain portion has been attributed to the indication of good things and the finding of the various artifice of evils: yet it begins to live in them, and to obtain wisdom according to the portion of the continuous course of the circling Gods, etc.

Where by "Gods" he understands the lower enumerations from the ten roots, to which various names of God, or of the one Jove, are attributed. Hence also Synesius says in the same Hymn:

> O soul, drinking from the perennial fountain of good things, ascend to the parent with conceived prayers in supplication, nor delay, leaving earthly things to the earth; soon indeed joined with God the Father, you shall exult with God:

Where by "father" he intends **Ehieh** or the root. And here he seems to denote the manner of the Mind's ascension from the body to **Ehieh** through the grades of the Sephiroth, which are nothing other than the orders of Jacob's ladder, through which the angels and souls descend from heaven to earth, and again ascend from earth to the heavens. Nor indeed would I have you understand that I am speaking here only of the Macrocosmic heaven and earth, but also of the Microcosmic heaven and earth.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the Microcosm (Man) as a mirror of the Macrocosm (the Universe), specifically focusing on how the divine Sephiroth are mapped onto the human soul and body. It transitions from the general concept of celestial influence to the specific role of the "Mind" (Mens) and the restoration of humanity's divine nature through Christ, contrasting the fall of Adam under Mars with the rise of Christ under Venus/Jupiter.</meta>

# SECTION I. PORTION II. PART I.

...namely concerning the internal and external man himself, in whom all the divine **Sephiroth** <note>In Kabbalah, the ten emanations or attributes of God through which the universe is created.</note> are ideally expressed as exactly as in the **Macrocosm** <note>The "great world" or the entire universe.</note>; And in the **Microcosm** <note>The "little world" or the human being, seen as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note> the Mind itself is referred to as **Hochma** <note>term: Hochma (Hebrew: חָכְמָה‎), meaning Wisdom; the second of the ten Sephiroth.</note>, according to that saying of Hermes Trismegistus in the *Pimander*, book 1: *His Mind's eye can be raised to the highest things;* And in the 4th Sermon he speaks of this Mind thus: *Whoever are supported by this nature of God are held to be immortal rather than mortal, following the comparison of their works; they embrace with their intelligence all things that are on the earth, and in the sea, and if there is anything beyond them above the heaven, and they raise themselves so far that they even behold the Good itself.* <note>original: "Quicunq; hac Dei natura fulti sunt... ut ipsum quoque bonum intueantur."</note> And this is that which is found in the Evangelist: *No one can know the Father except through the Son.* Hence also by the Apostle, Man is called the **Temple of God**, and elsewhere, the **Tabernacle of the Holy Spirit**. To which also Sextus the Pythagorean philosopher <note>referring to the *Sentences of Sextus*, a collection of moral aphorisms popular in the early Church.</note> seems to agree: Hence it is said by Hermes Trismegistus: *Man is a divine animal, which is not to be compared to the earthly brutes, but with the celestial beings; Indeed, he says that the true man is even more excellent than the inhabitants of heaven themselves, or at least possesses an equal lot.* Indeed, he proves his assertion thus: *Whoever (he says) of the celestial beings descends to the earth, leaves the limit of heaven; but man ascends into heaven, and measures it, nor does he escape the things that are lowest or those that are sublime, and he diligently inquires into all other things; and what is more, without even leaving the earth he is lifted into heaven, so great is the power of human nature:* Wherefore (he says) *one must dare to say that a terrestrial man is a mortal God, but the celestial God is an immortal man.* <note>original: "hominem terrenum Deum, sed mortalem, Deum vero cælestem immortalem hominem." This is a famous Hermetic maxim emphasizing the shared nature of humanity and divinity.</note> From these sayings of his, therefore, it is to be drawn out that the external man is a mortal God, but his internal man, or the prince of the internal, is an immortal God; insofar as the Mind is subject to no passions, as it is that to which even the fates themselves are subjected. And this is the reason why that Priest <note>Likely referring to Hermes Trismegistus or a similar ancient authority.</note> breaks out into these words: *Man is a great miracle, to be adored and honored: For he passes into the nature of God, and is as if he himself were God; he knows the race of Demons,* etc. Which indeed he seems to understand concerning the spiritualized or regenerated man, such as he is by the power of the Mind, which is of the divine nature of the Messiah: Whence it is read in the *Resolutions of the Theologians* (Vol 2, Part 1, Part 3, Q. 3) that the immortality of man is not by nature but by grace; And upon this Augustine says: *God created man immortal not from the condition of nature, but from the benefit of the Creator, that is, of the universal Mind, creating and informing all things.* Therefore Adam, the first man, by his sin hid this deity or divinity of man, by which he was created immortal in the beginning, and in this way contracted the rust of mortality for himself and his descendants; But Christ, a man full of the Holy Spirit, liberated the divine nature of man from the chains of sin and darkness, and revealed its life-giving splendor to the world by his justice; so that, what one had prepared for destruction, the other preserved from ruin by the life-giving spirit: Therefore, what **Samael** <note>In Kabbalistic tradition, the archangel of death and the prince of demons, often associated with the planet Mars.</note>, the destructive Demon of **Mars**, ordained by his fate for the ruin of man, this the beneficent and Jovial Spirit of **Venus** <note>The author associates Christ's restorative influence with the positive astrological qualities of Venus and Jupiter.</note> cast down, and reduced man to his original state of health: For this same thing was denounced from the beginning by a certain prognostic from the stars themselves, which pour out fate upon men: <margin><image-desc>manicule (pointing hand)</image-desc></margin> For according to Firmicus <note>Firmicus Maternus, a 4th-century Roman lawyer and astrologer.</note> and others, Adam was born under the sign of **Aries**; which is the House of Mars, and the Dominion of the Spirit Samael, in which place because his malice was exalted, therefore his detriment and depression were to be expected in the sign opposite to it, namely (where Mars is said to have his fall and weakness) in **Libra**: That indeed which also happened: For it is said by Astrologers, that Christ was born under the same sign, which is attributed to the goodness of Venus and Jupiter: From these things therefore we see how the higher things act upon man, and print their ideal impressions into his heaven; And by consequence, that the Sephirotic numberings are found no differently in the heaven of man than in the heaven of the world, of which man himself is the son, through his unique soul, which is the Messiah, the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>term: Tetragrammaton (Greek for "four letters"), the sacred four-letter name of God in Hebrew (YHWH).</note>: Which since it is also the mind of man himself, and as it were the trunk of the human Sephirotic tree, there will be no doubt that the divine numberings themselves are as much in the internal man as in the spiritual world. Furthermore also, since God is triune, and in a threefold manner, related to the Trinity, communicates as much with man as with the world, any of which manners is again divided by another threefold partition, attributed to the triple order of the three Hierarchies or the choir of Angels, to which ternary division multiplied by 3, if unity (which is the God of one or the **Monad**) is adapted as a root, it constitutes the number ten, and therefore by the triple principal order led into itself, with the addition of unity (thus 10), He decreed to create man himself, who for this reason is not foolishly called the knot of all things: For he distinguished the race of men by grades, namely the superior and celestial, and the inferior or terrestrial, and according to the nature of these grades he ordained the intervals of the lives of men, and the conditions of the soul. **Ehieh** <note>The divine name "I AM," associated with the highest Sephiroth, Kether.</note> therefore, or the Father in **Cheter** <note>term: Cheter (Hebrew: כֶּתֶר‎, Kether), meaning "The Crown," the topmost of the Sephiroth.</note>, the crown or summit of all things, possessing the formal essence in himself, which is presented to his intellect alone, and understanding himself, begets Wisdom, the Messiah, the Word, or the power of himself, who is called the Son in the Numbering of **Hochma**, from Cheter, that is, springing forth from the bosom of the father with a light leap. And hence it is that the name of the Father and the Son is found in the Deity: For the one God without distinction of persons contained his power in himself; nor did he wish to reveal or emit it, before he thought of the fabric of the world: But then, according to the doctrine of Hermes Trismegistus, *The Monad generated the Monad, and reflected its splendor back into itself:* Or, as is held elsewhere by the same; *When he had said these things, he changed his form, and suddenly revealed the universe; that is, he made the hidden manifest;* and by his manifestation, that is, by the splendid emanation, all deformed things were informed <note>In the sense of being given shape or "form."</note>. From this follows in his context: *For I beheld a certain immense spectacle, namely all things converted into light.* Indeed, this same Mind made man out of nothing as if he were something, according to that in Psalm 139: *Your eyes saw my unformed substance, and not yet existing;* for in your book all my members were written down. # ON THE PRIMARY PRINCIPLES OF THE MICROCOSM

In this way also, from the flow of the Son from the Father, and of the Holy Spirit from both, the world was ideally outlined before its real creation: Just as the Royal Prophet <note>referring to King David</note> boasted that he received the image of the temple completely described from the hands of God. Therefore, Wisdom having been produced—since it is most similar to the producer and emanating from it by a supernatural progression—it takes the name of the Son, as has been said; whence also the name of the Father is used, as was likewise said, insofar as there is a most certain relationship between father and son. Moreover, the budding fiery love proceeding from both is called the most Holy Spirit, the inviolable bond of both, insofar as it connects the offspring with the parent in eternal love; and in this way the power of the third **Sephiroth** <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> is established, namely **Binah** <term>Understanding</term>, to which the name **Elohim** is attributed.

To the first two [Sephiroth] joined by the Spirit, the orders of the higher Hierarchy, the **Seraphim** and **Cherubim**, correspond; since through the Seraphim, **Ehieh** <note>original: "Ehieh"; a divine name meaning "I Am," associated with the highest crown.</note> sends his influences, and through the Cherubim, **Hochma** <term>Wisdom</term>, as was said above. Furthermore, St. John teaches us in Chapter 1 that *in the Word was life and the light of man.* And Hermes Trismegistus, in the *Pimander*, book 1, affirms that the Word of the Lord sees and hears within man. Similarly, he instructs us in the same place that the Mind is God the Father, and that there is no difference in essence between the Word (or Son) and the Father, and that their union is of life, and that this union occurs through that fiery bond. Furthermore, St. Paul testifies that man is the temple of God and of the Holy Spirit. 

Why then should we doubt whether the higher Sephiroth are in man or not, and consequently the powers of the angels, the Seraphim and Cherubim? Similarly, **Binah** (Prudence or Understanding related to the Holy Spirit) sends its flow through the order of **Thrones**. This Word, guided by the Spirit, judges the world, as the Psalmist testifies: *He has prepared his throne for judgment; which seat the Father grants to the Son, giving him all power of judging.* Similarly, it is said of him in the *Apocalypse* <note>The Book of Revelation</note>: *I have overcome, and I sit on the throne of my Father.* God also gave the capacity for judgment to men; concerning which gift the Holy Scriptures treat everywhere. And the Wise Man in *Proverbs 21* says that *he who follows justice and mercy will find life, justice, and glory.* And in *Wisdom 1*: *The judges of the earth ought to cherish justice and think of the goodness of the Lord.* Also, the seventy Elders, to whom it was given to judge the people with Moses, possessed the virtue of the Spirit of this order or Sephiroth.

Moreover, man receives clemency, goodness, grace, and mercy from the influx of **Chesed** <term>Mercy/Kindness</term>; over which the name **El** presides, passing through the order of **Dominations**. From this, man has the power of ruling by virtue of the influence of this Sephiroth passing through this order. The Sephiroth **Geburah** <term>Strength/Severity</term> infuses power, force, severity, and the will to punish into the human spirit through the order of **Powers** <note>original: "Potestatum"</note> by the impulse of the divine name **Elohim**. 

But the sixth Sephiroth, **Tiphareth** <term>Beauty</term>, gives him grace, beauty, and ornament; and, insofar as its influences pass through the order of **Virtues** into the sphere of the Sun, it attributes to every man clarity and life, both natural and moral, by the assistance of the name **Eloah Tetragrammaton**. **Netzach** <term>Victory</term>, which is the seventh Sephiroth, flows into man and gives a triumphant Spirit and victory through the power of the name **Jehovah Sabaoth**, that is, the God of Hosts; whose influxes, insofar as they pass through the order of **Principalities**, distribute kingdoms and provinces to men, and other ruling dignities, both spiritual and civil. Therefore, the influx of this order is placed over kingdoms and provinces, and likewise over emperors and kings. 

Over princes and governors presides the order of **Archangels**, and likewise it teaches the Prophets. Finally, the **Angel**, according to the testimony of Christ, is attributed to every man. Therefore, through the choirs of Archangels, the Sephiroth **Hod** <term>Glory/Splendor</term> flows into the sphere of Mercury; and through the orders of Angels, that last numbering, called **Yesod** <term>Foundation</term>, flows. 

And in this way we see how the ten Sephiroth and their virtues are found as exactly in the **Microcosm** <note>Man</note> as in the **Macrocosm** <note>The Universe</note>. Indeed, it is also for this reason that these numberings are compared to a tree having its root on high and its branches below. Thus man, who was made in the likeness of God, is called by Aristotle—for the reasons stated above—the "inverted tree" itself, since his root is in the head, while the branches tend downward. For God gave man an upright face; whence he is best likened to the Tree of the divine Sephiroth, which indeed consists of divine names, whose trunk is the ineffable name, the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God: YHWH.</note>, from which the other titles draw their strength like boughs or branches. For God, who is compared to **Ehieh**, said: *Let us make man in our image.* This word "Let us make" is referred to the Son, and *He breathed into him the breath of life;* by which the Holy Spirit is understood. 

And here we have the principal Sephiroth cohabiting in the superior region of man; namely in the head, as if in the heaven of heavens, in which is the chief seat of divinity; where the root is God the Mind, as Wisdom is in the heaven, and the bond of both for life is the Breath or divine inspiration and spirit. Just as mention was made of the root, trunk, branches, and bark, so also that allegory is very often transferred to the head, shoulders, legs, feet, right and left sides, or the chest which is compared to the trunk, over which the name Tetragrammaton presides; arguing from this that the fabric of man is, as it were, the truest subject or tabernacle of those divine Sephiroth. Furthermore, because man was made in the image of God, therefore, just as God himself is named **Ilan** <note>Hebrew for "Tree."</note>—that is, the Archetypal Tree—containing the trunk, branches, and root within himself, so also Man may not indirectly be called the Microcosmic Tree. But concerning these ten numberings, over which preside as many divine names springing from unity or **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing unity or God.</note>, we have made mention, though hidden, in our booklet *On Divine Numbers*; where we made a demonstration fashioned from three pyramids, <meta>in which...</meta>

### SECTION I. PORTION II. PART I.

...at the summit of which we have represented God in the image of a flaming triangle: There we also declared how the **Two** <note>original: "Dias"; the Dyad</note> flows from the **One** <note>original: "Monade"; the Monad or Unity</note>, and the **Three** <note>original: "Trias"; the Triad</note> from both; these are indeed the roots of simple numbers. For unity is the root of duality, and that is the root or proximate principle of the first number, namely the triad, which is the root of any simple number; the square of which is 9, so that, if unity is added to it, the number ten is produced. Therefore, from unity to the simple number ten, those ten divine emanations proceeded, flowing from **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing 1.</note> even unto **Jod** <note>The tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing 10.</note>, which denotes 10. These were the ideal properties of the future world brought forth in the simplicity of the realm of the **Infinite** <term>Ensoph; from the Hebrew 'Ein Sof', meaning the Boundless or Infinite Godhead</term>; according to whose exemplar the world was afterwards created. 

And these properties were those divine numberings, called **Sephiroth**, from whose influences—through the orders of the first heaven into the second heaven, and finally by their descent on the third day down to the center of the machine—the world and the creatures of the world, and their virtues, were made and perpetually preserved according to the will of God. Thus, in the first place, 3 declares the perfect emanation of the first perfection; since in it is the beginning (1), the middle (2), and the end (3)—namely 1, 1, and 1 gathered together into one. Likewise, it shows the simple and complete perfection of the persons in the Trinity, which are attributed to **I Am** <note>original: "Ehieh"</note>, the **Crown** <note>original: "Cheter/Kether"</note>; **the Lord** <note>original: "Jah"</note>, **Wisdom** <note>original: "Hochma"</note>; and **God** <note>original: "Elohim"</note>, **Understanding** <note>original: "Binah"</note>. These are the simple Sephiroth, from which the less simple ones in the branches of the tree are derived. 

Thus, by multiplying 3 by itself, 9 is produced, to which by adding unity, 10 arises, namely **My Lord** <note>original: "Adonai"</note>, the **Kingdom** <note>original: "Malchut"</note>. For to 1 is referred 4, to 2 is referred 5, to 3 is referred 6; and again to 1 is referred 7, to 2 is referred 8, and to 3 is referred 9. This indeed holds itself thus: 1. **I Am/Crown**, or Identity, flows through the first choir of the higher angels <note>The Seraphim</note>, which is "Otherness," into the spheres having a triple nature, namely into its first threefold region, or the *Primum Mobile* <term>the 'First Moved' sphere in traditional astronomy</term>. Likewise, 2. or **the Lord/Wisdom** flows through the second order of the same Hierarchy, namely through the **Cherubim**, into the second sphere of the same triplicity, namely into the eighth heaven <note>the sphere of the fixed stars</note>; and 3. or **God/Understanding** flows through the third order of the same Hierarchy, namely the **Thrones**, into the third sphere of the same, namely into that of Saturn.

Then, through the second revolution or operation, 1. or **I Am/Crown** acts upon 4. namely **God/Mercy** <note>original: "El Chesed"</note> through the first order of the second Hierarchy <note>The Dominions</note> into the first sphere of the second triplicity, namely into the sphere of Jupiter; And 2. or **the Lord/Wisdom** impels the fifth Sephiroth, **God/Severity** <note>original: "Elohim Gheburah"</note>; through the second order of the second Hierarchy <note>The Virtues</note> it pours its flows into the second region of the second triplicity; and so on with the others. From this, therefore, we see how the infinite power of God worked toward the procreation of nature before anything formed existed. For in this way the world was made from the origin, and in this way also, in a miraculous manner, man was created; whence both the one and the other are said to be created in the image of God, insofar as they have the exemplar of the emanations of the super-substantial idea for their soul and form, or "first act." Hence, I say, the Sephiroth or divine numberings are in the world; and from there they are also found in the human spirit, no differently than a most splendid image in a most polished mirror, by which both the world and man receive the dimensions proper to their great mass, and the lights with which those dimensions are adorned and marked with distinguished beauty, by which they exist even to this very minute of time; since, as the Wise Man witnesses, by their favor all things are created and nourished, of which indeed man himself is the earthly prince.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*On the Mystery of the 10th and final Sephiroth, Malkuth, in the Microcosm and Macrocosm; And that because of Adam’s sin it is closed to us; How the 10 Sephiroth are applied to man; And that they contain within themselves heaven and earth.*<-

The Kabbalists, moved by the aforementioned reasons, say that man is an **inverted tree**, insofar as he is given a mouth and a sublime countenance, as has been said: For indeed, since man is made in the image of God, it follows that he is not inaptly called a tree, since God Himself is called the Archetypal Tree, comprising within Himself the trunk, the branches, and the root. From this it also follows that man, His image, possesses similar parts of that tree within himself, by which he is disposed by the Creator in his works toward both severity and mercy. 

Now, the root of this kind of Sephirothic tree is **I Am/Crown** <note>original: "Ehieh Cheter"</note>, whose downward flows descend through the lower Sephiroth, and finally into the **Kingdom** <note>original: "Malchut"</note>. Just as, therefore, when the root is cut from a tree, the flowers, leaves, and fruits wither and perish, so (say the Kabbalists) through the sin of Adam, **Kingdom** was cut off from the root of **I Am/Crown**, and from the trunk of the **Four-Lettered Name** <term>Tetragrammaton; the holy name YHWH</term>, and consequently from the benefit of all the Sephiroth; and thus **Kingdom** remained stripped of every good influence. Wherefore, this dimension remaining thus empty can confer no good upon us. But before Adam sinned, **Kingdom** received influences continually from the supreme root; the properties of all the Sephiroth and all the orders of angels looked upon one another with mutual love according to the orders of their ranks, so that the same happiness and friendship found among those above was also among those below. The heavens were joined with the elements in a certain bond of mutual embrace, and one filled the channels of the Sephiroth of the other, through which influences moved downward, and they performed their duties with perfect precision...
