[con]tinue; they are perceived to agree, just as the celestial Aries agrees with the terrestrial ram, Taurus with the bull, Gemini with the twins, Cancer with the crab, and so forth. And indeed, both Astrologers and even some Christian Philosophers and Theologians have written wonderful things concerning the comparison of the superior or ideal Zodiac with the interior one, and about the miraculous events that usually occur from their variation. This must necessarily happen insofar as the motion of that super-celestial sphere is slower than that of the celestial. They say, therefore, that various effects are produced in the world because of the diverse operations of the parts of one Zodiac upon the others—namely, the invisible Zodiac upon the visible. This could not happen unless the motion of the superior sphere differed from the motion of the inferior.

For in the beginning of the world, the first degree of Aries in the invisible Zodiac surpassed that first degree of the visible Aries; and therefore, because of the harmony of the influences, they said that age was the Golden Age, insofar as in it the same element did not attack its like with contrary actions. And this is the reason why that age had its origin with Paradise. They assign this reason for the matter: they observed that the invisible Zodiac moved by one degree and 28 minutes every 100 years, and consequently its revolution is completed in 49,000 years. This time they called the **Platonic year** <note>original: *annum Platonicum*; a great cycle of time after which the stars and planets return to their original positions.</note>, in that they said after it was finished, all things would return to their same pristine state. 

But setting these things aside, we conclude that, just as **Chokmah** <note>original: *Hochma*; the Sephirah of Wisdom, representing the second emanation of God.</note> flows from its invisible Zodiac into the visible Zodiac, so too the seven lower **Sephiroth** <note>The "emanations" or attributes of God in Kabbalistic thought.</note> correspond to the seven Planets, and contain within themselves the ideal and invisible planetary spheres; any one of which pours its own property into the real sphere and its visible star. And, just as the vital power flowed into the Planets from the Zodiac before they themselves had any power of life, so also souls received their essential and intellectual being from the invisible Zodiac before they were clothed with the nature of the visible Zodiac. 

And, just as the influxes of the power of life occur from the visible Zodiac into the Planets, so also souls are poured out from Chokmah into the lower Sephiroth through the circles of the intelligences, before they penetrate to the starry sphere. Hence it is said by the Cabalists, that God pours in the soul, which passes through the superior Sun, **Tiphereth** <note>original: *Tiphe-reth*; the Sephirah of Beauty or Compassion, often associated with the Sun.</note>, and drinks in its influx, and clothes itself with that property of the Sun-Tiphereth. Therefore, according to them, there is a superior Sun, which is the middle Sephirah or dimension; and consequently there are also invisible and ideal Planets, which are the seven lower [emanations] from Chokmah—for **Malkuth** <note>original: *Malchut*; the final Sephirah, representing the Kingdom or the physical world.</note> is attributed to the region of the lower world, as some maintain. 

We conclude, therefore, that it is most certain that God, three and one, is the infuser of souls into His Sephiroth first, and then through the orders of intelligences into the ethereal region, so that by the mediation of the visible stars they are transported into the lower things for the generation of men. For God is the prime agent, and consequently the first giver of forms; and hence, insofar as the soul is the **primary act** <term>actus primus: the foundational state of being or existence.</term>, it must proceed immediately from the first actor. From Him, therefore, has flowed all life, form, and order. 

Therefore, although all souls emanate from a single source, which the Cabalists call the "northern fountain of **Gevurah**" <note>original: *fontem Gheburis aquilonaris*; Gevurah is the Sephirah of Strength and Judgment, often associated with the North.</note>, we nevertheless derive the luminous fountain from the supernatural essence of the Lords of the three superior Sephiroth. Nevertheless, they pass through other dimensions or Sephirotic media before they slip down into the spheres, and from them into bodies or the **spermatic mass** <note>The physical matter or "seed" from which a body grows.</note>; from which they receive various properties. Hence it happens that each of the souls receives that portion of light whose nature is the medium to which it is exposed, or with which it is accustomed to be joined, just as is more clearly explained in the preceding parts. 

However, how the soul or the human **Mind** <term>Mens: the highest, divine spark of the human soul.</term>, which is a ray or spark of divinity itself, carries away with it the natures of each sphere in its descent—both super-celestial, celestial, and animal—we have openly demonstrated, first in *Treatise 1, Section 1, Book 4, Chapters 3 and 4, Of the Physical History of the Microcosm*, and in *Book 12, Chapter 4 of the same*; and also in *Treatise 1, Section 2, Book 3, Chapters 1 and 7, of the Microcosmic History*. But now finally in the following chapter we will show that the trunk of the whole tree is that ineffable name, the **Tetragrammaton** <term>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</term>, without which no soul can descend or exist.

# CHAPTER IX.

## That the ineffable name Tetragrammaton is the trunk of the Sephirotic tree, of both the Macrocosm and the Microcosm.

The Hebrews, as was said above, from their most hidden mysteries, firmly assert that the soul emanates from the great four-letter name of God, **Jehovah** <note>original: יהוה; the Tetragrammaton.</note>, like infinite branches and leaves from the trunk of a tree; from which all other names of God presiding over all the Sephiroth arise, like branches from the trunk of some tree. And since **Yod** <note>original: *Jod*; the first letter of the Hebrew name of God.</note> signifies the same as Jehovah, or all four letters, insofar as it denotes the number ten—and 1, 2, 3, 4 joined together make 10—therefore Yod is deservedly called the root of the tree, from which the powers of the trunk and branches arise. Wherefore Yod is attributed to **Ehieh** <note>original: *Ehieh*; "I Am," the name associated with Keter.</note>, or **Keter** <note>original: *Cheter*; the highest Sephirah, "The Crown."</note>. But **He** <note>The second letter of the Tetragrammaton.</note> rules the third Sephirah, to which the Holy Spirit is referred, insofar as it denotes respiration:

# CONCERNING THE PRIMARY PRINCIPLES OF THE MICROCOSM
### 155

The third letter of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, יהוה (YHWH).</note>, **ו** (Vau), corresponds to the sixth **Sephirah** <note>One of the ten divine emanations in Kabbalistic thought.</note>, over which **Eloah** <note>A Hebrew name for God.</note> presides; insofar as its seal is the "Truth of the Lord" <note>original: *Emeth Adonai*</note>; and it is the Word or Unity in the letter **ה** (He)—that is, God placing his tabernacle in the sun. Therefore, **ו** (Vau) properly refers to the center of the entire **Sephirothic tree**; and for this reason, it is likened to the presiding light of the superior Sun, **Tiphareth** <note>The Sephirah representing Beauty and the Heart.</note>. The final **ה** (He), however, is joined to **Malkuth** <note>The final Sephirah, representing Sovereignty or the physical Kingdom.</note>, which sends its influences into the elemental region. The **Cabalists** <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah).</note> also seem to recognize this kind of arrangement of letters in the "ideal trunk" (according to whose image the world received its proportion and measure); and among more recent writers, **Reuchlin** <note>Johannes Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist and scholar of Hebrew and the occult.</note> also seems to approve of it. This name, therefore, is the **Archetypal** and eternal Idea, encompassing the essence of Divine Majesty; according to its model, the dimensions of both the **Macrocosm** <note>The "great world" or the universe.</note> and the **Microcosm** <note>The "little world" or man.</note> are truly outlined and most skillfully fashioned, both in terms of their internal Being and their external existence. For their internal essence is impressed upon the dimensions of the **Sephiroth**; but in the external existence of both, the **י** (Jod) looks out from the darkness from the tens into the hundreds and thousands; and its first aspect is in the **ה** (He), or the first Spirit, which is the **Empyrean** <note>The highest, most fiery part of heaven.</note> in the Macrocosm, and the intellectual spirit in the Microcosm. This element measures a tenfold dimension; and therefore, just as the number ten is the most simple of all joined numbers, so also the Empyrean Spirit in the world and the intellectual spirit in man is the most simple, subtle, and pure.

Afterward, the **ו** (Vau)—which in numbering denotes unity over the **ה** (He), which is the figure of the number five—designates the **ה** or the ethereal heaven, or the middle, whose Spirit is hidden by the light of Unity. For "Unity placed its tabernacle in the sun," which light or Unity hid with its own radiance and beauty; so that it is not the **ה**, but the Unity within the **ה** forming the **ו** (Vau), which appears in the solar body in the Macrocosm, and also in the arterial blood of the Microcosm, which its redness usually hides. Furthermore, the last or lowest **ה** (He) denotes the lower waters, which the **ו** (Vau) separated from the higher: hence it is said that "it separated the waters from the waters," and in the Microcosm, the animal heaven from the natural, or divine things from earthly things. And this **ה** denotes the number one thousand; just as the **ו** indicates the second place, which is the square of the number ten. But truly, because the number one thousand is denoted by the Hebrews by a large **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, א.</note>, just as Unity is denoted by a small Aleph (whose image is **Jod** in its first composition), it is therefore signified that **יהוה** (**Jehovah**) is truly the **Alpha and Omega** <note>original: *α & ω*; the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, meaning the beginning and the end.</note>—that is, the principle in creation and generation, and the end or the ultimate in corruption and death: which is indeed manifested by this kind of demonstration.

Where **A.** is the beginning of generation; **B.** is the growth of the fetus toward life; **C.** is the vigor, perfection, and middle of human age; **D.** is the decline toward death, which is the final line of things, by which both the Being and essence of the composite return through resolution to that which it was in the beginning. Hence, that ineffable name will stand in this way, with that line reduced into a circle; which is indeed most suitable for the name of the **Tetragrammaton**, insofar as it consists of spherical Elements.

<image-desc>A circular diagram with a dashed vertical line and a dashed horizontal line intersecting at the center. At the top point (C) is the letter א (Aleph). At the bottom point (A) is another א. Point B is on the left horizontal axis, and point D is on the right. Small Hebrew letters ו (Vau) and ה (He) are placed around the circumference and near the central horizontal line. A single dot marks the center of the circle.</image-desc>

Here **A.** or **י** (Jod) denotes the dark **Aleph** insofar as it is the final process of deprivation or resolution, and the bright **א** insofar as it is the origin of generation: for "night is as bright as day to God." By the flow from **A.** to **B.** the rise of life or generation occurs; and from **B.** to **C.** is growth or vegetation; in **B.** is the vigor of life or the "sun at the noon of life"; from **C.** to **D.** is the decline of life; and at point **D.** is death, and from **D.** to **A.** is the dissolution into that which it was in the beginning. So it appears that **Jod** is the **Alpha and Omega** of the circle, insofar as it is that which begins and ends the motion of every created or generated thing.

<margin>1 Kings 19:4</margin>
For the soul or essence passes from the letter **Jod** <note>The first letter of the Tetragrammaton (יהוה), representing the divine spark or the Father.</note> during creation and generation, and after corruption <note>The decay or death of the physical body.</note> it returns once more to **Jod**. For through generation, the soul descends from the unity of matter into a multitude, and through corruption or death, it is released and ascends back into that which it was before—namely, into **Jod**. This seems to agree with that discourse of the Royal Psalmist in Psalm 25:1: *The soul of the righteous is lifted up to God*; and in Psalm 42:3: *The soul says, "When shall I come, that I may appear in the presence of God?"* <note>original: "Anima dicit; quando accedam, ut appaream in conspectu Dei"</note> Similarly, in 1 Kings 19:4, Elijah said: *Now, O Lord, take my soul; for I am no better than my ancestors.* Does not the breath of life also return to the one who breathed it <note>The Creator</note> once its duty is fulfilled? Hence the Wise Man <note>Referring to Solomon in Proverbs 20:27.</note> said that *the soul of man is the lamp of the Lord*. From this, it is necessary that once the compound <note>The human being, composed of body and soul.</note> is dissolved, the divine light returns again to its own proper source, with divine grace assisting, insofar as the world is measured from **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing the number 1.</note> or **Jod** with a cipher <note>The letter Jod represents the number 10, often written as a 1 with a zero (cipher) in Kabbalistic mathematics to show the return to unity.</note> back to the "Great Aleph." Therefore, in a circular dimension, all things have proceeded from God and all things shall return again into God. For God the Father is that "Being in potential," into which gross matter will be spiritualized through dissolution; and the Son is the "essence actually shining," into which the soul, dissolved by sublimation, shall be exalted; and all this shall be done by the power of the loving bond of the fiery Spirit; for in the Spirit we shall live again. This, then, was the beginning of both the **Macrocosm** <note>The "Great World" or universe.</note> and the **Microcosm** <note>The "Little World" or man</note>; and here also shall be the end for both: namely, that "In the beginning was the Word," in which was life; and that shall be the end into which life, as if into its own fountain and origin, shall return. Hence this Word is rightly called in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation.</note> the **Alpha and Omega** <note>original: "α & ω", the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet.</note>, which is the Tree of Life for both the living and the dying; because it has triumphed over death, hell, and the Devil: may His name therefore be blessed forever!

#### CHAPTER I.

->*On the Mysteries of the letters of the name of Adam, and of other names proper to Man.*<-

---

<image-desc>A large square ornamental woodcut initial 'Q' featuring a circular central scene of a figure kneeling in prayer or contemplation within a landscape, surrounded by decorative floral and scrolled motifs.</image-desc>Just as we declared in our treatise on the secondary or physical principles of the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note> that there were three "mothers" of the world as origins—namely, Aleph <note>original: א</note>, or the light hidden in the empty earth or darkness (that is, Existence in potentiality); Mem <note>original: מ</note>, representing the Waters or the created thing in actual existence; and Shin <note>original: ש</note>, which connects both mothers in a triple arrangement by a bond of unity (for Shin <note>original: ש</note> is the hieroglyphic image of the Holy Spirit)—so we also say that the physical principles of the Microcosm <note>The "Little World," referring to the human being as a reflection of the universe.</note> shine forth from the hieroglyphic characters of his name. As for his name, we find it described by three letters of immense depth: namely, Aleph <note>original: א</note>, Daleth <note>original: ד</note>, and Mem <note>original: מ</note>. Let it not seem absurd to the scholars of this world when I say that a great mystery is contained in the names of creatures; for we read that God brought all the animals of the earth and every bird of the air to *Adam* to see what he would call them. And *Adam* himself gave names to all the animals, all the birds of the heavens, and every beast of the earth. From this it is certain that, guided by divine demonstration, he gave names proper to the nature and condition of every living creature. Consequently, since all things received their Being and essence through the Word <note>original: Verbo</note> and through divine "fiery characters" uttered by the mouth of Elohim <note>The Hebrew name for God as Creator.</note>, it must be that the power of every creature was obtained through the holy letters of its name, which contain its very Being. For so it is handed down by David in the Psalms: *The Lord attributed names to every star*; these names truly agreed with their distinct natures. Indeed, the ideal and spiritual characters, which are the true imprints of the life and existence of creatures, are mystically impressed within them. Therefore, the first name given to man, as found in Genesis, is Adam <note>original: אדם</note>, because, as some maintain, he was created from the dust and of the earth. For *Adamah* <note>original: אדמה</note> is properly earth of a red and clay-like color that has been tilled. By this description, it is denoted that man is not "empty" or "untilled" earth, but is filled with the tincture of divine light and the brightness of the Holy Spirit. His mass was a bloody flesh imbued with a fiery and heavenly spirit. For this earth was so <margin><image-desc>A hand-drawn manicule (pointing hand) in the left margin, pointing towards the text regarding the Sephiroth.</image-desc></margin>prepared by the Creator that it received within itself all the virtues and images of all the Sephiroth <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalistic thought through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> through that divine breath of life. Consequently, he was not "earth" in the literal sense, but rather a heaven, or a heaven upon earth—a celestial, super-celestial, and God-like earth. His splendor was so exalted before the Fall and his transgression that all darkness was drowned out by the power of the light, and the body of Adam shone like a Ruby <note>original: Rubini</note>. We derive this also from the characters of his name, as we shall show more extensively below. Therefore, "Adam" <note>original: אדם</note> is the same as a Ruby or a "pyropus" <note>A fire-red gemstone, likely a garnet or ruby.</note>, a precious stone endowed with transparency. The name Adam, meaning "Man," therefore comes from the root *adam*, "to be red" <note>original: אדם</note>; hence *adom* <note>original: אדום</note> means red or ruddy. He received his material substance from the universal created earth, prepared in the clouds; but he received his vivid tincture from heaven, and his "fifth essence" <note>The quintessence or purest element.</note> of reason from the Spirit and breath of God, or from Wisdom—proceeding from Chokhmah <note>original: Hochma; the Sephirah of Wisdom.</note>...

# ON THE SECONDARY PRINCIPLES OF THE MICROCOSM

The second Sephira <note>One of the ten emanations or "countings" in the Kabbalah through which the Divine is revealed.</note> received these; and thus Hermes <note>referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with hermetic philosophy</note> spoke most excellently: *Its father was the Sun, its mother indeed the Moon, and the wind carried it in its belly* <note>original: "Pater eius erat Sol, mater vero Luna, & ventus portavit eum in ventre suo;" a famous line from the Emerald Tablet.</note>. Or, as others assert, the earth was its mother, and heaven its father; but by the power and bond of the divine spirit, a third "one" was produced: namely, that great miracle, the honorable animal called Man, who, as Trismegistus testifies, passes into the nature of God and is, as it were, God himself. And this true Adam is that Microcosm <note>The "Little World," meaning the human being as a reflection of the entire universe.</note>, to whose dominion, because of his excellence, all the beasts of the earth, the birds of the sky, and the plants of the vegetable kingdom are subjected. Thus it follows that this word *Adon* <note>original: אדון</note>, which means "Lord," is understood to apply both to God and to men. 

But, to look more closely at the parts of this name *Adon* <note>original: אדון</note> through a more exact examination—so that from its characters we may finally find its entire nature and disposition, both internal and external—we believe it must first be observed that the Aleph <note>original: א</note> in *Adon* is related to the earth just as it is in *Arats* <note>original: ארץ</note>, which likewise signifies "earth." We mentioned this word earlier when we declared that the Aleph <note>original: א</note> denotes the earth, which was once empty, but is now fertile and radiant by the presence of Aleph <note>original: א</note>, that is, the paternal light. In the name *Adam* <note>original: אדם</note>, however, it argues for the essence of light or the formal perfection of man, by which he is called the son and image of God. And just as this active principle is found at the front of the name, so at the end the Mem <note>original: מ</note> occurs—the hieroglyphic for "Water," or the universal passive substance—representing the spirit receiving the rays emanating from the radiant Aleph. 

For Aleph <note>original: א</note> is the character of the Messiah, or the power of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, or the eternal emanation from the "dark Aleph" <note>Potentiality before creation.</note>, sent out from the potential darkness so that by the act of this Wisdom, all the waters (denoted by Mem <note>original: מ</note>) might be shaped, appearing from the potential power of the radiant spirit. This is the reason why Mem <note>original: מ</note>, insofar as the waters emanated immediately from potentiality into Being, is accepted by some as "the Son." For in the book of Abraham, *The Sefer Yetzirah* <note>original: "De Jetzirah," the Book of Formation, an early Kabbalistic text.</note>, Mem, the second "mother," denotes the second person, or the Son and the Word, insofar as it designates Being proceeding immediately from the power of the dark Aleph. 

But we, in fact, accept Mem for the matter and spirit in which the radiant Aleph (or Wisdom) is carried, and which it carries and moves by its own act, giving life and Being to every part of it. The bond between Aleph and Mem is the power, or that "glue," emanating from the potential Aleph and the essential one, by which both are joined in Daleth <note>original: ד</note>. This denotes a house, or an entrance, or a door through which the breath of the Mem <note>original: מ</note>, or the portion of spiritual water with the divine rays of Aleph (the emanation of manifest unity), penetrates into the earthy mass to form man. Hence the earth is tinted red; and *Adam* <note>original: אדם</note> is rightly called "reddish earth," out of which the rays of the radiant Aleph, penetrating its substance, render it so illuminated that it becomes like *Adem* <note>original: אדס</note>, which is to say, like a precious ruby.

The characters of other Hebrew words signifying man also explain the excellence and divinity of this noblest creature. Thus man is also called *Enosh* <note>original: אנוש</note>, as some would have it, from a "deadly sickness," insofar as it proceeds from the root *anash* <note>original: אנש</note>, meaning "to be sick." But the effect denotes that the matter is far different, since we see this name adorned with many sacrosanct characters, such that it consequently denotes a man most full of divinity. For Aleph <note>original: א</note> argues for the first person in the divinity and Unity itself, and refers in every way to God and the Trinity; Vau <note>original: ו</note> is one of the three spherical letters by which the ineffable Tetragrammaton is expressed, containing within itself He <note>original: ה</note> and Aleph <note>original: א</note> (that is, five and one); Shin <note>original: ש</note> is also the hieroglyphic of the Holy Spirit. 

Thus in this word, Nun <note>original: נ</note> is referred to the Father, Vau <note>original: ו</note> is attributed to the Son, and Shin <note>original: ש</note> is proper to the Holy Spirit; and therefore the intention of this word is to be turned not toward a bad meaning, but the best. This can also be proved in this way: God, by His spirit, is accustomed to attribute names to men that are most proper to their natures—for example, Esau, Jacob, Abraham, and many other Patriarchs. It is proved by the effect that if the name of the Patriarch Enoch <note>The author likely conflates or compares the name Enosh with Enoch here.</note> had denoted ruinous events, he would never have been esteemed as so just and blessed that he never tasted the stings of death and was snatched away by God himself to walk with Him. From this it is clearly enough declared that the characters of this word attributed to man are holy and argue for the divinity of the creature, which we have confirmed by the effect of the Patriarch called by that name. 

Again, men are sometimes called *Methom* <note>original: מתם</note> by the Hebrews; here, his moist and spiritual nature, both super-celestial and physical or mundane, is explained. For the Metaphysical is denoted by He <note>original: ה</note>, adapted to the Holy Spirit; the Physical indeed by Mem <note>original: מ</note>, referred to water and mundane moisture; and Thau <note>original: ת</note> in the middle denotes his opaque body, which is capable of receiving both spirits. For Thau <note>original: ת</note> denotes a visible sign, or the terrestrial character of the species; hence that character was impressed as a sign on the face of Cain. Furthermore, it is said by the Kabbalists themselves that among creatures, there is a symbol of man himself and of human nature, which is the perfection and end of all creatures, just as Thau <note>original: ת</note> is the completion of all the Hebrew elements <note>referring to Thau being the final letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>. *Adam* therefore is man from the aforementioned root *Methom* <note>original: מתם</note>. 

We conclude, therefore, that wherever man turns in the contemplation of the characters of his name, he perceives himself full of divinity and—according to the teaching of the Apostle—he discovers with open eyes that he is the temple of the Holy Spirit, and his members are the receptacle of God and the Word. There are therefore three Mothers by which human nature was created: namely, Aleph <note>original: א</note>, referred to the Word; Mem <note>original: מ</note>, assigned to the spirit (for all things moist and fluid belong to the spirit); and Daleth <note>original: ד</note>, accommodated to the Earth or the dark Aleph,

From this it is clear that Light, spirit or water, and Darkness or earth are the physical principles of the Microcosm <note>The "Little World," a term for a human being viewed as a reflection of the entire universe.</note> itself.

# CHAPTER II.

->On the first principle of Man, which was earth, or darkness.<-

The three supercelestial fathers of both man and the world are found and consist within the dimension of the great name, the Tetragrammaton <note>The sacred four-letter name of God in Hebrew, YHWH.</note>, as was said above; these we have affirmed to be the primary and supercelestial principles of all things. However, the "Mothers" were revealed in the first physical arrangement of both the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe.</note> and the Microcosm. At their command, Darkness—and from it, light and water—were brought forth into the world for its metaphysical and physical perfection. These Mothers are, as it were, passive, insofar as they received the actions or impressions of the fathers—namely Y, H, and W <note>The first three letters of the Tetragrammaton: Yod, He, and Waw.</note>—by which they were made pregnant, each of the three according to her own kind. Therefore, we have called these mothers—namely Aleph, Mem, and Shin <note>The three "Mother Letters" of the Hebrew alphabet in Kabbalistic tradition, representing Air, Water, and Fire.</note>, whose wombs are Darkness, Water, and Light—secondary principles. 

But in place of Aleph <note>associated with Air/Spirit</note>, we find darkness in the world and Daleth <note>The fourth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note> in man; which is also a hieroglyph of eternal wisdom in a dark house. Aleph denotes wisdom uncovered and appearing outwardly; hence it is placed before the word for "face." And Mem <note>The Hebrew letter representing water</note> at the end argues for water or the moist and passive principle. Therefore, we will first discuss the nature of the dark earth, signified by Daleth, which is the first physical principle of man: for God formed Adam from the slime of the earth before he breathed the breath of life into his face. Thus, we shall begin with his earth extracted from the slime of the ground, and then afterward speak of the medium through which the breath passed, and finally of the God-like breath itself floating in that moist medium—words which I hope will be highly relevant to our purpose, though I shall be brief. 

That species of darkness, which was last in the Macrocosm, is first and foremost in the Microcosm; and so it is, as it were, the base and foundation of the entire human structure. It was into this that God, after he had duly prepared it according to his pleasure, breathed his breath of life. By this means, the supercelestial and immortal God willed to fashion man—an earthly God endowed with mortality—from these two principles of differing natures: so that, clothed in slime, he might look about himself keenly, and endowed with the breath of life, he might wisely love divine things. Regarding the reason for this matter—namely, the joining of the celestial nature with the terrestrial for the composition of the Microcosmic machine, and especially why the Divine Mind is enclosed in an opaque body—we have spoken clearly in *Treatise 1, Section 1, Book 7, Chapter 3: On the History of the Microcosm*. Similarly, in *Book 5 of the same Treatise and Section*, we have said much concerning the nature of the human body, what its "earth" was like, and other matters not to be looked down upon. Indeed, I would wish you to read that entire book, as it pertains solely to this subject: the description of the external Microcosm. Concerning this union of the soul with the body, Synesius <note>Synesius of Cyrene (c. 373–414 AD), a philosopher-bishop who wrote on the descent of the soul into matter.</note> sang thus in his Hymns, speaking of the soul or the heaven of man:

> A part also, by a heavy bond, was allotted a terrestrial form; and separated from its parents, it drank in dark oblivion, admiring the unpleasant earth with blind anxieties.

For, as Hermes Trismegistus <note>The legendary sage of the Hermetic tradition.</note> says, the body is like a wall hedging in the soul; and it is also like a matrix, regarding and nourishing all the influences of the ideal Sephiroth <note>The ten divine emanations of the Kabbalah.</note> of its own heaven, no differently than that great earth of the Macrocosm, which is therefore called the mother of all things. Because of the great portion of heaven it receives into itself, it is most rightly called by *Job 4:19* the *house of clay* of the internal man, who has an earthly foundation. And because of the divinity it retains within itself, it is called the temple of God and of the Holy Spirit—just as Christ himself, speaking enigmatically, used the word "temple" for his body in *John 2:21*. Regarding this human principle or base, *Job 16:18* speaks in this sense: *O earth, cover not my blood, and let my cry find no place.* Similarly, the Sage in *Wisdom 9:15* <note>The text cites verse 11, but the quote is from 9:15.</note> speaks of it thus: *The corruptible body weighs down the soul, and the earthly habitation presses down the mind full of many cares, etc.* From this it is clear that the body is like a dark prison of the Microcosmic heaven itself, no differently than we see the heaven of the Macrocosm surrounded on all sides by the darkness of hyle <note>original: "hylæ"; Greek for "matter," specifically the chaotic, unformed substance of the universe.</note>; for beyond the curvature of the heavens, nothing is found except darkness, which extends infinitely beyond the edges of the sky. In this same way, terrestrial darkness covers the heaven or human soul floating in the supercelestial spirit within the celestial medium. These, then, are the shadows that blind the soul and impress upon it the marks of self-oblivion. Hence Job says in *Job 37:19* <note>The text cites 27:19.</note>: *Man cannot, because of his darkness, order his speech with God.* And the Sage in *Ecclesiastes 5:17* says that *a man eats in darkness all the days of his life, and for this reason there is much anger and infirmity in him.* From this comes the unhappiness of man, as shall be said in its proper place below.

ON THE SECONDARY PRINCIPLES OF THE MICROCOSM.

# CHAPTER III.

## *That the human condition is twofold: namely, either from his external part, by which he is called mortal and most vile, or at least from his internal portion, by which he is called immortal, divine, and the very image of the creator himself.*

What the "earth" is, from which the external part of man was fabricated, we have already declared clearly enough in Book 7, Treatise 1, Section 1 of our *Microcosmic History*. Namely, it is the more dreg-like and darker part of the total mass of the waters, from which mass—as St. Peter testifies—both the earth and the heavens came forth. And since the composition of man is partly from that **dead head** <note>original: "capite illo mortuo," an alchemical term referring to the solid residue left over after distillation or sublimation.</note>, or that dreg-like substance left in the center of the **Alembic** <note>An alchemical vessel used for distillation; here used as a metaphor for the crucible of creation.</note> after the subtle was separated from the thick by the power of the universal fire sent by the creator (which portion, by divine preparation, became his external self); and partly from a threefold exalted spirit, each of which excels the other by many degrees in purity and simplicity (which tripartite spirit is known to serve him in place of the triple heavens—namely the Empyrean, the ethereal, and the elemental); it follows, I say, that man sometimes takes his name from his earthly and exterior side, and sometimes claims his name in respect to his interior heaven.

By reason of his external self, he is therefore sometimes called **Flesh**, as can be seen in Psalm 56:5 and 12; and in Psalm 77:39: *Man is flesh, a spirit that goes and does not return.* Sometimes he is called **Mortal**: hence Psalm 144:3: *What is man, that you acknowledge him? The son of a mortal, that you take account of him? Man is like a vanity; his days pass like a shadow.* And in Job 14:1: *Man decays like rot, like a garment eaten by moths; Man born of woman is short of days, and full of trouble.* And Job 25:6: *Man is rot and mortal, and the son of man a worm or a slippery thing.* And in chapter 8:11, he is compared to a rush <note>A wetland plant or reed.</note> which cannot lift itself up without mire. Similarly, Moses seems to assert in Genesis 3 *that insofar as man is dust, to dust he must return.* Sometimes he is called miserable and most abject, as in Job 7:17. And elsewhere in chapter 14: *Man born of woman... is filled with many miseries.* This discourse of Job in 14:5 proves the impurity of man: *Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? Not even one.* That man is also, in this same respect, a more miserable creature than a plant, is told in Job 14:8. Similarly, Job 39:17: *Man is vile, and to be angry with God, or to rebuke him, or to contend with him is the height of madness.* Furthermore, in Ecclesiastes 6:7, the internal man is distinguished from the external in this way: *All the labor of man is for his mouth; and yet his soul is not filled.*

And indeed, this misery and mortality of man came upon him from the darkness of Adam immediately after his transgression and fall; namely, because of his sin. For his body, which was as visible as a **most precious Ruby** before his fall, is now darkened through the lack and loss of light—which in creation was granted to him alone among other animals by the benevolence and mercy of the creator. By that means, what was spiritual has now been left material, gross, and dark; for the Prince of Darkness is powerful there, where darkness powerfully predominates. From here, then, is the origin of the diseases of the body and the disturbances of the vital soul, and finally of death. Hence man, on account of the most wretched condition of his external self, is very frequently called mortal, vile, and subject to the changes of corruption, both by the Philosophers and also by the sacred scriptures.

But truly, insofar as we look upon his internal self, we find him called **Divine**; since in that respect we find him to have been made in the image of God (Genesis 5:1). For, as everything divine is held to be most perfect, so also no man can be called perfect in the absence of **Wisdom**, which is from God, as we find in Wisdom 9:6. For although there is a spirit in every man, it is the inspiration of the Almighty that makes him understand. Hence in Job chapter 33:4 <note>The text cites 33:6, but the quote is from 33:4.</note>, speaking exultantly in these words: *The Spirit of the mighty God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty has given me life.* Because of this divine portion of man, man is called by **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>original: "Mercur. Trismegist." A legendary Hellenistic figure seen as the author of the Hermetic Corpus, which blended philosophy, alchemy, and magic.</note> in *Asclepius* 3: *a great miracle, and a creature to be adored and honored, insofar as he passes into the nature of God.* Furthermore, the same man, in respect to his supercelestial portion, is called immortal and eternal; hence that High Priest <note>Likely referring again to Hermes or a similar sage.</note> breaks forth into these words: *Man (he says) is the third Lord of eternity, as the World is the second, and God himself is the first fountain of eternity.* Similarly, in his *Pimander* 3, he says that Man, among all earthly living things, is judged to be of a **double nature**: mortal indeed because of his body, but immortal because of the substantial man himself. ### CHAPTER IV.

->*Whatever is said in the sacred letters concerning Darkness and Earth, almost all of it can be rightly understood concerning the human body.*<-

In the description of the ideal **Sephiroth** <term>Sephiroth: the ten divine emanations or attributes in Jewish Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</term> of the greater world, and also throughout our entire history of the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm: the "Little World," referring to Man as a reflection of the universe.</term>, I have asserted and constantly maintained—supported by the authority of the most excellent authors—that the Microcosm behaves just as the Macrocosm does. I have maintained that a portion of all parts of the world, taken both in the abstract and the concrete, is found equally in man as in the greater world. Hence the World is called by the Sages "the image of God," and Man the "image of the world," since the ten Sephiroth are the archetypal patterns for the dimensions of both the world and man. From this it follows that in the intellectual world, mention is made of the "land of the living"; concerning which Ezekiel 26 speaks thus: *When I shall have given glory in the land of the living.* And indeed, the Kabbalists maintain that this "land" is contained within the Sephirah **Malchuth** <term>Malchuth: "Kingdom," the tenth and final Sephirah, representing the physical realm and the presence of the divine in the world.</term>, which sends its influences into the sphere of the Moon. And the Archangel <note>likely referring to Archangelus de Burgonovo, a 16th-century commentator on Kabbalistic texts</note> says in his commentary on *Kabbalistic Dogma*: *that the whole garden of paradise, and every true pleasure, is rooted in that most ancient eternal father, the first origin of all; or rather, it is planted in that divine essence, which is the true land of the living, from which all life and all delights and pleasures sprout forth. And the tree of life was in the middle of paradise because the divine Word, which is the true tree of life, is a person in that most holy Trinity; and having put on human flesh, conversing with men, he always held the middle place, being born, dying, and rising again. Therefore, although the garden is planted in the Father, it is also planted in the Son, who receives all things from the father.* These are his words. From these fountains, therefore, as if from the highest Sephiroth, the influences of the land of the living are poured through Malchuth into the sphere destined for it by God the Ordainer. Hence the Word, flowing successively through the Sephiroth, is called the "fountain of life," according to that passage in John: *In the Word was life*; which is also called the "book of life" by David; and in your book all are described under divine images and patterns—that is, in the Sephirotic numbering. But in the real world, we have the earth, which is its center. Yet this is not the land of the living, but of the dying, insofar as it is corrupted and defiled because of the sin of Adam, and for this reason is subject to changes. Finally, in the Microcosm, there was from the beginning a land of the living, in which the power of the Word abounded; but after his fall, the actions of the Word and the Mind within it were obscured and became rarer, involved in darkness and incomprehensible. For Christ was as if crucified within us, and the Soul either slept perpetually, or was sick and delirious, as we read in Iamblichus, Proclus, and Porphyry. For, according to that passage in Wisdom 9—repeated often and never enough—*The body, now made dark, weighs down the soul, and the earthly habitation oppresses the mind*, which is that God-like breath of life breathed into Adam. And to say in a word how things truly are: the entire human fabric, since the fall of Adam, has collapsed into a deformed and lethal dissonance. Hence it is that darkness has dominion over the mass of the body; and consequently, the prince of darkness <note>Satan/Lucifer</note> has a portion of possession in it. For just as the angels of light are stronger in the light, so also the princes of darkness—who are properly called "shunners of light" <note>original: "lucifugi"</note>—become more robust in the darkness itself. ### ON THE SECONDARY PRINCIPLES OF THE MICROCOSM

<margin>Psalm 107:11. Psalm 139:11. Job 17:12 & 28:3. John 1. Job 19:8. Matthew 4:16. Job 37:19. Matthew 6. Genesis 3. Genesis 6:11. Psalm 64:10. Proverbs 5. Psalm 69:35. Psalm 74:2. Psalm 82:5. ...moreover, the body is understood by David in Psalm 107:11, where they are called **deathly shadows** <note>original: "Umbræ lethales"</note>. And that passage in Psalm 139:11 can be understood as referring to the body: *Darkness is not hidden from you.* In the same way, that "earth" which Job (17:12) calls *darkness and the underworld* can be understood as the body because of the iniquity of the flesh. So too in Job 28:3, *God has set a time for darkness*, where "darkness" can refer to the body, to which a span of life is assigned. Likewise, "darkness" is taken to mean the body in that passage from Saint John 1: *That light, which was the life of men, shone in the darkness.* Similarly, in Job 19:8: *He has placed darkness in my paths*, which is to say, the opaque body which weighs down the soul. 

Regarding this "earth," we also understand the passage in Matthew 4:16: *The people walking in darkness* (that is, in the opaque body) *saw a light*; and *to those sitting in the region of the shadow of death, light has dawned.* By the "region of death," the body is understood, because it is mortal; and by "light," the soul or Mind <term>Mens: the higher, divine intellect</term> is understood, which is the human life and light. Furthermore, that passage in Job 37:19 is understood as the body: *For we are wrapped in darkness*; and so it is in many other places. 

Furthermore, "earth" itself is most often related to the human body in the Holy Scriptures. Hence, in the Lord’s Prayer: *Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven*, which means: just as it is in my internal self or spirit (which is the Microcosmic heaven), so let it be in my external self or body (which is the earth of the Microcosm). Thus also that phrase in Genesis 3, *The earth is cursed because of Adam's sin*, can be understood as the body, which is thereby rendered mortal. And Genesis 6:11, *The earth was corrupt before God and filled with violence*, can be understood as the Microcosmic earth <note>The human body as a reflection of the world's physical matter</note>. Indeed, what follows seems to confirm this: *For all flesh had corrupted its way.* 

Likewise, this passage—*You have visited the earth and watered it, and greatly enriched it; you have multiplied it with the river of God full of water*—can be referred to the body. And the Wise Man <note>King Solomon</note> spoke in nearly this sense in Proverbs 5, speaking immediately before of the body: *Drink water from your own cistern and from the flow of your own well; let your fountains be dispersed abroad, and divide your waters in the streets. Keep them for yourself alone, let no strangers share them with you; let your vein be blessed, etc.* All these things he intended to refer to the body by speaking allegorically. Similarly, Psalm 69:35: *The earth shall praise God*; and Psalm 74:2: *The dark places of the earth are full of the cruel and violent*; which can be said as much of the body as of the earth of the Macrocosm <term>Macrocosm: the universe or "great world"</term>. 

Moreover, in Psalm 82:5, it is said that *the foundations of the earth are moved*; which is, by interpretation: "The laws of nature are corrupted, and the body disagrees with its soul." So in Psalm 104:30: *God renews the face of the earth.* This can certainly pertain to the regenerated body. In Job we also read: *O earth, cover not my blood.* In a similar respect, Psalm 104:32 says that *the earth trembles when God looks at it*; this is something that can truly be said of the body, as may be found in many places in the sacred writings. Nay, even as the mundane earth has its poles <note>original: "cardines," literally hinges or axes</note> according to Proverbs 8:26, so also man has his own, as we shall show below. In Genesis 45:18 it is said: *We eat of the fatness of the earth*; which can also be understood as the human earth, insofar as everything in it is nourished by everything else in its proper order. And in Leviticus 25:21, we find that *God alone is the author of the earth's yield and fertility*; this also admits of an interpretation regarding our "earth" <note>our body</note>. And in Deuteronomy 11:17, it is said that *sterility of the earth is brought about because God shuts the heaven*; and this too can be said and pronounced regarding the earth and heaven of the Microcosm. Thus also we could bring forth infinite other passages regarding the relationship of both earths—namely, the Macrocosmic and the Microcosmic. From this, the great friendship, contiguity, and connection which usually exists between both those "earths" will very easily appear to the judgment of a wise person.

### CHAPTER V.

->On the human Element which arises from that physical principle of the Microcosm, namely Earth.<-

**AS** the earth was like the darker dregs and the denser part of the universe of waters, so also the dark, dense, dusky, and gloomy juice is its blood, arising from its own proper vein. This juice, although in its primordial Being and nature it does not differ from the substance of the universal waters, nevertheless carries with it the color and condition of its source. Hence, according to the condition of its "earth" through which it passes, it is found to be either livid, black, or dusky. For, just as universal water is nothing else than a medium participating in the nature of both extremes—namely, darkness and light—so also it is either brighter and clearer if light presides over it, or darker and gloomier if darkness has dominion within it. 

Nor, indeed, is the juice or humor of any condition found in the earth (or human body) anything other than the nature of the "sphere of moisture," which is contained between the source of fire or light and the source of earth or darkness. And, just as we find that in the Macrocosm, earth and fire are two extremes, and the sphere of moisture is a medium participating in both extremes in both its nature and its opposite location, so we also perceive the upper part of that sphere of moisture to participate in the fiery extreme because of its close proximity to it, while the lower part participates in the extreme opposite to it, to which it is observed to approach more closely by natural motion and property of substance. From this it is clear that the nature and substance of the upper portion differ from those of the lower; for the Spirit or moist nature, tending downward, is condensed by the coldness of the earth near it, and is reduced into a thick and visible substance, retaining the cold nature of the earth within itself; but that which floats upward is made subtle by the heat of the fire,

### SECTION I. PORTION II. PART II.

And through that action of fire, it is called invisible, preserving the power of fire within its natural substance through retention. Thus, it is hot on the side of its nearest extreme, and moist by the nature of the middle: for by the mutual action of opposition between one cold extreme and another hot one, a moist intermediate nature is produced, which before the appearance of light and activity was nothing at all in actuality. So also, the lower portion of the moist medium attracts natural coldness from its dark extreme, but humidity from its own sphere. These portions of the sphere of humidity are distinguished by name: the upper is called **Air**, while the lower claims for itself the name of **Specific Water**.

From these points it is clear that one half of the sphere of humidity—namely the lower—is subject to the earth, while the other—namely the upper—is attributed to fire. And this indeed occurs in the same way in the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosmus: man as a "little world" reflecting the universe</term> as it does in the **Macrocosm** <term>Macrocosmus: the great world or universe</term>. In each of these portions, various degrees are found that differ from one another; for that part which clings to the earth itself is dense, thick, muddy, and slimy, participating in the obscurity of its blackest extreme, to which it is neighboring and almost continuous. For the sphere of humidity is like **Mercury**, turning itself toward whatever nature it is applied to. Thus we see in visible water, which turns black by contact with ink or gall-nuts and vitriol, turns white in the company of gypsum, turns red by the mixing of blood or red clay <note>original: "boli"</note>, and turns yellow by the application of saffron; and so it is always fit to receive all impressions, natures, and colors. Similarly, the air is like a **perfume-casket** <note>original: "myrothecium"</note> for all odors, both foul and sweet. 

But at this point it must be carefully observed that the sphere of humidity behaves differently in man than in the world; since, just as the world was made from darkness, water, and light, so man was made from the world. Consequently, it is necessary that the sphere of humidity in him be denser, thicker, and more visible than that of the world. Thus we find **phlegm** <term>pituita: one of the four bodily humors</term> and urine to be thicker than the clear water of the greater world; indeed, we sometimes find them glassy and viscous. And in this way, the substance of the sphere of fire in the Microcosm is also visible, such as **yellow bile** <note>original: "bilis flava"</note> itself.

The reason, therefore, that these elements are not found in so simple a degree as those of the Macrocosm is this: they approach more closely to composition, and are like those imperfectly mixed things called **Meteors** <term>Meteora: in older science, this referred to any atmospheric or transient phenomena, not just falling rocks</term>. In a similar regard, the elements of the lowest region in the greater world differ by one degree of perfection and simplicity from the simplicity of their principles—namely pure light, the primary darkness, and the original water. Therefore, in respect to those principles, they are as if leaning toward composition, and are in the first degree of imperfect mixtures, which is why they are also called "meteors." For a pure and simple element cannot be found in the nature of things; consequently, those things numbered in the elementary heaven are in a way mixed and prone to composition. Yet, the **humoral elements** of man approach one degree closer to composition than those of the world. From this it follows that, just as the elements of the lower world relate to the first physical principles—namely Darkness, Water, and Light—so also do the moist elements of the Microcosm relate to those of the Macrocosm. Consequently, if Earth, the double portion of the sphere of equality, and Fire differ in simplicity from the universal Darkness, Water, and Light—whose characters are **Aleph** א, **Mem** מ, and **Shin** ש <note>These are the "Mother Letters" in Hebrew mysticism, representing Air, Water, and Fire</note>—then surely the humoral elements of man also stand distant in simplicity from those first physical principles by two degrees.

From these things it is clearly evident that, just as Earth, the Sphere of equality, and Fire are derived immediately from those three original principles of nature (as products of the first kind from primary principles), so also are the human **humors** generated from those worldly elements (as from nearby principles), flowing forth as products of the second kind from the first products of the world. And yet, as far as we are concerned, neither the elements in the Macrocosm nor the humors in the Microcosm should be called truly and perfectly "products," insofar as they are only on the way toward perfect composition, and are only in the state of imperfect mixing. Nevertheless, a humor is more "perfected" toward composition than the element from which it arises, yet less "perfect" than the element in respect to the simplicity of the principle from which it descends. Therefore, from condensed air comes **blood**; and yet blood is only at the halfway point toward the perfection of **flesh**.

Just as primary Water was the nearby principle of the air of the lower world, and that air was like the first step of mixing in the formation of blood, so also air is the nearby principle of the sanguine humor itself, which is like the second step of mixing toward the completion of flesh and the other components of the dark body. Hence, blood is called the "nearby cause" of the growth of the body itself, and **semen** <note>original: "sperma"</note>—which is the subtle part of the blood—is the cause of generation; we shall discuss these more broadly below. We say, therefore, that the primary principles are the nearby and closest causes of the sublunary elements (which we have said elsewhere are like the expressions and strainings of the triple darkness propelled from the three heavens during creation), and that those impure elements are the immediate causes of the human humors themselves. From the extract and purer part of these humors comes blood, which is like a "meteor" or imperfect mixture tending toward the goal of the perfection of flesh. But to return to our subject: it is certain that every element is the nearby cause of the humor in man that matches its condition...

# ON THE SECONDARY PRINCIPLES OF THE MICROCOSM

...suitable to its condition, just as it is established that any Macrocosmic principle propagates the element most adapted to its own nature: just as darkness brought forth the earth itself into the nature of things, pure water [brought forth] the sphere of equality, and light within the spirit [brought forth] the element of fire. Whence also the macrocosmic earth generated in man the humor or thick water of **Melancholy** <term>Melancholy: from the Greek 'melas' (black) and 'chole' (bile); traditionally associated with the element of earth</term>, according to its nature—dense, thick, dark, black, or of another condition according to the disposition and color of the "earthly water" from which it arises.

So also the lowest region of the sphere of humidity produced a humor similar to itself in man, called **Pituita** or **Phlegm**; yet the upper orb of that same sphere produced **Blood**, which is nothing other than a chylous <note>original: "chilosus," referring to chyle, the milky fluid drained from food in the intestines</note> fluid reddened by a second concoction <note>In ancient medicine, "concoction" was the process of "cooking" or digesting food into humors via bodily heat</note> and converted into blood by the heat of the hepatic <note>liver</note> fire. For **Yellow Bile** is the offspring of the fiery element, made from parched aerial water, or a portion of the element of fire itself floating in a spirit of a nature compatible with it; of which we shall speak elsewhere in its proper place.

As for the true nature of this Melancholic humor, it must be noted with diligence that it is a mixture made from the immediate substance of the black earth and the lowest portion of the region of water which is contiguous with the earth. The "mineral" or source of this earth is according to the disposition of the seed flowing from such earth, or of nourishment retaining an earthly faculty; the influence of **Saturn**—along with the fixed stars that serve him—concurs in its formation and governance. And this humor produced by the earth and nourished by its star is usually livid, dusky, and dark, approaching the nature of the "slime of the earth" <note>original: "limi terrae," a reference to the biblical material of man's creation in Genesis</note> from which man was corporally made from the beginning.

The second region of the element of water, which passes over that water, is salty (like the sea in the world), and it is formed from the "adustion" <term>Adustion: the "burning" or overheating of a humor, which changes its medical properties</term> of phlegm because of the nature of the salt of the earth arriving by chance. This creates a humor tending partly toward melancholy because of its proximity to the mud and filth of the earth, which is a deeper species of melancholy. Whence also a certain melancholy arises from adust phlegm; and this indeed is a lighter species of melancholy, in which visible darkness and soot do not appear; yet because of the internal heat arising from the saltiness, it denotes the origin of "flatulence" <note>internal winds or gases</note> and the rise of many symptoms. 

And since we see that the earth itself in the Macrocosm is separated from the more liquid and transparent spirit of heaven by the power of light (or divine fire), just as the pure is separated from the impure—so that the earth is, as it were, that blackness and ash left behind after the separation of the celestial nature from the earthly dregs—it follows then that the matter of the bilious humor is reduced by adustion into the consistency of the blackest earth. This is no different than how the substance of a lit coal is left black and dark once the vigor of the fire is removed; but while the fire persists, it is reduced to livid ashes reflecting the nature and color of Saturn. Therefore, Wise Physicians have also found a third nature of the melancholic humor proceeding from **adust bile**, which they have called "scraping" <note>original: "radentem," likely referring to its corrosive or irritating effect on the body's tissues</note>; this indeed is accustomed to bring with it wonderful, or rather horrendous, effects—since sometimes the **Devil** joins himself to it, as will be said in its proper place.

And this is that "forced familiarity" which sometimes occurs through the rotation of the elements, in whose circle the fire is near to the earth. But because there is perpetual war and discord between earth and fire—inasmuch as one acts and the other suffers—it follows quite often that by the first act of fire itself, air is converted into a dense and sharp water, and that water finally into earth or the melancholic humor. For thus blood, by adustion, becomes black and smoky water, or a mud like that of the earth, having within itself the sharp, biting disposition of fire. 

But these "ultimate" melancholic humors, since they are accidental and not natural, we shall omit here, as they exist as manifest "meteors" <note>In this context, "meteors" refers to transient phenomena or disturbances occurring outside the body's normal natural state</note> contrary to nature, by whose presence melancholic diseases are for the most part excited in the body. We shall return instead to that **natural melancholy** arising from the elementary earth, which we say is the mover of the entire human disposition, rendering one's condition such as it is: namely, more fixed, grave, sad, sluggish, ingenious <note>The "melancholic genius" was a common Renaissance idea that this humor, while difficult, led to deep thought and creativity</note>, and slow in actions and works, if we consider the character of the man's soul. 

As for the habit of the body, it renders him livid or leaden-colored; it makes the hair black, plentiful, hard, and not at all curly; the lips pale and large; the tongue leaden; the joints large; the bones great; the face wide; the skin rough-pored; the ears large and hanging; the forehead wrinkled and inclined toward the earth; many hairs on the eyelids; deep-set eyes and a large nose; large teeth like those of horses; a large mouth; the skin of the neck like leather; large hands; large feet with massive joints; wide shins; large knees filled with nerves and veins. Generally, this humor makes the man (whom it naturally rules) have a nervous and veiny body, yet thinned and lean, of a taller stature, a pale color, and skin smelling like a goat. This occurs because of the coldness and dryness of this humor, which it has from the element of earth due to its proximity; indeed, this humor is nothing else than "thin earth," which is "thick and muddy water." Consequently, it is cold and dry in its condition; and yet it is a "humor" insofar as it is water; for the earth itself is nothing other than the densest water, if we give any credit to the opinion of St. Peter, who says clearly that the heaven and the earth were from water from the beginning <note>A reference to 2 Peter 3:5</note>. Nor should our discourse be turned to the intent that anyone should believe that every man's condition is therefore naturally...

SECT. I. PORT. II. PARS II.

...[it is] melancholic, since every human is fashioned from an external earthly substance, drawn from the element of earth itself and prepared by the Creator into a muddy house for the human soul; for sometimes the lower portion of the sphere of moisture holds dominion over the human composition, and then its condition is phlegmatic; but sometimes its upper half presides over the whole structure, and then the blood claims a stronger power within it; similarly, sometimes the sphere of fire will exercise its burning faculty in the composition, and then bile <term>Bile: Also known as choler, the humor associated with fire and a hot, dry temperament</term> will be the Master of that body and its machine. We could indeed report more about this humor; but since the needs of our subject call my pen to other matters, we shall therefore descend to the discourse on the second principle of man.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*Concerning the second principle of Man, which is signified by the Mother, or the character*<-
->*Mem; namely, concerning the Spirit or the human*<-
->*heaven.*<-

Having explained that principle of Man which corresponds to the earth of the world no differently than that earth corresponds to Darkness, and Darkness to the potential character of the small **Aleph א** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, here representing a primal, unmanifested potential</note>; which stands in the same proportion to **Jod** <note>The letter 'Y', often representing the divine spark or seed</note>—which is found in the first place of the number ten (of which it is the image and which it denotes)—as **Jod י** does at the beginning of the fingers <note>original: "primordio digitorum," referring to the base-ten system of counting on the hands</note>, which is the Father of numbers; and this principle of man is signified by the character of its name **Daleth ד** <note>The letter 'D', meaning 'door' or 'gate'</note>, which denotes a house or door, insofar as the body is the house of the divine soul; it follows now that we speak of the second principle of man, namely the moist nature, which is signified by the character **Mem מ** <note>The letter 'M', associated with water (Mayim)</note> in the name of Adam.

This **Mem** stands in relation to the sphere of moisture—indeed, to the universal moist nature elsewhere called by the name of Water (to which **Mem מ** is attributed among the three "Mothers" <term>Mothers: In the Sefer Yetzirah, an ancient Jewish mystical text, the three 'Mother' letters are Aleph, Mem, and Shin, representing the elements of air, water, and fire</term> of the world)—just as the letter **He ה** of the **Tetragrammaton** <term>Tetragrammaton: The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH</term> relates to it, like a Father to a Mother. And indeed, the character of the element **Mem מ** is rightly attributed to the heaven of both the Microcosm <note>Man, viewed as a "little world"</note> and the Macrocosm <note>The Universe, or "great world"</note>, insofar as the heaven of the Microcosm contains within itself a portion of every Macrocosmic heaven: For his intellectual and rational spirit corresponds to the proportion of the Empyrean heaven <note>The highest, most spiritual heaven of pure light and fire</note>, the vital spirit is referred to the ethereal heaven, and the natural spirit, which looks toward the sublunary <note>below the moon</note> sphere of moisture, is seen by its nature to equal the elemental spirit.

Consequently, the same Cabalistic Mother, namely **Mem מ**, is attributed to the spiritual composition of the Microcosm. For, as we have clearly demonstrated elsewhere, every spirit is of the nature of water; indeed, the sacred scriptures indicate to us that the uncreated spirit rules over the waters, saying that the spirit of **Elohim** <note>God</note> was moved over the waters, or acted upon the waters, no differently than a male upon a female: to which active spirit the character **He ה** of the Tetragrammaton is assigned. For it is necessary that the father acts upon the mother to procreate things in the world, both the great and the small.

This portion of man is therefore his heaven, or internal portion; by virtue of whose act man is called immortal and a divine animal, just as by reason of his internal part being defiled by filth and darkness he has acquired the marks of disturbances and diseases and the name of mortality. And yet, through the conjunction and proximity of the lowest portion of the human heaven with the mass of darkness, the whole lower mass of the nature of moisture is disturbed, infested by darkness, and subject to changes, and sometimes affects the entire Microcosmic spirit with restlessness, since it is founded upon that mass as its base.

Indeed, just as the **Evil Demon** <note>original: "Cacodæmon"</note> has power in the lowest region of the world by divine permission, malevolently agitating at times the winds, the air, the clouds, storms, and visible waters, so too the **Devil** sometimes enters the lowest region of the human heaven and is accustomed to disturb the entire machine of the Microcosm, as not only the sacred scriptures teach us, but also the authorities of other trustworthy authors and daily experience itself provide certain faith in this matter. But in truth, just as wicked demons have no power over the matter of the ethereal heaven—since it is too pure and excellently purged of all defilement of darkness—so also they can have no force or power over the moist spirit corresponding to life; so that, although their rage may be impetuous in the lower heaven of man, it cannot harm his life. Hence God said to Satan: *Behold, he is in your hand, but save his life;* <note>Job 2:6. The author interprets "life" or "soul" here as the higher ethereal spirit</note> that is, the body and that airy spirit by which the body and the material composition are nourished are in your hand, so that they are in your power; but the ethereal spirit, which is the receptacle of life, shall not be permitted to you, that you may touch it.

Thus also we read that an evil spirit from God vexed Saul; yet it could not destroy his life, because its power in no way extended into the ethereal region. Nor was the unclean spirit able to affect the soul of the **Demoniac**—that is, the vital spirit—even though its name was **Legion**, indicating the strength or union of many Demons; but nevertheless it so vexed the lowest spirit of that man, and agitated the body nourished by that spirit in such a furious manner, that *no one could bind him with chains,* as we can read in Mark 5:2. Concerning this [power] of the Devil...

[Header: Concerning the Secondary Principles of the Microcosm]

We shall make broader mention of the human spirit’s dominion elsewhere, where we will treat the metaphysical causes of diseases. Indeed, we distinguish this Microcosmic <note>Microcosm: The "Little World," a philosophical concept viewing the human being as a miniature reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note> heaven into three regions or kingdoms, according to the order of that Macrocosm. In the highest of these, the **Mind**, like the supreme emperor of the entire watery empire, is accustomed to reign and stand above; in the middle, however, that **solar light** dominates, providing life to the Microcosm in its own proper Spirit; and over the lowest or aerial region, the **sublunary fire** presides. This fire, receiving the soul from the higher kingdoms, governs the lower "gross spirit"—both the visible and invisible—at its command. For fire is the primary receptacle in the lowest region for all superior influences, by whose powers and actions the fire itself and all lower things are driven and moved by natural motion. Thus, it is certain that in the lowest Spirit of the Microcosm, **Bile** acts within the fiery nature, and finally, celestial power acts through fire in the aerial region upon the moist nature of a thicker and lower order; this action is properly called the **natural faculty**, which has its dwelling in the fountain of the **liver**. In this region, therefore, this Spirit is observed to incline toward passions and changes—either toward generation through "spermatic meteors" or toward corruption and destruction through "putrid meteors" <note>Meteors: In this historical context, "meteors" refers to any atmospheric or bodily phenomena (like rain, wind, or vapors), not just space rocks.</note>. This occurs both because the Spirit cannot satisfy the natural appetite due to a defect of native heat, and also because malignant spirits are found to be stronger in this portion of the heaven than in the higher ones, due to their proximity to the place or seat of darkness.

# Chapter VII.

## Concerning the human element, or the double portion of the sphere of moisture, which arises from the thicker and denser part of this principle, which is Mem.

From the thicker part of this moist principle arises that **human element** which Physicians are accustomed to call **phlegm** or **pituita**; it is, as it were, the foundation of the entire principle of **Mem** <note>original: "Mem," the Hebrew letter מ, traditionally associated with Water in Hermetic and Qabalistic philosophy.</note>, or the universal Spirit of the Microcosm. But truly, because we asserted in our preceding discourse that in the lowest world that sphere of moisture is twofold—namely, either the supreme portion, which participates in the element of fire (by virtue of which subtle action it is invisible and called **air**), or that lowest portion, which tastes of an earthly disposition and has become apparent and visible due to its condensing and gathering faculty (which it derives from cold) and is distinguished by the name of **water**—so also, for the same reasons, the spiritual part of the lower heaven of man (that is, the sphere of its equality) is divided into two portions. One is more dense and visible, which is either **chyle** <term>Chyle: A milky fluid produced in the intestines from digested food, once thought to be the precursor to blood.</term> or is called **pituita** or **phlegm**; because of its weight, this tends more downward. The other is called **flatus** <note>original: "flatus," meaning wind or gas.</note>; it is either a hot and moist vapor, which for the most part gathers into superfluous drops in the brain or is converted into necessary and healthful humor for the maintenance and nutrition of the body; or it is a hot and dry exhalation, which because of its dryness is not usually gathered into sensible liquid (or at least very rarely), but is driven hither and thither in the body in the manner of a wind.

And just as we see in the Macrocosm that the visible part of the sphere of moisture, which we call clear water, is distinguished into three regions differing in nature—namely, into **clouds and mists** (which are exalted "meteors"), and into **fresh water** (which is either May-dew or falls from the mountains, from which springs usually flow), and into **salt water** (which is contained in the sea or within its limits)—so also we say that there are three distinct differences in the visible part of the human sphere of moisture. 

The first of these, which we compare to the substance of mists or clouds, is that **chylous substance** which is drawn out from foods and drier nourishment by the virtue of the **stomach** (which we can not inaptly relate to the lowest region of the air). And just as we see that vaporous air—collected from the aqueous and earthly substance of the Macrocosm through refinement partly in the lowest and partly in the highest region of the air—is converted into a mist or a small cloud, which by the natural motion of the planets and elements passes into the nutrition of other creatures, or in an invisible way by congealing itself turns into dew or visible rain, falling down to the earth and sea; so also that moist smoke or vapor, leaping out from the moist nature of foods in the ventricle or stomach by **antiperistasis** <note>Antiperistasis: A philosophical concept where a quality (like heat) is intensified when surrounded by its opposite (cold).</note>—that is, by reason of the surrounding heat of the neighboring parts, namely the liver and viscera—is circulated and sublimated so many times until it passes into a chylous substance. That is, it is reduced into a substance like a small white cloud or mist, which finally, in an almost imperceptible manner, usually penetrates through the **mesenteric veins** <note>original: "meseraicas venas," the veins draining the intestines.</note> to the cavity of the liver, as if by **diapedesis** <term>Diapedesis: The passage of fluid or cells through the walls of a vessel; here used to describe how nutrients "sweat" through the veins to the liver.</term> and transudation, or in the form of a thicker vapor. 

Thus we see a vanishing mist leave behind it droplets of dew on the grass and herbs as evidence of its condensed substance, by which the herbs and plants are afterward refreshed and increased. In this same way, by the operation of the liver and the attractive power of the veins, the entire **human plant** is irrigated and nourished. But if by chance the mesenteric veins are obstructed, and the full passage of the chyle to the liver is hindered, and a natural heat more intense than average is excited, then that vapor, in its excessive circulation...
