# SECTION I. PORTION II. PART III.

...is not granted to one gazing only with the eyes of the Sun <note>The physical eyes or outward sight.</note>, but only to him who is accustomed to beholding the internal nature of a thing with the eyes of the intellect. For what is seen in the **sperm** is that lower **spirit** which is the foundation of the soul; it is no less obvious to the eyes through its condensation than a visible cloud or mist, which was previously invisible air. And this visible spirit is, as it were, the foundation of the body or the external man, and the medium of all those <term>meteors<note>In this context, "meteors" refers to any transitional, "imperfectly mixed" substance like vapors, clouds, or bodily fluids, rather than space rocks.</note></term> which are accustomed to arise in the human body. **Hermes** <note>Refers to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure associated with the *Hermetica*.</note> narrated all of this most exactly in the 10th book of the *Pimander* in these words: *Reason is in the soul, the soul is in the spirit, and the spirit, diffused through the veins, arteries, and blood, moves the living creature in every part.* <note>Original Latin: "Ratio in anima, anima in spiritu, & spiritus in corpore..."</note> Therefore, by the virtue of this lower spirit, water is quickened and moved because of its unbreakable bond with the air; and finally, the earth moves immovably in the center of all things because of its proximity to the water. The permanent Mind, as the prime mover, moves the intellectual spirit; thus animated, it drives the middle soul, by whose motion the lowest spirit is incited. This spirit is finally observed to propel the humors—both the invisible flatulent and vaporous ones, as well as the four visible ones—whether they exist in the body naturally or unnaturally. And this motion stands forth as much in creation as in generation, and in growth as much as in diminution and corruption. Just as the motion of nature always tends toward perfection (moving from multiplicity into simplicity) or toward complete composition (moving from simples into multiplicity), so too must a medium always be required that participates in some way in both extremes—though in an imperfect manner and ratio, since it regards the number two <note>The "binary" or duality, representing the fall from unity into division.</note>.

However, as far as the elements of both worlds are concerned, they themselves—insofar as they are not "simples"—can be recounted among the number of imperfect mixtures or "meteors." For in the **Macrocosm** <note>The universe or "Great World."</note>, we judge the primary darkness reflected at the center to be the true element of **Earth**, expressed by the **Cabalists** through the letter **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, א.</note>. We hold the purified Waters—extracted from that darkness by divine alchemy from the beginning, being as subtle and spiritual (or airy) as they are gross and more visible—to be the true species of moisture, signified under the hieroglyphics of **Mem מ**. And we repute the sincere Light created on the first day to be the only pure **Fire** in this world, which the Cabalists noted by the hieroglyphic **Shin ש**. But truly, since the common elements depart from this kind of simplicity and purity because of a greater or lesser mixing of one with another, we therefore consider them in the place of "imperfect mixtures" or "meteors," insofar as they have exceeded the degree of simplicity and have, in some way, looked toward any composition. Thus, this earth of ours is mixed with heterogeneous parts, which in its creation was, as it were, identical and homogeneous. The element of **Water** is polluted by fragments of earth; indeed, it is even subjected at times to the assaults of fire, as may be seen in thunder. Pure fire is found nowhere. Almost all the principles of the world appear to us to be confused and imperfectly mixed, and one element seems to yearn to rotate into the nature of another, until that which was finally separated by corruption is reduced back into a terrestrial body. It is observed to retreat and return to what it was before, hastening through the steps required for dissolution. And so, the **head is said to eat its own tail** <note>A reference to the Ouroboros, the snake eating its own tail, symbolizing the cyclical nature of the universe.</note>, and a spherical motion—from the starting point to the end point, and from that point back again to the start (which is indeed the circular course of the world or nature toward generation and corruption)—is always observed to act in the world.

What else should be thought of the human elements than that they are removed further from purity than those of the world, and consequently should be held as "imperfectly mixed," approaching more closely to composition and being nearer to the nature of "meteors"? This is to be understood as much in the elements of generation as in those of nutrition. For, to begin first with those of human generation: we see that in its beginning, the **human sperm** applies form to the compound and even establishes the foundations of the matter of the external man. However, the internal man (whose basis is the condensed aery spirit or the visible matter of the sperm), attracting to himself something similar from the regions of the heavens by a magnetic faculty, extends the visible spirit of the sperm which carries and contains him. Thus, he gives life to his visible vehicle, by which he also draws similar air to himself. From this, the air—continually attracted to the exterior mass—is condensed into a clearly aqueous humor called **pituita** <note>Phlegm or mucus.</note> due to the rawness and coldness of the external and mundane air. Finally, by a greater or lesser earthly dryness, it is reduced into a fleshy, nervous, cartilaginous, or bony substance. We say, therefore, that the sperm was the first stage of generative meteorology, mixed from an aery and ethereal (or fiery) spirit. The second was the cooked *pituita*, which is **blood**, or the raw kind, which is called **phlegm**. In this imperfect mixture, the element verges more and more toward the medium of perfection, which is the body. Thus, blood is an imperfect state of mixing in generation—namely, between the visible sperm (the starting point) and the human body. It is also the medium in the nutrition of the offspring between **chyle** <note>The milky fluid produced during digestion.</note> and flesh: since from chyle arises blood (which is chyle cooked a second time), and from the third "breathing upon" the blood—namely, its union, assimilation, and coagulation—comes flesh and those things which are derived from and nourished by flesh. That the sperm is, as it were, a "meteor" and an imperfectly mixed mass is clear, because it is not a simple element by itself, nor a perfectly composed thing already generated, but a thing risen from simple elements and moving on the path toward generation. Thus, indeed, we see that in the cloud of the greater world, the poten- <note>Catchword: poten- (likely "potentia," meaning power or potentiality).</note>

### CONCERNING THE TERTIARY PRINCIPLES.

In it resides the generative and spermatic power of all plants, according to that which is written in <note>original: "Exod. 11. 14. & 28. 23. & 29. 23. Psalm. 68. 10. Iob. 5. 10. & alibi"</note> *Exodus 11:14 & 28:23 & 29:23, Psalm 68:10, Job 5:10, and elsewhere.* This cloud exists in the Great World <note>The Macrocosm or Universe.</note> just as **sperm** does in the Lesser World <note>The Microcosm or Human Body.</note>, since both are nothing other than condensed air. Such also is that "thick water" made from mixed **quicksilver** <term>Mercury<note>In alchemical thought, Mercury represents the principle of liquidity and volatility, while Sulfur represents heat and combustion.</note></term> and **sulfur**, from which—as from an imperfect mixture or proximate cause—metallic composition is made.

It must therefore be diligently understood that **sperm** in an animal, **seed** or grain in a plant, and indeed even the **cloud** itself (which is the more remote cause of plants), and the "thick water" (which is the mother of metals), are nothing other than **Sulphur** more or less proportioned within its own **Mercury**. These two, when mixed, are nothing besides a <term>meteor<note>In this context, a "meteor" is an "imperfect mixture"—a substance like a vapor or fluid that is caught in transition between pure elements and solid matter.</note></term> or an imperfect mixture; that is, something sublimated between the thick compound toward which it tends, and the thinnest simple elements from which it is derived. But now, to return to the "meteors" of nutrition and growth, both remote and proximate: we say that **chyle** <note>The milky fluid of digested food produced in the stomach.</note> in the stomach relates to the Microcosm just as a **cloud** does in the belly of the Macrocosm. And as we see from experience, a cloud is made of a greater quantity of water with smaller amounts of fire, earth, and aerial spirit—as can be seen in a thundercloud, which contains stone, lightning, and a wondrous spirit. In the same way, chyle potentially contains earthy **melancholy** (both natural and unnatural), and likewise **bile**, and finally true and exquisite **blood**. All of these are covered and submerged by the multitude of waters occupying the place of chyle or <term>phlegm<note>Latin: "pituita".</note></term>. Thus, by a stronger digestion, this entire mass is transmuted into red blood, which we also sometimes see happen in the cloud itself in the aerial sky. Furthermore, we are taught how by divine power water can be converted into blood in *Psalm 105:29.* Within this mass also reside wind, flatulence, and vapor, which are very easily drawn out from its belly when excited by animal heat.

Finally, through the animal's second digestion, these animal elements are separated from one another: **choler** (or yellow bile), showing a fiery nature, is poured into the gallbladder; **melancholy** (or black bile) is drawn from elsewhere; and **phlegm** (or the more serous part) penetrates to the kidneys; while the **blood**, not yet purely purged, waters the entire body through the rivulets of the veins. Here it is clearly evident that each of these humors are not simple elements, but mixtures of a "secondary condition," derived from those worldly elements which, in the first stage of mixing, departed from the true simplicity of the elements. Hence, although in an animal **bile** is compared to the element of fire, this is not because it is a simple element, but insofar as it participates more in the nature of fire. For its basis is a watery humor made subtle by the quality of fire, in which it abounds; its form, however, is a fiery substance floating in dense air as its own proper vehicle. From this it is clear that the mixture of this humor is most imperfect, and consequently it is held to be in the place of a fiery or "shining" cloud. Just as the presence of such clouds usually produces natural effects in the world and promises pleasant weather, so too this element produces great benefits for the body and its health. But truly, sometimes it behaves like lightning, flashes, comets, and other such "fiery meteors" that affect bodies poorly. Sometimes it even tints the face of the sky with redness and yellowness, promising a future commotion of the air and the excitation of winds—just as this bilious fire, if impeded in its natural motion, is accustomed to tint the skin and surface of the body with a foul **jaundice** <note>original: "icteritia"</note>, and to stir up flatulence and disturbances within it, and other such things. And here we wish the Reader to be informed that, just as the element of fire in its contracted substance produces visible meteors in the world—for example, comets, lightning, flashes, "torches," "leaping goats" <note>An ancient term for a type of streaking or jumping atmospheric fire.</note>, *ignes fatui* <note>Will-o'-the-wisps or "fool's fires."</note>, etc.—so too the bile, when preternaturally affected in the body, produces "meteors" of a condition and color such as itself. For example: inflammations, jaundice, **rosacea** <note>original: "guttam rosaceam"</note>, **dysentery**, etc. Similarly, just as the invisible substance of the element of fire, when contracted into the visible mass of a comet or another such visible meteor, is accustomed to generate "invisible meteors" in the air—by which not only is the air itself infected, but also plants are poorly affected, animals are seized by plague, famine is produced in the land, and infinite other inconveniences arise in the world—in exactly the same way, the matter holds for "invisible meteors" exhaled from this malevolently disposed visible meteor in the body of the microcosm: namely, plagues, fevers of every kind, **smallpox**, **pneumonia** <note>original: "Peripneumonia"</note>, **pleurisy**, and infinite other such accidents. This same thing can be said regarding the effects of **Melancholy** operating preternaturally, both manifest and occult; and also regarding those of **Phlegm** and poorly mixed **Blood**. When these are ill-disposed, both with contagious or corrupting vapors and by their manifest substance and quality, wretched illnesses are accustomed to be produced in the world, just as can be seen from the poisonous disposition of the earth and waters in certain places of the world. Furthermore, beyond what was said above, it appears that the elements which are now found are impure and removed from their primary natures, since the Elements in their simplicity consist of portions of water and light, such that the lower two (insofar as they abound less in light) are called passive, while the higher two are active. So also is the substance of the heavens, for the substance of the ethereal heaven is made from the substance of the Empyrean heaven which serves as its place and is called **Mittaton** <note>Likely referring to the archangel Metatron, often associated in Kabbalistic and Hermetic thought with the "Soul of the World" (Anima Mundi) or the governor of the celestial spheres.</note> or the **Soul of the World**; its passive part, however, is the middle portion of simple waters without respect to its composition with any form.

SECTION I. PORTION II. PART III.

Then, descending further downward, the substance of the middle heaven is, as it were, the **form** of the substance of the waters of the lowest heaven, which is the bottom-most part of the spirit or universal water. From this it is clear that just as the form of the upper water is most pure—insofar as it is derived immediately from the presence of God and is **uncreated light**—so the form or light of the ethereal or middle heaven is less pure. This is because it is nothing other than **created light**, or the purest spirit of the higher heaven adorned with the rays of uncreated light. This light acts upon the watery substance of the middle heaven just as a male acts with a female. Similarly, the form of the elemental heaven is composed of the substance of the **Empyrean heaven** <note>The highest, most spiritual heaven, associated with pure fire and the dwelling place of God.</note> and its form, along with the thicker substance of the middle heaven. All of these serve as its "form." Finally, it is composed of its own dense substance which, in respect to that same form, is distinguished into the four elements or three spheres: namely Fire, Air, Water, and Earth; or the spheres of fire, humidity, and earth. Thus, it is rightly said by the Philosophers that the heaven acts upon the passive elements—whose matrix is the earth itself—no differently than a **cock acts upon a hen**, or a male upon a female.

We see, therefore, according to what has been said, that the entire **worldly spirit** <note>original: "spiritus mundanus"</note> can be called an "imperfect mixture" in relation to the body composed of the four elements. However, in reality, the substance of the Empyrean heaven is most perfectly mixed within itself from the light of the first emanation and its own simplest substance. The substance of the middle heaven is less perfectly mixed, and that of the elements is the least mixed of all. For the deeper the light is truly immersed into the **dark abyss**, the more imperfect and multiform is its union within the mixture. Yet, by "imperfect mixture," the Philosophers mean that which is on the way toward a complete composition of the four elements, but has not yet reached the goal of perfection in its composition.

The elements, therefore, for the reasons alleged above, are "mixed" insofar as their form is derived from the double substance of the two higher heavens and a portion of the simplest light. This mixture is called "imperfect" because it has not yet reached the midpoint of the completion of a composed body, whether that body be created or generated. Thus, the Elements are called "simple" by the Philosophers, not because they equal the purity of the Empyrean or Ethereal substance, but insofar as they are considered simpler than sublunary <note>Objects or substances existing below the moon, in the terrestrial realm.</note> things. And yet, these things I say concerning the Empyrean, Ethereal, and elemental heavens I do not conceive in the common way. For all these substances are also present upon the earth. We do not say a Bishop is "sublimated" or "elevated into the atmosphere" <note>original: "meteorizatum"</note> in the way the common people do, expecting him to be in the higher places of the worldly heavens; rather, we understand him to be exalted in **dignity and honor**, even though he always maintains the same distance upon the earth. In the same way, impure lead passes into the perfection of gold through the length of time and is "sublimated," yet it is nonetheless not raised from its place. 

But returning to the matter: in respect to the universal substance of the heavens, the lower or sublunary Elements can be called "imperfectly mixed" even when considered as compositions in themselves, but they are said to be mixed in the **first degree**. **Meteors** <term>imperfect mixtures<note>In Renaissance science, "meteors" included all atmospheric phenomena like rain, wind, lightning, and comets, viewed as substances in a state of transition.</note></term> are called "imperfect mixtures of the second order" because they are in the middle between the elements (to which the first degree of the starting point is attributed) and the fully elementalized compound. Thus, when the substance of the lower worldly spirit is set on fire—that is, when a portion of the element of fire passes into the air—comets and other fiery meteors are produced by this double substance, such as "leaping goats" <note>A historical term for a type of streaking atmospheric light or fire.</note>, falling stars, lightning flashes, and so on. If a portion of it is enveloped with water, thunder and lightning-bolts are produced by this double mixture. In this process, the active force in the air is the ignited spirit of the sphere of fire, and the moisture of the air is the passive part; or, the water of a cloud undergoes the actions of both air and fire. From this, the **Mercurial spirit** <note>The volatile, fluid principle that acts as a bridge between spirit and matter.</note> drawn from the air acts as the vehicle for the fiery light, from which both the matter and the form of the lightning-bolt are derived.

### CHAPTER V.

-> *Concerning the various degrees of meteors, or imperfect mixtures, before reaching the completion of composition: And that the first degree is the immediate cause of the following degree.* <-

As has been said and declared in the preceding parts, the substance of the Empyrean heaven is the true soul of the middle heaven, and again, its substance is the soul of the lowest heaven. The origin of them all is **Unity in God**. Likewise, every preceding meteor is, as it were, the soul and life of the one immediately following it on the path toward a perfect mixture. The origin of all these is the "point of departure," or that simple element from which it is derived and from which it receives its name and primary being. For example, in a fiery meteor, we see that the first principle is the pure element of fire. Then, the second degree is the "spiritual element" or the first degree of mixing, which is commonly called the "element of fire"—for a pure element can hardly be extracted or even conceived in the nature of things by the human mind. Then the third degree is a thicker mixture of dense air with fire, and it becomes a visible comet or some other meteor of this kind. Finally, by expanding itself, it proceeds and penetrates into more sensible elements, such as water and earth. If it tends toward corruption, it affects things with evil, disease, and the worst events; if it tends toward generation, it proceeds toward the perfection of composition in a life-giving and benevolent way. The first degree of an incomplete mixture is 2, which is found between 1 and 3; it denotes the mixture of the purest heaven in the world and the **intellectual spirit** in man. But because it proceeds further toward the deepest composition (which consists in the cube), we move to a still more evident degree of composition: then the starting point is 2, the goal is 4, and the middle or "imperfectly mixed" state is 3. For such is the relationship of the substance of the highest heaven to that of the stars in the **macrocosm** <note>The great world or universe.</note>, and of the rational spirit to the vital spirit in the **microcosm** <note>The small world or human being.</note>. 

Afterward, 5 intervenes between 4 and 6, and 6 between 5 and 7. But the most manifest middle between 4 and 8 (that is, the square and its cube) is 6. This is the state in the greater world (the elemental heaven) of the aerial "meteors" between the four elements and completely composed bodies; and in the lesser world, it represents the natural humors in relation to the flesh, or the most perfect composition of the fleshy body. This movement consists in the natural faculty of man, in which the lowest portion of the human soul—namely the aerial spirit—predominates. To this spirit, the humors (whether they are natural or contrary to nature) are linked, just as water is to air, air to fire, or earth to water, by this "glue" of nature. 

But if the humors are natural, then it proceeds exactly toward generation from 1 (that is, from 2 to 8). Therefore, the **Unity** <note>The number 1.</note> in the world denotes simple **form** without consideration of matter; and 2 indicates **matter** without the addition of form, yet it indicates that God has descended into a "moist nature." 3 indicates the link of matter with the first form in its genus, denoting a heavenly condition. 4 declares the universal matter of the world distributed into the four elements by a formal presence; this is nearly the halfway point to composition and the true starting point from which imperfectly mixed elements immediately arise. 

From these, the worldly "meteors" are derived in the number five, which is the complete midpoint in generation (between 2 and 8). In the "meteor" of 5, it is more fiery and subtle; in 6, it is more aerial. Therefore, 6 is also the middle between the square and the cube, the place where—as if in their own proper vehicle—the "meteors" are born in both the macrocosm and microcosm. 7 indicates the life-giving water in the world (the water of the clouds), and in the microcosm, the blood of the **chyle** <note>A milky fluid of fat and lymph formed during digestion.</note> which is the "meteor" of nutrition, or the sperm, which is the "proximate meteor" in generation.

# SECTION I. PORTION II. PART III.

If the female element is added, an "imperfect" mixture is created. This is the closest cause for the perfect composition of a fetus, marked by the final stage of generation, which matches the perfection of a complete cube. Thus, a path is mapped out through degrees of perfection found at the extremes: one is the degree of perfect simplicity (namely, 1), and the other is perfect composition (namely, 8), which is the final boundary of generation. In this entire progression, the "meteors" <note>In 17th-century science, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena (rain, wind, lightning) as well as the shifting fluids or "humors" within the human body.</note> of both the **Macrocosm** <note>The Great World or Universe.</note> and the **Microcosm** <note>The "Little World" or the Human Being.</note> are natural and produced through the process of generation. 

However, if those meteorological humors—or imperfectly mixed substances—behave "preternaturally" <note>Against the normal course of nature; abnormally.</note> toward the composition, then they certainly tend toward corruption. Through dissolution, they strive to return to their own root by the same means, but now arranged in a contrary manner. Thus, the perfect composite (8) is first resolved back into 7, and 7 into 6, 6 into 5, 5 into 4, and so on, moving backward until the entire composition is reduced again to the root from which it was first derived.

The reason for these different actions in nature arises from the disposition of **Unity** <note>Referring to God as the "One" or the Monad.</note>. For the completion of generation occurs by the emission of His rays and the manifestation of His act; but when those rays contract back into Himself, a regression occurs—moving from generation through disturbance toward the diminishing and weakening of the composite—returning to the boundary from which the progression began. This is confirmed perfectly by the words of the Royal Psalmist, which are as follows: ***Psalm 104:28-29.***

> *When God gives to the creatures, they gather (here he includes the order of creation and generation); when He opens His hand, they are satisfied with good (here he seems to prove the reason for the nutrition and preservation of the composite, both internal and external). When He hides His face, they are troubled (here he denotes the occasion of sickness and infirmity, or the movement toward corruption and against the nature of the composite); when He takes away their spirit, they die (here he tells the reason for the completion of death and corruption, and by "spirit" he argues for the root or the **radical moisture** of life <term>Radical moisture: a vital fluid thought by early physicians to be the fuel for the "lamp" of life</term> into which the divine light moved to achieve the perfection of life).*

What could be clearer or more effective than these words of the Prophet to confirm our doctrine—namely, the progression toward generation and the regression toward corruption? Hence, **Job** said (10:12): *You have granted me life and favor, and your visitation has preserved my spirit.*

Therefore, the shining favor of the face of **Jehovah** concurs in the generation of the spirit proper to it, in which it moves as if in a vehicle. This is the same as what the Psalmist says in *Psalm 30:6*: *Life is in the favor of Jehovah.* And *Psalm 90:14*: *Life's prolongation is the favor of God.* And *Psalm 18:29*: *If you light my lamp, O Jehovah my God, you will make my darkness shine.* Similarly, in *Psalm 31:17*: *Let your face shine upon your servant; save me in your favor.* In countless other places in the sacred letters, it is argued that God—the most absolute simplicity, purity, and unity—is that unique Sun giving life, grace, and glory to creatures. In His absence, nothing but miseries, diseases, and death are to be expected, according to *Job 30:26*: *When I looked for light, then came darkness.* <note>original: "Lucem speranti mihi evenit caligo"</note> His presence, however, brings inexplicable joy with it, according to *Psalm 4:7*: *The light of Jehovah’s face has put more joy in my heart, etc.* And *Psalm 106*: *He whom Jehovah visits with His salvation shall enjoy the good and happiness of His chosen ones, so that he may rejoice with the gladness of His nation.*

We conclude, therefore, that the root of generation is 2, its square is 4, and its cube is 8. The first meteorological stage (or the stage of "imperfect mixture" that is visible to the senses) must start from 4 (the elements) and is observed in the fifth order, which holds the middle position between the root 2 and the cube 8. We conclude also that 1 (the simplest) is the first act and mover in both creation and generation; it urges the entire mundane spirit toward the completion of the creature's composition, and is present to inform that spirit for such a work and to preserve it according to its species. Hence, by its absence, the perfection of the composition falls away and is reduced, as it were, to nothing. 

Indeed, we consider it most worthy of note that God is said to put on as many "garments" in the world as there are units He penetrates. Since He looks toward the composition of the earthly creature through the cubic number (eight), there are also as many degrees of "moist nature" attributed to Him as He willed to penetrate to complete the composition. 

1. His first garment (namely, 2) is the nature of the purest heaven, which is called the **Empyrean** <note>The highest, most spiritual part of heaven, associated with pure light and fire.</note>; this garment is called **Light**. Hence it is said in *Psalm 104:2*: *That light is the cloak or garment of God.* 
2. The second is 3, or the **Sun**, which is made of the substance of the middle heaven; hence it is said: *And He placed His tabernacle in the Sun.* 
3. The third is 4, or the **universal elements**; hence it is said: *He made heaven His throne and the earth His footstool.* 
4. The fourth is 5, or the **fiery meteor**; hence it is said: *That Jehovah was in the pillar of fire by night.* 
5. The fifth is 6, or the **aerial meteor**; hence it is said: *That Jehovah flies upon the wings of the wind.* 
6. The sixth is 7, the **watery meteor**; where we find in *Psalm 105:39*: *God spread a cloud for a covering.* And *Psalm 104*: *The thick cloud is the vehicle of God.* 
7. The seventh and last is 8, the **earthy meteor**; for it is said: *God dwells in thick darkness (1 Chronicles 6:2 and 1 Kings 8:12).* And elsewhere it is said: *The earth shall be opened and bring forth a Savior.* 

Who is also unaware that God chose the human body—which is a perfectly mixed substance—as a covering for Himself? In these places, therefore, we see how God has "put on" all the degrees of composite progression in both creation and generation so that He, existing as the simplest being, might lead man to the boundary of perfect composition. By this, He makes man a participant in both extremes, so that man, experiencing the lowest things through his senses, might likewise grasp and contemplate the higher things through his understanding.

## CHAPTER VI.

### *How the reasoning behind various worldly mixtures can be best drawn from the consideration of my double worldly pyramid; and concerning the true speculation of Physical Pyramids.*

Indeed, this progression of nature is not only to be sought in the great and immense world <note>The Macrocosm or Universe.</note>, but also in the movement of every single creature from its starting point toward its goal: that is, from the point of extreme "crudity" <note>Rawness or unrefined state.</note> to that of complete maturation. For the breadth of such movement toward perfection in the greater world was clearly explained in our previous works through the adaptation of two pyramids of differing dispositions—namely, the **formal** <note>The pyramid representing Spirit or God's Light.</note> and the **material** <note>The pyramid representing physical substance and darkness.</note>.

For example, let us consider the extreme rawness and immaturity of an **apple**. In that state, we find its matter consists of the "primary waters" of the world, almost entirely deprived of actual light or an "essential form." Or, at the very least, it is endowed with almost no trace of perfection or activity. In this raw mass, we place the beginning of the "formal pyramid’s" point <note>The *conus* or apex.</note>. From that point, the fruit approaches its base or peak step-by-step as it moves toward its degree of perfection or maturity. In this movement, one can understand and perceive that as the perfection of the formal pyramid increases and abounds in the apple (which is seen in the stages of ripening), it increasingly converts the material nature of the apple into its own likeness. Thus, at the end of its maturation, the "formal act" <note>The active, spiritual principle.</note> of the apple is mixed equally with its passive, material nature—the "suffering female"—by whose mutual union a complete seed is produced, fit for the procreation of its own kind.

This, I say, is the intent and purpose of my pyramids: to show both in every individual subject of the world and in the world as a whole the variety and continuity of action and motion, as well as the diversity of the degrees of change in matter as it "suffers" <note>In the sense of being acted upon by an outside force.</note> such continuous action from its starting point to its end.

Indeed, this same movement is usually observed to be even more perfect in **minerals**. For in **quicksilver** <note>Mercury; *argentum vivum*.</note> (in which formal heat is very weak), one can perceive the beginning of the formal pyramid's movement as if in a subject of "thick water." The next step of its progression is discerned in **lead**, where it begins to hasten toward the perfection of **gold**. Then it passes through **tin** to **silver**, and from there into **gold**, in which the fiery rays of "formal light" are made manifest even to the eyes of fools. Previously, these rays were repressed and hidden because of the inequality of the matter, which was not yet fully subject to the actions of the form. This was a sign that the "assaults" of matter had not been completely defeated and subjected to the intense appetite of the fiery form. 

From this it is clear that just as the beginning of the movement toward the perfect composition of metals is in quicksilver, so we say its completion is in gold. Nature does not tend beyond this boundary of perfection but rests within it, unless it is further stirred by the artifice of the most sagacious philosopher <note>A reference to Alchemy and the creation of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>. This same progression exists in the **animal** subject: its starting point is the **seed**, in which that spark of the formal pyramid occupies the point. By the multiplication of this spark, movement occurs from the fluid seed (or "raw animal water") toward the completion of the fetus and its perfect maturity, which in man we call **youth**.

The intermediate steps of these progressions can most rightly be called **meteors** <note>In Fludd's time, "meteors" referred to any changing, intermediate, or atmospheric phenomena, including fluids within the body that are not yet "fixed."</note> or **imperfect mixtures**, insofar as they are on the way to a perfect composition but have not yet reached the goal of nature. In this motion, if some obstacle occurs to them by which they are hindered on their path, they can most aptly be called **diseases** or "morbid and preternatural meteors." Sometimes they even retreat and return to those principles from which they emerged, producing the death of the composite or the destruction of the thing being formed. But if these "meteors" proceed without any hindrance to the end destined for them by nature, they are called **natural**, and they bring about generation, life, and health to the creature, both the one being born and the one already born.

And this is the intention of our pyramids, both in any individual thing that can be born or decay, and in the universal world. At this point, I thought it worthwhile to explain to you from the opinions of the most excellent men that our invention of the pyramids—in both the **Macrocosm** and **Microcosm** and in the progression of every creature—was not published by us foolishly, since it seems to wander in no way from the path of truth.

In the first place, it is said in the book called *The Gate of Light* <note>original: *Porta lucis*; This refers to the Latin translation of the Kabbalistic text *Sha'are Orah*.</note>, Chapter 2:

> *That all things having life tend upward by their own instinct, and all things influencing life tend downward.*

For in this sensible world, whatever mixture consists of the four elements either lacks a manifest soul (the producer of diverse and wandering motion), lying immobile and resting like a **stone**; or it is quickened by a manifest soul and grows like a **plant**; or it moves in many ways and merely lives like **irrational animals**; or it speaks rationally like a **man**. 

Furthermore, we observe in metals that during their **sublimation** <note>The process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then becomes solid again, used here as a metaphor for purification.</note>, that which is more noble boils up into higher "spirits" when refined by alchemy, so that the things that are higher always seem purer. Likewise, in the lower regions, things are said to be sallow, squalid, and weighed down by filth; whereas in the upper regions, we admire things that are white, illustrious, and adorned with incredible beauty, following them with songs of praise. These are the words of the author in the place cited above.

Here, therefore, our intention regarding the "opposed pyramids" is best explained: here the actions of one "exalted pyramid" upon the "passions" <note>Reactions or receptions of influence.</note> of another "depressed" pyramid are living characters and impressions. And this is the reason why the Greater World is divided into two most fitting portions—namely, **Heaven** and **Earth**. According to this exemplar, God also composed **Man** (the Microcosm), as the most sacred scripture records, out of two things: the **Mud of the earth** and the **Breath of life**, so that, clothed in mud or earth, he might look toward lower things...

You see therefore (Readers, carried aloft on the wings of reason) what the nature of my pyramids are, not only those of the world, but also of every perfect creature. From this, it will be right to gather the degrees of **meteors** <term>Meteors: In the 17th century, this term referred to any atmospheric phenomenon (rain, wind, comets, etc.) or "imperfect mixtures" of elements that had not yet reached a stable state.</term>—that is, of imperfectly mixed things. For departing from one extreme, nature makes many degrees of imperfect mixture toward a condition that is fiery or lucid, as well as airy and watery, before a measure is made into a "perfectly mixed" thing; from the other extreme, the degrees incline toward an earthy and watery nature. Moreover, the "perfectly mixed" things of the vegetable, animal, and mineral kingdoms are those which are fitly constituted from the imperfect meteors of any nature.

### CHAPTER VII.

->**Concerning the general but brief enumeration of the differences of meteors, both healthy and unhealthy, in both worlds.**<-

As for the specific difference of all meteors, this occurs in respect to the disposition of matter, which is altered according to the greater or lesser power of the lucid form predominating in it. We say also that among meteors, both healthy and unhealthy, some are **super-heavenly**, others **heavenly**, and others **Elementary**. These we divide into the **invisible** or the **visible**. We say that the invisible do not differ in effect from the visible, although their shapes are not so apparent to the eyes. For example, we are taught by experience itself that although a visible **comet** seems to be consumed and reduced to nothing in its own time, nevertheless its form or substance does not perish; rather, it becomes invisible through expansion. Just as an artificial fire does not truly die, even though it seems to us to be extinguished, but is rendered invisible by expansion; therefore, they also exercise the same invisible effects in the air as they produced in their visible state, though perhaps not as strongly. So we also observe that when a hearth is extinguished, heat is still felt; and when a comet vanishes, famines and pestilential diseases are produced and rage even in the absence of the visible meteor, and so it is in other cases. By similar reasoning, we see that when a watery cloud is absent, the humidity of the air remains; and even a cloud, with no rain following, vanishes and is transmuted into the air in an invisible manner. Furthermore, both the **vapors** (which are the immediate causes of moist meteors) and the **exhalations** (which immediately produce fiery ones), as well as the denser **fumes** (which give birth to imperfect mixtures of an earthy nature, from which minerals arise), can be considered in the first series of invisible meteors.

In the **microcosm** <term>Microcosm: The "little world," referring to the human being as a reflection of the Macrocosm (the universe).</term> or man, we find this same distinction of meteors. For just as in the macrocosm we see a visible comet or an ignited meteor, so also a **bilious humor** <note>Yellow bile, associated with heat and fire in the four humors theory.</note> preternaturally ignited seems to play the part of a visible meteor. But if that putrid and ignited humor vanishes from sight through expansion into a drier fume and is transformed into an invisible spirit, that exhalation acts upon a nature similar to itself—namely, upon the **vital spirits** themselves. From this, a thick and putrid fever turns into a subtle and pestilential one; by its invisible condition, even those who are at a distance from the sufferer and far from contact are infected. From these things, therefore, we would have you understand that there are no visible meteors which do not also have invisible forms and images that carry out the same effects as the visible ones (though not in so intense a degree). Visible meteors are more concerned with the visible parts of the body, just as invisible ones affect the invisible parts more. This is clearly shown in thick and subtle poisons, insofar as "spiritual" poisons kill even while the body remains uninjured to the judgment of the eyes; for they work upon the invisible **animal spirits**. In every thing, like tends to enjoy its like, whether in malice or benevolence. Thus also, vapors most easily unite themselves to vapors in both worlds; and "foreign winds" or flatulent spirits are observed to invade the thinner spirits of the human extremities and are accustomed to press and stretch the **diaphragm** (by which they wage war strongly against the vital spirits). So many palpitations and tremors of the heart follow, and the imagination is struck by fears just as often. We see no differently in the **macrocosm** <term>Macrocosm: The "great world" or the universe at large, which early modern thinkers believed was perfectly mirrored by the human body.</term>, where flatulent exhalations attempt to reach the middle region of the air. They try to penetrate it with steady and long-lasting motion so that they might mix with the clearer spirits of life that dwell above in the regions of fire and the ether. In this conflict, such a great noise is made and such a clamor in the lower air, just as bellows and belching are excited in a man dominated by "wind" <note>In the medicine of this period, "wind" or "flatus" referred to gases produced by digestion or humors that were thought to cause various ailments.</note>.

Regarding the differences between the visible meteors of the world, it must be understood that some are simple, while others arise from those same simples, which we therefore call "compounds." We divide the **simples** again into humid and dry. We subdivide the **humid** either into **aerial**, which are related to the heat of fire—such as thick and almost visible vapors in both worlds—or into **watery**, participating in the coldness of the earth, such as rain, showers, dew, springs, and rivers. Finally, there are the **intermediates**, which participate partly in the aerial and partly in the watery nature: the first degree of these is the mist, the second is the little cloud, and the third is the cloud itself. 

Those **microcosmic** things can be quite directly referred back to these **macrocosmic** simples; for just as the microcosm is aptly called the "son" of the macrocosm itself, so it is necessary that he receives from his father his parts and his "meteors," by which his external self is generated and later corrupted. Therefore, the Macrocosm has ignited meteors, both visible and invisible, which, if they are healthy and naturally consistent with the effects of innate heat (and indeed of the bile itself), lead to actions in the body that are both manifest and imperceptible. But if they exist contrary to nature, they tend to produce fevers and other inflammations, such as the **sacred fire** <note>original: "ignis sacer." Historically known as Erysipelas or St. Anthony's Fire, a painful skin infection.</note> or **Erysipelas**, and **gutta rosacea** <note>Rose-colored spots or acne rosacea.</note>, etc. 

They also contain dry terrestrial meteors, such as dry fumes, the "melancholy wind," and such a humor naturally implanted in men of that complexion. Both worlds also share in the nature of humid meteors; for just as there are vapors in the macrocosm that are both good and healthy as well as bad and disease-bearing, so too in the microcosm are found fumes of similar conditions, both watery and aerial. Just as rain and showers exist in the world, so too are **catarrh, rheum, distillation**, or the **defluxion** <note>Terms for the discharge of fluid or mucus from the brain or lungs.</note> of various kinds found in the microcosm. Even **springs**—whether sulfurous, salty, sweet, acidic, or tainted with bile—are perceived in man mostly in the form of **fistulas** <note>Abnormal passages or "pipes" formed by disease in the body.</note>, just as in the macrocosm they contribute to health or infirmities according to the disposition of one’s complexion. The **ponds and lakes** of the macrocosm are compared to **dropsy** <note>original: "hydropi." ## *A brief compendium of the whole, or a universal mirror of causes, in which the remote and highest (or primary) causes, as well as those intermediate ones of many kinds, and finally those which are closest or near to composite bodies (which we have not unwisely named "meteors") are most exactly observed.*

To conclude this section of the second treatise of the second volume with a summary of everything preceding, we thought it worthwhile to reduce all the previous teaching into the hollow of a single artificial mirror. In this mirror, there are as many spheres as there are causes found and recounted—counting from that infinite and primordial cause down to the perfectly composed thing itself (which is the final effect of the causes). Thus, between the primary and uncreated causes—which are also called the "Numbering" ones—one may behold the middle causes (which are related to numbers). Their object or effect is the thing itself, perfectly mixed or "numbered," whose near cause is the multiform "meteor," as can be seen in that mirror. From this, therefore, we can draw forth infinite secrets, explain many mysteries, and unravel the secret of true astrology. This is something that common Astrology is denied from perfecting, since its "head" extends only to the fountain of fate and the seat of the stars. 

But we seek higher and truer principles than Porphyry <note>A 3rd-century Neoplatonist philosopher</note> ever knew or the doctrine of Ptolemy <note>The famous 2nd-century astronomer whose geocentric model dominated the Middle Ages</note> revealed to the world in any age. We do not fly on the wings of pagans, but are carried on high by the mystical feathers of the Kabbalists <note>original: "caballorum"; likely a variant of "cabbalistarum," practitioners of Jewish mysticism</note>, the Indians, and the Egyptian sages. We strive for that true wisdom to which Sacred Scripture attributed such force and power that they say the stars or light are in no way comparable to it in effect. This is that wisdom (I say) which makes man master of the stars, reveals hidden things to him, distinguishes times, understands the minds of men, and disposes all things in heaven as on earth. 

This wisdom (I say)—and not that vain and false version practiced among men today—is the foundation of this science of mine. Although it is expressed here with paper and ink, if anyone can perceive and distinguish its formal wheels and count them in their mind, they will realize that my intention is neither vain nor ridiculous, contrary to the opinion of the ignorant masses or the envious crowd. And though I seem to explain the mystery of this "Mirror of Wisdom" <note>original: "speculi sophici"</note> in a material voice or with a rough, common, and unpolished pen, I beg the wise man to believe that I have woven the thread of this following discourse with a "fiery pen" cut without hands from marble-earth born of divinity, and in a language familiar to the mind. I have veiled it somewhat in a dark shadow, imitating nature in its actions. For where on earth can we find a soul without the veil of a body, or formal light without material darkness, or good without the pollution of evil, or joy without the stain of sorrow, or heaven without the dark covering of earth, or finally, generation without the lethal cup of corruption? 

Nor indeed was creation by God performed without the labor of six days, although at the end of the blessed Sabbath, rest shone forth. In this rest, infinite nature did not proceed further in its motion toward the completion of finite nature. For after the defilement of imperfection was laid aside, in the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place, the Sun was created in the 4th place as the ornament of heaven and earth. Yet 1, 2, and 3 gathered together are 6, designating as many days of labor. If a fourth unity is added to this, the number of rest or the Sabbath is produced, which is seven. Or if the value of the quaternary number <note>The number 4</note> is considered, it completes the series of simple numbers <note>1+2+3+4 = 10</note> and fulfills the "denary" number <note>The number 10</note>, by which the divine properties called the *Sephiroth* <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself</note> are explained, beyond whose naming there is no progression in numbers. 

Nevertheless, as far as it is contemplated by common eyes and noticed in the manner explained by me, you will find this most polished spherical mirror contains a knowledge that is not at all common and yet most true. Though it is expressed partly in a metaphysical manner, and partly in a Kabbalistic and physical way, you will find it should not be despised or neglected. # ON THE TERTIARY PRINCIPLES.

...they were nothing before the moment of creation, and divinity itself is said to be hidden—either regarding the divine act, or in the sense that all things are truly considered after the mystery of creation, in which God is said to be manifest and not hidden. Therefore, the prior state of unformed matter is explained by the subterranean hemisphere of a mirror, in which the "Dark Aleph" <note>original: "Aleph tenebrosum"; Aleph (א) is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, here representing the numerical value of 1 and the beginning of all things</note> is expressed in the center of the *hyle* <term>hyle: A Greek term used in philosophy to describe the fundamental, raw matter of the universe before it is given shape</term>, which is a hieroglyph of the hidden God. This "matter-earth" is said to be "without form and void" <note>A reference to Genesis 1:2</note> because it lacks any action of light, and divine grace is not perceived to act within it. Due to this lack (without which nothing can be filled), potential matter is called "empty," and is indeed called "divine power" because God lay hidden within it. Yet, he is potentially ready, as far as we are concerned—once the rays of his beauty, which were previously contracted within himself, are finally revealed—to act upon that matter. The Creator brought this power into action at the same moment he began to create the world. 

And just as here on earth, when the Sun is absent, night immediately invades everything, so too by the absence of the "Divine Sun" or "Divine Act" (which we call Wisdom, a Sun older than the world itself), we have placed the lower hemisphere of the mirror. On its left side, we have set out the dawn of Day, of splendor, and of the act of divine Wisdom; just as on its right or opposite side, the evening time is denoted after the setting of the Divine Sun or the end of the world. In the daytime hemisphere, the outer circle indicates the degrees of perfection and imperfection of every creature, both in the progress of creation and the sequence of generation. Thus, the movement of Wisdom in creation was made from the point of the East to the Meridian of vigor; between these extremes of perfection is the meteorological midpoint tending toward both generation and nutrition, which is called "Increase." Similarly, between the point of perfection (the Meridian vigor) and that of corruption and death (the setting of the Sun), is that meteorological midpoint called "Decrease," which tends from the height of life toward disease and rot, its opposite, until it reaches the twilight of death. Hence it is said that **the birth of one is the death of another**, and indeed many mysteries lie hidden here which would be too long to recount in this place.

**The Second** sphere, however, denotes the degree and order of progression in creation and generation: from "nothing" and the "Dark Aleph" (or "Small Aleph"), denoting unity, to the specific formation of the world whose Sun rises in *Jod* <note>original: "Jod" (י); the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing a point of divine emanation</note>. This is the character of divine emanation out of the darkness and the sign of the number ten, whose end is the "Great Aleph," which is signified by the number one thousand, beyond which there is no further progression. Thus *Vau* <note>original: "Vau" (ו); the sixth Hebrew letter, often associated with the connection between heaven and earth</note>, denoting the Sun, indicates the exaltation of the Sun at noon, and the period of the perfection of life or the maturity of age. Proceeding from there, things decrease until a regression is made back to unity or nothingness and toward divine power away from action.

**The Third Sphere** indicates the "three fathers" of the world, or the uncreated and supernatural causes. Among these, the letter *He* <note>original: "He" (ה)</note> is doubled in the archetypal world <note>The "Archetypal World" is the realm of divine ideas or the blueprint of the universe</term>, just as in the created world the waters were divided from the waters. Thus, with these four triumphant and spherical letters, the essential name of God <note>The Tetragrammaton: YHWH (Jod, He, Vau, He)</note> is explained most exactly, and by no others. They are called "fathers" by the followers of Moses because they act upon the first "mothers" of the world (the created principles) much like a male acts upon a female for the creation and production of the whole. 

*Jod* therefore corresponds to the rising of the Sun in this sphere, according to common understanding; the first *He* denotes the ascent toward the noon; *Vau* is likened to the Sun at noon; and the final *He* indicates the waning of the Sun, and because of this, it signifies the thickening of the day's moisture and the approach of night and darkness. But truly, insofar as the true Wisdom of the world is established as the Sun of our hemisphere, it moves from the North in a thin spirit until it is exalted in the South, which is the middle path where the Equinoctial line intersects the Meridian. Thus it is said in 

> *Job 37:21. Golden light comes from the North; and through the North, for God is terrible in praise.* 

This is that Wisdom which 

> *is more precious than the Sun, and compared to the light of the Sun or the stars, is found to be prior, as the Wise Man testifies in Chapter 7:29. For she is a reflection of eternal light and the image of God. Ibid. verse 26.* 

And so from the meridian point, *Vau* passes into the thick clouds of the South. Closely following the "Fathers" in the uncreated circle are the "Mothers," the first of which, *Aleph*, receives the act and is acted upon by *Jod*. The first *Mem* <note>original: "Mem" (מ/ם); the Hebrew letter associated with water</note>, or the "Open Mem" that initiates, receives the most subtle spirit, full of divinity, from the first *He*, signifying the arrangement of the intellectual world, which *Vau* and *Shin* <note>original: "Shin" (ש); the Hebrew letter associated with fire or the spirit</note> (or the firmament) divide from the elemental world. Afterward, *Shin* corresponds to the actions of the divine character *Vau* and denotes the arrangement of the ethereal or stellar world, giving life and light to every star. Finally, the last *Mem*, or the "Closed Mem" that finishes, corresponds to the elemental world and receives its life and power from the final *He* of the four-letter name. Both of these letters are the fathers and mothers (or the principles) of the elemental world. In this way, the three principles of the world were created by the essence-making influx of the purely formal and uncreated principles into their own potentiality or matter.

And these are the meteors pertaining more to the soul and spirit.

Therefore, the spirit is the vehicle of the soul, and the body is the receptacle for both. Furthermore, the spirit of subtle generation and the act of life run back and forth through veins, pores, and invisible passages in the body, whether it be animate or inanimate. ### ON THE TERTIARY PRINCIPLES.

Or from a universal nature of this kind, various **meteors** <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric or celestial phenomenon, including rain, wind, clouds, and comets, not just falling rocks from space.</note> are generated from various combinations of water and fire—or spirit and action—whether they occur according to nature or contrary to it. If the greater portion is water, "water-meteors" are produced; if the predominating part is fire, "fiery" imperfect mixtures are produced. If they are moderate, they are airy, moist, or dry according to the nature of the divine property flowing into them. For example: **Elohim** <note>original: "Elohim"; a Hebrew name for God often associated with justice and the laws of nature.</note> rains down from **Binah** <note>The Sephirah of "Understanding."</note> into the **Thrones** <note>The third rank of angels.</note> a firmness of union. These influences are directed by the angel **Zadhiel** into the sphere of **Saturn**, attributing to it a receptive, freezing, fixed, firm, and stable disposition in any matter. From there, guided by its **Olympic Spirit** <note>The governing intelligence of a planet in Renaissance magic.</note>, its effects are rained down upon the earth. It oversees and cares for the union of bodies and spirits—indeed, the very union of soul and body. Similarly, in the elemental world, it holds its primary kingdom in the middle region of the air, just as the influence of **Ehieh** <note>original: "Ehieh"; "I Am," the name associated with the highest Sephirah, Keter (the Crown).</note> flows from the Crown into the region of fire, and **Jah** flows from **Chokmah** <note>The Sephirah of "Wisdom."</note> into the highest circle of the air. So also in that same penultimate circle, the lower seven **Sephiroth** <note>The ten emanations or attributes of God in Kabbalah.</note> pour their virtues and meteors—not unlike their own properties—directly and perpendicularly into the sphere beneath them. For example: **El** flows from **Chesed** <note>The Sephirah of "Mercy" or "Kindness."</note> through the **Dominations**, carried by the angel **Zadkiel**, pouring his influences into the sphere of **Jupiter**. From there, they are liberally rained down to the lower realms, giving natural power to the lowest region of the air. From this, the so-called "healthy meteor" and the vapor of life are derived, from which comes the internal and natural spirit—the life-giving vapor mixed with natural heat—and from which the **Mercury of Life** (the root of generation) usually springs. On the other hand, **Elohim Gibbor** flows from the Sephirah **Geburah** <note>The Sephirah of "Severity" or "Strength," associated with judgment.</note> through the **Powers** (guided by the malevolent angel **Samuel** <note>Likely a variant of Samael, the angel of death and severity associated with Mars.</note>, carrying influences opposed to life) into the sphere of **Mars**. Because of this, that planet is called "malevolent" and the "lesser misfortune," just as Saturn is called the "greater misfortune" due to its freezing dryness. Therefore, the influences of Mars act harshly and pour an impulsive force, full of violent fire, into the lower realms, which its Olympic Spirit conducts downward into the element of fire. Consequently, in both worlds, preternaturally hot exhalations carrying unhealthiness are stirred up, from which fiery meteors are ignited—both visible ones like "Beams," comets, and perpendicular fires, and invisible ones, from which follow plagues, the wasting of the earth and body, decay, and dryness accompanied by famine, as well as fevers in the **Microcosm** <note>The human being, seen as a miniature map of the entire universe.</note>, Erysipelas, and so on; and one must proceed in this way with the rest.

Finally, the last wheel of the mirror explains the "meteors" of any body—be it animal, vegetable, or mineral—from which they are composed according to the laws of nature. Such are **Mercury**, authored by the water produced by **Ehieh**; **Sulphur**, whose principle was the created light or fire, receiving its power from **Jah** flowing from his throne **Chokmah**; and **Salt**, which is the union of both Mercury and Sulphur, flowed into by **Elohim**. These three are Salt, the simplest earth and the center of all bodies; for the philosophers write that the center of the earth of the **Macrocosm** <note>The universe as a whole.</note> is most pure and secure from defilement. The other meteors of the same circle are partly healthy and partly unhealthy according to the property of the Sephirah from which they are rained down. This final sphere is the ultimate meteor, or the "proximate matter," or the "immediate cause" of perfect composition in animals, plants, and minerals alike. Therefore, although meteors of this kind are imperfectly mixed in themselves, because they approach more closely to perfect composition, they are called "more composite meteors"—that is, the proximate cause of perfect mixing or composition. In composite things, **Mercury** is called that **radical moisture** <note>The essential life-fluid that maintains the body’s vitality.</note> by which the agent or **innate heat** (which is **Sulphur**) is nourished. Sulphur is that agent which works as the "form" upon the matter adapted for it to give the composite thing its essential being. **Salt**, which participates in both of these, is that central earth which attracts from the four elements the parts necessary for composition and growth. Thus, every composite thing has as the meteors closest to its generation Mercury (from the part of subtle water), Sulphur (from the part of subtle fire)—from whose mixture the soul is made—and a more fixed Salt (from the part of subtle earth), from which, as from a secret boundary, the mass of the body and the "tabernacle" of the aforementioned soul takes its beginning.

From these things it is clear that **God** is the "most remote cause" for the composition of any creature; between God and those proximate causes, many other intermediate causes intervene, as is clearly explained in the mirror itself.

Regarding the primary, uncreated causes or supersubstantial principles—namely, **Jod** י, **He** ה, **Vau** ו, and the final **He** ה <note>The four letters of the Tetragrammaton, the sacred name of God.</note>—we have made extensive mention in the first three books of Part I, Portion I, Section I, which we have noted in the third sphere of this mirror.

Regarding the ten divine names and the **Sephiroth** subject to them, we have spoken openly in Section I, Portion I, Part I, Book 3, Chapter 3; and in Portion II, Section I, Part I, Chapters 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9. SECTION I. PORTION II. PART III.

### First Experiment: Concerning the meaning or mystery of every Hebrew word through its discovery and revelation, and this solely by the contemplation of the "fathers" Jod, He, and Vau, and the "mothers" Aleph, Mem, and Shin, whether they are present or absent.

Indeed, a wonderful light is brought to Hebrew words by the presence or absence of these truly holy and formal characters. These characters act as seals; for those who look closely, they reveal the secret sense or the essence-making mystery of a word. For first, regarding the "fathers" <note>In Kabbalah, the letters of the Tetragrammaton (YHVH) are often called "fathers" as they represent the primary divine energies.</note> or purely formal letters (which are also called "round" for reasons we have discussed above), it must be understood that since they are the principles of all principles, in which the unique uncreated essence consists, their presence undoubtedly hides some divine mystery within the word where they are found. Where more of these characters are found, a greater presence of divinity exists, even if it is not so clearly explained by the common Hebrew meaning. For example, in the word **יה Jah** <note>original: "Jah"; a shortened form of the divine name Jehovah, representing the absolute essence of God.</note>, nothing but the divine essence is repeated. And also in **יהוה Jehovah**, these characters are considered solely within the divine essence without any consideration for created or material characters, which is why they denote the divine essence alone.

Closely following these in excellence are the "mothers" **א Aleph**, **מ Mem**, and **ש Shin**, which are, as it were, the closest and primary garments or vehicles of divinity in nature. For the soul **א Aleph** <note>The letter Aleph is associated with the element of Air and the mediating spirit.</note> is of the radiant **י Jod**; the life **ש Shin** <note>Shin is associated with Fire.</note> is of the **ו Vau**; and the internal creating spirit **מ Mem** <note>Mem is associated with Water.</note> is of the **ה He**. Therefore, where these two species of characters are mixed together, the intention or mystical meaning of that word is undoubtedly most excellent. The more "fathers" abound in a word, the more noble that word is judged to be. For instance: **אהיה Ehieh** <note>original: "Ehieh"; "I Am," the name associated with the highest crown of divinity.</note>, in which the essence and property of God the Father is beheld; and **אלהים Elohim**, God the Holy Spirit, or the God of the Waters. Where the final **Mem** (denoting water) is united with **Vau** and **Aleph**, it forms **אלוה Eloah**, and so on for the others. Hence, the "round" characters combined with the "mothers" denote a Divine act within nature.

By a similar logic, if only the "mothers" are found in words, they denote a thing highly exalted in the mysteries of nature, especially if the word contains many characters of that nature. Thus, in the word **שמים Shamayim** (the heavens), we see the open **מ Mem** and the closed **ם Mem**, which are hieroglyphics for the thinner and denser waters <note>In this cosmology, the "heavens" were thought to be composed of a celestial, fiery water.</note>. Similarly, **Shin** is the seal of light with which the heavens are adorned, and the **ש Shin** (the hieroglyphic of the spiritual world) is the head of the heavens and the life of the world. Thus **שמש Shemesh** (the Sun) contains two mothers, and specifically the luminous mother twice. This denotes that just as **יה Jah** or **יהוה Jehovah** is the most excellent essence of the archetypal or uncreated kingdom, so too is **שמש Shemesh** (the Sun) in the typical, created, or natural kingdom. For the Sun is the visible prince and commander of all visible creatures in the world. Finally, where all these letters are perceived to be absent, little good or at least little external light is to be expected. We could produce an entire volume on the presence or absence of these formal characters, but it is not our purpose to dwell on them alone.

### Second Experiment: Concerning the wonderful explanation of the Sephirotic number, in which equal portions are found corresponding to each Sephirotic property.

There is no number to be found in the world divisible into so many equal parts as **one thousand and eighty** (1080), which we find can be partitioned into ten portions corresponding to each **Sephirah** <note>The Sephiroth are the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note>. Thus, its half is 540. Its third part is 360, which is the number by which the days of the year are divided. Its fourth part is 270. Its fifth part is 216. Its sixth part is 180. Its eighth part is 135. Its ninth part is 120, which is the space of time God assigned for a human life <note>A reference to Genesis 6:3.</note>. Its tenth part is 108. Its fifteenth part is 72. For 72 is the sum of the 22 letters joined with the 50 Gates of Wisdom; likewise, there were 72 powerful angels of the whole earth according to the opinion of the Kabbalists. For according to the Kabbalists, from the number of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> arises the number 72, from which 72 angels are produced by a certain divine outflow, as if from the seal of the Creator. Finally, its twentieth part is 54. In these ten portions of that number, the mysteries of the ten Sephiroth are undoubtedly comprehended, representing the archetypal natures and divine properties in this world—a fact which some of the ancient Rabbis attempted to proclaim even more clearly and loudly.

### Third Experiment, not to be overlooked: Concerning the union of the three superior Sephiroth with the rest.

In the progress of Chapter Seven, Section I, Portion 2, Part One, we discussed the nature and connection of the three principal and more essential Sephiroth with the seven following ones, and their various outflows into the lower realms, by which all things in this world are under the power of the three...

### ON THE TERTIARY PRINCIPLES.

We can prove that the things described above are subject to the higher <term>Sephiroth</term><note>The ten emanations or attributes of God in Kabbalah through which the universe was created.</note> and the names presiding over them. And although the seven lower divine properties are said to have their own operations in this world, nevertheless all of them refer back to these three related to the Holy Trinity, just as less important things are referred to those that are more important. Here, indeed, the connection of the persons and the chaining of the things placed under them is best discerned in three Hebrew words: namely <term>סוֹפֵר סִפּוּר ספר</term> <note>original: "Sopher, Sippur, Sepher"</note> — the Writer, the Writing, and the Written. 

In this system, the letter **ס** <note>Samech</note> refers to the Sephirah <term>Cheter</term> <note>Keter, meaning 'Crown'</note>, over which the name **Ehieh** presides; the letter **פ** <note>Phe</note> refers to <term>Hochma</term> <note>Chokhmah, meaning 'Wisdom'</note>, which is dominated by **Jehovah**; and the letter **ר** <note>Resh</note> refers to <term>Binah</term> <note>Understanding</note>, which **Elohim** commands. Just as ten letters are found in those three words, so too each of these letters appears three times in the series. For **ס** is found in positions 1, 4, and 7; **פ** in 2, 5, and 8; and finally **ר** in 3, 6, and 10, while in the ninth position, the letter **ו** <note>Vau</note> remains as a point of connection or a bridge. 

Now, if we count downward from the sphere of the Sephiroth (which is the sixth from the outer circumference) into our prefigured mirror, we find that positions 1, 4, and 7—namely the orders of <term>Seraphim</term>, **Dominations**, and **Principalities**—pertain to the letter **ס** or **Cheter**, to which the Father **Ehieh** is referred in the order of the Holy Trinity. Furthermore, in the celestial or stellar world, positions 1, 4, and 7 are referred to it: that is, the First Mover, the sphere of **Jupiter**, and the sphere of **Venus**. Similarly, in the elementary world, positions 1, 4, and 7 correspond to it: namely, the element of fire, the lowest region of the element of air, and the Animal kingdom itself. 

From these things it is clear enough that the property of the Sephirah <term>Chesed</term> <note>Mercy</note>, over which the name **El** dominates, stands in the same relationship to **Cheter** (over which **Ehieh** presides) as the number 1 stands to 4; and therefore **Chesed** flows into the **Dominations**, which in the fourth position relate to the **Seraphim** commanded by **Ehieh**. So too in the 7th position, the Sephirah <term>Netzeth</term> <note>Netzach, meaning 'Victory'</note> regards **Cheter** in its quality, just as 1 regards 7 through 4. Therefore, those things that stand perpendicularly beneath **Chesed** are found in the four-fold number from **Cheter**. Those things contained under **Netzeth** are found in the seven-fold series in every world. 

Furthermore, to come to the hieroglyphic character of **פ** <note>Phe, representing the second person in the Trinity</note>, its positions in the intellectual world are 2, 5, and 8, to which correspond the **Cherubim**, **Powers**, and **Archangels**. Those things that lie below the **Cherubim** in the lower worlds regard **Hochma** in the number two; the **Powers** regard it in the number five; and the **Archangels** in the number eight. In the celestial and elementary worlds, it looks upon those places subject to **Hochma**, <term>Geburah</term> <note>Strength/Severity</note>, and <term>Hod</term> <note>Glory/Splendor</note>, along with the vegetable kingdom. 

The character **ר** <note>Resh</note>, related to the third person in the Trinity, claims for itself positions 3, 6, and 9. From this, **Binah** is referred to it in the 3rd, <term>Tipherets</term> <note>Tiferet, meaning 'Beauty'</note> in the 6th, and <term>Jesod</term> <note>Yesod, meaning 'Foundation'</note> in the 9th—or **Jesod** with <term>Malchut</term> <note>Malkuth, meaning 'Kingdom'</note>, insofar as **Malchut** is the receptacle of all things. At the same time, all properties placed under these Sephiroth have a relation to the spirit of **Binah**, as does the mineral kingdom. 

By these things one may see that the three first Sephiroth, with the divine names presiding over them, hold within themselves the power of the entire world and every region of it. Furthermore, it is clear that the remaining 7 later Sephiroth are, as it were, subordinate to these supreme ones. Here, therefore, we have the true and most essential aspects of the super-celestial influences upon these lower things—aspects to be placed many degrees above those of the common astrologers. If anyone could draw out their secret meanings, they would become a participant in astrology that is as much intellectual as it is celestial and terrestrial. Here lies hidden the greatest mystery, which it would be profane and a religious crime to reveal to everyone.

For in the "right-hand radiation" or aspect: 
- The **conjunction** ☌ refers to unity (1).
- The **sextile** aspect ✶ refers to the number 2.
- The **trine** aspect △ refers to the triple number (3).
These aspects correspond to the three lords of the Sephiroth, from which all other radiations depend; and these aspects are called "good." 
Furthermore:
- To the **square** aspect □ corresponds the number 4.
- To the **fivefold** aspect corresponds 5.
- To the **opposition** ☍ — ◯ refers the sixth number. 
Furthermore, in the "left-hand radiation":
- The **fivefold** aspect corresponds to the number 7.
- The **eight-fold** to 8.
- The **trine** to 9.
Then, in the tenth number, unity repeats itself again from the trine, where the return to the **conjunction** is made. This is the true logic of the aspects of the "ideal stars." It is arduous and difficult for the unlearned—indeed, even for the most learned of this world—to distinguish their formal progressions or to reveal them to themselves or the world without proper contemplation.

---

### Fourth Experiment: Concerning the condition and disposition of the Soul of the Newborn.

By considering this mirror according to a certain common method, it will not be difficult to perceive in some way the disposition of the soul of one who is born. First, we look at the planet predominating on that day at the moment of the Sun’s rising above the earth; in the place of that planet, we shall estimate the Sun’s operation on that day. Next, we look at the ascending planet at the hour of birth. 

Having thus gathered the location of the planet of the day in the mirror, one must ascend upward in the same arc as far as the Sephirothic orb. There you will perceive the supreme and primordial cause of its influence. Having also considered its aspect with its own origin, one must afterward seek which planet of the whole sky was stronger in dignities at the moment of the Sun’s ascent above the earth. Once its seat is found, one should also ascend to its Sephirah, where its condition and the logic of its aspect must also be contemplated. 

Therefore, just as we find the Sun on that day (along with its Sephirah and the predominating planet and its Sephirah) to agree or vary in state, condition, and the intuition of its radiation, so too may we divine concerning the condition, certainty, or constancy—and also the piety, mercy, or severity—and the good or bad fortune of the newborn...
