### Johannes Kepler’s Epitome of Harmony.

The subject of Johannes Kepler's Harmony consists *first* in the proportional position of the Planets in the heavens; *Next*, for the completion of his harmony, he establishes the earth itself among the number of moving stars of heaven; *Thirdly*, he makes the Sun that immobile center, and yet the source of motion, around which he says all the Planets except the Moon move. <meta>Continuity: Following the previous page where Robert Fludd defended his mystical demonstrations against Johannes Kepler's criticisms, Fludd now begins a detailed analysis of Kepler's own theories regarding the "Harmonice Mundi" (Harmony of the World), specifically how Kepler uses the five regular Platonic solids to explain planetary distances.</meta>

### TO THE KEPLERIAN APPENDIX.

...from the Euclidean, Proclean, and Copernican doctrines, he derived the various proportions of the five regular geometric solids, although he admits that his discovery surpasses the intentions of Pythagoras, Aristotle, or Plato. For in that which they applied the proportion of the **Cube** to the earth, this author of ours attributes the **Cube** to Saturn, and establishes its proportion to the interval between the spheres of Saturn and Jupiter. They also gave the **Tetrahedron** <note>A four-faced pyramid.</note> to fire; he gives it to Mars, and grants its proportion to the distance between the spheres of Jupiter and Mars. Furthermore, they attributed the **Dodecahedron** <note>A twelve-faced solid.</note> to heaven, but he accommodated its proportion to the space between the spheres of Mars and the earth. From there, they made the **Icosahedron** <note>A twenty-faced solid.</note> a symbol of the element of water, but he appropriated its nature to Venus and to the distance between the spheres of the earth and Venus. Finally, the **Octahedron** figure <note>An eight-faced solid.</note>, which they applied to Air, he ascribes to Mercury and its proportion to the dimension between the spheres of Venus and Mercury. The reasons why such confidence has possessed him, so that he twists the sayings of the Philosophers to his own opinion in this way, he seems to explain with these words: *Preface to Book 1: When they gave the Cube to the earth, perhaps they understood Saturn, whose sphere is removed by the interposition of Jupiter; for Saturn has obtained the slowest motion, closest to rest. Thus Aristotle read that the Octahedron was given to Air, when perhaps they understood Mercury, which is surely the swiftest of all, just like air itself; perhaps Mars was insinuated by the word Fire:* and so on for the rest. Thus he says. He even gathers from the opinion of Proclus <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher who wrote on geometry.</note> that the Pythagoreans themselves held a reciprocal opinion—namely, that those five solids were not handed down for the elements, but for the Planets themselves; Proclus teaches that the unique end of Geometry is to teach how heaven received figures suited to certain of its parts. Another support, by which he seems to establish this opinion of his, is found on *folio 59 of Book 2*, where he speaks of the five solids of the Pythagoreans in these words: *I said in the preamble of my book, that it seemed agreeable to me that the doctrine of the Ancients was the same, but hidden in the manner of a sect.* <note>Referring to the Pythagorean tradition of keeping scientific and mystical knowledge secret.</note> 

However, how these solids are adapted with their angles to the intervals of the spheres of any Planet, he indicates more expressly in *Chapter 3 of Book 5*. But, so that these things might better agree among themselves, and so that his harmony might be more symphonious, he judged it necessary to count the earth among the stars. *His discourse is of this kind, in Chapter 3 of Book 5:* But, because among the common crowd of students it is still a new thing, and a dogma most absurd to the ears of most, that the Earth is one of the Planets and is carried among the stars around an immobile Sun, therefore let those who are offended by the novelty of this science know that these harmonic speculations also hold a place in the Hypotheses of Tycho Brahe <note>A famous Danish astronomer who proposed a system where the Sun orbits Earth, but other planets orbit the Sun.</note>: moreover, that this author has all other things in common with Copernicus which pertain to the disposition of bodies and the rationale of contemplation. He only transfers the annual Copernican motion of the earth into the whole system of the Planets, and into the Sun, which occupies the middle of it by the consent of both Authors. Thus he says. He also says there that, according to the opinion of Copernicus, the earth measures a circle with the real motion of its body, walking in the middle between the outer circles of Mars and the inner circles of Venus. 

Finally, as far as pertains to the Sun, he seems in the same chapter—following the opinion of Copernicus (to whom alone he persuades everyone to give credit in *Chapter 3 of Book 5*, having left behind the ancient Astronomical Hypotheses of Ptolemy, etc., and in *Chapter 4 of Book 5* the "fantasy" of retrogradations and stations)—to establish that the earth, along with the rest of the Planets (for he establishes 7 Planets besides the Sun), with the sole exception of the Moon, is carried around an immobile Sun. But truly, he makes the Moon's motion irregular compared to the others; for he makes the earth its center, just as the Sun is the center for the earth itself and the rest of the Planets. Therefore Saturn and Jupiter, between which is the interval of a **Cube**, just as between the latter and Mars there is the distance of a **Tetrahedron**; similarly Mars and the earth, between which the space of a **Dodecahedron** is expressed, as between the earth and Venus is the distance of an **Icosahedron**; finally Venus and Mercury, between which is interposed the dimension of an **Octahedron**, he makes to circle the immobile Sun, and to move above its center, from which they receive their motion: Whence in *Axiom 4, Chapter 9 of Book 5*, and in many other places, he makes the Sun the source of motion. 

From these proportions of the regular solids to one another, therefore (of which any one is taken from another like a son from a father, and the lesser from the greater, as the Tetrahedron from the Cube, and the Dodecahedron from the Tetrahedron, and the Icosahedron from the Dodecahedron, and the Octahedron as if from the center of all, and hence he says one is extracted from the other by a certain harmonic proportion), he strives to compose a harmony, because of the variety of the eccentric motions of the Planets proportionally arising therefrom. And first, he shows various degrees of kinship of harmonic proportions with the five regular figures in *Chapter 2 of Book 5*. Hence in *Chapter 9, Proposition 8*, he shows that because of the proportion of the **Cube**, there are attributed to Saturn and Jupiter 1:2 and 1:3—that is, the **Diapason** <note>original: *Diapason*; the interval of an octave.</note>, and the **Diapente** <note>original: *Diapente*; the interval of a fifth.</note> over an octave—and that the joined proper proportions of the extreme motions have roughly 2:3, the **Diapente**. To Venus and Mercury he attributes a greater harmony, 1:4, the **Disdiapason** <note>original: *Disdiapason*; a double octave.</note>; to Jupiter and Mars 1:8, almost a **Trisdiapason** <note>original: *Trisdiapason*; a triple octave.</note>. And so in the others: and this indeed is the force of his purely celestial Harmony. But he composes another "mixed" harmony from the variety of the **aspects** <note>The angular relationships between planets in astrology.</note> of these Planets so disposed, and from the angle they make with their radiations upon the earth. In which species of Harmony he seems to return to the proportion of regular figures in a plane, just as in celestial harmony he follows the directions of the same in a solid. This, unless I am mistaken, is the subject of his whole book, this is the foundation of his doctrine.

### *An Epitome of My Physics and Worldly Harmony.*

From unity—whether divine power or darkness—I produce duality: namely, light (the universal form and act) and water (matter and the passive principle). I believe that this duality, or the root of the world, having been expanded through multiplication into itself and dilated into its square, procreated the four elements of the world. These are distinct from one another and fill the concavity of the world’s structure everywhere. Their earthy dregs of darkness—acting like a horrific shadow or a deformed chaos in the capacity of the world, disturbing everything from every side—were reverberated into the center of the world's circumference by the power of divine light; this I call the Earth. 

I also say there is a pyramidal proportion in the watery nature, whose base is in the Earth, while its cone tends upward toward the circumference like a flame of fire. I assert that in this physical pyramid, a continuous alteration from the coarse to the subtle occurs without fail, because of the unequal proportions of invisible light hidden within the worldly matter, which produces various actions and hidden motions. I make these acts of nature the foundations of my **Worldly Harmony**, and not quantitative measurements, as **Johannes** <note>Johannes Kepler</note> has judged. 

Finally, I make a third progression from the quaternary <note>the number four</note> to the octonary number <note>the number eight</note>, so that at last, by this cubic dimension, I may arrive at things composed from the number four. Beyond this step, there is no natural progression in this world. I say that in this alteration, the most exact harmony of Nature in generation and corruption appears daily even to the blind: namely, a progression from the number four to the Cube or Octonary in generation, and a regression from the Cube or Octonary to the Square or Quaternary. This is the composition from elements through generation, and from composition a resolution back into them, like a backward movement from the "goal to which" to the "starting point." And so, after creation, all things take on generation and corruption. For I affirm this to be the **Wheel of Nature**, assiduously driven in the world, according to that saying of the Philosopher: *The generation of one is the corruption of another.* 

Yet the permanent root of these things is always in the same act, possessing as it were the privilege of creation, so that from there the four elements may be preserved in their being: namely, **Light** and **Water**, which are the foundations of the world. I conclude, therefore, that the harmony of the pyramids is that which is made by the ratio held between the root, the binary, and the square—that is, between light and water and the four elements which arise from them, as a square from a root. The elements are thus nourished and preserved in their being and essence by a certain harmonic respect proceeding from the principal roots. Their active nature (the form) is administered to the elements by harmonic proportion, and this act is the true wisdom of the world; while the passive nature, sounding in a fit and convenient measure of form, grants the succession of matter to them. The harmony of Generation, Augmentation, and Corruption and decrease occurs by a reciprocal ratio held between the square to the Cube. And this is the final step of Harmony, whose first and primordial step was between unity (divine power) and duality, and the second between duality and the quaternary number. This, in brief, is the subject of my Physical Philosophy; these are the foundations of my worldly harmony.

### *A Comparison of My Worldly Harmony with that of Johannes Kepler, declaring in what they agree and in what they differ.*

<margin>Book 1. With the Preface. Proposition 25. Book 2. Of the 5 bodies.</margin>
**Johannes Kepler** derives the origin of his Harmony from the five regular bodies of mathematics <note>The Platonic solids</note>: namely, the Cube, Tetrahedron, Dodecahedron, Icosahedron, and Octahedron, and he does this according to the opinion of the Ancient Philosophers. This is also the subject of my Harmony, although instead of those geometric terms, I have used physical words. Regarding the subject, therefore, we agree in this: that he himself twists the five geometric bodies of the Pythagoreans, Platonists, and even Aristotle from their proper sense to his own, dragging them as if by the hair. He offers this excuse: *In the Preface to Book 1: When they compared the Cube to the earth, perhaps they understood Saturn for the earth; and so for the rest.* In this, by poorly applying suppositions and imaginations, he laid the fabulous foundations of his Harmony. 

Furthermore, in *Proposition 25 of Book 2*, it seems to me he asserts as agreeable that this same doctrine (he means the relation of the five bodies to the intervals of the planetary orbits) was also held by the Ancients, but hidden in the manner of a Sect. So he says. Thus, he seems inconstant and uncertain regarding the intentions of the Philosophers. Yet he reveals their minds in words plainly contrary to himself when he says: *Pythagoras, Plato, and Aristotle called these worldly figures insofar as they respected the five simple bodies of the world.* From this, they made the **Cube** a symbol of earth, the **Icosahedron** of water, the **Octahedron** of air, the **Tetrahedron** of fire, and the **Dodecahedron** of heaven. How poorly Johannes has applied these bodies to his own intentions will be very easy to discern for anyone who considers that the entire world was completed on the third day of creation, before the Sun and stars were placed in the heaven. For on the third day, the Elements were completed and ordered according to the laws of nature, and on the [fourth] day...

### TO THE KEPLERIAN APPENDIX.

...and on the second day, heaven was completed. From this, one can see that if they <note>the ancient philosophers</note> had applied these geometric figures to the five bodies of the world, they undoubtedly would not have even thought about the distances of the stars from one another; for the stars were not created before the completion of the world. Therefore, **Kepler’s** opinion regarding the intentions of the Philosophers is incongruous, and consequently, the foundations of his *Mundane Harmony* <note>original: "Harmoniæ ejus mundanæ"; referring to Kepler’s work *Harmonice Mundi*</note> are very weak. But in truth, that intention of the Philosophers agrees in all things with the subject of my own Harmony. For in my opinion, light emerged with watery matter from **Chaos** or **Hyle** <term>Hyle: a Greek term for primordial, unformed matter</term>—the opaque and dark matter—just as if from a mother’s womb. This birth is best explained through the extraction of the **Tetrahedron** <term>Tetrahedron: a four-sided pyramid, which in Platonic philosophy represents the element of Fire</term>—representing fire or primary light—out of the **Cube**, which is the largest and most opaque body <note>the Cube represents Earth</note>. Does he <note>Kepler</note> not seem to acknowledge this very thing in these words from *Chapter 1, Book 5*: *The Cube is the outermost and largest, because it is primordial and contains the ratio of the whole*? What does this have to do with Saturn or its orbit, which is the smallest part of the whole?

We say, therefore, that just as the **Tetragon** <note>a four-sided figure or square</note>—which is also a Body—was born from the primordial Cube through a first and virginal birth, so too did the formal light first appear from the darkness with its watery body (or secondary matter); this was the work of the first day. For thus, according to the book of **Ecclesiasticus** <note>also known as the Wisdom of Sirach</note>, "Wisdom was created before all things," and thus duality was created within unity, possessing a **trigonal** <note>triangular</note> power within itself, through which the Trinity in unity operated in the world, retaining within itself the virtue of the **tetragon** (the four more universal elements).

Then we arrive at the second work of creation, in which the **Dodecahedron** <term>Dodecahedron: a twelve-sided solid representing the Heavens or the Universe</term> is extracted from the bowels of the Tetrahedron. For, once the luminous spirit was made on the first day, the heaven or "expanse" was created from its bowels on the second day. Because this was the fifth element <note>the "quintessence"</note>, its symbol is composed of **pentagons**. The number of angles of one plane of the Tetrahedron, multiplied by the sides, produced the sides of the heavens expressed through the figure of the Dodecahedron. For this reason, it is right to believe that the eighth heaven itself <note>the sphere of the fixed stars</note> was divided into twelve places by reason of its belt, which is called the **Zodiac**.

The work of the third day is the gathering of the waters into their place, the symbol of which is the **Icosahedron** <term>Icosahedron: a twenty-sided solid representing Water</term>. From its belly, the hidden air immediately flew out, the symbol of which is the **Octahedron** <term>Octahedron: an eight-sided solid representing Air</term>; for air is produced if water is refined. The residue of the dark Cube, however, settled into the Earth, and now receives the name of "fertile earth," which was previously called "empty earth" by **Moses**. Our physical history of the world introduces all these things, though the terms are changed for the sake of the subject, using physical names instead of mathematical ones. Is not all of this encompassed in the words of **Hermes Trismegistus** in his *Third Sermon*?

> *There was an infinite shadow in the abyss; moreover, water and an intellectual spirit were present in the chaos through divine power. Then the holy splendor blossomed, which led out the elements from beneath the sand and the moist nature.*

And when things were indistinct, the light parts soon flew up into the high region, while the heavy parts settled beneath the moist sand. Once things were distinguished and balanced, being carried by a fiery spirit, the heaven shone forth in seven circles.

By "infinite shadow," he understands (speaking in a geometric manner) the **Cube**, beyond which there is no further progression in the regular bodies; it is the primordial and most opaque body. When it was "pregnant," it was called **Chaos**, and it gave birth to water with a luminous spirit. By the power and action of that spirit, the universal water of heaven and the elements were produced in order—namely, one from another—and all things, carried by other fiery spirits, were distinguished. Whatever was foul and heavy from the cube settled entirely beneath the "moist sand." The wise man <note>Hermes</note> acknowledged that all this was done before the Planets were established in the celestial palace, as he seems to indicate with these words: *Once things were distinguished and balanced, being carried by a fiery spirit...* (here he teaches that the fiery spirit is the reason for the Music and mundane harmony) *...the heaven shone forth in seven circles.*

With these words, he clearly seems to teach that the mundane harmony was completed before the seven Planets appeared in the sky. Consequently, it is not the motion of the seven Planets, but that divine and fiery spirit revealed from Chaos—distinguishing all things and weighing them in the scales of justice, governing and sustaining every region of the world by its virtue—which existed before all things and was primordial, and therefore existed before the Planets. This spirit, I say, gives life, Harmony, and concord to the elements and things composed of elements, and by no means do the Planets or their motions do so.

We conclude, therefore, that these five bodies belong truly to my Harmony and according to the intentions of the Ancient Philosophers. He <note>Kepler</note>, however, has used them in a spurious way, and in every respect contrary to the thoughts of the said Philosophers, who undoubtedly had the mirror of truth before their eyes, by which they adapted themselves to the most accurate truth of that matter. In other things, except for the common rudiments of Music, we certainly agree on little or almost nothing. Insofar as he follows **Copernicus**, I do not disdain to embrace the ancient doctrine of **Ptolemy**. He yearns to measure nature and its unities by the identity of lines, and he grasps mundane Harmony through mathematical dimensions. I, however, attribute my natural harmony to the hidden actions of **form** within mundane matter. He establishes the planetary motions as the foundations of Harmony; I ascribe the power of my Harmony to the motion of the fiery spirit, swimming from the beginning everywhere through the waters of the world and stirring it with a diversity of harmonic proportions.

And so we see that there is very little agreement between us, because he misuses the true principles of the Philosophers and turns them toward a foreign meaning, while I bind myself as exactly as possible to the sayings of the Philosophers and the testimonies of the Holy Scriptures.

->DISCURS. ANALYT.<-

# Testimonies and authorities, both Philosophical and Divine, confirming or refuting the Harmony of *Johannes Kepler*.

In the first place, he made the five regular solids of **Geometry** the foundation of his *Harmony*: Next, he established the motion of the *Planets* as the cause of his harmony, which he seems to make twofold; namely, either from radiations onto the earth making various angles there—about which he speaks throughout Book 4—or from the eccentricity of the *Planets’* motion, or their variation from the Sun, about which he speaks everywhere in Book 5. And indeed, so that he may erect this Harmony upon more secure bases, he establishes the Earth as one of the *Planets*, and teaches that it is carried among the stars around an immobile Sun. He calls the Sun the center of the planetary orbits—of *Saturn*, *Jupiter*, *Mars*, *Earth*, *Venus*, and *Mercury*—and consequently calls it the center of the world in Book 4, Chapter 9. However, he wishes the Moon to have the Earth for its center. Finally, he seems to assert that the different intervals of these motions' harmony, from which the consonances are composed, took their origin from various proportions of the five regular solids of **Geometry**. For the harmony of the aspects <term>aspects: the specific angular distances between planets in astrology, such as a square (90°) or trine (120°)</term>, he uses his own invention; to confirm this in Chapter 7, Book 4, he makes the *Earth* an animal, and attributes to it a peculiar soul, which he says is accustomed to being ignited and provoked by the angles of *Planetary* radiations to stir up rains, tempests, and whatever meteors <term>meteors: in the 17th century, this referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, or lightning</term> occur in the regions of the air.

In the holy scriptures, no arguments are found regarding the wandering stars or their aspects for the purpose of exciting tempests and meteors; but those scriptures acknowledge that the Sun and Moon were created on the fourth day for this use: that the Sun indeed should bring daylight and rule over the day, while the Moon with the stars should perform this same duty for the night; likewise, that they might be signs for fixed times, for days and years (*Genesis 1*). And in *Psalm 104:19*, he established the Moon for fixed times, *the Sun knowing its setting*; and *Psalm 136:8, God made the Sun to obtain dominion over the day <note>original: "nocte" (night), but Fludd likely means "die" (day) based on the context of the verse and Psalm 136:9</note>.* He makes no mention here, therefore, of the aspects whose harmony he <note>Kepler</note> says causes so many alterations here on earth, but rather of the uses mentioned above. From this, it indicates that all the stars depending on the Sun and Moon themselves have no more power than that for which they were made from the beginning. I confess, indeed, with the most learned Philosophers—namely from the *Platonic Orpheus*—that the Sun is most rightly called the "right eye of the world"; and that *Heraclitus* said, not foolishly, that the Sun is as if it were the soul of the world; inasmuch as if it were removed, no vital breath or respiration would remain in it. Some truly wish it to be called the "Heart of Heaven," because, just as in the heart there exists a living fountain of blood moistening and watering the other members of the human body and infusing vital motion, so in the Sun there seems to be the vegetation and preservation of all things both inferior and superior, insofar as it is said to disperse heat and life everywhere by its light. And they make their reasoning in this way: because light is a simple act, converting all things to itself with life-giving heat, permeating all beings, and leading their qualities and virtues through all things, while dispersing darkness and gloom. And hence they say that *Phoebus* <note>Apollo, the Sun god</note> sits in the middle, shining with golden hair, and holds a scepter like a king and commander of the world. *Iamblichus* and *Proclus* affirm that all the virtues of the celestial beings are in him, and for this reason, they believe the soul of the world exists in the Sun, and they established that "sphere of equality" or "sphere of the soul" through which this soul passes. Although, I say, all these things can be rightly presented—and furthermore, that this same teaching was published in our book on the *Macrocosm*, namely regarding the Admirable effect of the Sun, and regarding its position and motion by reason of the intersections of pyramids <term>intersections of pyramids: Fludd’s theory that the universe is shaped by two overlapping pyramids—one of Light (descending from God) and one of Matter (ascending from Earth)</term>, and many other things—I would nevertheless wish the diligent Reader to rightly grasp and understand the sense of both the Philosophers' and my own discourses. Specifically, that all these things ought to be understood regarding the visible Sun, than which nothing in this world can be judged more worthy or noble in terms of the senses and sensible effects. But in truth, if we look a little more accurately with rational eyes into the sayings of the Philosophers, we will perceive that there is a certain invisible Sun of the world dwelling everywhere, which surpasses the visible Sun as much as the soul surpasses the body, or the spiritual surpasses the material. Hence, just as *Plato* used to call the celestial Sun the "visible son of God," so also the holy scriptures call Wisdom (which dwells and operates invisibly everywhere in the world) the invisible emanation of God. Wherefore the wiser of the Philosophers fell into this opinion: *From God* (they say) *arises something closest to Him*, namely Nature itself, which is that invisible fire from which *Zoroaster* and *Heraclitus of Ephesus* taught all things were generated. And in *Ecclesiastes 1*, we find that *Wisdom was created first*. And this is that fiery force which the *Spirit of the Lord* (which is fiery love), when it was carried over the waters, produced in them; without its vigor, nothing can be generated or endure. This is that inspiration inspired into created things by God when it was said at the birth of the world, *Increase and multiply*. This, I say, this Nature, invisibly bright, is that Sun which was not made on the fourth day, but from the beginning; by its virtue the world was completed through the mediation of the Word before any visible Sun was established in the heavens. It excels the visible Sun in virtue as much as the spiritual and invisible son of God excels that visible one of heaven. This secret Sun is present everywhere, and supplies life to everyone; it is present to all things night and day, without which nothing can live or subsist. Happy indeed is he who can uncover or make known that Nature; for by its presence, the mysteries of the whole world are revealed. And indeed, although this Wisdom-light is hidden of itself and

->TO THE KEPLERIAN APPENDIX.<-

...invisible, yet because of the most suitable reception of its rays from a well-polished body, and one most excellently disposed for this through its effect, it appears to our eyes. Through their reflection—as if from a well-prepared mirror adapted for the gathering of infinite rays into a single center—a heat is excited most certain to the touch. Such, therefore, is the composition of the solar body above all other stellar bodies; to which, on account of the extreme purity and unity of its substance, a polishing was given only to reveal the beam of the invisible Sun to worldly eyes, although not plainly in that manner in which it exists in its divine essence. And, as we perceive united force to be stronger—and for this reason the invisible rays of the Sun itself moving in the air, when collected into a single point of a burning mirror, burn or heat from a distance—so also, for the same reason, a portion of the rays of the invisible Sun dispersed everywhere penetrates into the center of the solar body. It enters as if into a subject most excellently disposed to receive so noble a form. By gathering into a single point or center from the middle, it first visibly illuminates the world, and by its circular reverberation, it emits everywhere actions and rays more subtle and visible. 

Whence this entire power is wrongly attributed to the celestial Sun, because the rays of light and heat are perceived by the senses to be derived from it, and not from **Wisdom** <note>original: *Sapientia*</note> lurking everywhere in the world, albeit invisibly on account of its purity, which is the fountain of solar light and the life of every thing. It is as if someone were to say that the burning mirror is the origin of fire and heat, and not the Sun. From this it is clear that the solar body is, as it were, that instrument of **Wisdom**, by which it renders its effects more sensible in the world; since in it, its rays and luminous nature delight more and are gathered in a certain way to cherish the lower creatures with its heat, but especially to rule during the day, just as the **Moon** (which the Philosophers call the *left eye of the world*) rules with the stars in the nighttime. 

Therefore, because of this so ample creeping-forth of divine light from the luminous or fiery fountain of the Spirit of **Wisdom**, and its so copious presence in the Sun, it was said that *the Lord could place his tabernacle in the Sun* <note>A reference to Psalm 19:4, which Fludd interprets as God dwelling within the solar light.</note>. And we acknowledge the Sun of heaven to be held among the most excellent creatures of the world and truly to be so, insofar as we know any thing claims as much of God for itself as it is capable of light. Therefore, the visible Sun has its nobility from that invisible one, which the Cabalists <note>Cabalists: Practitioners of Jewish mysticism, whose ideas about the "Soul of the World" heavily influenced Fludd's philosophy.</note> call the angel **Metatron** <note>original: *Metattron*; a high-ranking celestial being in mystical tradition, often seen as the mediator between God and the universe.</note> or the *soul of Messiah*, or the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>original: *Tetragrammati*; the four-letter Hebrew name of God (YHWH), considered the source of all cosmic power.</note> (which they have made the *world soul*), and which the sacred scriptures call **Wisdom**, or the *brightness and pure emanation of the power of God*. 

But truly, since that which makes something a certain way is itself more so, it follows that that **Wisdom**, which makes the luminous power of the Sun, is more noble and bright than the Sun itself. Wherefore, *since the orb of the lands* (as the Sage says in the Book of **Wisdom**, chapter 1) *is filled with His Spirit*, no less than the heaven, why should we not attribute the harmony of the elements and things composed of elements to the principle rather than the thing principled? He who at every moment and incessantly, though invisibly, acts and labors with His fiery love toward the generations, corruptions, mutations, alterations, and rotations of the elements and those things composed of them. We acknowledge, indeed, that there is the greatest power in the celestial Sun; but we attribute all of it to the unique soul of the world, operating as invisibly in the world as it does visibly in the Sun. Thus, by the gathering of light and the fiery nature expanded through the air, we see terrestrial fire and flame—nay, even lightning and flashes—to be procreated, which again vanish by expansion. And this indeed the more skillful of the Philosophers acknowledged when they uttered this saying: *There is nothing in the very circle of the firmament, besides the soul, which bears a greater likeness of God than the Sun and its light*: by which they seem to argue that the invisible soul of the world is far more noble than the Sun or its light.

And although the nobility of this subject and the sublimity of the divine nature persuaded me to weave these things together with a more polished thread of speech, yet according to my custom (for such, I confess, is the thinness of my wit), I am compelled here to walk in pedestrian speech <note>Pedestrian speech: Fludd is apologizing for using plain, non-poetic language to explain these complex ideas.</note>, so that I may explain the reason and origin of the creature's power to the world. By this, I may open the difference between the Heathen idolaters of this world—who are accustomed to worship the *hosts of heaven*, neglecting the true God—and true Christians, who adore the true **Wisdom**, or the power of the **Tetragrammaton**.

Here, then, is the title we can attribute to the visible Sun: namely, that it is the visible seat of the world soul, just as the entire mundane spirit is the invisible seat of its universal soul. Consequently, the **Harmony of the world** proceeds from that soul or primary luminous Nature—namely, **Wisdom**, which is the first act of the world—and not from a secondary one alone, except insofar as Nature is accustomed to accelerate her effects in that palace of hers. For Nature is hidden, like a bellows-blower, while the Sun is like the Organ, and the chief instrument of the world, and the pipe through which the sensible Harmony is seen and perceived by its effect, although it uses infinite other imperceptible instruments in the lower parts to perfect its operations in the world, as may be seen everywhere in the sacred letters and will appear more broadly in what follows.

### ANALYTICAL DISCOURSE
<meta>catchword: -dom</meta>

...of the Planets, or by the soul of the earth being stirred up. We also find that God renews the face of the earth—*Psalm 104:30*—not the Sun or the motion of the heavens, though this is commonly said. In the same way, we are taught in *Leviticus 25:21* that God is the cause and author of the fertility and yield of the earth. And we learn that the sterility of the earth happens because God shuts the heaven—*Deuteronomy 11:17*.

But he <note>Referring to Kepler or the conventional astronomer.</note> will perhaps respond with that old axiom: *that God acts in the highest heavens by the ordered execution of a star.* And indeed, I would have thought the same myself, had I not understood that *the Throne of Jehovah is in the heavens, but his footstool is on the earth;* unless, I say, I had perceived from the holy scriptures that the *Spirit of Wisdom fills all things by its lucid act, and is present everywhere to the world—Wisdom 1*—of which indeed there is no number—*Psalm 147:4–5*.

I would have thought that all events of the lower world depend on the motions of the stars, and that storms and <term>meteors <note>original: *meteora* — in Fludd's time, this referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just space rocks.</note></term> are stirred by them, had I not known from the testimony of *Job 28* that this Wisdom is hidden from the eyes of all living things; whose path God alone knows, *who made a weight for the winds, and weighed the waters by measure, placed a law for the rains, and a path for the sounding storms;* unless I had recognized that this Wisdom, present everywhere, is far more powerful than the Sun and Moon and all the stars; since by its power Jehovah founded the earth and established the heavens—*Psalm 14* <note>Fludd likely refers here to the sentiment found in Proverbs 3:19.</note>—and whose *Being is such that it is a breath of the power of God, and a pure emanation of his glory, an act, finally, whose image is far more beautiful than the Sun, and above every arrangement of the stars—Wisdom 7.* 

Unless I had known Wisdom to be older than every creature, inasmuch as she was ordained from eternity before the earth was made. She placed a decree for the sea, established the foundations of the earth, strengthened the fountains, fitted the heavens and firmed them, and established the circuit upon the face of the abyss. Unless I had perceived from the holy scriptures that *God through this, His Wisdom, sent forth snow like wool, and scattered frost like ashes, cast down His ice like morsels, and by this same Word melted them again, and as soon as He blows His wind, made them fluid—Psalm 147.* Unless I had believed, I say, that the thick clouds were God's chariot, which goes upon the wings of the wind—*Psalm 104:3*—and that they had light from His tabernacle, which illuminates those things going in a circuit, by which He might do all those things that are prepared upon the surface of the world, whether for a scourge or for kindness—*Job 37:12*. Unless I had found from many other places in the Holy Bible that *the treasures of Jehovah are the storehouse of snow and clouds and thunders:*

I would perhaps believe that either the stars could produce all these things, or that the soul of the earth, stirred by anger, could perform such things. But why should I search for such secrets of nature from the opinions of Aristotle or others, or attribute mysteries of such great importance to the earth by following the authority of <term>Pagans <note>original: *Ethnicorum* — referring to non-Christian classical philosophers like Aristotle.</note></term>, when we are taught in *chapter 3 of the Prophet Baruch* that it is not fitting to desert the fountain of all Wisdom and seek the art and science of understanding in Pagan authors, as the Agarenes did, and those who seek in Teman; since they never recognized true Wisdom? To what end should I assign any faith to Pagans, who place the admirable operations of nature in the stars as agents and the earth as the patient, and say they emanate from there, while I would reject the holy scriptures or the fountain of all Wisdom? 

For indeed, unless Wisdom reveals itself to us, can anyone find the reason for storms and meteors and the motions of the ancient heavens? *Have you entered,* says God, *into the treasures of the snow, or do you have inspection of the treasures of the hail? Job 38:22. Who disposed the measures of the earth, seeing that you are knowing? Or who stretched the line upon it? Upon what do its sunken bases rest, or who laid its cornerstone? Job 38:18.*

Indeed the works of God are wonderful and ample, which He made in Wisdom—*Psalm 103:24*—to the knowledge of which there is no access except through that same Wisdom which made them. For to the wise man—not the worldly, but the <term>Theosophical <note>original: *Theosophico* — referring to a wisdom derived directly from God rather than through human observation or logic.</note></term>—is given the knowledge of the certain constitution of the world: the virtues of the elements; the beginning, middle, and end of times; the changes and solstices; the varieties of seasons and storms; the circuit of the year; the positions of the stars; the natures of living creatures; the furies of wild beasts; the forces of winds; the thoughts of men; the differences of plants; and the powers of roots; finally, the acquisitions of this knowledge are revealed to him by a hidden power—*Wisdom 7:17*. 

This, therefore, is the true star of the sacred fountain, whose *house is supported by seven columns;* these are the seven true Planets; from the observation and presence of which true Astrology is drawn out, while the adulterated kind is relegated to eternal oblivion. This is that true worldly Harmony, constantly striking the strings of the soul with concordant or discordant proportions according to the merit of the subject. This is she herself who turns the heavens and leads the Planets, and inspires in them a slow or swift soul according to her will; when she ceased from her office, *the Sun and Moon stood still in the midst of heaven and did not hasten to the sunset for the space of one day—Joshua 10:13.* By her retrograde motion the Sun went backward, when in the time of Hezekiah the shadow of the sundial was drawn back by ten degrees. 

What therefore do either the Pagans or their disciples know, to whom this Wisdom is unknown? Since, as the Royal Prophet witnesses in *Psalm 92:7, a brutish and foolish man does not understand the works of God.* And *Psalm 88:13: The works of God cannot be known in the dark.* Therefore the presence of the splendor of Wisdom is required, so that we may be illuminated by it; without which, as *Job 5:9* witnesses, *there is no searching out the great works of God, so wonderful and innumerable are they.* Thus in *Job 42:3* and *Psalm 136:6* we find that the works of God are wonderful and beyond man's grasp; and of the mysteries of the clouds it is said in *Job 37:15: Who knows the wonderful works of God, perfect in knowledge, concerning the balancings of the thick cloud?* 

It is divine wisdom to which we must recur for the knowledge of the true secrets of Nature, and not human wisdom, which is dull and infected by vain opinions. Therefore there is need for the assistance of the divine Spirit, who teaches all things—*Psalm 143:10*—which Spirit is indeed Wisdom herself, who speaks thus of herself: *I, Wisdom, dwell with prudence, and find out knowledge of witty inventions—Proverbs 8:12.* This spirit is indeed the Teacher of the true art; by which we are taught in *Exodus 28:3, 31:2, and 35:30.* For the learned and wise of this world are foolish before God—*Matthew 11:25.* He, therefore, who seeks true Wis-

### TO THE KEPLERIAN APPENDIX
<note>This refers to Robert Fludd's rebuttal to Johannes Kepler’s *Harmonice Mundi* (The Harmony of the World, 1619). Fludd, a Rosicrucian and physician, favored a mystical, "divine" harmony over Kepler’s mathematical and astronomical calculations.</note>

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 1:18</margin>
<margin>Wisdom 9:17</margin>
<margin>Proverbs 3</margin>
<margin>Job 28</margin>
...[they have acquired] Wisdom, upon these very people understanding pours out science and knowledge like a rain shower, and exalts them with glory. God sends this spirit from the highest places to give understanding to men, so they may know his secret counsels and his hidden works. Hence in Proverbs 30:1, Wisdom is called the "knowledge of the holy." And this is the reason why she is estimated as more precious than carbuncles <note>original: *Carbunculis* — rubies or deep red gemstones.</note>. Neither shall gold be given for her, nor shall her price be weighed in silver or precious stones. 

From this, indeed, comes the greatest madness of men: to speculate upon such secrets of nature and the wonderful works of God without His Spirit. It is a much greater madness to boast that they clearly understand these things and can demonstrate them through common Geometry. They claim to understand the harmony of His miraculous works—such as the positions of the stars and the logic of their motions—so exactly that they do not fear to condemn the writings of other ancient Authors to whom the vision of truth appeared, all so that they might impose a more glittering face upon their own inventions. 

As for me, this indeed suffices: to know that God, who commands the stars, is closer to the stars [than we are], and that His spirit blows where it wills without any hindrance from the stars or any evident obstacle from their radiations. I know, I say, that He Himself is closer to the earth than the stars are, and that His wisdom governs all things as He wills and is present to all. Whoever obtains this Wisdom will truly be the master of both types of Astronomy <note>Fludd distinguishes between physical astronomy (tracking stars) and spiritual astronomy (understanding God's influence).</note>; without His presence, all Astrologers are blind. For such a man shall rule over the stars, because he is governed by a higher principle, which has made the stars and the elements themselves subject to him. As a true emperor of the heavens, he will possess dominion over all things until the very end; for, just as all things were made through Him, so also shall all things be transfigured through Him. Thus, indeed, this is that true Wisdom which is, was, and shall be, and which reigns, has reigned, and shall reign forever. We conclude, therefore, that this foundation of his <note>Referring to Kepler.</note> "worldly harmony" is a mere fiction, and in no way to be approved or esteemed by Christians.

<margin>chapter 3</margin>
<margin>book 2 prop. 25 & book 5 chapter 3</margin>
<margin>Axiom 4 book 5</margin>
<margin>Wisdom 7</margin>
Let us therefore arrive at his second species of Music. In order to direct it toward the goal of his intention, he first makes the earth a "star" <note>original: *sidus* — used here to mean a wandering star or planet.</note> and has it move around an immobile Sun. To support this side, he has Aristarchus of Samos the Pythagorean, Copernicus, and Tycho Brahe; but against him, he has almost everyone skilled in Astrology and natural philosophy, except those who, led by the imaginary opinion of the Magnet, imagine that the earth itself turns upon Magnetic poles. 

The followers of Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the ancient proponent of the Geocentric (earth-centered) model.</note> are rejected, and they in turn reject these inventions and hold them as trifles. Hermes Trismegistus, Plato, and Aristotle placed the earth as immobile and the center of the world, making it the place of rest. No one, whether among the Ancients or the moderns, ever doubted whether the sun was mobile or the earth immobile. Yet all are deceived, according to those who—taught by a "new experiment"—affirm that the earth is a star and moves around an immobile sun between the orbits of Mars and Venus, as do Copernicus and Kepler. 

In fact, informed by experience, we find that calculations according to the doctrine of Ptolemy have not strayed far from the goal or path of truth. Let us therefore approach the Sacred Oracles <note>The Bible.</note> so that we may diligently inquire into their opinions on this matter. First, we ask: how is it possible for the immobile Sun to be the source of motion, when it is the unique attribute of God to move all things while remaining immobile Himself? Second, how can the Sun be the source of motion, unless by "the Sun" he understands the very Wisdom of God, which alone is more mobile and swifter than all moving things?

<margin>Deuteronomy 10:14</margin>
<margin>Nehemiah 1:7</margin>
<margin>Job 28</margin>
<margin>Proverbs 22</margin>
<margin>Job 26, verse 7</margin>
<margin>Job 38, verse 4</margin>
Far be it from us Christians to ascribe an attribute of God to a creature. If the earth is also a mobile star in heaven, there would be only a single "heaven" in which the body of the earth moves alongside the bodies of the Planets. But if this is so, why did Moses say, "The Heaven of heavens belong to the God of Gods"? And Nehemiah 1:7 says: "Jehovah made the heavens of heavens and all their host; the earth and whatever is in it," etc. 

Furthermore, if the earth moves around the center of the Sun and receives its motion from the Sun (the source of motion), what did that same earth do when it was created on the third day, before the placement of the Sun in the heavens <note>In Genesis, the earth is created on the third day, but the sun, moon, and stars are created on the fourth.</note>? Did it rest? Or if it moved, from what source did it receive such motion, or around what fixed center? By the proportion of what regular body did it make its motion, or with which star did it resonate in harmonic consensus? 

It is certainly difficult to answer, since the Sun and stars did not yet exist. But he will perhaps respond that the Sun was a congregation of light rays dispersed through the vast cavity of heaven, and consequently, the earth could move by the power of that act. But we reply that it is necessary for such a motion to be outside the proportion of harmony, because it lacks a certain center around which it might move, as well as any other consonance to which it might relate by proportion. 

By similar reasoning, we say that if the harmony of the world depends on the daily motions of the Planets, it follows that before the placement of the stars in heaven, there was no harmony in the world—which was completed on the third day. And yet, the holy scriptures acknowledge a harmony which Wisdom (or the Word) placed in the world before the creation of the stars; for she "made a weight for the winds and weighed the waters by measure." She fitted and strengthened the heavens, established the circuit upon the surface of the abyss, fortified the clouds above, strengthened the fountains, and set a decree for the sea. She disposed the measures of the earth and extended a line upon it, arranging it "over nothing." She most skillfully laid its cornerstone, extended the North over the sea, and made the heaven revolve upon the North pole.

### ANALYTICAL DISCOURSE
<page-num>44</page-num>

This is indeed the most exact Harmony of nature, which God administered in the creation of worldly matter and its frameworks; this is that present harmony by which the parts of the world were so linked together in creation and are always preserved in the same consensus. But perhaps someone will say that circular motion was not in the heavens at that time, nor was there any harmony in it. But this is also completely false: For, says Wisdom <margin>Sirach 24</margin>, *I alone have compassed the circuit of the heavens* (that is, without the help or presence of the stars) *and have walked in the depths of the abyss, in the waves of the sea, and in all the earth.* <note>Fludd quotes the Vulgate version of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:5, personifying Wisdom as the force that moved the heavens before physical objects existed.</note> Thus, in its harmony, this fiery love established the heavens at that time. Who would also doubt that Wisdom itself fulfilled the turns of the stars in the heavens and on the earth before the stars were positioned in the sky? And does it seem probable that this power of the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God (YHWH), often used by Renaissance occultists to represent the divine spark in nature.</note>, this unique life of all things, would rest and be idle after the creation of the stars? She who is indeed the true source of motion, more mobile than all things that move? On the contrary, this is that divine light which I signified through my **formal pyramid** <note>A recurring diagram in Fludd's work representing the descent of spiritual "form" into "matter."</note>, which was unequally present in worldly matter, and which matter embraced more or less according to its greater or lesser dignity; the world is filled with its rays through invisible means, without which worldly matter would be reduced to nothing.

As for the mobility of the earth, or the immobility of the Sun, insofar as the Sacred Scriptures seem to deny this entirely in the most express words, I see no reason why we should adhere to this opinion of Copernicus or his disciple Kepler, since the Scriptures are the source and origin of truth. Regarding the nature of the earth in its mobility or firmness, we read in <margin>Psalm 104:5</margin> *that Jehovah founded the earth upon its bases, that it should not be moved forever or eternally.* Similarly, regarding the property of the Sun, which they themselves called immobile, it speaks in these words in <margin>Psalm 19:5</margin>: *The Sun itself, like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, rejoiced as a giant to run its course; its going forth is from the end of the heaven, and its circuit even to the end of it.* Similarly, in <margin>Psalm 104:19</margin> it is said *that the Sun knows its setting;* and in <margin>Psalm 113</margin>, *From the rising of the Sun, etc.* <margin>Psalm 104:22</margin>. When God forbids the Sun, *it does not rise.* <margin>Job 9:7</margin> <note>The original text cites Job 28:10, but the quote "it does not rise" refers to Job 9:7.</note>. And <margin>Joshua 10:13</margin> records for us *that the Sun and Moon stood still in the midst of heaven for nearly a whole day.* Similarly, we find that in the time of King Hezekiah, God made the Sun go backward; indeed, the shadow of the dial was moved back by ten degrees. Furthermore, in <margin>Ecclesiastes 1:4-6</margin>, where both the earth and the Sun are discussed, we receive this kind of discourse: *A generation passes away and a generation comes; but the earth stands forever; the Sun rises and sets, and returns to its place, and being reborn there, it circles through the south and turns to the north, the spirit goes circling through all things, and returns to its circuits.* What, then, could be plainer to prove that the earth rests while the Sun moves? What? Does Johannes [Kepler] think that the Prophets were ignorant of the secret and mystical motions of the heavens, or that the calculation of the times and motions of the Planets was hidden from them, such that they did not know the difference between the mobility and immobility of the Sun and the earth? Truly, we are taught in <margin>1 Chronicles 12:32</margin> *that from the tribe of Issachar there were those who knew the knowledge of the times, to teach the Israelites what ought to be done; that is, that they might prescribe for them the hours and days of choice.* And in <margin>Esther 1:13</margin>: *Wherefore the king saying to the wise men who knew the times, etc.* From which it can be seen that if those skilled astronomers of that age had known such a mystery of motions, without a doubt such a great error would not have crept into the divine Bible.

Finally, regarding the intervals having the proportion of the **five regular bodies** <note>The Platonic solids (cube, tetrahedron, etc.). Kepler’s *Mysterium Cosmographicum* proposed that these shapes dictated the distances between the planets.</note>, by which the orbit of one Planet is distant from another, this reasoning of its dimensions seems indeed to be most distant from the true harmony of the world, since before the creation of the Planets, the world had its complete harmony, as was declared above. And we say that there is not a material proportion, but a formal one, which constitutes the physical dimension of the world’s harmony. For it is indeed the divine spirit that moves and impels the Planets by various proportions of actions, both by natural and artificial motion; even though we said natural motion occurs more through the resistance and reaction of the body than by mere spiritual motion, which is why it is slower. That the spirit moves a Planet was said above from <margin>Ecclesiastes 1</margin>: *The spirit goes circling through all things, etc.* But what more shall I say? The Philosophers themselves, whom he seems to cite for the discovery of those bodies, in no way support his opinion; for they apply the use of these five bodies to the five elements of the world, whereas he applies them to the Planets and their distances. You see, therefore, how weak the foundations of the Author of the *Harmony of the World* <note>Johannes Kepler</note> are, and how remote from the testimony of the Bible. And yet he himself did not hesitate to burst forth into such words as these <margin>Proposition 25, Book 2</margin>: *Nothing could seem more plausible than that the intervals of those six celestial orbits were taken from the five figures by the Creator, in this order: that the Cube is conceived in the mind between the orbits of Saturn and Jupiter, etc.* This fiction of his, I say, he attributes to the Creator of the fabric, ignorant of how difficult a thing it is to find such secrets of the heaven without the help of the divine spirit. Hence it is said in <margin>Job 38:37</margin>: *Who shall declare the account of the heavens? etc.* For according to <margin>Wisdom 9:15-17</margin>, *Because of the burden of the soul in a troublesome body, we hardly guess those things that are on earth; but who shall search out those things that are in the heavens, and who shall know the counsel of God, unless God has given Wisdom and sent his holy spirit from the holy heavens?* From this, therefore, one may see that those Astronomical demonstrations, and the unities of his Geometry, as well as the most harmonious intervals of his world harmony—even numbers broken down into the smallest parts—are very unstable and published rather as opinion than confirmed by the truth of the matter.

Why, indeed, shall we speak many words about the vain Astrology against which Pico della Mirandola <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494), an Italian Renaissance philosopher who wrote a famous critique of divinatory astrology.</note>, in every kind of learning...

### TO THE KEPLERIAN APPENDIX
<page-num>45</page-num>
<meta>catchword: Testimo-</meta>

...renowned, has it become so weakened in times past? Tell me, why do you refer all things to the heavens, oh Astrologer destitute of true wisdom? What do you actually recognize regarding the natures of the stars and the motions of the Planets? And what do you devise concerning the most hidden mystery of the **Worldly Harmony** <note>original: *Harmonicæ mundanæ*; referring to Kepler's book *Harmonice Mundi* (The Harmony of the World).</note> arising from them, when you are in no way able to predict the powers and properties of even the smallest earthly thing? Why do you observe the stars and the constellations and their motion—or rather, why do you lie about them—when you cannot even grasp a single earthly particle by measurement? What is more ridiculous, what is more absurd, than to think one can happen upon the figures of the eighth heaven <note>The "eighth heaven" or firmament was the sphere of the fixed stars in the traditional geocentric model.</note> through the wandering application of the stars? What extraordinary virtue do you believe such imagined images possess? What of the triplicities, the "smoky," "bright," or "empty" degrees, the Masculine with the Feminine; what harmony or amazing events do they bring if the stars bear their aspects? <note>Fludd is mocking the technical jargon of traditional astrology, such as "triplicities" (groups of three zodiac signs) and "aspects" (angles between planets).</note> And what truth or virtue do other such empty things of that kind display? Although such motions, the natures of the stars, and the various adaptations of things among themselves may seem to have some significance, I am nonetheless persuaded that a man cannot properly distinguish them unless they are shown to him from heaven by some miracle, as is declared in the book of Wisdom. 

Porphyry <note>A 3rd-century Neoplatonist philosopher.</note> vainly said that if anyone knew the figure of their birth and the "Lord of the figure," they would find their **Daemon** or personal genius and through it be released from the fate of their birth. But, he adds, it is impossible to know that figure or to find this genius because the rules of Astronomy and Astrology are incomprehensible and uncertain. Yet Iamblichus <note>A student of Porphyry who focused more on theurgy and divine intervention.</note> says that the Daemon is neither known nor given by that birth chart; otherwise, it would not release us from the fate of birth, but would instead give us over to a more ancient and higher principle—that is, to the spirit of the gods. He asserts, following Porphyry's opinion, that innumerable rules of Astrology and doubts about nativities <note>original: *genesi*</note> are tossed about. From this, it appears that knowledge of these things cannot be had. Therefore, he believes that the most certain truth concerning the stars can only be obtained through **divine prophecy**—that is, what is given to men by the spirit of wisdom. Once possessed of this, we have no need at all for the enumeration of rules and artificial predictions. Furthermore, he adds that it is impossible for a man to demonstrate knowledge of this through mathematical science, since different opinions are carried among us, some contradicting others. For in every science and art, because of dissenting opinions, we would be forced to say that no true knowledge exists. So much for Iamblichus; I have dealt with these matters abundantly in the 13th book of my *Treatise on Horoscopes*. <note>original: *Tract. meo de Genethliac.*</note> 

From this, the vanity of the mathematical sciences appears because of their corruption. Saint Jerome also mocks Astrologers and "Calculators" <note>original: *Genethliacos* and *Mathematici*. In the late Roman period, "Mathematici" was a common term for astrologers.</note> in this way:

> These are they who lift themselves up against the knowledge of God; promising themselves a fabricated knowledge of everything that happens in the world, they refer it to the rising and setting of the stars. These are they who are commonly called "Mathematicians," who think human affairs are ruled by the course of the stars and the gliding of the constellations; and while they were promising safety to others, they were ignorant of their own punishments.

These are the words of Jerome. But for a moment, I pray, let us attend to the speech of the Prophet Daniel, who teaches how frivolous it is to practice astrology in the absence of wisdom (Chapter 2, verse 27):

> The mystery which the king asks, the Wise men, Magi, Soothsayers, and Diviners are unable to show to the king; but there is a God in heaven revealing mysteries, who has indicated them to you, etc.

Even the ethnic Egyptians themselves confessed this, according to Genesis 41:38:

> They called all the Magi of Egypt and all its Wise men, etc. And there was no one who could interpret the dream for Pharaoh.

Then it follows: *Are not interpretations from God?* (Genesis 40:8). *Can we find a man like this* (referring to Joseph) *in whom the Spirit of the Gods is?* (Genesis 41:38). *Since the Gods have made all things known to you, there is no one so prudent and wise as you.* (Genesis 41:39). And in Exodus 8, when Moses surpassed the Magi in the production of signs, the Magi themselves confessed with these words: *This is the finger of God.* Hence, the Sage says in the passage cited above:

> Who shall investigate the things that are in heaven, and who shall know the counsels of God? Unless God has given wisdom and sent his holy spirit from the highest places.

Who also, by their own nature, is so wise in mind that they could find—through Geometric dimensions and the identity of lines—the reason how the earth is suspended over nothing? Or the dimension of the cornerstone which the Creator laid at the foundation of the earth? Or what dimension did God use when he made a weight for the winds and weighed the waters by measure, and set a law for the rains and a path for the sounding storms? Truly, Wisdom understands these things (Job 28:25). *Have you,* says God, *considered even the breadths of the earth? Tell me, if you know all that.* (Job 38:18). 

Does **Joannes** <note>Johannes Kepler.</note> really think that a harmony of this kind was made by the Creator according to the standard of the **regular bodies** <note>The five Platonic solids, which Kepler famously used to explain the spacing of the planetary orbits in his *Mysterium Cosmographicum*.</note>, or composed by his quantitative lines? Not in the least! Rather, it was made by an invisible power, most full of divinity. For it is certain that the worldly harmony—indeed, the entire universe—is sustained by the wings of Wisdom; without Her divine Geometry, not even for a moment could the world endure in its state. Let not Joannes boast of himself, then, or of his *Astronomical Harmony*, nor let him think that any certain rules exist in Astrology or Astronomy that are not contaminated by the corruption of human opinions. We conclude, therefore, that where the foundations are weak—cast into a fabled land and dissenting from the truth—it is impossible for the entire building not to be scattered by the wind and the rain.

### ANALYTICAL DISCOURSE

### Philosophical and Theological Testimonies supporting our Worldly Harmony.

First of all, I proposed for the construction of my **Macrocosm** <note>The "Macrocosm" refers to the entire universe as a "great world," mirroring the "Microcosm" or human being.</note> two contraries: namely, **Darkness** and **Light**. I held that shapeless darkness existed within the divine power before the construction of the world. But truly, since the function of darkness was to deform and obscure, just as the function of light was to form and illuminate, I have said that these two principles are contrary by nature. To **Darkness** (or shapeless matter) belong the potential companions of cold, weight, and rest; whereas the associates and effects of **Light** are **Heat**, motion, and lightness. For just as the divine power is said to be "contrary" to its own act—because it is hidden, invisible, at rest, and "nothing" in relation to us, insofar as its absence leaves all things shapeless—the divine act differs from that power in every way as far as we are concerned. Through this act, and within it, God is revealed to the world, making all visible things out of nothing; for His presence gives form to everything. Hence, just as God, by His divine power, contracted His rays into Himself to hide His Majesty (whereby all things were shapeless and overwhelmed by darkness), so for His revelation He dilated Himself. Thus, the darkness was driven from His lucid presence toward the edge of the sphere—that is, from the highest peak of the heavens down to their lowest center. Therefore, the roots or bases of my two **pyramids** <note>Fludd famously illustrated the universe as two overlapping pyramids: one of "Formal Light" descending from God, and one of "Material Darkness" ascending from the Earth.</note> are physically through God, from God, and toward God: namely, the dark matter from the divine power, which once purified ascends toward God; and the more it tends upward, the more it participates, step by step, in the light. 

For the confirmation of this opinion of ours, we have not only the composite of the Philosophers of the highest divinity, but also the testimonies of the Holy Scriptures themselves. For **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure viewed as the author of the *Hermetica*, ancient texts on philosophy and magic.</note> says in the *Pimander*, book 3: *An infinite shadow was in the abyss, while water and a thin spirit were within the Chaos: but a holy splendor flourished, which led forth the elements from beneath the sand and the moist nature; and although they were indistinct, the light ones soon flew up into the high region, while the heavy ones settled beneath the moist sand.* <note>original: "Umbra infinita in abysso, aqua autem & spiritus tenuis in Chaos inerant..."</note> Here he seems to recognize that water and the thin spirit were potentially within the darkness, and that heavy things submerged in darkness (that is, the Earth) settled in the center upon the appearance of the divine splendor beneath the "moist sand." Furthermore, that same author says in the first sermon of the *Pimander*: *The Divine Mind in its power changed form at the beginning and revealed the universe suddenly.* This means that from the Mind of divine power was made the Mind in divine act; that is, from a hidden God was made a manifest God, and He migrated from the **dark Aleph** into the **bright Aleph**. <note>The Hebrew letter Aleph (א) was used by Christian Cabalists to represent the unity of God; Fludd distinguishes between God's hidden, dark state and His revealed, creative light.</note> From this it follows: *For I beheld a certain immense spectacle, namely all things converted into a light, exceedingly sweet and pleasant; which delighted me wonderfully as I watched.* (This, therefore, is the true symbol of the **Tetrahedron** <note>A four-sided solid; in Platonic philosophy, the tetrahedron represents the element of fire and light.</note> or of universal fire and Light according to the opinion of the Pythagoreans and Platonists, brought forth from the **Cube** or Chaos.) 

Then he proceeds thus: *A little later, a certain horrifying shadow glided beneath in an oblique revolution, being then exaggerated by an ineffable countenance into a moist nature.* Here, then, the water is separated from the deformity of the darkness, and the second matter of all things comes forth into the light. Wherefore he says in the fifth book of the *Pimander*: *Shall I sing your praises in those things which you have brought into the light out of darkness, or in those things which still lie hidden, stored away in the secret womb?* <note>original: "Cantabo ne laudes tuas in iis quae in lucem è tenebris eruisti, an in iis, quae latent adhuc arcano sinu recondita?"</note> That is, in the water already brought into act, or that which is still hidden in the divine power and the deformed womb of **Hyle** <note>term: <term>Hyle</term> (from Greek *hýlē*); a philosophical term for "primordial matter" that has no form of its own.</note> after the manner of things hidden. Then he descends, and so proceeds from the two roots—namely the light and water created—toward the **square** or the four elements, saying: *Truly, the Word standing by the moist nature* (here he denotes the union of the Word with the waters) *cherished it; and from the vitals of the moist nature a pure and light fire immediately flew out and sought the heights* (And Genesis 1 says: *The Spirit of the Lord was moved over the waters*). *The light air, obeying the spirit, took the middle region between the fire and the water: but the Earth and water lay so mixed together that the face of the earth, overwhelmed by the waters, appeared nowhere.* These are his words. 

From this, the true mystery of the **five regular bodies** <note>The "Platonic Solids" (tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron) which were believed to be the geometric building blocks of the universe.</note> is clear. For out of the universal, shapeless water (of which, and through which, after its purification and information, as St. Peter testifies in his second Epistle 3:5-6: *The heavens were of old and the earth, consisting by the Word of God*)—or rather, out of its vitals, a pure and light fire leapt forth. Then, next, the air appeared in the middle place between the divided or sublunary water and the fire; indeed, the earth and water were so mixed together as thick water with thin, or dregs with a purer substance. 

We see, therefore, that we have three things as a root: namely, **God’s power** (which is darkness), **God’s act** (which is light), and **the waters brought into act** (or power brought into act, or created waters, or waters mixed with light). This mixture was created from a duality consisting within an uncreated unity. And in these consists that primary **Harmony of the World**, according to whose pattern the world was later completed; its proportion is as 1 to 2, and 2 to 3, and 3 to 4. For 3 reflecting back into 1 represents the number four (the **Quaternary**); in which number the letters of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH (יהוה).</note> are most exactly found. The remaining consonances, which concur for the Harmonic disposition of the world according to the pattern of these proportions, are composed from these, if we consider the matter exactly—such as the **Disdiapason** <note>term: <term>Disdiapason</term>; a double octave, representing a 4:1 ratio.</note>, the **Diapente with Diapason** <note>term: <term>Diapente</term>; a musical fifth (3:2 ratio). Combined with an octave, it creates a 3:1 ratio.</note>, the **Diapason with Diatessaron** <note>term: <term>Diatessaron</term>; a musical fourth (4:3 ratio). Combined with an octave, it creates an 8:3 ratio.</note>, etc. Regarding these consonances of the divine Harmony, we have discussed them clearly in our little book *On Divine Numbers*. Truly valid testimonies from many places of the Holy Scriptures concerning these things of the structure...

This spirit of the water, thus tinged, was afterwards called "created light." And, just as form is mixed into every creature so that it may exist, so also divine light is present in every structure, lest a "vacuum" exist within it; for without it, it could not subsist for even a moment of time. ### Philosophical and Theological Testimonies Supporting our Worldly Harmony.

In the first place, I have supposed two opposites for the construction of my **Macrocosm** <note>The "Great World" or the universe as a whole, mirroring the "Microcosm" of man.</note>, namely **Darkness** and **Light**. I have proposed that shapeless darkness existed within the divine power before the construction of the world. Insofar as the powerful companion of Darkness (or shapeless matter) was cold, weight, and rest, the associate and effect of Light was Heat, motion, and lightness. For in this way, even the divine power is said to be "contrary" to its own act, because it is hidden, invisible, and at rest—being nothing as far as we are concerned, insofar as it deforms all things by its absence. 

In contrast, the divine act differs from its power in every way regarding us, insofar as through it and in it, God is revealed to the world, stirring all visible things out of nothing. For by His presence, He gives form to all things. Hence, just as God, through His divine power and the hiding of His Majesty, contracted His rays into Himself (whereby all things were shapeless and overwhelmed by darkness), so for His revelation He dilated Himself. Thus, the darkness is driven away from His lucid presence—from the highest peak of the heavens down to their lowest center—toward the outer edge of the periphery. 

Therefore, the roots or bases of both of my pyramids <note>Fludd famously used two intersecting pyramids to diagram the universe: one of Light (descending from God) and one of Matter (ascending from the center of the Earth).</note> are physically through God, by God, and toward God: namely, the dark matter from the divine power which, once purified, ascends toward God; and the more it tends upward, the more it participates, step by step, in the light. To confirm this opinion of ours, we have not only the concept of the highest divinity held by the Philosophers, but also the testimony of the Holy Scriptures themselves.

*For Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with a complex system of philosophy and magic; Fludd treats him as a peer to Moses.</note> says in the third mandate: "An infinite shadow was in the abyss, but water and a thin spirit were within the Chaos. Then a holy splendor flourished, which led the elements forth from under the sand and the moist nature. We must establish the foundations or bases of our worldly Harmony. For in the first place, we find in **Genesis 1** support for the "Potential First Matter" of the world—the shapeless darkness, or the horrific and lethal shadows. Out of these, the Creator, by the power of the radiant Word, revealed the foundations of the world's waters and brought them into the light. We find there that the earth was "void and empty," or desolate; that is, no light actually existed within the darkness to give it form, but rather the darkness was destitute of any actual presence of God. But conversely, after this earth was created on the third day and filled with the act of God, it is said in the same place (verse 10): **And He saw that it was good.** That is, it participated in the divine goodness and act, without which nothing is good, and all things are called empty and desolate. Thus, the fertility of that created (that is, "actuated") earth followed in the budding of green herbs and the production of seeds, by reason of the divine power which it now possessed.

Furthermore, it follows at the beginning of the same chapter: **And darkness was upon the face of the deep.** This means that all the "potential waters," which he calls the "abyss" <note>The Latin *abyssus* refers to the primordial deep or the vast, unformed waters of creation.</note> (which were the material subject of the world), remained at rest in the presence of darkness. They stayed in that same potential state until they were brought into act by the manifestation and revelation of the radiant Spirit of **Elohim** <note>original: *Spiritus Elohim*; the Hebrew name for God used in Genesis</note>, becoming "something" out of "nothing." But light in its own nature, without respect to matter, is purely an igneous Spirit, the divine offspring of **Elohim**, or the first and immediate emanation from the very source of light.

And hence **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the *Hermetica* are attributed; Fludd views him as a primary philosophical authority.</note> said in the place cited above: **The Word standing by the moist nature cherished it, etc.** And in Sermon 3: **The holy splendor flourished, etc.** And **St. Peter** in his **2nd Epistle 3:5-6**: **The heavens and the earth were of water, and through water, consisting by the Word of God.** This means that the water, from which all things were made, was informed by the presence of the divine Spirit, or the Word of God, or Wisdom. And just as the Form is mixed into any creature so that it may exist, so also divine light is present in every structure, lest a vacuum exist within it; for without it, nothing could subsist for even a moment of time.
