It **disposed the measures of the earth, stretched the line upon it, and laid its cornerstone** (**Job 38:4**). It **stretches out the North over the empty place, and hangs the earth upon nothing; it encompasses the waters with bounds, until light and darkness come to an end** (**Job 26**).

Who can narrate the wonders of this uncreated light? Who can express with a tongue its power, through which all things were made, and without which nothing was made; for in it is the life of all things? And this is that unique Word, **"Let it be"** <note>original: *Fiat*</note>, hidden in the darkness before the creation of the world. For although it flowed out from the Father, it nevertheless returned into the Father, according to that saying of **Hermes Trismegistus**: **The Monad generates the Monad, and reflected its heat into itself.** But when He decided by His secret counsel to fabricate the world in the lap of **hyle** <note>term: *hyle* — The Greek word for "matter," used by philosophers to describe the raw, unformed substance of the universe.</note>, God revealed His form, and the Word now "made" came forth; by its power the waters appeared and became visible, and were distinguished into various proportions.

But if these things are not enough for the readers—insofar as many (I know) have said that I have fallen into a great error because I affirmed the first matter to be formless, that is, uncreated—I will bring forth even more evident testimonies confirming my opinion to the mind, proving namely that the aqueous foundations of the world leaped out from the belly of **hyle** and Chaos by the power of divine light. For first, in **Job 12:22**, we find this: **He who reveals deep things out of darkness, and brought out the lethal shadow into light.** Here, by "revelation," he understands "creation"; by "deep things," he understands the waters or the informed abyss; and by "lethal shadow," he understands the earth, which was void, desolate, and empty. It is called "lethal" <note>Lethal here implies "dead" or "non-living" rather than "deadly."</note> because its soul was void, but it has now been made alive.

Thus, from this place, we perceive that heaven and earth themselves leaped out from the primary darkness, or the lap of **hyle**. Again, we read in **Wisdom 11:18**: **God made the world out of formless matter** <note>Fludd notes different translations: Pagninus uses "formless matter," Tremellius uses "created," and Jerome/The Vulgate uses "invisible matter."</note>.

Here indeed, the entire mystery of the whole creation is openly declared: First, namely, that the first matter from which the world was created was uncreated or "uninformed" matter; which, insofar as it is formless, is called "nothing," because it is not in "act." And consequently, that darkness was like a mother from whose womb the world—that is, the universal water—came forth.

Moreover, how God bore Himself within the darkness, we have abundantly declared. So also in **1 Chronicles 6:1** and **1 Kings 8:12**, it is narrated that Jehovah **said He would dwell in thick darkness.** And **Psalm 18:11**: **He made darkness His secret place, His pavilion round about Him was dark waters and thick clouds.** Similarly, **Psalm 97:2**: **Clouds and darkness are round about Him.** And **Psalm 104**: **Thick clouds are the chariot of God.** And **Psalm 105:39**: **God spread a cloud for a covering.** And **Job 22:15**: **Thick clouds are a hiding place for God.** And although these things may not seem in all these places to be taken for the primordial darkness that was upon the face of the abyss, nevertheless, he who understands me rightly will perceive that the reasoning is the same regarding the hiding of God in the primordial darkness as it is in the re-

For as the form is, so also is the matter; since matter conducts itself in proportion to the very form that makes it what it is.

For this reason, we say that the assertion of **Johannes Kepler** is erroneous, where he wished to claim (in Text 20) that the formal pyramid was unequal to the material proportion. For who, if they are consistent, can doubt the shape of the Physical formal pyramid if they follow these proportions of nature: *Heavy Earth, Spongy Earth, Quicksilver, metallic water, salt water, tasteless fresh water, mist, clouds, vapor, air, exhalation, fire, ethereal Spirit of many degrees, and finally the Empyrean Spirit,* where the cone of the material pyramid ends, insofar as matter can be purified no further? 

Therefore, the cone <note>the pointed tip</note> of this [material] pyramid ends in the center of the formal base. For if light was created on the first day, and this before the creation of the "middle heaven," where would it exist if not in some third and supreme heaven? If the light of the whole world was created there, is it not likely that its spirit exists in the highest degree of purity? Even the smallest light acts, and by acting it moves, and by moving it heats, and by heating it thins out that which is thick. O, how pure and subtle must that spirit be which is the receptacle of such great, pleasant, and divine light! 

Do we not see by daily experience (or demonstration *a posteriori* <note>reasoning from effects back to causes</note>) that by the power of an inferior fire, the **Spirit of Wine** arises? This is called the "fifth essence" <note>the quintessence</note> because of its subtlety; it is such because of the perfect heat of its internal light. It claims the highest place of dignity by natural instinct; if the act of fire is applied to it, it will imitate the sweetest act of divine light by burning—doing so without any injury or harm to flesh, linen, or paper. After this naturally ascends the fiery Spirit of wine, which, because of the density of its substance, burns and damages things as it flames, since it has more matter and less fiery form; thus it tends to harm because of the strong resistance of the matter. This is followed by the **oil of tartar** <term>oleum tartari: a concentrated potassium carbonate solution used in alchemy</term>, which burns when compared to air, but in a more violent and rapid manner. Next comes the phlegm; then the liquor of dissolved Salt of Tartar, and finally the dregs of the whole. 

Do we not see here the order of all nature shining most exactly even in a tiny creature? And yet should we doubt the action and passion of these pyramids—of light and of the darkness of humid matter—when the formal substance of terrestrial fire is the same as that celestial fire from which it descended in the beginning? Now also, we see heaven, the elements, and earth in this single creature. Are not all the heavens found in proportion within the earth itself, as much as in the ethereal and empyrean heaven of the world? Indeed they are, if you have understood me correctly.

> *God, reigning in the highest summit of the heavens, is nevertheless the center of every thing and every part of the world; whose circumference, nonetheless, is outside all things.*

Understand me, then, in both ways: either in the common sense or the mystical; it matters not here. For a Bishop is said to be exalted in dignity, even though he does not leave his station on the earth. For earth is accustomed to be converted into heaven through purification, and the imperfect is raised into perfection without consideration of the measurement of lines. This is quite different from what our Johannes [Kepler] thought—who, being fuller of Mathematical doctrine than instructed in true Physical erudition, foolishly thinks all units must be measured by lines. Do we not see heaven and earth within man himself? And yet the earth is on the outside, while heaven is on the inside: nonetheless, the "summit of the heavens" is where the most pure and simple mind dwells. To this mind, the earth is called the "center" insofar as earth is furthest from the circumference (the heaven); thus God's purity is as distant as possible from the impurity of the dark earth.

But let us return to the matter. We see that every thing naturally tends toward its own country: just as a heavy thing tends downward and rests there, so fire tends upward. In its motion, according to its nature, fire forms a pyramid, as we see in a candle. This figure consists more in the ascent of smoky matter than in the nature of pure light: and yet, such is that form, because the disposition of the form makes it so by natural instinct. What we mean by "physical pyramids," we have explained in a book dedicated solely to this matter at the end of the *Technical History of the Microcosm*. We have received the reasons for these pyramids from the wise Rabbis and elsewhere:

> *For in the book **The Gate of Light** <note>original: "De porta lucis"; refers to the Sha'are Orah, a famous Kabbalistic text by Joseph Gikatilla</note>, chapter 2, it is said that all things having life tend upward by their instinct (that is, toward perfection), and all things infusing life always turn downward.*

From this, the appetite of matter (tending upward toward the palace of form) and the duty of the inflowing form are declared clearly enough. Furthermore, considering these positions of the pyramids in terms of the dignity or worthlessness of the subject, **Reuchlin** <note>Johannes Reuchlin, a famous German humanist and scholar of Kabbalah</note> describes them thus:

> *The sublimation of metals occurs when that which is more noble boils up into higher spirits, having been sublimated by Alchemy, so that those things which are higher always appear purer. Thus also, things among the inhabitants of the lower world are said to be leaden and squalid, weighed down by filth; while we admire those among the inhabitants of the upper world as white and illustrious, adorned with incredible beauty, and we pursue them with songs of praise.*

Thus he spoke. And certainly, if one proceeds from the highest imperfection to "more-than-perfection" by the act of light, there indeed the degrees and proportions of harmony are the same, and—

### ANALYTICAL DISCOURSE

...just as we find in the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the entire universe.</note>, we shall find even in a tiny creature springing from the disturbed abyss. The midpoint of movement—stretching from the squalid base of imperfection to that most exalted divine light which is continuous with the Deity—will be the seat or degree of perfection. This is the seat of the **Soul of the World**, whether in the small or the great, through which the "sphere of equality" passes. Here, the proportion is a double one: just as a string on a **Monochord** <term>Monochord: a single-stringed instrument used by ancient and Renaissance theorists to demonstrate the mathematical ratios of musical intervals</term> sounds an **Octave** <note>original: "Diapason"</note> when pressed in the middle, reaching from the starting point (the base of earth or imperfection) to the goal of perfection (which is contiguous with God). Thus, the proportion from the starting point to the middle—the place of the **Sun**—is to the whole string (reaching from earth to God) as 1 is to 4, or as an Octave is to a Double Octave <note>original: "Disdiapason"</note>, or as 1 is to 2.

Indeed, I would wish **Johannes Kepler** to understand that in measuring this "string," there is no need for linear measurements or mathematical proportions, but rather purely physical and formal ones. Without these, it is impossible to progress in the study of **Natural Music**.

The **Alchemists** <note>original: "Chymici"</note> seem to hint at this, albeit in enigmatic speech, when they say that "everything naturally flees from its adversary but delights in its like." From this they conclude that the **Sun** (or **Sulphur** <note>In alchemy, Sulphur represents the active, fiery, and masculine principle of nature.</note>) is nothing other than pure fire hidden within **Mercury** <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the passive, fluid, and feminine principle of matter.</note>. They say that its weights and properties are relative to the sulphur existing within the mercury. For the element of fire—which does not dominate in raw mercury—is the very thing that "digests" or matures matter, whether in the Macrocosm, the Microcosm, other creatures, or even in a ripening apple. Therefore, everyone who concerns themselves with true Philosophy must know how much subtler the element of fire is than the other elements, and by what proportion it is able to overcome them. The true "weight," then, is found in the first elementary composition of Mercury, and not in any other work. In a clearly similar way, the composition of our "natural pyramids" is formed in both the great and the lesser world, and the true harmony of both is adapted to such proportions. The Sun, therefore, receives its light through an Octave from God, via the **Spirit of Wisdom**, and it disperses the gifts of Wisdom through the **World Spirit** <note>original: "Spiritum mundanum"</note>. And this string of harmony is the same in the world itself as it is in a creature only an inch long.

For the progression from the highest degree of imperfection to the goal of supreme perfection, passing through the "moderately perfect," exists in the smallest thing just as in the greatest. In the most imperfect degree, there is only a tiny portion of light (or fire, or sulphur); as it progresses, the portion of fire gradually overcomes the matter, until it turns the whole of the matter into a fiery nature, or a "Sun" of the highest degree. In the **Microcosm** <note>The "Little World," specifically the human being.</note>, there is a higher degree of Wisdom than in any other creature; and therefore, with the assistance of Grace, it can most easily be led back to divine perfection.

Hence **Reuchlin** <note>Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a German humanist and scholar of the Cabala.</note> says:
> *God composed the better nature of man out of two things, as the most sacred scripture stands: from the mud of the earth and the breath of life. Thus, clothed in mud, he may prudently care for bodies; and endowed with the breath of life, he may wisely love divine things and aspire to them.*

And **Mercurius Trismegistus** says: *Man is a great miracle, an animal to be adored and honored; for he himself passes into the nature of God.* And **Saint Paul** says: *From corruption he shall ascend to incorruption; from a mortal he shall become immortal.* Thus **Adam**, who was the root of the whole human race, being infected, infected all the branches and leaves of the tree, according to that passage in Romans: *The root of bitterness sprouting upward hinders, and through it many are defiled.* But a holy root produces holy branches; and such was the **Second Adam** <note>A common theological title for Jesus Christ.</note>, whose root descends and moves against the root of the lower movement. For the earthly Adam moves against the heavenly Adam. These are the words of **Archangelus** <note>Archangelus of Borgonovo, a 16th-century Franciscan Cabalist.</note> in his Cabalistic dogma. By these words, he seems to suggest that the internal or "formal" movement—which we have depicted as a pyramid—is reflected in the external movement of man himself. Regarding the "descending act" and the "passive ascent" of the Macrocosm, he speaks thus:
> *Whatever stands apart from God in the first and purest act must necessarily enter into matter. When natural philosophers describe the breadth of beings, they place pure act without matter at the summit; at the bottom is matter without form.*

So says he: By "matter without form," he understands the earth, which is empty in itself but fertile by accident, insofar as it receives the influences emitted from above by God and the **Sephiroth** <term>Sephiroth: in the Jewish Cabala, the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite (Ein Sof) reveals itself</term>. The earth is their receptacle and, as it were, their womb. From its belly, a smoky matter gradually ascends, always dilating more as it tends upward. This is due to its increase in proportion to the "luminous acts," whose nature is always to strive toward purification and refinement. Therefore, just as matter stands in its purity, so we are accustomed to judge the proportion of the form dwelling within it. For we can only see the proportion of the "acting nature" by its effect, and not otherwise; because it is the "invisible fire" of **Zoroaster** and **Heraclitus**, of which Job 28:12 says: *Wisdom is drawn from secret places; it is hidden from the eyes of all living things; it is concealed even from the birds of the air.*

We conclude, therefore, as was said before: just as the soul is said to be in the whole and in every part of the whole, so too the pyramidal progression of physical matter proves that an internal form exists within it, exactly matching the matter itself. Consequently, that "mathematical musician" <note>A dismissive reference to Kepler.</note> spoke ill-advisedly when he said the formal pyramid was unequal to the material one. For as the disposition of the matter is, so too is the proportion of the form; since it is the nature of form to make the matter like itself. It is certain that matter, in its ascent, follows a pyramidal progression understood in a physical way: water is ten times subtler than earth; air is subtler than water; fire is subtler than air; and the **Quintessence** (the matter of heaven) is subtler than fire; and so on with the rest. Indeed, in every element there are infinite degrees of subtleness, which would be impossible to list here.

From this it is clear how futile is that argument of Johannes [Kepler], by which he tries to prove that there is no unity in natural things that cannot be measured by those same [mathematical] lines. It is as if a handful of earth could not be turned into water! In such a case, the "units" differ according to a mathematician because of the expansion of one and the constriction of the other; and yet, by physical reasoning, they are the same when considering their **philosophical weights**. For a greater proportion of fire (or sulphur) indicates a subtler substance, while a smaller proportion indicates a coarser one; and thus, in both subtleness and coarseness...

### TO THE KEPLERIAN APPENDIX

Proportions of identity in physical things consist as much in perfection as in imperfection; these behave differently than they do in Mathematics. And yet, in the mathematical fashion—that is, by means of mathematical pyramids and their units—I have demonstrated this, because it was impossible to aptly explain physical proportions in their own order, as they are infinite in their motion. From these pyramids mixed together, as if from the four universal elements, the **Cube** is composed in physical reality—a composite body consisting of the number eight <note>A cube has eight corners, which Fludd associates with the stability of matter.</note>—which by its own nature is earth or clay, or some similar compact substance, whether in the sublunary or the celestial heaven. 

And in this final species of worldly harmony, there is a twofold difference in the subject and its motion: either it is carried toward generation and growth, or toward corruption and diminution. (The effects of which are declared by constant experience in the composite things of the animal, vegetable, and mineral kingdoms.) Or, it remains always as it was made in creation, but continually receives life and motion from **Divine Wisdom**, which acts by "walking" everywhere in the cavity of the world. It receives life, I say, so that it may exist and have continuity in the nature of things; and it obtains motion, whether manifest or hidden, so that it may perform that office for which it was created and destined by its Creator. 

Of this kind are the mineral bodies in the sublunary regions, since they live an occult <note>Hidden or inner life.</note> life and have the duty of serving mankind. In the celestial regions, however, there are the bodies of the stars, whose office it is—under the dominion of the Sun—to rule the day and transform the shadows of night into daylight. And when the Moon dominates with the other stars, their office is to provide light to the encroaching shadows of the night, and to serve as signs for seasons, days, and years. Their motions are contained within that **Harmony** which emanates from the sympathy of the universal elements, just as this harmony emanates from the threefold, simple, and primordial Harmony. 

Therefore, the "concert" of the stars is contained in the **Cubic** species of harmony, which depends on the greater or lesser predominance of light within the stellar bodies. According to the stated proportions, this harmony moves the bodies in which it resides either faster or slower, and places them higher or lower in the ether and its orbs. For thus we see that a war engine <note>original: "tormentum bellicum," a cannon.</note> loaded with more gunpowder tends to carry its ball further and faster, and an artificial firework <note>original: "fusum artificiale."</note>—according to the greater proportion of its fuel or flame—is carried higher toward the region of heaven. These motions are therefore durable, and the bodies in which they exist are of such a nature. 

But truly, since the motion of the stars proceeds from the elements of heaven themselves, it is clear that the harmony proceeding from there is derived from those very elements. In these elements, the nature of things—or Wisdom—lay hidden before the stars were created. For it is necessary that the thing produced follows the principle <note>The source or origin.</note>, just as a son follows a father, and the "elemented" follows the element. Just as it is absurd to attribute the origin of a father's life to his son, so it is no less absurd to apply the harmony of the elements to the **Planets** themselves, which are things made of elements. And if you wish to know from the testimony of the Sacred Font <note>The Bible.</note> what this elemental harmony is like, and what motion it arises from, read the 19th and final chapter of **Wisdom** <note>The Book of the Wisdom of Solomon.</note>, starting from verse 17, where you will find words clearly revealing the motion and Music of the elements:

> For while the elements are changed among themselves—just as the sound of a quality is changed in an organ or a psaltery (he does not say a sound of quantity)—they all keep their own sound; which may be surely estimated from the sight itself. For earthly things were turned into aquatic ones, and whatever was swimming passed over to the land; fire prevailed in water beyond its own power, and water forgot its extinguishing nature, etc. <note>original: "In se enim dum elementa convertuntur..." quoting Wisdom of Solomon 19:17–20.</note>

Here, indeed, one may perceive the power and harmony of the elements; yet in this harmony, no mention is made of that of the Planets. On the contrary, this kind of harmonic action and passion of the elements exercised its strength in the "World Pyramids" long before the fourth day of creation. Indeed, there was a rotation of one element into another, through which motion occurred from the immaturity of plants toward perfect maturity, by the motion and proportion of the increase of **Sulfur** in **Mercury** <note>Fludd is using alchemical terms here: Sulfur represents the active/masculine principle (form/light) and Mercury the passive/feminine principle (matter/moisture).</note>—that is, of fire in water, whether thin or thick—and from a simple number to the multiplication of species through created seedbeds. Wherefore, God said before the fourth day, addressing His Wisdom:

> Let the earth bring forth green herb, and such as may seed according to its kind, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after its kind, and having each its seed according to its species. And God saw that it was good. <note>original: "Germinet terra herbam virentem..." quoting Genesis 1:11–12.</note>

But if this harmony was infused into these composite creatures after the creation of the elements, how much more did God infuse a power similar to harmony into the elements themselves? Wherefore it was said after the appearance of the Divine Spirit:

> And God saw the light, that it was good; and He made the firmament, which He called heaven. And God said, let the waters that are under the heaven be gathered together, and let the dry land appear, and He called the dry land earth, etc. <note>Genesis 1:4–10.</note>

Is there not here an admirable harmony of the elements in the **Worldly Organ**, whose blower was **Elohim** <note>God.</note>, whose sound or voice was the **Word** from His mouth, and whose adapter of harmonic consonances and powers was that **Fiery Spirit**? This Spirit—the form of worldly harmony proceeding from the Breather and the Voice—infused power and action into every element in its own degree, according to the dignity of its matter. This is perfectly declared by these words of the Royal Psalmist in Psalm 33:6:

> By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all their power by the spirit of his mouth. <note>original: "Verbo Domini firmati sunt coeli..."</note>

From this Spirit of Wisdom, therefore, proceeds the Harmony of the whole world, attributing and conferring power to every species according to the proportion ordained for it by the Creator at creation for the legitimate execution of its office. Nor should this Spirit be sought in "heaven" in the common sense; for it is everywhere in the expanse of the world, and always works everywhere, according to that saying in Matthew:

> Heaven is his throne, and the earth is his footstool; <note>Matthew 5:34–35, referencing Isaiah 66:1.</note>

And Wisdom 1:7:

> The Spirit of the Lord fills the whole world, and that which contains all things has knowledge of the voice. <note>original: "Spiritus Domini implet orbem terrarum..."</note>

This, then, is the true **Sun of Nature**,

# ANALYTICAL DISCOURSE

...giving life and glory to the world and its creatures, and nourishing the hosts of the heavens by his presence, making them move; his hidden tabernacle is in the center of his elements, while his symphonic rays penetrate everywhere and are present everywhere. Now let us descend to the division of the world, or the four universal elements, into parts—namely, the three heavens. For following the extension of the number two into its **square** and **cube**, there follows the **number three** <note>The ternary number</note>, which includes that imperfect and material number <note>two</note> along with the primordial unity, whereby two unities so confused are reduced into a single number, which is the root of perfect things. Thus also its property in the world follows the watery nature divided into Elements. Therefore, according to the properties of the Divine Trinity, the world is distinguished into three regions that do not differ in the matter of their physical units. These distinctions were produced by **Wisdom**, whose spirit was the **glue** <note>original: "gluten"</note> between the water and the light, or rather the offspring of divine power and its very act. For "act" is that effect of light by which one unit of matter differs from another. And again, each of these heavens is subdivided into three other regions; for instance, the **Empyrean heaven** <note>The highest, most spiritual heaven of pure fire and light</note> into three hierarchies, and again each of those into three other portions attributed to the orders of angels; and so on for the others. For this is the work and office of the **fiery spirit**, which distinguishes all things first through its root of 3, into its square of 9 (which is how many regions each heaven is divided into), and then into its cube of 27—which, according to the **Platonists**, is the mathematical measure of the entire semi-diameter. Therefore, the ternary division comes from the side of the soul or the informing power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH</note>, while the binary progression comes from the side of the informed matter. For the universal elements were produced immediately after divine power was reduced into act. But the heavens were completed on the second and third days. Regarding the multitude of heavens, we have testimony from the sacred scriptures: *Jehovah established the heavens by his wisdom, Proverbs 3:19. The heavens of heavens belong to the God of Gods, Deuteronomy 10:14. Jehovah made the heavens of heavens, and all their host, Nehemiah 9:6. The heavens of heavens, and the waters that are above the heavens, praise God, Psalm 148:4.* From these it is clear that there is a number of heavens, which appears to be three; of these heavens, the first was the work of the first day. For in what place would the light be put, if not in its own proper Empyrean heaven, seeing as neither the ethereal nor sublunary heavens were yet created? Does not **Paul** also say that he was snatched up into the "third heaven," where he confesses he saw wonderful and ineffable things? Yet he <note>Kepler or a similar opponent</note> nonetheless wishes the entire harmony of the world to arise from the outer motions of the **Planets**—motions which are indeed circular. Consequently, he denies that any harmony can be found in the degrees of distance between one end of the world-machine’s semi-diameter and the other, as appears from the text of 18, 19, 20. Truly, however, we perceive that **Plato**, in his *Timaeus*, used the **number three** for the formation and measurement of the world; it is the first odd number for the root of the composite world by which it is distinguished into regions. Its square is 9 and its cube is 27. By this number he measured the ratio of the world's orbs, concluding from it that the further one proceeds from the periphery, the thicker the degree of worldly substance becomes; not otherwise than progress is made from a root toward a cube in the depth of a body. But truly, since three sets of nine are found in 27, Plato arranged them in this way toward his cube, by which he measured the world’s semi-diameter: 9, 9, 9. If **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing 1</note> is added, which signifies unity, the number **one thousand** is produced, beyond which there is no further progression. Hence, just as the Hebrews have a "Small Aleph" for the unity of all things and the starting point, so the "Great Aleph" denotes the number one thousand, which is the destination. For this reason, the one God is called **Alpha and Omega**, the beginning and the end. For the number ten is the root of the number one thousand (which is a cube), whose square is 100. Thus Plato most aptly delineated the fabric of the world in the number one thousand, namely 9, 9, 9. In these formal dimensions he placed the entire harmony of **Worldly Music** <note>original: "Musicæ mundanæ"</note>. **Francesco Giorgio of Venice** <note>A Franciscan friar and influential Christian Kabbalist</note> also seems to agree with this, having completed an entire, indeed a massive, volume on this same subject, and wrote most learnedly. Therefore, the Hebrews establish the first "nine-fold" number as a simple number, insofar as it is contained under 10; and they wish it, on account of its simplicity, to be a formal and essential number, attributing it to the **nine orders of Angels** who are in the intelligible world. The difference between these orders denotes the variety of degrees and harmony by which one excels another in proportion and arrangement. **Dionysius**, **Isidore**, and other fathers of theology fell into this same opinion. Is this harmony, then, derived from the motions of the Planets? The second order of tens, insofar as it is found in the square or number 100, participates in thicker matter; hence these are attributed to the elementary worlds. Finally, the third descends into the cubic number or one thousand, insofar as it is more material and closer to composition, in which are contained 9 types of things that can be generated and corrupted in the elementary world. This descent from simplicity to composition, and the harmonic propagation between one sphere and another in that descent, was recognized by Plato and other wise men. This metric harmony of the world is not attributed to the motions of the planets, for they make their own harmony, proper to themselves as particular creatures; their duties pertain to sound in the world's offices, and not to the universe as a whole. The universe's harmony consists in a greater or lesser proportion of **eternal light** in the worldly spirit, or, speaking chemically, the degree of **Sulphur** in **Mercury**. Furthermore, the Author himself <note>Pythagoras</note>, in the preface of his third book, recognizes this descent from unity in the number nine to have been the opinion of **Pythagoras** himself, who in his **Tetractys** makes the matter of the world descend in my fashion from unity into an even number—from the root 2, through the square 4, to the Cube...

->**8** --- **12** --- **18** --- **27**<-
->(o) --- (m) --- (y)<-

Here, beginning from the binary number <note>the number 2</note>, twice 2 is 4; twice 3 is 6; twice 4 is 8; twice 6 is 12; twice 9 is 18. Then we proceed to the ternary number <note>the number 3</note>, and we say that three times 2 is 6; three times 4 is 12; three times 6 is 18; and three times 9 is 27. From the first triangle **1, 2, 3**, we conceive the first and simplest type of composition, which is made from the elements of the **Empyrean heaven** <note>The highest heaven of pure light and fire</note>; this is the composition that exists in the radical number of the angels. From the second triangle **1, 4, 9**, we gather the composition of the secondary species, namely from the ethereal elements; this belongs to the stars, contained within the square number. In that greatest triangle, however—**1, 8, 27**—the entire world consists with its base; this denotes the composition from the sublunary elements <note>The world below the moon, including Earth</note>, from which imperfect bodies (such as meteors) and perfectly composed bodies (such as animals, vegetables, and minerals) are made.

The reason for this is that the substance of the elements is ordered on the left side, while their form is ordered on the right. We see here that **1** is the author of both the odd and even numbers, distributed equally to each side. For from **1**, as if from an eternal power, matter is derived on one side, which is also brought into action by **1**; hence, 2 becomes 3, and they denote the bond and unity of light with spirit in the first composition of elements. Next, on the left side of the second triangle, **1** is joined with 4 (the square of matter), and the second composition of elements is made. Finally, from 8, the **1** looks downward and produces the thicker elements of the third composition.

In the highest region, therefore, unity is joined with 2 by an inviolable bond, and the angelic soul is created with such a body through the number 3, where 1 is the soul and 2 is the body. In the middle region, 3 mixes itself with 4 and 2, and the stellar soul and body are made according to the perfection of the number 9; here, 4 and 2 indicate 6 (the corporeal elements of the star), and 3 (the addition of which produces 9, the square of the ternary number) represents its soul. From these things, it is quite clear that the angelic composition of the higher heaven, which consists in 3, is the soul of the bodies of the middle heaven. Hence, the Cabalists <note>Followers of Jewish mysticism</note> called the Soul of the World the *Angel Metattron* <note>original: "Angelum Metattron"; Metatron is often described in mystical texts as the celestial scribe or the "lesser YHWH"</note>.

Finally, 4 and 8 make 12, by which number it is right to indicate an imperfectly mixed body; if the planetary body (namely 6) is added to this, it teaches the complete composition from the elements, which is 18. Its form will be 9, or the total composition of heaven, which is called the life of the lower world, but understood in a hidden way. Thus, the composition of the elementated creature will be completed in 27, which is the end of the world as well as of those things created within it.

There is, therefore, a **double proportion** <note>original: "proportio superbipartiens secundas"; a ratio of 2:1</note> in the constitution of the elements, such as 2 to 1, 4 to 2, and 8 to 4. Similarly, the procreation of creatures proceeds in a **triple proportion** <note>original: "proportione tertias supertripartiente"; a ratio of 3:1</note>, such as 6 to 3 and 12 to 6. And for the union of a composed creature with its elements, the power of a triple nature is required, which is the "binding" of the elements. In its simple formal progression, it moves from the root 3 to 27; and by reason of composition, as 18 to 9 and 27 to 18. In this progression, the number nine always increases itself by its own dimension until it reaches the cube of its root <note>3 cubed is 27</note>.

From these things, one may see that the soul of the Empyrean heaven and the form of the angels is an immediate emanation from **1**. The entire composition of this heaven is like the soul of the middle heaven, whose "fifth being" <note>the quintessence</note> is called the life of lower things. And yet, both matter (whose immersion into even multiplicity is observed through the left side of the Triangle) and form (which descends on the right side from unity to odd multiplicity) have their origin in **1**. Therefore, the whole—both formal and material—is in truth nothing other than merely "One," although to us, it seems to be immersed in multiplicity.

Upon this depends the universal Harmony of the world: from here all proportions arise, to which the Music of creatures is adapted. For in the **double proportion** <note>The ratio of 2:1</note> consist 2 to 1, 4 to 2, and 8 to 4, from which the *Diapason* <note>An octave</note> and its doubles are forged; consequently, the creation of the elements, from which the world is forged, arises from it. In the **sesquialtera** <note>The ratio of 3:2, known in music as a Perfect Fifth</note>, we find the relationship of elementary matter to the form of the composite; thus 3 relates to 2, 9 to 6, 6 to 4, 12 to 8, 18 to 12, and 27 to 18. From this follows the complete mixing of form with elementary matter. In the **sesquitertia** proportion <note>The ratio of 4:3, known in music as a Perfect Fourth</note>, imperfectly mixed things are produced, so that they might sound between matter and form to complete the composition; thus 4 relates to 3, 8 to 6, and 12 to 9.

And so the universal Harmony of nature is completed, initiated from that point which is above all being. From the inspection and observation of that figure, we perceive that the creatures of the Empyrean heaven (that is, of the highest created purity) are composed of two things: light and spirit. From the observation of its base, those of the middle heaven are composed of three: the two higher ones and a third, thicker one (as seen in the base **4, 6, 9**). The lowest, however, is composed of four: namely, from the sublunary elements increased by proportion. So we see that 2 proceeded immediately from 1 through doubling, from which, with 1 added, 3 is made—the triangle of the first composition, denoting...

<meta>This page concludes Robert Fludd’s critique of Johannes Kepler. Fludd continues using the "Platonic Lambda" (the triangular numerical arrangement from the previous page) to map out the hierarchy of the universe, moving from the angelic realm down to physical matter, and finally contrasting his mystical "Gematria" with Kepler's astronomical calculations.</meta>

### ANALYTICAL DISCOURSE

...otherness, or the angelic nature; according to whose pattern all the small particles of the world were established, according to that verse of Job: *Who laid its cornerstone?* <note>original: "Quis jecit lapidem ejus angularem?" Job 38:6.</note> Thus the triangle stands as in the higher place, 1, 2, 3. Where to this heaven or composition are attributed the first two letters of the Tetragrammaton: יה <note>The Hebrew letters Yod and He (Yah), representing the first part of God's holy name.</note>. Then, by adding in a transverse way 3 to the number 4, it produces the number seven, the attribute of human life, just as the Hexad <note>the number 6</note> is attributed to his body. Hence it is said: *You made man a little lower than the angels.* <note>Psalm 8:5</note>. But in the order of nature, 1, 2, 4 from one side and 3, 9 from the other denote the Triangle of the second composition, which relates to the first as a square from a root: therefore it denotes the middle heaven with its bodies, which are defined as the denser parts of those orbs. From which it is clear that both heavens are found abundantly in the internal man.

The remaining creatures, however, come from the descent and composition of the deeper soul into the matter of the earth. Whence the wise have adapted the Ennead <note>the number 9</note> to all creatures. For the triangle seeks a deeper base for their composition, and then it will stand thus: 1, 2, 4, 8 on one side, and 1, 3, 9, 27 on the other, as shown above. Whence the first triangle is like the root to the lower things, the second like the square, and the lowest like the Cube, both in the composition of the world of the heavens and in the constitution of those same creatures. 

Whence it is clear that Universal Harmony occurs by descending, and by no means from the circular motion of the Planets; for these did not exist in the nature of things except finally after the worldly fabric, which was made step by step by descending, as we gather from the sacred scriptures. And so it is established from there that the intentions of Plato and Pythagoras were far different than adapting the mysteries of the five regular solids <note>the Platonic solids: tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron</note> to the motions of the Planets; rather, they referred them to the distances of the elements from one another, by which the harmony of forms and matters differed because of the variety of proportions. 

But truly Arithmetic and Geometry of this kind, by which this Harmony is made, are not common, but truly formal, comprised under this Hebrew word *Ghematria* <note>Gematria: a Kabbalistic method of interpreting Hebrew words by calculating their numerical value</note>; which is concerned with the profound meditation of the Kabbalah, Natural Magic, and true Alchemy—that is, the Elementary, celestial, and supramundane or intelligible science. We conclude, therefore, that we primarily have the sacred scriptures and also the arguments of the most excellent Philosophers defending this our opinion about the Harmony of the world, which in every way seem to oppose the foundations of Kepler. 

I likewise have a most exact demonstration of this worldly Harmony in the experiment of a certain most noble creature; in whose dissection <term>anatomization<gloss>the act of dissecting a body to study its structure</gloss></term> I observed all these things with my eyes and mind; which indeed I have decided to publish at the end and completion of my works for the common benefit. Which indeed, though it be a small secret compared to that greatest arcanum <note>secret mystery</note> which the most celebrated Brothers of the Rosy Cross <note>original: "Fratres de Rosea Cruce," the Rosicrucians, a secret society of sages Fludd often defended</note> confess they understand; nevertheless, just as they themselves (I know well) understand and possess the celestial bread of Angels, about which the sacred scriptures have sung such wonders everywhere, so also I shall expose for the public good, God willing, the physical secrets of the earthly bread, perceived by no one until now as far as I know. And I shall call that treatise of mine *The Minor Key of Philosophy, or an Ocular Experiment*; because the title *The Key of Philosophy and True Pansophy* <note>Pansophy: universal wisdom or all-encompassing knowledge</note> most rightly belongs to their secret, which seems to differ not at all from that Key of David, as may be gathered from their writings. 

Finally, as for the Harmony of the Planets, we say that it is specific to them and ordained by the Creator, so that in its proportions, by which they are naturally moved, *there may be signs for fixed times, and for days and years;* <note>Genesis 1:14</note> and so that in the daily motions, namely of the Sun, light *may be present for the earth for the daytime, and rule the day*, and the Moon with the other stars may have the power of obtaining dominion over the night. *Psalm 136:8.* We do not read in the sacred scriptures that they were ordained by God for any other use; although the Sun of heaven in its acquired perfection seems to perform wonders: For that preeminent Sun is the only and unique Wisdom, but invisible in itself, present everywhere night and day, exhibiting and liberally pouring out glory and life to every creature. Without which morning star there is no true science of Astronomy, no certain prediction of Astrologers, or right knowledge of the Harmony of the world.

And so I have successfully woven this discourse to the last part of Johannes Kepler’s Appendix—though not as I wished, yet as I was able—invited to this work not by my own will, but incited by the stings of another’s envy, with the immense thanks of God the Best and Greatest leading the way.

->F I N I S.<-

He references the Rosicrucians and announces a future work based on anatomical observation that will prove his metaphysical theories.</summary>
